focus.explanation: A dismissal of the Government's whole legislative programme as 'gimmicks' without naming a single measure, cost or mechanism. It is directed at a policy document rather than at the party as a tribe, which keeps it off the floor, but there is no policy content to engage with.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: This Government is shaping up to be the Grinch who stole Christmas—the “Grinch who privatised Christmas”.
focus.explanation: Characterisation of the other side with no named policy, figure or outcome. 'Privatised' gestures at a policy direction but nothing is specified. No individual is insulted, so this is a Focus item rather than a Civility one.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Sorry, kids, nothing under the Christmas tree this Christmas but pseudoephedrine, cigarettes, and guns, and especially bad luck if you wanted a Government that would give us a stable climate.
focus.explanation: Four real policy areas are named — pseudoephedrine reclassification, smokefree law, firearms law and climate — but they are carried entirely inside a party-framing joke with no mechanism, figure or outcome attached. A real policy point wrapped in framing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: But there’s one person I actually feel especially sorry for in this whole fair pay agreement debacle, and that is the new Minister for Workplace Relations and Safety, whose colleagues are already leaking on her within the first five minutes.
focus.explanation: The content is the other side's internal divisions — who is leaking on whom — rather than the fair pay agreements themselves. No mechanism, figure or outcome is named.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Fair pay agreements were designed to raise the bar for pay and conditions for poorly paid industries. The idea is simple: people working alongside each other who are doing a similar job in the same sector should be able to work together to make sure the minimum pay in their sector is fair for everyone.
focus.explanation: Squarely on the measure at issue: what fair pay agreements are for and how sector-level bargaining is meant to work. No party framing at all.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: All they care about is making it easier for businesses to get out of paying proper wages.
focus.explanation: Attributes a motive to the other side rather than engaging the repeal itself. It stays within the wage-policy topic, which keeps it off zero, but nothing about the measure — cost, coverage, effect — is offered.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: How embarrassing that up at COP28, this Government got called to account for wanting to reverse the oil and gas exploration ban.
veracity.explanation: Asserts as fact that at the COP28 climate conference the New Zealand Government was publicly criticised or challenged over its intention to reverse the 2018 ban on new offshore oil and gas exploration permits. Not a verdict on whether the reversal is right.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Contemporaneous COP28 (Dubai, Nov–Dec 2023) records and reporting: true if New Zealand was publicly called out at or around the conference — e.g. a Climate Action Network 'Fossil of the Day' citation, a formal statement by another delegation, or on-the-record criticism from conference participants — specifically over reversing the oil and gas exploration ban; false if no such public criticism at COP28 can be found.

veracity.statement: All we have is the official advice to the new Government that spells out in black and white that young people, women, Māori, and Pasifika will be harmed most of all of this legislation is removed.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that official advice provided to the incoming Government states that young people, women, Māori and Pasifika would be the groups most harmed by repeal of the Fair Pay Agreements Act. The claim is about what a document says, not about whether the prediction in it is correct. The garbled clause ('most of all of this legislation is removed') is a live-speech slip for 'most if this legislation is removed'.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The officials' advice to the incoming Government on repealing the Fair Pay Agreements Act 2022 — MBIE briefing to the incoming Minister and/or the regulatory impact statement for the Fair Pay Agreements Act Repeal Bill: true if that advice identifies young people, women, Māori and Pacific peoples as disproportionately affected by repeal; false if the advice contains no such finding or identifies materially different groups.

rigor.statement: But here’s the thing: the science tells us that we need to stop extracting oil and gas.
rigor.explanation: A real inference about a real policy, but it rests on a bare appeal to authority: 'the science' is invoked without naming a body, report or finding, and the leap from a scientific finding to a specific policy conclusion (cease extraction) is asserted rather than shown.
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: But there’s one person I actually feel especially sorry for in this whole fair pay agreement debacle, and that is the new Minister for Workplace Relations and Safety, whose colleagues are already leaking on her within the first five minutes.
civility.explanation: Mock pity aimed squarely at a named individual — the tone is sneering rather than substantive, and the point is her weakness within her own caucus rather than anything about the policy. Short of a direct insult, but it lands on the person, not the argument.
civility.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Fair pay agreements were designed to raise the bar for pay and conditions for poorly paid industries. The idea is simple: people working alongside each other who are doing a similar job in the same sector should be able to work together to make sure the minimum pay in their sector is fair for everyone.
specificity.explanation: Names the policy and describes its mechanism (sector-wide bargaining setting a minimum for similar work), but carries no figures, no coverage numbers and no timeframe.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: This is a Government that is focused on action, it is focused on results, it is focused on delivery, and we will deliver on what we have promised.
specificity.explanation: A string of generic virtues — action, results, delivery — with no policy, figure, mechanism or timeframe attached. Nothing here could be checked or acted on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We will narrow its focus to focus on inflation, which is the real killer for the household budgets of people across New Zealand, and it puts people into poverty.
specificity.explanation: Names a real mechanism — narrowing the Reserve Bank's mandate to inflation alone — so there is more than a slogan here, but no timeframe, no legislative vehicle and no target figure.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: In fact, in reading and science, our 15-year-olds are now a year behind where they were when testing first started.
specificity.explanation: Names the instrument (PISA), the cohort (15-year-olds), the domains and the size of the drop in years of schooling. Someone could go to the PISA tables and check it.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: The fair pay agreements is a well-intentioned idea, but the reality is that the majority—97 percent, in fact—of firms in New Zealand are small businesses.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that 97 percent of New Zealand firms are small businesses, which he immediately defines as having 20 or fewer employees.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ Business Demography Statistics (enterprise counts by employee size band) for the most recent year before December 2023: true if approximately 97% of New Zealand enterprises have fewer than 20 employees (the definition he gives in the following sentence); false if the share is materially different from 97%.

veracity.statement: In fact, in reading and science, our 15-year-olds are now a year behind where they were when testing first started.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that New Zealand's PISA reading and science results have fallen by about one year of schooling since the first cycle of testing.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: OECD PISA mean scores for New Zealand 15-year-olds in reading (first cycle 2000) and science (first cycle 2006) compared with the 2022 cycle released 5 December 2023, converted using the OECD convention of roughly 20 score points per year of schooling: true if both declines are approximately 20 points, false if either is materially smaller or larger.

veracity.statement: The previous Government, without a mandate, introduced co-governance provisions without discussing it with New Zealand.
veracity.explanation: Asserts two things about the 2020-23 Labour government: that it had no electoral mandate for co-governance provisions, and that it introduced them without public discussion.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Labour's 2020 election manifesto and policy releases, plus the public consultation record for the co-governance provisions of the Three Waters / Water Services Entities legislation and the Māori Health Authority: true if no such co-governance commitment was put to voters and no public consultation preceded the legislation; false if either the manifesto foreshadowed it or a documented public consultation process was run.

veracity.statement: We jumped a generation, previously, from coal, in many cases, straight to trying to find renewables which we didn’t actually have, and as a result we started importing record amounts of coal.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that New Zealand began importing record quantities of coal, presented as a consequence of moving away from gas before renewable capacity existed.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MBIE Energy in New Zealand / quarterly energy statistics on coal imports by volume: true if annual coal imports in 2021, 2022 or 2023 exceeded every previous year on record; false if earlier years were higher.

rigor.statement: There are about 546,000 small businesses in this country, and this well-intentioned but misguided aim to try and lift up the minimum wage—and I’ve talked to many, many small businesses—makes it actually impossible for many of them to hire new, young people to give them a chance.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion rests on anecdote ('I've talked to many, many small businesses') and on a count of small firms, neither of which shows that hiring becomes impossible. There is also a category slip: the premise is about Fair Pay Agreements, the conclusion about lifting the minimum wage, which are different instruments.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: We jumped a generation, previously, from coal, in many cases, straight to trying to find renewables which we didn’t actually have, and as a result we started importing record amounts of coal.
rigor.explanation: Post hoc reasoning: record coal imports are attributed to the skipping of gas as a transition fuel with nothing offered to connect them — no supply data, no counterfactual, and no account of the Huntly and hydro-lake conditions that also drive coal burn.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: There are about 546,000 small businesses in this country, and this well-intentioned but misguided aim to try and lift up the minimum wage—and I’ve talked to many, many small businesses—makes it actually impossible for many of them to hire new, young people to give them a chance.
focus.explanation: Squarely engages a named policy — Fair Pay Agreements — and its claimed effect on a named group of firms. The reasoning is weak, but that is Rigor's concern; nothing here is party-bashing.
focus.subject: speaker

civility.statement: When I hear the concerns expressed about Māori and the approach this Government is taking, now, let me just say that I know the Opposition has a role to take to criticise the Government, to raise issues, and to try and give themselves a chance to win back again, but let’s be responsible about the terminology we use here, because this is a Government that is focused deeply on what it’s going to deliver for Māori.
civility.explanation: Contested ground where he had a real opportunity to turn on his critics and largely did not — he concedes the Opposition's legitimate role and argues about the substance. The mild imputation of electoral self-interest ('to try and give themselves a chance to win back again') is pointed without landing on any person.
civility.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: This is a place of privilege, where there have been more All Blacks than parliamentarians.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the total number of people ever capped as All Blacks exceeds the total number of people ever elected to the New Zealand Parliament.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Compare the New Zealand Rugby register of capped All Blacks (test debutants since 1903) with the Parliamentary Library's count of all persons who have served as members of the New Zealand House of Representatives since 1854. True if the All Black count is the larger; false if the count of MPs is larger.

veracity.statement: When I thought about how there was division and it was devoid of “Pacific”, it’s because of a very simple reason: there is no Pacific representation in the Government.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that no member of the governing parties (National, ACT, New Zealand First) as at December 2023 is of Pacific descent.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The caucus lists of National, ACT and New Zealand First following the 2023 general election, checked against Parliamentary Library / official biographies for MPs identifying as being of Pacific descent. False if any sitting government MP is of Pacific ethnicity; true if none is.

veracity.statement: Even when the Rt Hon Winston Peters was the Minister of Foreign Affairs under our Government in 2017, there was a focus on Pacific—on the Pacific reset—because we knew how important the Pacific would be to our geopolitical outcomes here in Aotearoa New Zealand.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Winston Peters, as Minister of Foreign Affairs in the government formed in 2017, pursued a named Pacific policy called the 'Pacific reset'.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MFAT records and ministerial speeches from the 2017–2020 term: whether a foreign policy initiative named the 'Pacific Reset' was announced and pursued by Winston Peters as Minister of Foreign Affairs. True if such a named initiative exists on the record; false if no such policy was announced under him.

veracity.statement: Is that—yes—trying to scramble to find money, to find $800,000 from taking away te reo bonuses, and trying to find money through smoke-free?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the removal of te reo Māori proficiency bonuses was worth $800,000 and was undertaken to find savings.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Public service agency announcements and Cabinet/Public Service Commission material from late 2023 on the discontinuation of te reo Māori proficiency allowances, and the savings figure attributed to it. True if the reported saving is approximately $800,000; false if the figure is materially different or no such removal occurred.

veracity.statement: Who will actually most benefit by keeping those smoke-free rules in? It is Pacific and it is Māori people.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Māori and Pacific people are the populations that stand to gain most from retaining the smokefree legislation, which rests on their having the highest smoking prevalence and smoking-related harm.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: New Zealand Health Survey daily-smoking prevalence by ethnicity and Ministry of Health / Hauora tobacco-harm estimates for the period. True if Māori and Pacific rates are materially above the national average; false if their rates are at or below it.

veracity.statement: Just wait until the rest of the world finds out that we are peeling back some of our world-leading gun reforms.
veracity.explanation: Asserts as a present fact that the incoming government is unwinding parts of New Zealand's post-2019 firearms law reforms.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The published National–ACT and National–NZ First coalition agreements and the government's stated legislative programme as at December 2023: whether they commit to repealing or amending the post-2019 firearms measures (e.g. rewriting the Arms Act 1983 or disestablishing the firearms registry). True if such commitments are on the record; false if no rollback of the 2019–2020 reforms is proposed.

divination.statement: From a leak of a Cabinet paper from someone on the other side, to protests on your very first day, I suspect and I think many other people in this House suspect that this marriage is going to end in divorce.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that the newly formed National–ACT–New Zealand First coalition will break down rather than serve out the parliamentary term.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Whether the National–ACT–NZ First coalition formally dissolves (a governing party withdrawing from the coalition agreement, or confidence and supply being withdrawn) before the next general election. True if the coalition breaks up before the end of the 54th Parliament; false if it remains intact to the dissolution of that Parliament.

focus.statement: From a leak of a Cabinet paper from someone on the other side, to protests on your very first day, I suspect and I think many other people in this House suspect that this marriage is going to end in divorce.
focus.explanation: Names no policy, measure or figure: the content is a leaked Cabinet paper, protests, and a prediction about the governing parties' internal relationship. Almost entirely about the other team rather than the substance of anything before the House.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: No, they’ve spent most of the time on that side of the House, basically, trying to personally attack us—basically, they just spent it on us.
focus.explanation: Purely about the other party's debating conduct. No policy, measure, figure or outcome is named, and there is nothing left once the characterisation of opponents is removed.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Every single one of you on that side of the House, when you say yes to that bill going through repealing it, that is what you’re saying to the world—it’s that we’re no longer world-leading.
focus.explanation: Directed at a specific measure before the House — the bill repealing the smokefree provisions — and at the consequence of voting for it. It is framed as an address to the government benches rather than an analysis of the mechanism, which keeps it just short of the top.
focus.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: It was absolutely devoid of vision. There was no inspiration, and that’s why it’s so quiet on that side of the House, because it’s true, and you know it’s true.
rigor.explanation: Circular: the silence of the government benches is offered as evidence the criticism is true, and the truth of the criticism is offered as the reason for the silence. Nothing independent supports either half.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: When I thought about how there was division and it was devoid of “Pacific”, it’s because of a very simple reason: there is no Pacific representation in the Government.
rigor.explanation: A single-cause inference: the absence of Pacific content in the Speech from the Throne is attributed wholly to the absence of Pacific MPs in the governing parties. The counterfactual offered afterwards (a Pacific member would have flagged the gap) makes the mechanism plausible rather than shown; other explanations are not addressed.
rigor.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: So, again, it was devoid of vision, devoid of aspiration, and devoid of inspiration, and what I’ve seen over the last few weeks is, basically, a Government scrambling to pay for its promises—a Government that, one, clearly didn’t read the Pre-election Economic and Fiscal Update (PREFU) and didn’t actually have the competency or the ability to read and see what was in it, to interpret it, or to actually understand what the difference between time-limited funding and baseline funding is.
specificity.explanation: Opens with a string of generic abstractions (vision, aspiration, inspiration) with no content, but does name a specific document (PREFU) and a specific technical distinction (time-limited versus baseline funding). No figures, no named line items, no dates.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Is that—yes—trying to scramble to find money, to find $800,000 from taking away te reo bonuses, and trying to find money through smoke-free?
specificity.explanation: Carries a dollar figure and two named measures (te reo proficiency bonuses, smokefree policy) tied to a stated purpose of raising revenue. Falls short of the top because it gives no agency, timeframe or fiscal document for the $800,000.
specificity.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Everyone else could read the PREFU, but perhaps the Minister of Finance will now have a strong Treasury bench that might be able to help her out—maybe.
civility.explanation: Aimed at a named individual rather than at a policy: sarcastic condescension implying the Minister of Finance personally lacks the ability to read a standard fiscal document and needs officials to compensate. The trailing 'maybe' sharpens it into mockery.
civility.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Crime is up 50 percent in the last six years under this Government.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that total crime in New Zealand rose by 50% over the six years to 2023 (i.e. the period of the previous Labour-led government).
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Police recorded-crime / victimisation statistics (Victimisations Time Series) comparing calendar 2017 with 2023; true if total victimisations or recorded offences rose by approximately 50%, false if the rise is materially smaller (or if the figure only holds for a narrow subcategory such as retail ram-raids rather than crime overall).

veracity.statement: She didn’t want to talk about 20 years of educational decline in this country, but here on this side of the House, we will, and we are committed to reversing that trend.
veracity.explanation: Asserts as fact that New Zealand's educational achievement has declined over roughly two decades.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: OECD PISA mean scores for New Zealand in reading, mathematics and science from the early-2000s cycles through to the 2022 cycle (released December 2023); true if all three show a sustained material decline over that span, false if scores are flat or rising.

specificity.statement: Crime is up 50 percent in the last six years under this Government.
specificity.explanation: Carries a figure (50 percent), a timeframe (six years) and a named domain (crime) — precise enough for someone to go and check, whatever its accuracy.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The first principle is a return to equal citizenship in this country. Principle No. 2 is liberty—economic and individual liberty. Principle No. 3 is the value of the private sector and the farmers in this country as the engines of economic growth. Principle No. 4 is equal opportunity.
specificity.explanation: Setting out what the incoming government stands for, so there was substance to convey, but the answer is a list of abstract virtues — equal citizenship, liberty, opportunity — with no measure, mechanism, figure or timeframe attached to any of them.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We did a poll locally, and three-quarters of the Northcote electorate said they were unhappy with the way the country was going.
specificity.explanation: Names the instrument (a local poll), the population (Northcote electorate), the proportion (three-quarters) and the question asked — considerably more checkable content than the surrounding claims about a mood for change, though the poll itself is not sourced or dated.
specificity.subject: speaker

civility.statement: It’s a disappointment that the former Minister of Education Jan Tinetti didn’t want to talk about the Programme for International Student Assessment results that have just been released.
civility.explanation: Names a member and imputes avoidance — a suggestion she ducked inconvenient data rather than engaging it. Pointed and edging toward the person's conduct, but short of an insult or an attack on her character or competence.
civility.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: I met a person on the campaign trail whose husband actually had to leave this country and take a job in Australia just to pay the mortgage here in New Zealand. That is not the type of country we want to live in; that is not the type of country that we want our kids to grow up in.
rigor.explanation: A conclusion about the state of the whole country drawn from one encounter — an appeal to anecdote, with nothing offered (migration figures, mortgage-servicing data) to show the case is representative. The subject is a genuine policy question (cost of living), so this is a real inference and a weak one, not a jibe.
rigor.subject: speaker

divination.statement: So I’m really pleased with the package around tax, and I’m very confident that our finance Minister will find the money in order to pay for that.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that the incoming Finance Minister will succeed in funding the coalition's tax package. Not a commitment by the speaker himself — a prediction about whether a colleague's fiscal task will come off.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: The Budget 2024 documents (Budget Economic and Fiscal Update and the tax package costings, released 30 May 2024); true if the promised personal income tax reductions were legislated and funded with identified offsetting savings/revenue, false if the package was abandoned, materially cut back, or deferred.

veracity.statement: One of the reasons was that no longer did money go from the ministry to the DHB to the primary health organisation and then to the Māori health provider; it came straight from the centre to the organisation.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a factual claim about how Te Aka Whai Ora / Māori Health Authority funding was channelled: directly from the centre to Māori health providers, rather than through the Ministry → DHB → PHO chain that preceded it.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Te Aka Whai Ora / Ministry of Health commissioning and contracting records for 2022-23: true if the Māori Health Authority held direct commissioning contracts with Māori health providers such as Te Piki Oranga (bypassing DHB/Te Whatu Ora and PHO intermediaries), false if provider funding continued to flow via DHBs or PHOs.

veracity.statement: This is because Māori, as a whole, die so much earlier than those of us who are non-Māori, and that is a disgrace.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a present-day factual claim about a life-expectancy gap between Māori and non-Māori New Zealanders. The 'disgrace' clause is a value judgement and is not part of the checkable claim.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ period life tables / Ministry of Health ethnicity life-expectancy statistics current at December 2023: true if Māori life expectancy at birth is materially lower than non-Māori, false if the two are equal or Māori higher.

veracity.statement: Every other time we’ve introduced legislation, any colour of Government, the next Government has not repealed it when it comes to smoking, until now.
veracity.explanation: A historical claim about the New Zealand statute book: that no incoming government has previously repealed tobacco-control legislation enacted by its predecessor, and that the Smokefree Environments and Regulated Products (Smoked Tobacco) Amendment Act repeal is the first instance.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The legislative record for New Zealand tobacco-control statutes from the Smoke-free Environments Act 1990 onward: true if no substantive smoking measure was repealed by a subsequent government before 2023, false if any prior repeal (rather than amendment or replacement) of a smoking measure by a later government can be identified.

veracity.statement: He said—and I was listening to him carefully—that what Māori want is First World wages, and I wanted to say to him that that’s exactly what the people of Mt Albert want, too.
veracity.explanation: Relays a claim attributed to another member — that Winston Peters told the House on this sitting day that what Māori want is First World wages. What is checkable is whether he said it, not whether it is right.
veracity.subject: other
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Hansard transcript of Winston Peters' speech in the House on 6 December 2023: true if he stated in substance that what Māori want is First World wages, false if no such statement appears or the reported sense materially misrepresents what he said.

specificity.statement: One of the reasons was that no longer did money go from the ministry to the DHB to the primary health organisation and then to the Māori health provider; it came straight from the centre to the organisation.
specificity.explanation: Names the concrete funding mechanism and each link in the old chain (ministry, DHB, PHO, provider) against the new direct route — a checkable, actionable description rather than a general claim that things improved.
specificity.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: The Labour Government took steps to actually try and address that, and it’s going to get thrown away on the basis of some kind of idea that somehow other people are going to miss out.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion rests on a caricature of the opposing case: the incoming government's stated rationale for disestablishing Te Aka Whai Ora is reduced to 'some kind of idea that somehow other people are going to miss out', which is then dismissed without engagement. Strawman — the argument defeats a version of the position nobody advanced.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: It is what puts our country on the world stage. It helps our trade. It helps our identity.
rigor.explanation: The premise offered is a single anecdote — a delegation in Canada whose hosts enjoyed the waiata that closed the meetings — and the conclusion generalises from it to national standing and to trade benefit. Appeal to anecdote, plus a non sequitur from 'audiences enjoyed it' to 'it helps our trade'; nothing connects the two.
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: The Labour Government took steps to actually try and address that, and it’s going to get thrown away on the basis of some kind of idea that somehow other people are going to miss out.
civility.explanation: Fierce criticism of a decision to disestablish an agency. No individual is attacked; the dismissiveness is directed at the reasoning, not the person. Slightly under the standard for the sneering tone of 'some kind of idea that somehow'.
civility.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: But we’re going to get rid of the Productivity Commission for that, which actually is the body that recommended long-term planning for productivity—for things like ITPs.
veracity.explanation: Asserts two facts: that the coalition is disestablishing the New Zealand Productivity Commission, and that the Commission was the body that recommended long-term productivity planning of the kind embodied in the industry transformation plans.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Government announcements and legislation on the disestablishment of the New Zealand Productivity Commission (Cabinet papers / Budget 2024 documents), plus the Commission's published inquiry reports; true if the Commission was disestablished and its reports recommended long-term productivity/industry planning, false if it was retained or if long-term industry planning recommendations came from another body (e.g. MBIE's industry policy work) rather than the Commission.

veracity.statement: The Labour Government made sure that wages stayed ahead of inflation and they made sure the minimum wage went up.
veracity.explanation: Claims that under the 2017–2023 Labour government wage growth exceeded inflation and that the statutory minimum wage was increased.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ Labour Cost Index / average ordinary-time hourly earnings compared with the CPI over 2017–2023, and the MBIE schedule of adult minimum wage rates; true if annual wage growth exceeded CPI inflation across that period and the minimum wage rose each year, false if wage growth lagged CPI over material stretches of the period.

veracity.statement: They will be very sorry to see their wages slip backwards while the majority of tax cuts go to the wealthy in this country because, again, ideologically, the fundamental underpinning is a belief—an outdated belief—in trickle-down economics.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the majority of the incoming government's tax cuts accrue to wealthy New Zealanders.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Treasury / IRD distributional analysis of the coalition's personal income tax package by household income decile; true if more than half the total dollar value of the cuts goes to the top income deciles, false if the majority of the value goes to low- and middle-income households.

rigor.statement: Long since has that myth gone and long since has most of the world lost interest in that ridiculous philosophy, because it’s never worked and it never will.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion that trickle-down economics cannot work rests on an appeal to popularity (most of the world has lost interest) plus a bare restatement of the conclusion (it's never worked and it never will). No evidence or mechanism is offered to connect the premise to the claim.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: It is laughable that the Minister for Regulation is, in fact, setting up a Ministry for Regulation, which is sort of more regulation, isn’t it?
rigor.explanation: Equivocates on 'regulation': a ministry whose function is to review and reduce regulatory burden is not thereby more regulation of the economy. The inference from 'a Ministry for Regulation exists' to 'this is more regulation' trades on the word rather than the substance.
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: It is laughable that the Minister for Regulation is, in fact, setting up a Ministry for Regulation, which is sort of more regulation, isn’t it?
civility.explanation: Mocks the Minister's decision as 'laughable'. The ridicule lands on the policy arrangement rather than the person, but it is pointed and edges toward the Minister personally.
civility.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We need to make moves towards treating rentals as homes, not investments.
specificity.explanation: A statement of direction with no mechanism, no measure, no figure and no timeframe — nothing anyone could check or act on.
specificity.subject: speaker

focus.statement: We need to make moves towards treating rentals as homes, not investments.
focus.explanation: Squarely directed at rental housing policy rather than at the other party. Vague, but on the substance — the classic high-Focus, low-Specificity case.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: You cannot deny that if the proposal is to bring in a 90-day, no-fault termination, because that means that it doesn’t matter if you can now bring your dog to the rental—which I’d love—you could get kicked out in 90 days for doing nothing and for doing no harm.
focus.explanation: Names a specific measure — the reinstatement of 90-day no-cause tenancy terminations — and argues about its concrete effect on tenants. Entirely policy content, no party framing.
focus.subject: speaker

divination.statement: My fear is that we have a situation where we are going to see rents rise in this country but also insecurity of rent—insecurity.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that rents will rise under the incoming government's tenancy and housing settings. Not a promise about her own action; an outcome in the rental market.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ rental price index (and MBIE tenancy bond mean weekly rent) for the two years following December 2023; true if the national rent measure rises materially above its December 2023 level, false if rents are flat or fall over that period.

veracity.statement: For example, in the last six years, funding for Whānau Ora has increased by 145 percent. It has gone from servicing 13,000 families to 30,000 families—a huge increase—because the need is there.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a specific funding increase (145% over six years) and a rise in families served from 13,000 to 30,000 under the outgoing Labour government.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Vote Māori Development appropriations for Whānau Ora, Budget 2017/18 through 2023/24 (Treasury Estimates), and Te Puni Kōkiri / commissioning-agency reporting on whānau engaged; true if the appropriation rose ~145% and reported families rose from roughly 13,000 to roughly 30,000, false if materially different.

veracity.statement: In the 52nd Parliament, there was an inquiry by the Māori Affairs Committee into the inequities in health for Māori. The report was tabled in this House. It recommended by majority that a Māori health authority be established to address that.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that a named select committee in a named Parliament ran an inquiry, tabled a report, and recommended by majority the establishment of a Māori health authority.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Māori Affairs Committee's inquiry report on health inequities for Māori, 52nd Parliament (2017–2020), as tabled and published on parliament.nz; true if the report exists and its majority recommendations include establishing a Māori health authority, false if no such inquiry/report exists or the recommendation was not made by majority.

specificity.statement: For example, in the last six years, funding for Whānau Ora has increased by 145 percent. It has gone from servicing 13,000 families to 30,000 families—a huge increase—because the need is there.
specificity.explanation: Carries a percentage, a timeframe and two absolute service figures — directly checkable and actionable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: In the 52nd Parliament, there was an inquiry by the Māori Affairs Committee into the inequities in health for Māori. The report was tabled in this House. It recommended by majority that a Māori health authority be established to address that.
specificity.explanation: Names the Parliament, the committee, the subject of the inquiry and the recommendation — enough for a reader to locate the document.
specificity.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Now, I hear a lot of things that are going to be taken away. What I don't hear is how those inequities are going to be addressed.
focus.explanation: Directed at the incoming government's policy programme and the gap in it, not at the other party's character or internal state; but no specific measure, figure or outcome is named, which keeps it short of the accountability standard.
focus.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: I can take you around the urupā at my home and I can point to the graves of those who have passed away from smoking. Removing the barrier that is going to prevent more of that is a horrendous thing to do.
rigor.explanation: A real inference about a real measure, but the support offered is personal anecdote (graves at his urupā) and the causal step — that the smokefree legislation is what prevents those deaths — is asserted rather than shown. Appeal to anecdote and emotion carrying the weight of the conclusion.
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I just feel it's an absolute tragedy to go backwards after gaining so much. We will lose much more, it will be much harder to regain a Māori health authority, and the impact on Māori families will be huge.
civility.explanation: Severe condemnation of a government decision on a genuinely contested question, with no imputation of bad faith and no individual targeted.
civility.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: We’ve seen rents up $180 a week over the past six years.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that weekly rents rose by $180 over the six years to 2023 — a checkable claim about national rent levels.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MBIE tenancy bond data / Stats NZ rental price series: compare national median weekly rent for late 2017 with late 2023. True if the increase is approximately $180 a week; false if materially different (e.g. under $130 or over $230).

specificity.statement: We’ve seen rents up $180 a week over the past six years.
specificity.explanation: Carries a dollar figure, a unit (per week) and a timeframe (six years), so it can be checked or acted on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We have committed to repealing some of what we would consider to be poor or misguided legislation from the previous Government around the fair pay agreements, three waters, and projects like Let’s Get Wellington Moving and Auckland light rail.
specificity.explanation: Names four identifiable policies and projects to be repealed or cancelled, but gives no timeframe, sequencing or fiscal detail.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We’re committed to returning the Reserve Bank of New Zealand mandate to prioritise price stability, which is very important and is almost one of the most important things that we need to get on top of, because if we don’t get on top of inflation quickly, it is going to continue to erode the wealth of New Zealanders.
specificity.explanation: Names a specific institutional change (the Reserve Bank mandate, and the single objective it would return to), but supplies no legislative timeframe or mechanism.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We’re also committed to making New Zealanders safer, so we are getting rid of the prisoner reduction targets and cracking down on gangs.
specificity.explanation: One concrete, checkable action (removing the prisoner reduction target) paired with a slogan-level second limb ('cracking down on gangs') carrying no mechanism, numbers or dates.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: From 2024, I know Erica Stanford will make an excellent education Minister, and we are going to ensure that New Zealand children at primary and intermediate level are spending an hour each day on reading, writing, and mathematics.
specificity.explanation: Gives a start year, the school levels affected, the subjects and the daily hour — precise enough that compliance could be measured.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We are going to be a Government that reduces restrictions and reduces impediments.
specificity.explanation: A direction with no named regulation, sector, mechanism, quantum or date — nothing here could be checked or acted on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Now, there are four key things we are focused on, and that is to manage a stronger economy for New Zealand, to ease the cost of living crisis, and to deliver tax relief; secondly, to restore law and order; thirdly, to deliver better public services; and, fourthly, to strengthen our democracy.
specificity.explanation: An enumerated set of priorities, which is more than a single slogan, but every item is a broad aspiration with no mechanism, amount or timeframe attached.
specificity.subject: speaker

focus.statement: I think that when people look back on the 53rd Government and why those members are no longer on this side of the House—and this is just my opinion—they will probably see that they didn’t deliver on what they talked about when they were in Government, and when it came to the election campaign they failed to talk about the things that actually mattered to Kiwis.
focus.explanation: A general characterisation of the previous government's delivery and campaign, with no policy, measure, figure or outcome named. Party-directed rather than policy-directed, though it stops short of pure tribalism by gesturing at delivery.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: We have committed to repealing some of what we would consider to be poor or misguided legislation from the previous Government around the fair pay agreements, three waters, and projects like Let’s Get Wellington Moving and Auckland light rail.
focus.explanation: Entirely about named legislation and projects — the substance of what the government intends to change, not the character of the other party.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: We’re committed to returning the Reserve Bank of New Zealand mandate to prioritise price stability, which is very important and is almost one of the most important things that we need to get on top of, because if we don’t get on top of inflation quickly, it is going to continue to erode the wealth of New Zealanders.
focus.explanation: Squarely on the measure and the reason for it — monetary policy mandate and inflation — with no party framing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: From 2024, I know Erica Stanford will make an excellent education Minister, and we are going to ensure that New Zealand children at primary and intermediate level are spending an hour each day on reading, writing, and mathematics.
focus.explanation: About a defined education policy and how it would operate in schools, not about the other party.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: We are going to be a Government that reduces restrictions and reduces impediments.
focus.explanation: Genuinely policy-directed (regulatory settings) even though it names nothing concrete; the vagueness is Specificity's concern, not Focus's.
focus.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I think that when people look back on the 53rd Government and why those members are no longer on this side of the House—and this is just my opinion—they will probably see that they didn’t deliver on what they talked about when they were in Government, and when it came to the election campaign they failed to talk about the things that actually mattered to Kiwis.
civility.explanation: Criticism is aimed at a government and a party's record, not at any individual's character or competence, and it is explicitly framed as opinion.
civility.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: As a result, they were resoundingly rejected by the electorate, and we have been given a mandate on this side of the House to deliver for New Zealand.
rigor.explanation: Infers a mandate to deliver a particular programme from the bare fact of an election loss by the other side — an appeal to popularity that leaves a gap between 'they lost' and 'we are authorised to do these specific things'.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: We got in there because we’d campaigned on what the New Zealand people were interested in.
rigor.explanation: Post hoc reasoning bordering on circularity: the election win is offered as the sole evidence that the campaign matched public interests, and that alignment is in turn offered to explain the win. No independent evidence connects the two.
rigor.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: There is no excuse for what might have started this, but you can look at the Prime Minister of Israel, who’s been under suspicion of corruption and bribery since 2019, and ask the question—well, people think this is horrific.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Israeli Prime Minister has been under suspicion of corruption and bribery since 2019.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Israeli Attorney-General and court records on Benjamin Netanyahu: true if formal suspicion/charges of bribery, fraud or breach of trust were on foot from 2019 (police recommendations February 2019, indictment filed November 2019); false if no such proceedings existed by the end of 2019.

veracity.statement: It is a third the size of Auckland and the trapped civilian population—Gaza is smaller than Wellington City—is 2 million people.
veracity.explanation: Three checkable assertions: Gaza's area is about a third of Auckland's, Gaza is smaller in area than Wellington City, and its population is about 2 million.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Published land areas (Gaza Strip ≈365 km²; Auckland urban area / region per Stats NZ; Wellington City ≈290 km²) and UN/PCBS population figures for Gaza. True if Gaza is roughly one third of Auckland's area, smaller than Wellington City, and holds about 2 million people; false if any of the three comparisons is materially wrong.

civility.statement: There is no excuse for what might have started this, but you can look at the Prime Minister of Israel, who’s been under suspicion of corruption and bribery since 2019, and ask the question—well, people think this is horrific.
civility.explanation: Turns from the conflict to the personal legal exposure of a named leader as an explanation for events. It is pointed and edges toward the person, but rests on a matter of record rather than abuse.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I’m pleased to see that the Deputy Prime Minister—the Minister of Foreign Affairs—has put up a ceasefire in this motion. I welcome it.
civility.explanation: In a genuinely contested debate where she is moving amendments against the Government's wording, she credits the responsible Minister for what he did include. Engages the substance, attacks no one.
civility.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: No person with any ounce of moral courage can see this as anything but horrific; nothing more than a genocide.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion that this is a genocide is supported only by asserting that anyone who disagrees lacks moral courage — poisoning the well combined with a false dichotomy. No evidence or criterion for the characterisation is offered.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: But it is intolerable and grotesque to suggest the actions of the Israeli Government are self-defence. This is retaliation against civilians, and the international community has a duty to not let it continue.
rigor.explanation: Engages the motion's self-defence clause directly, but the rejection of the self-defence characterisation rests mainly on emotive adjectives; the one premise offered (civilians are being targeted) is asserted rather than connected to the legal test it is meant to defeat.
rigor.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: It is a third the size of Auckland and the trapped civilian population—Gaza is smaller than Wellington City—is 2 million people.
specificity.explanation: Carries a size ratio, two named local comparators and a population figure — concrete enough that a listener could go and check it.
specificity.subject: speaker

focus.statement: I wish we as a country had put this pressure out to the world, given the many thousands of dead, innocent civilians, many, many weeks ago.
focus.explanation: Criticises a specific policy action — the timing of New Zealand's call for a ceasefire — rather than the character or record of another party. Named policy, named shortfall.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: We believe on this side of the House that the Government has the wrong priorities and that they are out of touch, and I will tell you why.
focus.explanation: Characterises the governing parties in general terms — 'wrong priorities', 'out of touch' — without naming a policy, measure, figure or outcome. Party framing rather than policy content, though she goes on to supply reasons separately.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: I am sure the Government can go back to its books to see where else it can take some revenue and leave the smoke-free legislation that is impending where it is.
focus.explanation: Squarely on a named measure before the House — the repeal of the smokefree legislation — and engages the fiscal rationale for it rather than the character of the parties proposing it.
focus.subject: speaker

civility.statement: We believe on this side of the House that the Government has the wrong priorities and that they are out of touch, and I will tell you why.
civility.explanation: Sharp criticism aimed at the Government collectively; no individual's character, competence or motives is attacked. Under the re-anchored scale this is the expected standard.
civility.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: I have a very strong interest in Pasifika, and in the document that I read afterwards, there was very little mention of Pasifika.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Government document she read after the Speech from the Throne — the incoming Government's 100-day plan / Speech from the Throne of 6 December 2023 — contained very little reference to Pasifika or Pacific peoples.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The published text of the 2023 Speech from the Throne and the National-led coalition's 100-day plan; true if references to 'Pasifika'/'Pacific peoples' are absent or confined to a passing mention, false if the documents contain substantive Pacific-specific commitments.

veracity.statement: They’re actually the fastest-growing and youngest population of Aotearoa, and it’s a real shame that there is no member of the Government who is of Pasifika ethnicity, because on this side of the House, we have the Labour Pasifika caucus.
veracity.explanation: Three factual assertions: that Pacific peoples are New Zealand's fastest-growing population, that they are its youngest population, and that no MP in the incoming National/ACT/NZ First government caucuses is of Pasifika ethnicity.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ ethnic population projections and median age by ethnic group (true if the Pacific ethnic group has both the highest growth rate and the lowest median age; false if another group — e.g. Asian — grew faster); plus the roster of government caucus MPs sworn in for the 54th Parliament and their stated ethnicity, false if any government MP identifies as Pacific.

rigor.statement: I interpret today’s announcements as being that the Government has no commitment. It just does not understand that kaupapa.
rigor.explanation: Argument from absence of evidence: the silence of one day's announcements is taken to establish both an absence of commitment and an absence of understanding. The inference outruns what a single document's omissions can show.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: So the research and the evidence that has been provided in many of the Government agencies led by the Ministry for Pacific Peoples really tells it black and white: Pasifika are tuākana and tuāhine to Māori, and if Māori are worried, as we’ve seen very recently as of yesterday, then Pasifika need to be worried as well.
rigor.explanation: Appeal to unspecified authority ('the research and the evidence' from agencies, none of it cited) attached to a conclusion it does not support: the kinship relation between Pasifika and Māori is offered as the bridge from Māori concern to Pasifika concern, which is an appeal to analogy rather than a stated causal link.
rigor.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I am sure the Government can go back to its books to see where else it can take some revenue and leave the smoke-free legislation that is impending where it is.
specificity.explanation: Names the legislation, but 'go back to its books to see where else it can take some revenue' identifies no alternative revenue source, no amount and no timeframe.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The Labour caucus will be building the machinery towards 2026, and we may be down but in no way are we out.
specificity.explanation: 'Building the machinery' names no activity, resource or milestone, and the second clause is a rallying phrase. Only the year 2026 is concrete, and it is simply the date of the next election.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: The Government is pleased that 20 New Zealand citizens, permanent residents, and family members have now exited Gaza.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a specific count of New Zealand citizens, permanent residents and family members who had left Gaza as at 7 December 2023.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MFAT/Ministerial statements and media releases on New Zealand-linked departures from Gaza as at 7 December 2023; true if the cumulative figure is 20, false if materially different.

veracity.statement: The Government has also contributed $10 million to address immediate humanitarian need.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the New Zealand Government's cumulative humanitarian contribution to the Gaza response stood at $10 million at the date of the statement.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MFAT humanitarian funding announcements for the Israel/Gaza response between October and December 2023; true if the announced total reaches NZ$10 million, false if it is materially more or less.

veracity.statement: Anti-Semitism has gone through the roof in New Zealand in the past few months.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a large increase in anti-Semitic incidents in New Zealand over roughly October–December 2023. Hyperbolic phrasing, but the underlying trend claim is checkable.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Recorded anti-Semitic incident counts for October–December 2023 versus the preceding months, from NZ Police hate-crime reporting, the Human Rights Commission, and the NZ Jewish Council's incident log; true if the count rose sharply, false if flat or falling.

veracity.statement: On the streets here in New Zealand, there’s been a sense of mob rule at times, where even elected members of the New Zealand Parliament have felt free to use Hamas slogans like “From the river to the sea”, which, if you take Hamas seriously, and we should, do mean the eradication of Israel and its people.
veracity.explanation: Asserts as fact that sitting New Zealand MPs have publicly used the phrase "From the river to the sea".
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Public record (Hansard, speeches, social media, news reports) before 7 December 2023 of any sitting New Zealand MP using the phrase "From the river to the sea"; true if at least one such use is documented, false if none is.

veracity.statement: Jordan and Egypt both went to war with Israel with the intention of eliminating the Jewish state many times—1948, 1956, 1967, 1973.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that both Jordan and Egypt were belligerents against Israel in each of the four listed wars.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Standard histories and contemporaneous records of the 1948, 1956, 1967 and 1973 Arab–Israeli wars; true if Jordan and Egypt were both belligerents in all four, false if either was not a combatant in any of them (e.g. Jordan in 1956).

veracity.statement: In 1988, Jordan became the second Arab state, after Egypt, to formally sign a peace treaty with Israel, recognising that nation’s right to exist and establishing security relationships. There are precedents, but what it takes is for both sides to recognise each other’s right to exist as a precursor for a lasting peace.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a specific year for the signing of the Israel–Jordan peace treaty and that Jordan was the second Arab state to sign one.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The signature date on the Israel–Jordan Treaty of Peace as registered with the United Nations; true if signed in 1988, false if signed in any other year.

veracity.statement: We have seen 16,248 Palestinians being killed—7,112 of them are children.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a cumulative Palestinian death toll and a child sub-total as at early December 2023.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Gaza Ministry of Health casualty figures as reported by UN OCHA situation reports for 6–7 December 2023; true if the totals match 16,248 and 7,112 within reporting-day rounding, false if materially different.

veracity.statement: Every world leader has refused the call for a ceasefire—what is this Government willing to do to exert pressure on our allies, who will ignore this call?
veracity.explanation: Asserts universally that no world leader had supported a call for a ceasefire as at 7 December 2023.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Public statements by heads of state or government, and UN General Assembly/Security Council voting records, before 7 December 2023; true if no world leader had called for a ceasefire, false if any had (a single documented instance falsifies it).

veracity.statement: The United States has poured billions of dollars into Israel’s military.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that United States military funding to Israel runs to billions of dollars.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: US State Department Foreign Military Financing figures and Congressional Research Service reports on US military aid to Israel; true if annual or cumulative military assistance exceeds one billion US dollars, false otherwise.

veracity.statement: It means recognising the State of Palestine as we recognised the State of Israel in 1949.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that New Zealand extended recognition to the State of Israel in 1949.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MFAT and New Zealand diplomatic-history records of the date New Zealand recognised the State of Israel; true if recognition was extended in 1949, false if in another year.

specificity.statement: The Government has also contributed $10 million to address immediate humanitarian need.
specificity.explanation: Names a concrete amount and its purpose; someone could check the appropriation. Lacks recipient agencies or timing, so short of full precision.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We have seen 16,248 Palestinians being killed—7,112 of them are children.
specificity.explanation: Exact figures with a named population and a sub-breakdown; directly checkable against published casualty reporting.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: What is stopping the Government right now from introducing an Israeli sanctions bill to Parliament, just as we did in response to Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, or creating a special visa category for Palestinians displaced by this war, as our allies in Australia have done, as we also did for Ukraine?
specificity.explanation: Names identifiable mechanisms (a sanctions bill, a special visa category) and comparable precedents. No amounts, thresholds or timeframes, which keeps it short of fully actionable.
specificity.subject: speaker

civility.statement: On the streets here in New Zealand, there’s been a sense of mob rule at times, where even elected members of the New Zealand Parliament have felt free to use Hamas slogans like “From the river to the sea”, which, if you take Hamas seriously, and we should, do mean the eradication of Israel and its people.
civility.explanation: Pointed at the conduct of unnamed colleagues rather than their character, but associating fellow members with a proscribed terrorist group's slogan edges toward imputing bad faith. No individual is named or insulted.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: God, how low you get!
civility.explanation: A direct attack on the character of members opposite rather than on any argument or policy. Nothing in the substance of the debate is engaged.
civility.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: And by extension, if a Western liberal democracy like Israel falls to the terrorist attacks of a group like Hamas and its supporters—to the missiles, to the kidnapping, the hostage taking and all the abominable crimes against civilians—then what hope does a small nation of 5 million like New Zealand—a similar Western democracy—have if we were to accept the fall of the nation of Israel?
rigor.explanation: A slippery slope resting on a false analogy: nothing is offered to connect Israel's security situation to New Zealand's, and the two states' threat environments are simply asserted to be equivalent because both are Western democracies. The conclusion does not follow from what was supplied.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: In 1988, Jordan became the second Arab state, after Egypt, to formally sign a peace treaty with Israel, recognising that nation’s right to exist and establishing security relationships. There are precedents, but what it takes is for both sides to recognise each other’s right to exist as a precursor for a lasting peace.
rigor.explanation: A genuine inference: historical instances of mutual recognition preceding peace treaties are offered as support for the general claim that mutual recognition is a precondition for lasting peace. The conclusion tracks the evidence offered, though generalising from two cases is a real gap. Whether the 1988 date is accurate is Veracity's question, not this one.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Every child killed today would still be alive if we had done what was right by peace: a ceasefire, an end to genocide, and helping them to find the right solution.
rigor.explanation: A counterfactual asserted without any linking mechanism — no account is offered of how New Zealand's actions would have produced a ceasefire, nor of the timeline by which that would have prevented today's deaths. The conclusion outruns the premises; essentially an appeal to emotion in place of an inference.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: What is stopping the Government right now from introducing an Israeli sanctions bill to Parliament, just as we did in response to Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, or creating a special visa category for Palestinians displaced by this war, as our allies in Australia have done, as we also did for Ukraine?
focus.explanation: Names two specific policy instruments and two precedents for each, and puts a concrete question to the Government about adopting them. This is scrutiny directed at a measurable course of action, not party framing.
focus.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: There is no military solution to this problem, not when you have four generations of Palestinians living in refugee camps.
rigor.explanation: A genuine inference about the measure at issue: the conclusion (no military solution) is supported by one offered reason (multi-generational displacement). But the reason is asserted rather than developed — protracted displacement makes a military settlement harder, it does not by itself establish that none exists. A real gap between what is shown and what is concluded.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: We’re not just some small island nation; we have relationships, and we have always been at our best when we have led as an independent, principled voice on the world stage.
rigor.explanation: An argument about the policy question — whether New Zealand should break from its allies — but it rests on an appeal to national self-image and tradition. 'We have always been at our best when' asserts the conclusion it is meant to support; no instance or outcome is offered to show that independent stances have actually produced better results.
rigor.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: I take heart that New Zealand’s foreign Minister said, “The desperate need of the Palestinians for peace and statehood is undeniable. We hope that a way will be found to take forward the peace process with the representatives of the Palestinian people.” That was the Rt Hon Winston Peters in 2006.
veracity.explanation: Attributes a specific quotation on Palestinian statehood to Winston Peters as Minister of Foreign Affairs in 2006. What is checkable is the attribution and the wording, not the sentiment expressed.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministerial statements, speeches and MFAT releases by Winston Peters as Minister of Foreign Affairs in 2006. True if he made a statement containing this wording in 2006; false if the wording differs materially, is from another speaker, or is from another year.

veracity.statement: In the eight weeks of the conflict, thousands of Palestinians, the majority of them women and children, have been killed.
veracity.explanation: Two claims about the eight weeks to 7 December 2023: that the Palestinian death toll runs to thousands, and that women and children are the majority of those killed.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Gaza Ministry of Health and UN OCHA casualty reporting for 7 October to 7 December 2023. True if the reported death toll is in the thousands and women and children together make up more than half of it; false if the toll is materially lower or women and children are a minority of the dead.

veracity.statement: Whether we like it or not, it’s a strategy that’s been dubbed an apartheid strategy by many around the world.
veracity.explanation: A claim about what others have said, not about whether the characterisation is correct: that the term 'apartheid' has been widely applied to the situation internationally.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Published reports and statements by prominent international human-rights bodies and UN rapporteurs on Israel and the occupied territories. True if multiple well-known organisations have applied the term 'apartheid'; false if the characterisation is confined to fringe or isolated sources.

veracity.statement: It matters that until now, both the caretaker Government and our incoming Prime Minister have failed to call for a lasting ceasefire.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that as at 7 December 2023 neither the outgoing caretaker Government nor the incoming Prime Minister had called for a lasting ceasefire. The distinction between a 'lasting ceasefire' and the humanitarian pause language New Zealand had used is what the check turns on.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Official New Zealand statements, MFAT releases, press conferences and UN voting records up to 7 December 2023. True if neither the caretaker Government nor the incoming Prime Minister had called for a lasting ceasefire (as distinct from a humanitarian pause or truce) by that date; false if either had.

veracity.statement: I want to hold, as our Green amendment holds, that incredible loss of life that disproportionately has impacted the children of Gaza—7,000 that we know of.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a specific figure — roughly 7,000 children killed in Gaza as at the date of the debate, excluding those still under rubble.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Gaza Ministry of Health and UN OCHA figures for child deaths as at 7 December 2023. True if the reported number of children killed is approximately 7,000; false if it is materially different from that figure.

veracity.statement: Because every 10 minutes one of those kids—somebody’s everything—is killed in Gaza.
veracity.explanation: A rate claim about the present: that a child is being killed in Gaza roughly once every ten minutes as at 7 December 2023.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: WHO and UN statements on the rate of child deaths in Gaza, and Gaza Ministry of Health cumulative child-death figures for November–December 2023 divided by elapsed time. True if the implied rate is about one child every ten minutes; false if the rate is materially slower.

specificity.statement: In line with that UN Security Council resolution that New Zealand sponsored, New Zealand should now condemn the illegal occupation of Palestinian territory, demand that Israel immediately cease settlement activities in occupied Palestinian territory, and abide by its legal obligations as an occupying power—in particular, to bring its occupation of all Palestine territories, including in Gaza, to an end as soon as possible.
specificity.explanation: Names three distinct actions he wants the Government to take (condemn the occupation, demand settlement activity cease, insist on occupying-power obligations) and anchors them to a named instrument. Someone could act on it. Falls short of 1.0 because the timing is 'as soon as possible' and no mechanism or forum for the demands is specified.
specificity.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I call on the Government to resist the nervous and over-cautious advice of its foreign affairs officials who, as always, will be worried about being out of step with Canberra and Washington, and do the right thing.
civility.explanation: Pointed and robust, and it edges past the argument toward the people giving the advice: 'nervous', 'over-cautious' and 'as always' impute a habitual timidity of motive rather than engaging with the reasoning. No individual is named or insulted, so this stops well short of a personal attack.
civility.subject: speaker

focus.statement: It matters that until now, both the caretaker Government and our incoming Prime Minister have failed to call for a lasting ceasefire.
focus.explanation: Legitimate scrutiny: it names a specific position (calling for a lasting ceasefire) and identifies who she says has not taken it. This is holding the Government to account on a named policy question, not party-bashing, and it is exactly the case that must score high.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: The latest reports have 1,200 people killed as a result of Hamas’ attack on Israel on 7 October, while at least 16,000 Palestinians have been killed since then, according to the Gaza Health Ministry.
veracity.explanation: Asserts two casualty totals as at 7 December 2023: approximately 1,200 killed in the 7 October Hamas attack, and at least 16,000 Palestinians killed in Gaza since, sourced to the Gaza Health Ministry.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Israeli government/IDF published casualty figures for the 7 October attack, and the Gaza Health Ministry cumulative death toll as reported by UN OCHA for the week of 7 December 2023. True if the Israeli figure is around 1,200 and the Gaza figure is at or above 16,000 at that date; false if either is materially lower.

veracity.statement: More children have been killed in Gaza than in all the world’s conflicts combined in each of the past three years.
veracity.explanation: A comparative claim that the count of children killed in Gaza since 7 October 2023 exceeds the total number of children killed across all armed conflicts worldwide in each of 2020, 2021 and 2022 taken individually.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Gaza child death counts (Gaza Health Ministry / UN OCHA) for October–December 2023 compared against the annual UN-verified totals for children killed in armed conflict in the UN Secretary-General's Children and Armed Conflict reports for 2020, 2021 and 2022. True if the Gaza figure exceeds each of those three annual global totals; false if it does not exceed any one of them.

veracity.statement: The New Zealand Labour Party has been for weeks urgently calling for a ceasefire in Gaza and Israel to put a halt to the appalling attacks and violence so that a journey to a lasting peace can begin.
veracity.explanation: A claim about her own party's public record: that Labour had been calling for a ceasefire for a period of weeks before 7 December 2023, rather than adopting the position recently.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Labour Party press releases, caucus statements and media reports between roughly late October and 7 December 2023. True if documented Labour calls for a ceasefire exist across several weeks before the statement; false if the first such call is within days of 7 December 2023.

veracity.statement: When this outbreak of violence and mass murder occurred on 7 October, this Government was weeks from being formed—as the Government—despite some of the statements being made in this House today.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the coalition Government he speaks for had not been formed at the time of the 7 October 2023 attack, and was still some weeks away from formation.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The date the Sixth National-led Government was sworn in, per the Governor-General's record, compared with 7 October 2023. True if the swearing-in falls a matter of weeks after 7 October; false if the Government was already in office on that date.

veracity.statement: But the last pure Moriori died in 1936.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a specific year of death for the person conventionally described as the last full-blooded Moriori.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Death records and standard historical sources (Te Ara, Chatham Islands records) for Tame Horomona Rehe / Tommy Solomon, conventionally identified as the last full-blooded Moriori. True if he died in 1936; false if the recorded year is different.

specificity.statement: The latest reports have 1,200 people killed as a result of Hamas’ attack on Israel on 7 October, while at least 16,000 Palestinians have been killed since then, according to the Gaza Health Ministry.
specificity.explanation: Two named figures, a named date and a named source. Someone could go and check every element of it.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: In relation to the copies of the bills, as soon as they are available and the Government wishes to make them available to the Opposition.
specificity.explanation: Answering a direct question about timing with no date, no mechanism and no test for when the condition would be met. The content is self-referential — the bills arrive when the Government decides they arrive.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: As I said, we want to see a ceasefire that takes place. It requires conditions on both sides to be adhered to, as I’ve outlined.
specificity.explanation: Asked about a named instrument (UN Resolution 2712), the answer restates a general position with no reference to the resolution, no conditions enumerated here, and nothing New Zealand commits to doing.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Does the Government support an “immediate, durable and sustained humanitarian truce”, as called for in UN Resolution 2712?
specificity.explanation: Names the specific resolution and quotes its operative wording, so the question admits a checkable yes-or-no answer. A precise question carries as much content as a precise answer.
specificity.subject: speaker

civility.statement: What we want on this debate is sincerity, understanding, and insight, and not virtue signalling.
civility.explanation: Imputes bad faith to other members of the House — that their contributions are performance rather than sincere. Short of a direct insult, but no longer civil.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Stop lecturing to us as though, somehow, they’re perfect and the rest of us are not.
