veracity.statement: Now, if that wasn’t bad enough, by muddying the waters, the previous Government also went on to grow the size of Government, spending over 70 percent more, and this large increase in Government spending has had consequences.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the previous (Labour) Government increased government spending by more than 70 percent. The comparison years and spending measure are not stated, so the check must use the obvious reading: core Crown expenses from the start of the Labour government to its end.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Treasury Financial Statements of the Government of New Zealand, core Crown expenses, 2017/18 compared with 2022/23. True if the increase exceeds 70 percent; false if it is materially below that on the standard core Crown expenses measure.

veracity.statement: But essentially what we’re dealing with here is a real-world issue that, as Mr Stephenson just pointed out, families are hurting, cost of living is hurting, our business community and our farmers are hurting with record-high interest rates that’s driven as a result of the record-high inflation.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that interest rates and inflation in December 2023 were at record highs — an overstatement that is nonetheless checkable against the historical series.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: RBNZ historical OCR and average new-residential-mortgage rate series, and Stats NZ CPI annual inflation series, both back to their start. True if December 2023 levels exceed all previous readings; false if higher rates or higher inflation are recorded earlier (e.g. the 2007-08 or 1980s peaks).

veracity.statement: Ask yourselves that question, because we’ve got the data right here that shows us New Zealand’s inflation did not go as high as many other countries in the world.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that New Zealand's peak CPI inflation during the post-pandemic episode was lower than that of many comparable countries.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: OECD and national statistical agency CPI series for 2021-23, comparing New Zealand's peak annual inflation with those of the countries named on the graph (United States, Denmark, Ireland, Australia) and the OECD average. True if New Zealand's peak sits below many of these; false if it sits at or above most of them.

veracity.statement: I think we all know that the economic reforms of the 1980s did not lead to a giant increase in productivity.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that New Zealand's 1980s economic reforms failed to produce a large increase in productivity.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ productivity statistics and NZ Productivity Commission / Treasury analyses of labour and multifactor productivity growth from 1984 onward, compared with the OECD average. True if New Zealand's productivity growth after the reforms did not rise substantially relative to its own prior trend or to the OECD; false if it shows a large post-reform increase.

rigor.statement: That’s not too dissimilar to the circumstances we find ourselves in today, and that target did actually deliver the reduction in inflation that we’re looking for.
rigor.explanation: Reasons from a historical analogy: because inflation was ~7% in 1990 and fell after a single-mandate target was set, the same instrument will deliver the same result now. The inference is post hoc — it attributes the 1990s disinflation to the mandate alone without offering anything to rule out the other conditions of that period — and the analogy is asserted rather than defended.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: We have been convinced by a very persuasive argument from the Minister of Finance to support this bill.
rigor.explanation: The stated ground for supporting the bill is that the Minister of Finance argued persuasively. That is a bare appeal to authority — the reason offered is who made the case, not what the case was.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Now, if it were the case that the economic circumstances and CPI inflation that we experienced here in Aotearoa was entirely down to the fact that there was a dual mandate, how does that explain all of these other countries experiencing the same CPI inflation?
rigor.explanation: A valid comparative inference: if the dual mandate were the cause, countries without it should not show the same inflation profile, and the cross-country series is offered as the disconfirming evidence. Marked down slightly because 'entirely down to' is a stronger claim than the government side made, so the argument partly tests a position not actually held.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: The previous Government has muddied the waters by providing the Reserve Bank with a dual mandate, and we want to stop that.
focus.explanation: Names the specific measure at issue — the Reserve Bank's dual mandate — and states the change sought. Legitimate scrutiny of a named policy of the previous government, carried in party framing but anchored to the actual policy.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: This is all being done to further enrich their already rich mates.
focus.explanation: Entirely about the other side's supposed motives and who they are said to serve. No policy, mechanism, figure or outcome is named.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: By removing the dual mandate, will this Government push the official cash rate to an unachievable rate that the Governor can’t achieve, creating a forced recession?
focus.explanation: Squarely on the measure before the House: names the dual mandate's removal, the transmission channel (the official cash rate) and the outcome feared. Scrutiny of the actual policy, not of the other party.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: They did enrich a tiny number of people, many of whom donate now to the ACT Party and to the National Party.
focus.explanation: Shifts from the reforms themselves to who funds the parties opposite. There is a faint policy tether (the distributional effect of the 1980s reforms), but the weight of the sentence is on the other side's donors rather than on any measure or outcome.
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We’re also going to tackle Government spending and ensure that the Reserve Bank once again has a sole focus.
specificity.explanation: Two stated directions of travel. The mandate half names a real, identifiable change; the spending half carries no amount, mechanism or timeframe at all.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We as a Government have decided to cut out the fluff and the nonsense to get down to tin tacks.
specificity.explanation: Offered as a statement of the Government's approach, but names no measure, mechanism, figure or timeframe. Nothing here could be checked or acted on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: But if we want a truly equitable society that gives people equality of opportunity, then we need a much more holistic approach to the economy, one that respects our people—that looks after the dignity of people, and supports people and the essential need that we have for a healthy planet.
specificity.explanation: Offered as the alternative approach, but consists of generic virtues — holistic, respectful, dignified, healthy planet — with no mechanism, instrument, figure or timeframe that anyone could check or act on.
specificity.subject: speaker

divination.statement: What we know is that this Government is rushing through legislation before Christmas that will see people lose their jobs.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that the legislation being passed under urgency in December 2023 will cause job losses. Not a promise about the speaker's own action; a prediction about employment outcomes.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ Household Labour Force Survey employment and unemployment series through 2024, read alongside sector reporting on the December 2023 urgency legislation. True if employment falls or unemployment rises materially over 2024 in the areas the legislation touched; false if employment holds or grows.

civility.statement: This is all being done to further enrich their already rich mates.
civility.explanation: Imputes a corrupt motive — legislating to enrich wealthy associates — rather than engaging what the legislation does. No individual is named, so this stops short of a direct personal insult, but attributing bad faith is a genuine civility failure.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Or do you blindly repeat the talking points handed down to you from the party elite?
civility.explanation: Directed at members opposite as people: they are incurious and repeat instructions without thinking. This is mockery of the members rather than of their argument.
civility.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: The price of food, rents, and mortgages are at record highs, while wages have struggled to keep up, creating a cost of living crisis.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that food prices, rents and mortgage costs were simultaneously at record levels in late 2023 while wage growth lagged behind them.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ Food Price Index and rental price index, and RBNZ average new-mortgage interest rates, for late 2023; plus Stats NZ Labour Cost Index versus CPI over 2021-2023. True if all three cost series were at series highs and the LCI ran below CPI; false if any of the series was materially below its record or wages outpaced CPI over the period.

veracity.statement: Farm inflation is at all-time highs.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the rate of increase in farm input costs was at a record level at the time of speaking.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Beef + Lamb New Zealand / Stats NZ farm expenses price index (or Federated Farmers farm input inflation series) for 2022-2023; true if the annual increase was the highest on record for that series, false if a prior year records a higher rate.

veracity.statement: Grant Robertson’s focus meant that we had record-low unemployment in this country in 2018—3.9 percent we’re talking about, in terms of unemployment in 2018, 3.9 percent.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a specific unemployment rate of 3.9 percent for 2018, and that this was a record low.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ Household Labour Force Survey unemployment rate for the 2018 quarters; true if a 2018 quarter printed 3.9% and no earlier quarter in the series printed lower, false if the rate differs materially or if earlier quarters in the HLFS series were lower.

veracity.statement: So I’m just so proud of the economic management that Labour was able to roll out and that was confirmed in the Pre-election Economic and Fiscal Update and Stats New Zealand June quarter figures: the economy had begun to turn the corner then, and so this Government is inheriting so much of our great work—the economy’s growing again, wages were ahead of inflation while people were in work, and inflation was expected to return to the 1 to 3 percent target band in 2024.
veracity.explanation: Asserts three checkable things about named documents: that the June 2023 quarter Stats NZ figures showed the economy growing, that wage growth exceeded inflation, and that the 2023 PREFU forecast inflation returning to the 1-3 percent band during 2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ GDP release for the June 2023 quarter, Stats NZ Labour Cost Index versus CPI for the year to June 2023, and the Treasury Pre-election Economic and Fiscal Update (September 2023) inflation track. True if GDP grew in that quarter, wage growth exceeded CPI, and the PREFU shows CPI inside 1-3% during calendar 2024; false if any of the three is contradicted by those documents.

veracity.statement: But what we saw in the last term was a Government that had an increase of 83 percent over its two terms in Government—83 percent.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that government spending rose 83 percent across the two terms of the previous Labour-led government.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Treasury Financial Statements of the Government core Crown expenses for the 2016/17 and 2022/23 fiscal years; true if the increase between those two years is approximately 83%, false if it differs materially from that.

focus.statement: The other side of the House might keep blaming COVID and international circumstances, but on this side of the House, we aren’t blaming; we are acting.
focus.explanation: A contrast drawn entirely between the two sides' postures — who blames and who acts. No policy, mechanism or figure is named; strip the party framing and nothing about the bill remains.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: He brought kaupapa like wellbeing into play, and he got Māori to understand that the Reserve Bank could be more than just this little box that these useless National Party and ACT people want to focus on because their whole world is just tied up in one pathetic area.
focus.explanation: There is a genuine policy point about the breadth of the Reserve Bank's mandate, but most of the sentence's weight is a characterisation of the other parties.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: As we all know, you know, the National Party’s economic record is in tatters, trashed by Nicola Willis, as the whole world knows, repealing our beautiful smoke-free legislation.
focus.explanation: Names a specific measure — the repeal of the smoke-free legislation — which is legitimate scrutiny, but it is carried inside a general verdict on the other party's record rather than developed.
focus.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: The way to drive productivity is to support our businesses and our growers and our farmers by lowering inflation.
rigor.explanation: A real inference about the measure before the House, but the causal chain from lower inflation to higher productivity is asserted rather than shown — the conclusion outruns the single premise offered.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Grant Robertson’s focus meant that we had record-low unemployment in this country in 2018—3.9 percent we’re talking about, in terms of unemployment in 2018, 3.9 percent.
rigor.explanation: Post hoc attribution: the 2018 unemployment figure is credited to the dual mandate, but the mandate change was legislated in 2018 and took effect afterwards, so the cited outcome cannot have been produced by it. The conclusion does not follow from the evidence offered.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: So inflation is not only unnecessary for economic growth; as long as it exists, it is the enemy of economic growth.
rigor.explanation: A sweeping universal claim asserted with nothing offered to support it — no mechanism, no evidence, and no acknowledgement that the conclusion would need to hold at every level of inflation for the argument to work.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: It’s a muddled mess, as it is when the Reserve Bank is trying to serve two masters with the fact that they had these two objectives to serve.
rigor.explanation: Argument by analogy: the "two masters" metaphor is doing all the work, with nothing offered to show that two statutory objectives actually conflict in the Bank's decision-making.
rigor.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The commitment to beating inflation starts with ensuring the Reserve Bank is returning to a single mandate of keeping down inflation.
specificity.explanation: Names the actual mechanism the bill enacts — reverting the Reserve Bank to a single price-stability mandate — but supplies no target, timeframe or figure.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I’m just looking at my figures here, and we had a record employment rate in November of 2018 of 68.3 percent.
specificity.explanation: A named statistic with a figure and a date — someone could go to the HLFS series and check it directly.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: That went from just north of $76 billion in 2017—ended up being at $139 billion.
specificity.explanation: Two dollar figures with a named start year, tied to a named quantity — directly checkable against the Crown accounts.
specificity.subject: speaker

civility.statement: He brought kaupapa like wellbeing into play, and he got Māori to understand that the Reserve Bank could be more than just this little box that these useless National Party and ACT people want to focus on because their whole world is just tied up in one pathetic area.
civility.explanation: Calls the members of two parties "useless" and their concerns "pathetic" — the attack lands on the people opposite rather than on the single-mandate argument.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: We’re as embarrassed as the world is shocked to fund their dirty, rotten, filthy tax cuts—disgraceful.
civility.explanation: Extremely harsh language, but every word of it is aimed at a fiscal policy — the tax cuts — and no individual is attacked. Brutal about the policy, civil toward the person.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Nicola Willis is risking people’s lives because Winston made her look silly.
civility.explanation: A direct personal attack: imputes to a named member both recklessness with lives and capitulation out of personal humiliation.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: But it just shows you that this is what the Minister of Finance has to deal with—Winston Raymond Peters and Shane “Sell-out-the-Māoris” Jones.
civility.explanation: Attaches a mocking nickname to a named member that imputes betrayal of his own people — contempt aimed at the person, not at any argument.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: And when the member across the aisle there, the Hon Willie Jackson, talks about a Māori’s perspective, boy oh boy I’m pleased he’s on that side of the House and not this side of the House.
civility.explanation: Sneering dismissal of a named member personally — the relief is at not having to sit near him, not a response to anything he argued.
civility.subject: speaker

divination.statement: I’ll make a prediction. The other side of the House, despite all their lamenting”—this is now National—“will not change it back because they won’t have the opportunity in the foreseeable future.
divination.explanation: Jackson is reading out a forecast made by Shane Jones during the third reading of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Monetary Policy) Amendment Bill: that National would not get the chance to reverse the dual mandate in the foreseeable future. The forecast is Jones's, relayed by Jackson.
divination.subject: other
divination.falsification_criterion: The parliamentary record for legislation reversing the Reserve Bank's dual mandate; true if no bill restoring the single mandate had passed or been introduced by a National-led government within a few years of the original prediction, false if such a bill was introduced and passed in that window.

specificity.statement: What it means is the highest utilisation of labour resource that can be maintained without generating or accelerating inflation.
specificity.explanation: A precise operational definition of the statutory phrase — checkable against the Reserve Bank Act's wording — though it carries no figures or timeframes.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: It is time, and I will say it again, to do one thing well, and that is what we are here to do as a Government first up: we are going to do one thing well—and I will say it again.
specificity.explanation: A repeated slogan; no figure, mechanism, timeframe or named consequence of the mandate change is supplied.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: He’s talked about how you can take systems where there are dual mandates and you can take systems where there are single mandates, and you can see that the inflation’s been going up at the same rate or if not more than the ones with a single mandate—there is no correlation here.
veracity.explanation: Relays Grant Robertson's empirical claim that central banks with dual employment/price mandates have not had systematically higher inflation than single-mandate ones.
veracity.subject: other
veracity.falsification_criterion: Compare CPI inflation 2021–2023 across economies whose central banks carry an employment objective (US Federal Reserve, RBA, RBNZ pre-2023) with single price-stability mandates (Bank of Canada, Bank of England, ECB), per OECD/IMF inflation series. True if dual-mandate economies show no systematically higher inflation; false if they were consistently higher.

veracity.statement: This is the same Government that is—and I keep on banging on about it—about to get rid of the Productivity Commission, people.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the incoming Government was, as at December 2023, moving to disestablish the New Zealand Productivity Commission.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Government announcements and the National–ACT/NZ First coalition fiscal plan, plus the disestablishment decision record for Te Kōmihana Whai Hua o Aotearoa / NZ Productivity Commission. True if a decision to disestablish had been announced or was underway by December 2023; false if no such decision existed.

rigor.statement: Because what it is effectively saying is the way to get inflation down is to make sure that we have as much unemployment as we damn well can, and the wages will plummet as people compete for lower paid work.
rigor.explanation: Strawman: attributes to the single-mandate position a goal of maximising unemployment and suppressing wages, which no one advanced; the conclusion rests on that substituted premise.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: You’re talking about productivity, you’re talking about making this economy work, and you’re getting rid of the very independent tools that would be best to do it.
rigor.explanation: A genuine inconsistency argument (professing to want productivity while abolishing a productivity body), but it leans on an unargued premise that the Commission is the best available instrument.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Now, when you try to reduce emissions, you don’t do it by running a bus all around town trying to pick up every single person. You need to go somewhere faster so people actually get out of their cars.
rigor.explanation: Argument from a loose analogy: nothing is offered to connect bus-route design to central bank mandates, so the transport case cannot carry the conclusion that a second monetary objective must degrade the first.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Because what it is effectively saying is the way to get inflation down is to make sure that we have as much unemployment as we damn well can, and the wages will plummet as people compete for lower paid work.
focus.explanation: Squarely about the mandate change and its claimed transmission mechanism (employment, wages, inflation), though wrapped in a characterisation of what the other side 'really' means.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: We are stuck in the 80s, which is why we’re hearing anecdotes from it, because there is half the House stuck in the 80s and the 70s, and it’s time to move on.
focus.explanation: Characterises the other side's outlook as dated; no policy, measure, figure or outcome is named. No individual is insulted, so this is a Focus failure rather than a Civility one.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: However, we haven’t had a select committee process on this bill—not even a truncated select committee process, not even maybe a week to hear from people who could’ve been invited in to talk to us about this bill.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Economic Objective) Amendment Bill received no select committee stage at all, not even an abbreviated one, before this second reading on 12 December 2023.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Parliament's bill record (legislation.govt.nz / parliament.nz bill history) for the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Economic Objective) Amendment Bill: true if the bill went from first reading to second reading without referral to a select committee; false if any select committee referral or report exists for it.

veracity.statement: On this side of the House, we know that in the past few years we have managed an economy with very low unemployment, the lowest unemployment in 30 years.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that under the 2017–2023 Labour government New Zealand's unemployment rate reached its lowest level in three decades.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ Household Labour Force Survey seasonally adjusted unemployment rate series: true if the low point recorded between 2020 and 2023 is below every quarterly reading in the preceding 30 years; false if any quarter in the 30 years before was lower.

veracity.statement: And at the same time, yes, inflation went up as part of a whole worldwide phenomenon, but it is coming down.
veracity.explanation: Two assertions about the recent past and present: that the NZ inflation rise was part of a global episode, and that NZ inflation was falling as at December 2023.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ CPI annual inflation series to the September 2023 quarter plus OECD/IMF headline inflation series for comparable economies: true if NZ annual CPI inflation in the most recent quarters before December 2023 is below its 2022 peak and if the 2021–22 rise is matched across comparable OECD economies; false if NZ inflation was still rising, or if the rise was idiosyncratic to New Zealand.

veracity.statement: The National Party and the ACT Party campaigned on removing the dual mandate and getting the Reserve Bank focused back on achieving and maintaining stability in the general level of prices over the medium term, and that is exactly what this bill does.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that both National and ACT went into the 2023 general election with a stated policy of removing the Reserve Bank's dual mandate and returning it to a single price-stability objective.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The 2023 National and ACT election policy documents and published campaign statements on monetary policy: true if both parties publicly committed to removing the employment leg of the Reserve Bank mandate before the October 2023 election; false if either party made no such commitment.

rigor.statement: They don’t say the intended focus is exactly what we recommend; instead, they say the intended focus of this bill is consistent with the views we expressed.
rigor.explanation: A close textual inference: she distinguishes 'consistent with' from endorsement and grounds the distinction in the actual wording of the tabled Reserve Bank letter, which she has in front of her. The conclusion (the letter is not an outright endorsement) tracks the premise she offers.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: The National Party has chosen to avoid nuance. The Government doesn’t care about employment. That’s what this bill is telling us.
rigor.explanation: Non sequitur bordering on strawman: removing a statutory objective from the Reserve Bank's mandate does not entail indifference to employment, and she herself has just set out that the Government's stated reason was to prioritise price stability. Nothing is offered to bridge the legislative change to the imputed motive.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Inflation affects those who have the least the most, and that’s what this bill is about.
rigor.explanation: The premise is genuinely supported — he has just read International Labour Organization material on inflation's distributional impact — but there is a real gap between it and the conclusion. That inflation hurts low-income households does not establish that removing the maximum sustainable employment objective is what reduces it, and the step rests largely on an appeal to the ILO's authority rather than on any mechanism linking the mandate change to inflation outcomes.
rigor.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: So the Government could introduce legislation to amend the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act, to remove the economic objective of supporting maximum sustainable employment, or it could issue a new monetary policy committee remit only, which would require the monetary policy committee to place greater weight on price stability relative to maximum sustainable employment.
specificity.explanation: Names the statute, the specific objective at issue, and two distinct mechanisms (amending the Act versus issuing a new monetary policy committee remit), sourced to the regulatory impact statement. Someone could go and check each option.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We need to fix inflation in this country to fix this economy to make sure people can have good jobs, can build good businesses, and put food on the table.
specificity.explanation: A chain of general goods — fix inflation, fix the economy, good jobs, good businesses, food on the table — with no target rate, no timeframe, no mechanism and no figure. Nothing here could be checked or acted on.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Because consistently, in the time that I was the Minister of Finance and the time in which the Governor of the Reserve Bank has been in place, he has stated repeatedly that the Reserve Bank has focused squarely on inflation and that they don’t feel that at any point they have been compromised in that focus.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Reserve Bank Governor has repeatedly stated publicly that the Bank's focus on inflation was never compromised by the dual mandate (in force from 2018 to 2023).
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Public statements by RBNZ Governor Adrian Orr — Monetary Policy Statement press conferences, Finance and Expenditure Committee testimony, and RBNZ speeches, 2018–2023. True if he stated on multiple occasions that the employment objective did not dilute or compromise the Bank's focus on inflation; false if no such repeated statements exist or if he stated the opposite.

veracity.statement: So I’d just like to back up those sentiments from the former Minister because, as we’ve well canvassed—and, actually, as is reflected in the monetary policy remit review from June 2023—it’s pretty clear in black and white from the Reserve Bank of New Zealand that there hadn’t been any meaningful impact or other decisions that would have been made had they not had that dual mandate and solely the focus on price stability.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Reserve Bank's June 2023 monetary policy remit review states that the employment leg of the dual mandate made no meaningful difference to the decisions the Bank actually took.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The RBNZ's 2023 review of the Monetary Policy Remit (published June 2023). True if the review states or concludes that the maximum sustainable employment objective did not materially change the Committee's policy decisions; false if the review reaches no such conclusion or finds the objective did alter decisions.

veracity.statement: Not only do I share that objective from the member’s constituent but I too abhor unnecessary dependence, and I would point to the fact that the previous Government managed the singular achievement of increasing dramatically the number of people on a jobseeker benefit even while unemployment fell.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that under the 2017–2023 Labour government the number of people receiving Jobseeker Support rose substantially over a period in which the measured unemployment rate fell.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MSD benefit fact sheets (Jobseeker Support recipient counts) compared with Stats NZ Household Labour Force Survey unemployment rates, Oct 2017 – Oct 2023. True if jobseeker recipient numbers rose materially over a span in which the unemployment rate also fell; false if jobseeker numbers did not rise, or rose only alongside rising unemployment.

veracity.statement: I’d also note the Reserve Bank’s findings in its review last year, in which it said that a prioritisation of objectives was preferable.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Reserve Bank's own remit review found that prioritising monetary policy objectives (over treating them as co-equal) was preferable.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The RBNZ's review of the Monetary Policy Remit (2022–23 process, published June 2023) and its supporting analysis. True if the review states that a prioritised or hierarchical ordering of objectives is preferable to co-equal objectives; false if it makes no such finding or endorses the existing dual formulation.

focus.statement: The member is bringing a bill to the House. It’s a serious matter. It’s a matter of changing a law, a law that is a significant part of our economic framework, that is arguably part of our constitutional framework—hasn’t gone off to a select committee, hasn’t had the ability to be scrutinised.
focus.explanation: Names the specific measure before the House and the specific procedural defect (no select committee stage). Legitimate scrutiny of a named bill's passage, with no party-directed content.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: I would note that without amending the Act, the monetary policy committee (MPC) would still be required to have regard to maximum sustainable employment. So that would not achieve the objectives that we have, which is a single focus on price stability.
focus.explanation: Engages the legislative mechanism directly — what the Act requires of the MPC and why an alternative option was rejected. No party content.
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Secondarily, or a second question to put forward to the Minister, because as is canvassed in the regulatory impact statement, there are a number of different options before her—I believe three that her officials considered—and there are a number of pluses and minuses on page 7, for those who may be following along at home.
specificity.explanation: Cites a named document (the regulatory impact statement), the number of options officials considered, and the exact page carrying the analysis. Anyone following could check it directly.
specificity.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Well, look, I’d say to the member’s constituent that I share her desire to see high employment, and have received advice that the pre-condition for that to occur is price stability, which is the objective of this bill.
rigor.explanation: The inference from 'high employment is desirable' to 'this bill delivers it' rests entirely on unnamed, undisclosed advice — an appeal to authority. The claimed causal link (price stability as the precondition for high employment) is asserted rather than argued, so there is a real gap between what is offered and what is concluded.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: I would note that without amending the Act, the monetary policy committee (MPC) would still be required to have regard to maximum sustainable employment. So that would not achieve the objectives that we have, which is a single focus on price stability.
rigor.explanation: A valid inference: if the employment objective is set in statute, then changing the remit alone cannot remove it, so the remit-only option cannot deliver a single statutory objective. The conclusion follows directly from the stated premise.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Had the Reserve Bank been operating under a straight inflation-targeting objective in recent years, it would not have had a different outcome.
rigor.explanation: A counterfactual conclusion asserted rather than argued: the preceding context describes the whiplash between unemployment and inflation concerns, but supplies no mechanism linking the mandate's wording to the Bank's actual decisions. The conclusion is offered as contention, leaning on assertion rather than evidence.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Now, that’s actually quite different from what the Minister’s proposing, because she’s not proposing prioritisation; she’s proposing getting rid completely of the maximum sustainable employment objective.
rigor.explanation: A valid inference: if the Bank's letter endorsed prioritisation, and the bill deletes the employment objective rather than ranking it, the letter does not support the bill as drafted. The distinction drawn does the work and the conclusion follows from it.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Had the Reserve Bank been operating under a straight inflation-targeting objective in recent years, it would not have had a different outcome.
focus.explanation: Squarely on the measure before the committee — the effect of the single versus dual objective in clause 4. No party framing at all.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: So I come, then, to my question about the 2021 Monetary Policy Statement from the Reserve Bank that employment was above its maximum sustainable level.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Reserve Bank's November 2021 Monetary Policy Statement judged employment to be above its maximum sustainable level.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The RBNZ November 2021 Monetary Policy Statement text; true if it states employment was at or above its maximum sustainable level, false if it says employment was at or below that level or makes no such assessment.

veracity.statement: In fact, what we heard from the Reserve Bank Governor himself on multiple occasions is that that is not the case and that the dual mandate did not affect the focus on inflation.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Reserve Bank Governor has stated publicly, more than once, that the dual mandate did not reduce the Bank's focus on inflation.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Public statements by the RBNZ Governor — Monetary Policy Statement press conferences, Finance and Expenditure Committee evidence, speeches — before December 2023; true if he stated on two or more occasions that the employment objective did not affect inflation-focused decisions, false if no such statements exist or he said the opposite.

specificity.statement: This is important to my Amendment Paper that I’ve proposed to clause 4, which provides a more flexible approach to monetary policy.
specificity.explanation: Names the instrument and the clause it amends, but describes its effect only as 'a more flexible approach' — no mechanism, wording or threshold that anyone could check or act on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: But if we want to meet halfway, I have an Amendment Paper that would make the maximum sustainable employment objective subservient or subordinate to the inflation control objective.
specificity.explanation: States the concrete legislative mechanism — retain the employment objective but rank it below price stability — precisely enough that the amendment's effect could be checked against the clause. Lacks only the exact drafting.
specificity.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Now, as I noted last night, it would be a radical departure by the Minister to not believe that employment had any merit for consideration, and in order to help shape this discussion, since the Minister declined to answer that question as well last night, I refer the Minister and indeed the committee to amendments in my name to clause 4 that would try to meet the Government halfway.
civility.explanation: Contested debate with ample opportunity for a personal attack; instead the pressure is applied to the Minister's position and her failure to answer a specific question, and it is paired with an offer to compromise. Attacks nothing about the person.
civility.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: There’s a small number of central banks that have price stability as their sole mandate and focus and their sole economic objective. But a larger number have a dual mandate that equally weights price stability and employment objectives. Of course, this includes the US Federal Reserve.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a comparative fact about how many central banks have a sole price-stability mandate versus a dual mandate equally weighting employment, and that the US Federal Reserve is in the latter group.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Survey of the statutory objectives of comparable central banks (BIS/IMF central bank legislation databases). True if the number of central banks with a dual mandate weighting employment equally with price stability exceeds the number with price stability as their sole objective; false if sole-objective/inflation-targeting-only central banks are the larger group. The Federal Reserve sub-claim is settled by the dual mandate in the Federal Reserve Act.

veracity.statement: Because these are all still questions that are yet to be answered because we haven’t had the opportunity to go through a robust select committee process on this.
veracity.explanation: Asserts as fact that the bill has not been through a select committee process.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Parliament's bill record for the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Economic Objective) Amendment Bill. True if the bill was progressed through the House without referral to a select committee and without a call for submissions; false if it was referred to a committee that heard submissions and reported back.

veracity.statement: The Reserve Bank itself has supported the intention of clarifying its focus on inflation.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Reserve Bank has supported the intention behind removing the employment objective and clarifying its inflation focus.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand's published advice, regulatory impact material, or public statements on the removal of the maximum sustainable employment objective. True if the Bank stated it supported clarifying/narrowing its focus on price stability; false if it opposed the change or expressed no such support.

veracity.statement: Having asked the Minister twice now whether or not she received advice that, when the dual mandate was actually in place, that took the Reserve Bank focus away from inflation, and her not to have answered that question twice, it is clear that what we all know in this House is what the Reserve Bank Governor has said publicly, which is that it didn’t.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Reserve Bank Governor has publicly said the dual mandate did not take the Bank's focus away from inflation.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Public statements by the RBNZ Governor (Monetary Policy Statement press conferences, speeches, or Finance and Expenditure Committee evidence, 2018–2023). True if the Governor stated that the employment/dual mandate did not divert the Bank's focus from inflation; false if he said it did, or if no such statement exists.

veracity.statement: I get it; some people have this within their objective, like the Federal Reserve, like the Reserve Bank of Australia. Others have to refer to it: the Bank of Canada, the Bank of England.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Federal Reserve and Reserve Bank of Australia have employment inside their statutory objectives, while the Bank of Canada and Bank of England address it at one remove.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Statutory objectives: the Federal Reserve Act (maximum employment), the Reserve Bank of Australia Act 1959 s10(2) (full employment), the Bank of Canada Act and its inflation-target agreement, and the Bank of England Act 1998 (price stability primary, secondary objective covering employment). True if the Fed and RBA carry employment in their objectives and the BoC and BoE address it only secondarily; false if any of the four is placed in the wrong category.

veracity.statement: They don’t have it directly in there, but they still think about employment, and we are moving into very, very dangerous territory if the position of the Minister is that employment, and the consideration of employment, has no role whatsoever, because that then will take us to the example that I gave in the second reading debate of when, in 2013 and 2014, we had a Reserve Bank Governor with the single mandate who simply believed that it was time for him to start lifting the official cash rate even though unemployment was up over 5 percent at the time.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that in 2013–2014, under the single mandate, the Reserve Bank Governor raised the official cash rate while unemployment was above 5 percent.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: RBNZ official cash rate decisions for 2013 and 2014 and the Stats NZ Household Labour Force Survey unemployment rate for the same quarters. True if the OCR was increased in that period while the measured unemployment rate exceeded 5 percent; false if no increase occurred in that period or unemployment was at or below 5 percent when it did.

focus.statement: There’s a small number of central banks that have price stability as their sole mandate and focus and their sole economic objective. But a larger number have a dual mandate that equally weights price stability and employment objectives. Of course, this includes the US Federal Reserve.
focus.explanation: Engages the substance of the measure before the committee — the design of the Reserve Bank's mandate — and compares it against named institutions rather than attacking the other party.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Is she going to include some form of consideration for maximum sustainable employment or employment in general? Is she going to retain that remit which currently has a focus also on house price sustainability? Is there going to be a hierarchy therein?
focus.explanation: Squarely on the mechanism of the policy: what the replacement remit will contain and how its objectives will rank. No party framing at all.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: In answer to the member’s question: yes, I did receive advice that the dual mandate could affect monetary policy decisions, and in particular—as I have stressed—this is not just about the decisions the Reserve Bank makes but also the interpretation of those decisions.
focus.explanation: Addresses the substance of the measure — the advice received on the dual mandate's effect on monetary policy decisions and their interpretation — rather than the opposing party.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: She’s provided no evidence as to why that’s a problem. In fact, she’s refused to answer the question twice now of whether or not there is any evidence that it was a problem. So we can take from that that there is no evidence to back it up.
focus.explanation: Legitimate scrutiny of the measure before the House — whether there is evidence supporting the provision — not a characterisation of the other party.
focus.subject: speaker

civility.statement: So did she seek that advice on international best practice, and, specifically, whether she sought advice on having the secondary objective—if she was intent in this ceremonial act of repealing this piece of legislation solely because it had been enacted by a previous Government, whether she’d sought advice around the secondary objective?
civility.explanation: Imputes bad faith to the Minister — that the repeal is a 'ceremonial act' undertaken solely because the law came from the previous Government. Short of a direct insult, but it attributes a discreditable motive to the person rather than engaging her stated reasons.
civility.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Is she going to include some form of consideration for maximum sustainable employment or employment in general? Is she going to retain that remit which currently has a focus also on house price sustainability? Is there going to be a hierarchy therein?
specificity.explanation: Names the concrete remit components at issue — maximum sustainable employment, house price sustainability, and the ordering between objectives — so the answer would be checkable. Stops short of figures or timeframes.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: They don’t have it directly in there, but they still think about employment, and we are moving into very, very dangerous territory if the position of the Minister is that employment, and the consideration of employment, has no role whatsoever, because that then will take us to the example that I gave in the second reading debate of when, in 2013 and 2014, we had a Reserve Bank Governor with the single mandate who simply believed that it was time for him to start lifting the official cash rate even though unemployment was up over 5 percent at the time.
specificity.explanation: Anchors the argument in a named period, a named instrument (the official cash rate) and a numeric unemployment threshold, so the historical example can be checked. Marked down slightly because the mechanism connecting that episode to the present bill is left implicit.
specificity.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: And a further note that it is possible that some market participants will see the return to a single mandate as strengthening the Reserve Bank’s focus on price stability that, in turn, will lead to an adjustment in their inflation expectations, which have a direct impact on actual rates of inflation.
rigor.explanation: A three-step causal chain — mandate change, perception of strengthened focus, shifted inflation expectations, changed inflation — offered as the case for the provision. The transmission mechanism is a recognised one, but each link is asserted rather than supported and the whole chain is hedged on 'it is possible', so the conclusion is considerably stronger than what was shown.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: She’s provided no evidence as to why that’s a problem. In fact, she’s refused to answer the question twice now of whether or not there is any evidence that it was a problem. So we can take from that that there is no evidence to back it up.
rigor.explanation: Argument from silence: infers that no evidence exists from the Minister's failure to produce it when asked. A non-answer in a committee debate is weak grounds for a conclusion about the state of the evidence, though the inference is at least directed at the bill's evidential basis.
rigor.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: As the former Minister was just elucidating, we have quite a strong reliance on a report on the remit and the mandate from June 2023 from the monetary policy committee, which spoke about the need to have a potential hierarchical ordering of that dual mandate.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that a June 2023 monetary policy committee report on the Reserve Bank's remit and mandate exists and argued for a hierarchical ordering of the price-stability and maximum-sustainable-employment objectives.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand monetary policy committee's June 2023 remit/mandate report (RBNZ publications); true if such a report exists and raises a hierarchical ordering or prioritisation of the two mandate objectives, false if no such June 2023 report exists or it makes no such point.

veracity.statement: I’d also note, and Minister Robertson—the former Minister Robertson may remember this, that when he introduced the maximum sustainable employment objective, it was recognised that at that time that if the bank put more weight on employment stabilisation at certain points in the cycle, that could lead to higher volatility in inflation.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that when the maximum sustainable employment objective was introduced, the official advice of the time acknowledged a trade-off in which greater weight on employment stabilisation could raise inflation volatility.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The regulatory impact statement and Treasury/RBNZ advice accompanying the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Monetary Policy) Amendment Act 2018, which added the employment objective; true if that advice records the volatility trade-off described, false if the contemporaneous advice contains no such acknowledgement.

rigor.statement: Because if that is the case, then the words we have heard from the Reserve Bank Governor, Adrian Orr, in the Finance and Expenditure Committee hearings over the last three years are to be taken as untrue, and that’s a pretty serious allegation which underlines the proposal herein.
rigor.explanation: A conditional argument about the bill's premise, but it moves from 'the dual mandate deprioritised price stability' to 'Orr's evidence was untrue' — a false dichotomy that excludes the obvious third option that the Governor's assessment was simply mistaken rather than dishonest.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: There’s also the issue that there are real challenges to including maximum sustainable employment that arise from measurement issues, because it is more or less impossible to measure maximum sustainable employment.
rigor.explanation: Circular: the reason offered for the claim ('measurement issues') is a restatement of the claim itself ('impossible to measure'). Nothing independent is supplied to establish why the quantity cannot be estimated.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: And I’d note that some market participants, like Business New Zealand, have noted that with so many balls in the year, the bank can no longer concentrate on monetary policy’s prime purpose of ensuring relatively stable price levels over time.
rigor.explanation: Appeal to authority, and to an interested party: a business lobby group's opinion is offered as support for the mandate change without any evidence that the bank's concentration has in fact diminished.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: But, again, I do ask the Minister if she has seen any evidence as to whether that dual mandate has changed the focus or has meant that there has been a deprioritisation of price stability.
focus.explanation: Squarely on the measure before the House — asks for the evidence base for removing the dual mandate. Scrutiny of a named policy rationale, no party framing at all.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: And a single mandate makes clear what the objective of the monetary policy committee is, which is price stability—putting a lid on inflation. It also makes clear that other matters such as supporting New Zealanders with the cost of unemployment—that is the purview of fiscal policy, not monetary policy, because we don’t think it makes sense to ask the Reserve Bank to try to solve a problem which is actually the presiding role of the Government and its policy.
focus.explanation: Engages the mechanism at issue — what a single versus dual mandate does to the committee's objective, and the monetary/fiscal division of labour. No party content.
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: And just to potentially help move things along here with regard to getting more evidence on the table and therefore having a more thoroughly informed debate in lieu of not having a select committee process, the Minister has referred to the letter from the Reserve Bank Governor—and I thank her for tabling it—but may I ask her to table the letter that she wrote to the Reserve Bank Governor, because it feels as though there were a few options laid on the table therein, which means that potentially we could have a more informed debate if we were to understand what options she was seeking advice on and got a response upon.
specificity.explanation: Names a particular document (the Minister's own letter to the Governor), the counterpart already tabled, and the reason it is wanted. Concrete and actionable, though it stops short of stating what the letter is expected to contain.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Well, on this side of the House we can land on one thing, which is: we’re going to beat inflation, and this Act is going to help us do it.
specificity.explanation: A slogan closing the contribution — no target rate, no timeframe, and no account of the mechanism by which the Act is expected to help, in a debate where all three were available to state.
specificity.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Madam Chair, I’m going to take this opportunity to spell out once again—and repetition that I hope the House will indulge me in—the answers to the repeated questions that clearly the former member for Wellington Central has failed to grasp the answers to.
civility.explanation: Condescension aimed at a member personally — casting his questions as a failure to grasp answers already given, rather than engaging the point. Short of a direct insult but no longer civil.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Finally, I want to note that there are a number of amendments that have been tabled and suggested by the member Hon Grant Robertson, who can’t seem to make up his mind what the purpose of the Reserve Bank Act has been, because I can count several different ideas he has, which is rather symptomatic of the member—that he couldn’t just land on one thing.
civility.explanation: A personal attack: the tabling of several amendments is turned into a claim about the member's character — that indecisiveness is 'symptomatic' of him — rather than an argument about the amendments.
civility.subject: speaker

focus.statement: My understanding of the term “maximum sustainable employment” is that it’s a particular term used, because the “sustainable” part of that is that if there is any tension between full employment and price stability, price stability wins out. There is, in fact, a hierarchy built into the term itself.
focus.explanation: Squarely engages the statutory wording of the measure before the committee — what 'maximum sustainable employment' means and how it ranks against price stability. No party framing at all.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: The amendment restores the purpose of this monetary policy, and it would be to take out, remove in clause 7, the word “objective” and replace it with “welfare of working people”.
focus.explanation: Entirely about the mechanism of the amendment before the committee — which clause, which words, what effect.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: If I was to be really cynical, I’d say that the Government doesn’t care about people who don’t work, but they say they care about people who do work.
focus.explanation: A claim about what the Government secretly does and does not care about, with no policy, figure or outcome named. It gestures at the bill's employment objective but the weight is party characterisation rather than the measure. Hedged with 'if I was to be really cynical', which keeps it from the bottom of the scale.
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: My understanding of the term “maximum sustainable employment” is that it’s a particular term used, because the “sustainable” part of that is that if there is any tension between full employment and price stability, price stability wins out. There is, in fact, a hierarchy built into the term itself.
specificity.explanation: Names the statutory term and explains the mechanism it encodes (a hierarchy in which price stability prevails), but carries no figures, dates or clause references.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: But when you look at New Zealand and Australia—both of which have central banks with dual mandates—inflation peaked at 7.2 percent and 7.8 percent respectively. But in Sweden—which has a central bank with a primary price stability mandate—it peaked at 12.3 percent.
specificity.explanation: Three named countries, three inflation peaks to one decimal place, each tied to a named mandate type. Directly checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The amendment restores the purpose of this monetary policy, and it would be to take out, remove in clause 7, the word “objective” and replace it with “welfare of working people”.
specificity.explanation: Names the clause, the word to be deleted and the exact wording to be substituted. A drafter could act on it as stated.
specificity.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Now, I do take on board that there is an issue raised about the perception of others, but I wondered and I wanted to ask you: isn’t it our job as a Government and as a Parliament to lead, not to sap up the way that people misconceive things? We need to bust myths, not assist them.
civility.explanation: A contested exchange in which she could easily have turned on the Minister. She criticises the Government's approach — legislating to accommodate a misconception — and attacks no person. Pointed but entirely on the substance.
civility.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Aren’t we actually in a situation that will lead to the alienation of the very people that we seek to support if, in fact, they lose their jobs in great numbers because the Reserve Bank is untethered from any concern about their wellbeing through work—and isn’t that what we’re all here to do, Minister?
rigor.explanation: A chain of consequences asserted rather than shown: removing the employment limb is taken to leave the Bank 'untethered', that is taken to produce job losses 'in great numbers', and those to produce alienation. Nothing is offered to connect the links — a slippery slope. The argument is about the policy, so this is a reasoning defect, not a Focus one.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: So, unfortunately for the new Government, the perception that this dual mandate therefore makes it more difficult to focus on inflation seems null and void.
rigor.explanation: A general conclusion about mandate design drawn from three hand-picked countries, with nothing controlling for the many other drivers of inflation (energy exposure, fiscal stance, currency). Hasty generalisation from a small selected sample. The claim engages the policy question, so the defect is the inference, not the target.
rigor.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: But when you look at New Zealand and Australia—both of which have central banks with dual mandates—inflation peaked at 7.2 percent and 7.8 percent respectively. But in Sweden—which has a central bank with a primary price stability mandate—it peaked at 12.3 percent.
veracity.explanation: Asserts three peak inflation figures from the recent cycle — New Zealand 7.2 percent, Australia 7.8 percent, Sweden 12.3 percent — and characterises the mandate of each country's central bank as dual, dual and single-price-stability respectively.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Peak annual CPI inflation in the 2021-23 cycle: Stats NZ CPI for New Zealand, ABS CPI for Australia, Statistics Sweden CPI for Sweden. True if the peaks match 7.2%, 7.8% and 12.3% within rounding; false if materially different. Mandate characterisation checked against the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021 remit, the RBA Act/Statement on the Conduct of Monetary Policy, and the Sveriges Riksbank Act.

divination.statement: I know it’s going to be a bit of a rarity over the next 100 days, but it clearly shows that you can put together a regulatory impact statement very quickly.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that regulatory impact statements will be largely absent from the Government's legislation during its first 100 days in office.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Treasury/agency regulatory impact statements published for Government bills passed during the coalition's first 100 days (from 27 November 2023 to approximately 19 March 2024). True if most such bills proceeded without a published RIS or under an exemption/waiver; false if a RIS accompanied the majority of them.

focus.statement: So I suggest that if the Government is as determined to bring down inflation, then it provides as much focus on commerce law and ensuring that there’s indeed true competition across all parts of our economy.
focus.explanation: Squarely about policy — proposes competition/commerce law as an alternative lever on inflation. No party framing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: So my question for the Minister in the chair is: given that there is going to be the sole mandate, what mechanisms is the Minister going to put in place to ensure that we do not lose sight of those perspectives around employment when decisions are being taken by the monetary policy committee?
focus.explanation: Directed entirely at the measure before the House — the consequence of the narrowed objective and what institutional mechanism would substitute for it. Legitimate scrutiny of a specific policy change, with no party framing at all.
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: So I suggest that if the Government is as determined to bring down inflation, then it provides as much focus on commerce law and ensuring that there’s indeed true competition across all parts of our economy.
specificity.explanation: Names a policy domain (commerce law, competition) but supplies no mechanism, instrument, figure or timeframe — a direction, not an actionable proposal.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: There would be, for example, the ability to amend section 130 of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act, which would require a report on monetary policy to look at the impacts of the monetary policy committee’s approach on economic development and employment.
specificity.explanation: Names the exact provision (s 130), the instrument (an amendment), and precisely what the resulting obligation would be (a monetary policy report covering impacts on economic development and employment). Someone could draft it from this. Short of 1.0 only for carrying no figures or dates.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The first amendment that I will be tabling is that we extend the membership of the monetary policy committee to contain no fewer than one trade union or worker representative.
specificity.explanation: A concrete, checkable mechanism: a named body (the monetary policy committee), a named change (membership), and a numeric floor (no fewer than one worker or union representative). No timeframe or cost, which keeps it off 1.0.
specificity.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: But in terms of this piece of legislation, removing the dual purpose that we inserted into it is a backward step for a country that has prided itself on social justice, prided itself on ensuring that benefits flow to all New Zealanders, prided itself on being a leader in the world, and, at a time when other reserve banks have more than one purpose with monetary policy, we’re taking a backward step, which seems to be part and parcel of the direction of this Government.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion ('a backward step') rests mainly on an appeal to national self-image and tradition — pride in social justice, in benefits flowing to all, in world leadership — none of which bears on whether a dual mandate improves monetary policy. The one substantive premise (other reserve banks have more than one purpose) is asserted but never connected to the conclusion, and the closing clause generalises to the Government's direction rather than the measure.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Returning the Reserve Bank to a single mandate is by no means out of step with international best practice, so long as a flexible approach to inflation targeting is maintained—which is allowed for by this Act—which means that the monetary policy committee can still have regard to the impact on the real economy in determining how quickly to achieve their primary goal of sorting out inflation.
rigor.explanation: A real inference with its condition stated: flexible inflation targeting is offered as the mechanism by which real-economy effects remain in scope, and that mechanism does support the conclusion that a single mandate need not exclude employment considerations. Marked down because the appeal to 'international best practice' is asserted without a single example, so that half of the claim is unsupported.
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: It would be useful if members, in making contributions at this committee stage, had read the bills.
civility.explanation: Condescension aimed at the members opposite rather than their argument — it imputes that they have not bothered to read the legislation. Short of a direct insult, but it addresses the people, not the point.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Because we come back to the very beginning of this discussion: the Minister has presented no evidence to the committee that there is any conflict between the two.
civility.explanation: Pointed criticism directed entirely at the adequacy of the Minister's justification, in a genuinely contested debate where he could readily have imputed bad faith. He does not — no sneer, no attack on her competence or motives.
civility.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: The purpose of the bill already promotes the prosperity and wellbeing of New Zealanders and contributes to a sustainable and productive economy, so that is made clear.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the purpose provision of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act, as it stands under the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Economic Objective) Amendment Bill, already contains language about promoting the prosperity and well-being of New Zealanders and contributing to a sustainable and productive economy.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The purpose section (s 3) of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act 2021 as amended by the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Economic Objective) Amendment Bill 2023, on legislation.govt.nz. True if that section contains wording to the effect of promoting the prosperity and well-being of New Zealanders and contributing to a sustainable and productive economy; false if the purpose provision contains no such wording or was removed by the bill.

veracity.statement: As we know, this is, in fact, the view that the Reserve Bank stated to the Minister in the letter that she tabled to the House last night.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that a letter from the Reserve Bank to the Minister of Finance, tabled in the House on 11 December 2023, states that employment is a question of prioritisation rather than exclusion in monetary policy.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Reserve Bank letter tabled in the House of Representatives on 11 December 2023 (Parliament's tabled-documents record). True if the letter contains a statement that employment considerations remain relevant and the change is one of prioritisation rather than exclusion; false if the letter contains no such statement or says the opposite.

veracity.statement: The purpose of this amendment is providing that consideration to employment matters when the monetary policy committee does come to consider these matters, that they do not lose sight of that incredibly important factor that needs to be considered—accepting there is the sole mandate that the objective has been narrowed to, but there is not a central bank in the world, even those with sole mandates, that doesn’t have some ability to keep sight of employment as an objective.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a universal claim: that no central bank anywhere, including single-mandate central banks, lacks some ability to take employment into account in monetary policy. The checkable core is the universal quantifier — a single counterexample defeats it.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Published mandate and objective statements for single-mandate central banks (e.g. the ECB, the Reserve Bank of Australia, the Bank of England, the Swiss National Bank, Sweden's Riksbank) and comparative surveys of central bank mandates (BIS/IMF). True if every such bank's governing statute or published framework permits regard to real-economy or employment effects (e.g. via flexible inflation targeting or a secondary objective); false if at least one central bank's framework excludes employment considerations entirely.

rigor.statement: So the contention on this side of the House is that had the dual mandate actually caused the Reserve Bank to stay its hand and counteract inflation in a half-hearted way, then we would expect to see notable differences in the approach of our Reserve Bank as compared with those economies that have a Reserve Bank with a single mandate. That’s not actually the case.
rigor.explanation: A genuine modus tollens: states what the opposing hypothesis would predict (divergence from single-mandate central banks), then denies the observed consequent. The inference is valid given its premise; whether the comparative claim is accurate is Veracity's question, not this one. Marked down slightly because other factors could explain convergent policy.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: So the contention on this side of the House is that had the dual mandate actually caused the Reserve Bank to stay its hand and counteract inflation in a half-hearted way, then we would expect to see notable differences in the approach of our Reserve Bank as compared with those economies that have a Reserve Bank with a single mandate. That’s not actually the case.
focus.explanation: Engages the mechanism of the measure before the House — whether the dual mandate changed the Reserve Bank's actual conduct — with no party framing at all.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: So I think what we can see, members, is that just as they strayed away from economic orthodoxy and threw new objectives at the bank and threw it at the wall and failed to actually achieve anything, so they will continue for the next couple of years straying from the orthodox path, being prepared to put the economy at risk.
focus.explanation: Strip out the characterisation of Labour and nothing about the bill remains: no clause, figure, mechanism or named outcome. It is a claim about what the other party is like and will keep being like. Nothing is emitted for Rigor — a jibe about opponents' disposition is not an argument, and labelling it a fallacy would double-count what Focus already catches.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: That is why we actually need to retain both maximum sustainable employment and price stability in the objectives for the Reserve Bank.
focus.explanation: Names the two statutory objectives that are precisely what the bill before the committee alters. Squarely on the measure, with no reference to the other party at all.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: The Reserve Bank’s approach has not only been in line with international counterparts with a single mandate but they actually chose to tighten their approach to the availability of cash in the economy faster than some of their international counterparts with a single mandate.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the RBNZ's monetary tightening from 2021 onward matched, and in timing outpaced, that of at least some single-mandate central banks.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Compare the RBNZ Official Cash Rate decision record (Oct 2021 onward) against the policy-rate paths of single-mandate central banks over the same period — the ECB, the Bank of England and the Bank of Canada. True if the RBNZ began tightening earlier and/or raised rates by more over 2021–2023 than at least one of those banks; false if the RBNZ began later and moved less than all of them.

civility.statement: The Minister needs to tell us if she does not have confidence in the monetary policy committee to also take into account the effect of their decisions on employment and people’s enjoyment of a stable economy, because that would be a radical departure of the Government’s approach to what it is telling the RBNZ.
civility.explanation: A contested committee debate where an uncivil turn was readily available. The demand is pointed and presses the Minister hard, but it targets a stated position and its consequences, not the Minister personally — no imputation of bad faith or incompetence.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: In fact, when Grant Robertson, back in the days when he used to do the make-believe that he believed in economic orthodoxy and he was responsible, he presided over an Act in which Schedule 3, clause 20 specifically required the Minister to appoint only “a person who, in the Minister’s opinion, [had] the appropriate knowledge, skills, and experience”—the appropriate knowledge, skills, and experience—“to assist the monetary policy committee [in] its functions”.
civility.explanation: 'the make-believe that he believed' imputes insincerity to a named member — an accusation that he was pretending to hold convictions he did not hold. That is bad faith attributed to the person, not a criticism of the policy, and it sits short of a direct insult.
civility.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I have an Amendment Paper there inserting a new clause which suggests that there should be compensation for workers adversely affected by monetary policy.
specificity.explanation: Names a concrete legislative vehicle and a definite mechanism (compensation), but supplies no amount, no eligibility test for 'adversely affected', no funding source and no timeframe — the direction is clear, the how and how much are absent.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: If we have a look at Canada, the Bank of Canada is now required to actively seek a level of maximum sustainable employment.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Bank of Canada is under a requirement to actively pursue maximum sustainable employment, offered as a factual description of Canada's current monetary policy framework.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Bank of Canada Act and the 2021 joint Government of Canada / Bank of Canada monetary policy framework renewal statement; true if the Bank is formally required (statutorily or by the framework agreement) to actively seek maximum sustainable employment, false if its mandate is price stability alone with employment only an informal consideration.

veracity.statement: And yet this Government has come in and one of the first pieces of legislation—in fact, the first piece of legislation—is to remove the objective in the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act to try and get that to happen.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Reserve Bank of New Zealand (Economic Objective) Amendment Bill was the first piece of legislation of the incoming coalition Government.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Parliament's record of Government bills introduced from the swearing-in of the Sixth National Government on 27 November 2023; true if this bill was the first Government bill introduced, false if another Government bill (e.g. the Fair Pay Agreements Act Repeal Bill or a taxation bill) preceded it.

veracity.statement: In specific reference to member Woods’ proposal to review the Act, there is already a post-implementation review of the Act due by 2027.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that a post-implementation review of the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act is already scheduled and due by 2027, making the proposed amendment redundant.
veracity.subject: speaker
