specificity.statement: They voted for change because, unlike the previous Labour Government, they knew what a mess our economy had been put into and they knew that we had to have change to get maximum flexibility in our businesses to get our country out of the mess that it had been put in by the previous Labour Government.
specificity.explanation: 'A mess', 'maximum flexibility' — no figures, no mechanism, nothing about what the repeal actually does. She had a full call in which to supply detail and supplied none.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: But if you work a Tuesday to Saturday roster, given that most of our public holidays in New Zealand are on a Monday, you miss out on about six days of public holidays.
specificity.explanation: Names the roster pattern, the mechanism (Monday holidays fall outside the roster) and a quantity (about six days). Someone could check it or draft around it.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: There are examples in Auckland of bus drivers starting their day in South Auckland ending up in central Auckland for a four-hour break before starting their shift again.
specificity.explanation: Named location, named occupation and a stated duration, but no number of workers affected and no source for the example.
specificity.subject: speaker

civility.statement: They voted for change because, unlike the previous Labour Government, they knew what a mess our economy had been put into and they knew that we had to have change to get maximum flexibility in our businesses to get our country out of the mess that it had been put in by the previous Labour Government.
civility.explanation: Hard on the previous government's record and on no individual at all. Attacking a party rather than a person passes Civility cleanly; the tribalism is Focus's problem, scored above.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I just find it so offensive that people on the other side of this House actually think that stories about workers being mistreated in the workplace, having to go to the toilet in a bush, having to argue why they need to keep their job because they’re an older woman without savings and they just can’t stack a supermarket shelf that quickly—again, I’m seeing smirks.
civility.explanation: Attributes a state of mind to members opposite — that they find worker mistreatment amusing. Short of a direct insult, but it imputes callousness to identifiable people rather than engaging their argument.
civility.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: But if you work a Tuesday to Saturday roster, given that most of our public holidays in New Zealand are on a Monday, you miss out on about six days of public holidays.
veracity.explanation: Asserts two linked factual claims: that most NZ public holidays fall on a Monday, and that a Tuesday–Saturday roster worker consequently misses about six of them.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The public holidays listed in the Holidays Act 2003 and the weekday each is observed on (including Mondayisation): true if a majority of New Zealand's 11–12 public holidays fall on a Monday and a Tuesday–Saturday roster therefore forgoes roughly six of them; false if fewer than half are Monday holidays or the shortfall is materially smaller than six days.

veracity.statement: One of the reasons, as I’ve said in previous contributions, is that they have what they call enterprise bargaining, which is the comparable sector-based bargaining that we were looking to achieve.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Australian mechanism called enterprise bargaining is equivalent in scope to the sector-wide bargaining fair pay agreements would have created.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The definition of an enterprise agreement under Australia's Fair Work Act 2009: true if Australian enterprise bargaining sets terms across an industry or sector, false if it bargains at the level of the individual enterprise or employer.

veracity.statement: We have Countdown/Woolworths, owned by an Australian company and all the profit heads back to Australia.
veracity.explanation: Two claims: that Countdown/Woolworths is Australian-owned, and that all of its profit is repatriated. The second is the checkable and overstated part.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ownership records for Woolworths NZ (Countdown), plus its filed financial statements and the Commerce Commission's 2022 grocery sector market study on dividends remitted to the parent versus profit retained and reinvested in New Zealand: true if the company is Australian-owned and essentially all profit is remitted to Australia, false if a material share is retained or reinvested here.

veracity.statement: Back in 1991 when the Employment Contracts Act was brought in, it took away the ability for us to have sector agreements.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the 1991 Act removed the legal mechanism for agreements covering an entire sector.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Employment Contracts Act 1991 and the award system it replaced: true if the Act ended the national/occupational award system that set terms across a whole sector, false if sector-wide agreements remained available on the same legal footing after it.

rigor.statement: One of the reasons, as I’ve said in previous contributions, is that they have what they call enterprise bargaining, which is the comparable sector-based bargaining that we were looking to achieve.
rigor.explanation: A causal attribution drawn from a two-country comparison: Australia has a different bargaining system and higher wages, therefore the bargaining system is a reason for the wages. Nothing is offered to rule out the other differences between the two labour markets, so the conclusion outruns what was shown.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Thanking people is all very nice, but a thankyou and a box of chocolates doesn’t buy your supermarket shop for the week. It doesn’t pay your mortgage or your rent.
rigor.explanation: A modest but valid inference: public gratitude does not meet the material need it was offered in place of, so it is not a substitute for pay and conditions. The conclusion tracks the premise, though the premise is close to self-evident.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: If they’re forced to lay off staff, reduce production, or close their doors, everyone suffers, and the fair pay agreement will do nothing—nothing—to lift the productivity that New Zealand desperately needs.
rigor.explanation: The productivity conclusion is asserted, not derived. The premises offered — that Wairarapa employers behave responsibly and that layoffs hurt everyone — do not bear on whether sector bargaining raises or lowers productivity; the repetition of 'nothing' stands in for the missing link.
rigor.subject: speaker

divination.statement: We will make sure that these fair pay agreements become a reality when we are back on the Treasury benches in 2026.
divination.explanation: Alongside the commitment to restore fair pay agreements, this forecasts a political outcome the speaker does not control — Labour returning to government at the 2026 election.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: The result of the 2026 New Zealand general election and the government formed after it: true if Labour is in government following that election, false if it is not.

veracity.statement: We have saved two megatons of carbon already.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Clean Car Discount has already abated two megatonnes of CO2-equivalent as at December 2023. Ambiguous between emissions already avoided and lifetime savings locked in by vehicles purchased under the scheme; the criterion below treats the literal claim.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Transport / NZTA published estimates of CO2-e abatement attributable to the Clean Car Discount to December 2023, and Climate Change Commission commentary on them; true if the official estimate of emissions saved to date is approximately 2 Mt CO2-e, false if the official figure is materially lower or is a lifetime-of-fleet projection rather than emissions already avoided.

veracity.statement: The polling shows only 20 percent of New Zealanders oppose it. A majority of New Zealanders support it—52 percent.
veracity.explanation: Asserts specific published polling figures on public opinion of the Clean Car Discount: 20 percent opposed, 52 percent in support.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Published New Zealand polling on the Clean Car Discount from 2023 (e.g. Horizon Research, Talbot Mills, Curia); true if a poll reports opposition near 20 percent and support near 52 percent, false if the available polling shows materially different figures or no poll with those numbers exists.

veracity.statement: Finally, this Government has suppressed the climate analysis. There was a regulatory impact statement prepared on the repeal of this Act that says exactly what the estimated impact will be on our carbon budget, and the Government is refusing to release that as we repeal the bill.
veracity.explanation: Two linked factual assertions: that a regulatory impact statement on the repeal was prepared containing an estimated carbon-budget impact, and that the Government had not released it at the time of the repeal debate.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Ministry of Transport / Treasury regulatory impact statement register and the Land Transport (Repeal of Clean Car Discounts) Amendment Bill's disclosure statement; true if a RIS on the repeal existed and was unpublished as at 12 December 2023, false if no such RIS was prepared or if it had already been publicly released by that date.

veracity.statement: France has had one since 2008, and the highest fee now has gone from—it started at €2,000, then it was €30,000, now it’s up to €50,000 on the highest-emitting vehicle.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that France introduced a feebate in 2008 and that the maximum penalty has escalated from €2,000 at introduction, through €30,000, to €50,000 as at late 2023.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The French bonus-malus écologique schedule as set out in successive finance laws; true if the scheme dates from 2008 and the maximum malus for 2023 is €50,000 with the stated intermediate steps approximately right, false if the start year is wrong or the maximum malus for 2023 differs materially from €50,000.

veracity.statement: This wild scheme has led to a $300 million deficit, Julie Anne Genter—a $300 million deficit—between the amount of money recovered from long-suffering tradies, farmers, and big families who needed to replace a vehicle with a petrol diesel vehicle, and the amount of money paid out to people who receive subsidies for Teslas and other very expensive EVs.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that rebates paid out under the Clean Car Discount exceeded fees collected by approximately $300 million as at December 2023.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZTA Clean Car Discount scheme financial reporting and Treasury/Budget documents on the scheme's fee revenue versus rebate expenditure to late 2023; true if the shortfall is approximately $300 million, false if the reported gap is materially smaller or the scheme was in surplus.

veracity.statement: Over $120 million was paid out to people to buy vehicles worth more than $70,000.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that more than $120 million in Clean Car Discount rebates went to purchases of vehicles priced above $70,000.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZTA Clean Car Discount rebate data disaggregated by vehicle purchase price; true if cumulative rebates on vehicles above $70,000 exceed $120 million to late 2023, false if the figure for that price band is materially lower.

civility.statement: I have to address the misinformation in the Minister’s—basically, the Minister has a bunch of culture war talking points that have no evidence or basis in reality.
civility.explanation: Goes past the argument to the Minister's motive: characterising his contribution as 'culture war talking points' imputes bad faith rather than engaging what he said. Short of a direct insult, but no longer civil under the re-anchored scale where 1.0 is the expected standard.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Now, to that member, Julie Anne Genter, heckling irrationally from the sidelines, the member said it’s time to confront reality.
civility.explanation: A clear personal attack: names the member and characterises her as irrational and as heckling from the sidelines, rather than engaging the interjection's content (which was a question about industry support for the rebate).
civility.subject: speaker

focus.statement: The National Party does not care about equity. Do not believe what they say when they say that they care about equity, because they are giving tonnes of money to the wealthiest people through tax cuts back to landlords.
focus.explanation: There is a real policy referent — tax cuts for landlords and their distributional effect — but the weight of the statement is a characterisation of what the other party is really like and an instruction to disbelieve them. A policy point wrapped in party framing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Finally, this Government has suppressed the climate analysis. There was a regulatory impact statement prepared on the repeal of this Act that says exactly what the estimated impact will be on our carbon budget, and the Government is refusing to release that as we repeal the bill.
focus.explanation: Names a specific document (the regulatory impact statement on the repeal), a specific omission (its non-release), and the specific consequence (the House voting without the carbon-budget impact). This is scrutiny of a named process failure, not tribalism, and is the core job of an opposition MP.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: It was bad policy, it was bad law, and the ACT Party is proud—proud—to see the end of the Clean Car Discount, the ute tax, and restore some sanity into climate policy and transport policy after the last three years of frothing and boiling nonsense from the Green Party and their woke mates in the Labour Party.
focus.explanation: The policy content is a bare verdict — 'bad policy, bad law' — with no mechanism, cost or outcome named. The substance of the sentence is a characterisation of the opposing parties over a three-year period. No individual is attacked, so this passes Civility; it is the party-directed content Focus exists to catch.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Nothing—nothing—signals how out of touch the modern Labour Party is with its working-class heritage in this deeply regressive tax on working-class New Zealanders that sees them subsidising those in the leafy suburbs to buy their Teslas.
focus.explanation: Carries a genuine policy claim about the scheme's incidence — that fees fall on lower-income buyers and fund rebates for wealthier ones. But the sentence is built around what the claim shows about the Labour Party's character and heritage rather than around the policy mechanism itself.
focus.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: We know that relying on the emissions trading scheme (ETS), fuel being in the ETS, does nothing to help New Zealanders get into lower-emissions vehicles. What it does do is it means once people are already in high-emitting vehicles, they have to pay more to drive around.
rigor.explanation: A real inference about the policy: the ETS prices fuel at the point of use rather than at the point of purchase, so it raises running costs for people already locked into high-emitting vehicles instead of shifting purchase decisions. The mechanism supports the conclusion, but 'does nothing' overstates it — a sustained running-cost signal does feed back into purchase choices, and that gap between what was shown and what was concluded is unaddressed.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: That statistic alone confirms what ACT, what National, and what submitters to the Transport and Infrastructure Committee told that committee. The scheme was unnecessary.
rigor.explanation: Non sequitur. The statistic offered concerns who received the rebates — a distributional point about wealthy buyers — which bears on whether the scheme was fair or well-targeted, not on whether it was necessary to shift the vehicle fleet. The conclusion also leans on an appeal to authority: that ACT, National and the submitters said so is offered as part of what makes it confirmed.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: It hugely disadvantages rural New Zealanders who simply don’t have the option due to range to take up an electric vehicle.
rigor.explanation: A short but real inference about the policy: if EV range makes the substitute unavailable in rural areas, a fee on high-emitting vehicles is a cost with no avenue of avoidance, so it falls disproportionately on rural buyers. The step tracks. It is weakened by treating range as an absolute bar rather than a constraint that binds for some trips, and by ignoring the rebate side available to the same buyers.
rigor.subject: speaker

divination.statement: Vehicle manufacturers said, quite clearly, between 2025 and 2028 they’re going to completely retool manufacturing in Asia, South-east Asia, and Europe to produce almost nothing but EVs and hybrids.
divination.explanation: Relays a forecast that light-vehicle manufacturing across Asia, South-east Asia and Europe will be retooled between 2025 and 2028 to produce almost exclusively electric and hybrid vehicles. The forecast is the manufacturers'; the speaker is reporting it in support of his own case.
divination.subject: other
divination.subject_name: vehicle manufacturers submitting to the Transport and Infrastructure Committee
divination.falsification_criterion: Global light-vehicle production statistics for 2028 by powertrain (e.g. IEA Global EV Outlook, ACEA and OICA production data); true if EVs and hybrids account for the overwhelming majority of new light-vehicle production from those regions by 2028, false if internal-combustion-only models remain a substantial share of output.

divination.statement: So if you currently drive a Ford Ranger turbo-diesel, you’ll be able to get one—according to the manufacturers—in a hybrid in the next couple of years that will be very, very low with any emissions.
divination.explanation: Relays a forecast that a hybrid Ford Ranger will be available to New Zealand buyers within roughly two years of December 2023, with very low emissions.
divination.subject: other
divination.subject_name: vehicle manufacturers submitting to the Transport and Infrastructure Committee
divination.falsification_criterion: Ford New Zealand's model range and NZTA new-vehicle registration records; true if a hybrid or plug-in hybrid Ford Ranger is on sale in New Zealand by the end of 2025, false if no hybrid Ranger variant is available to New Zealand buyers by that date.

specificity.statement: Over $120 million was paid out to people to buy vehicles worth more than $70,000.
specificity.explanation: A precise, checkable figure tied to a defined threshold — a dollar total of rebates against a named vehicle price band. Someone could go to the NZTA rebate data and verify or refute it.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The answers are actually, Mr Scott Willis, in the macro, and getting the amount of renewable energy coming through that actually drives the innovation, it drives the uptake of the technology that is coming through in terms of electric vehicles and the like.
specificity.explanation: Offered as the alternative to the repealed scheme, so it is trying to convey substance, but it commits to nothing checkable: no generation target, no timeframe, no mechanism by which renewable supply is to be increased, and no figure anywhere. 'In the macro' is doing the work a policy would.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: The reality is Aotearoa is currently not on track to meet its climate targets.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that New Zealand's current emissions trajectory falls short of its stated climate targets, as at December 2023.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Climate Change Commission 2023 advice and MfE emissions projections against the emissions budgets and the NDC; true if official projections show a shortfall against one or more of those targets on current policy, false if they show the targets being met.

veracity.statement: The Climate Change Commission advised that the domestic transport emissions must be halved by 2035, for, as it stands, our transport emissions are one of the fastest-growing sources of greenhouse gas emissions in Aotearoa katoa.
veracity.explanation: Two factual assertions: that the Climate Change Commission advised halving domestic transport emissions by 2035, and that transport is among the fastest-growing sources of NZ greenhouse gas emissions.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Climate Change Commission's 2023 advice on the second emissions reduction plan for a transport-emissions reduction of about 50% by 2035; and NZ's Greenhouse Gas Inventory growth rates by sector. True if the advice states a reduction of that order by that year and transport ranks among the fastest-growing sectors; false if the advised figure or date differs materially or transport is not among the fastest-growing.

veracity.statement: This bill repeals the clean vehicle standard, which already saw a large increase in the purchase of electric cars since the policy was first announced.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the bill before the House repeals the clean vehicle standard, and that that scheme drove a large rise in electric car purchases since it was announced.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The text of the Land Transport (Clean Vehicle Discount Scheme Repeal) Amendment Bill, and NZTA new/used EV registration data from July 2021. True if the bill repeals the Clean Vehicle Standard and EV purchases rose materially after announcement; false if the bill repeals only the Clean Vehicle Discount, the Clean Vehicle Standard being a separate regime left in place.

veracity.statement: Overnight, world leaders, including a representative of New Zealand in the form of our climate change Minister, Simon Watts, agreed that the world and the globe needs to have stronger carbon-cutting plans in place by 2025.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that an international agreement concluded the previous night calls for stronger emissions-reduction plans by 2025, and that New Zealand was represented in it by Climate Change Minister Simon Watts.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The COP28 final decision text adopted 12–13 December 2023 and the NZ delegation list. True if the decision calls on parties to bring forward strengthened plans/NDCs by 2025 and Simon Watts attended as NZ's climate change Minister; false if the agreement contains no such 2025 call or NZ was not represented as described.

veracity.statement: This is a scheme that was set to be self-funding in 10 years. It needed a $300 million upfront cost, but its success is that it has overshot expectations, and for all New Zealanders that is a win.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the Clean Vehicle Discount was designed to be self-funding over a ten-year horizon and required a $300 million upfront appropriation.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Cabinet papers, Budget appropriations and Ministry of Transport design documents for the Clean Vehicle Discount. True if the scheme's design assumed cost-recovery over roughly ten years and the initial Crown funding was about $300 million; false if the design carried no such self-funding horizon or the upfront figure differs materially.

veracity.statement: This scheme is financially unsustainable and fiscally irresponsible, and taxpayers are currently footing the $302 million deficit.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Clean Vehicle Discount is currently running a $302 million deficit borne by taxpayers.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Transport / Treasury reporting on the Clean Vehicle Discount's fee revenue against rebate expenditure as at late 2023. True if the scheme's shortfall was of the order of $302 million and met from Crown funds; false if the figure differs materially or the scheme was not in deficit.

civility.statement: Mokopuna will suffer due to backwards thinking of those in power who are focused on capitalist profit over healthy, functioning, green, wonderful, blue taiao, particularly in Te Tai Tokerau.
civility.explanation: Imputes a motive — pursuit of profit ahead of the environment — to those in government rather than engaging what they have argued. No individual is named or insulted, but attributing bad faith is a real civility failure under the re-anchored scale.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Te Pāti Māori are deeply concerned with this Government’s ram-raid speed at which they are reversing policies that will reduce emissions and protect our taiao—just want to let the words “ram raid” sink in.
civility.explanation: Likens the Government's legislative pace to a criminal ram raid and then deliberately invites the House to dwell on the comparison. A pointed sneer rather than an argument about the pace of repeal, though it lands on the Government collectively and not on any individual.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: But, of course, because they don’t own businesses and have to work on farms, they don’t understand that, do they?
civility.explanation: Condescension aimed at members opposite — that they lack the life experience to understand the issue. Short of a direct insult, but it disparages the members rather than their case.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: So I am calling on those members that are barracking with their best climate denial sledges that we’re hearing across this side of the House to actually front up and tell us what they are going to do to reduce emissions.
civility.explanation: Labels the interjections of members opposite as "climate denial sledges", characterising their position discreditably rather than answering it. The demand attached to it is legitimate, but the framing sneers.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I note that the Minister won’t release the regulatory impact statement and there’s a reason, and we will be asking questions about that during the course of this debate.
civility.explanation: Insinuates an improper motive behind the Minister's withholding of the regulatory impact statement without stating what it is. Pressing for the document's release would be squarely civil; "there's a reason" imputes bad faith by implication.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: She’s spending too much time here in Wellington and needs to get out into our communities and understand what it is like for our rural communities and how they are experiencing it under this ute tax.
civility.explanation: A personal attack on the previous speaker rather than on her argument — where she spends her time and what she is said not to understand, not what she claimed about the scheme.
civility.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Mokopuna will suffer due to backwards thinking of those in power who are focused on capitalist profit over healthy, functioning, green, wonderful, blue taiao, particularly in Te Tai Tokerau.
focus.explanation: Names no policy, measure, figure or outcome; the content is a characterisation of the other side's mindset and priorities. Some climate-harm content remains, so not a floor score.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: But, of course, because they don’t own businesses and have to work on farms, they don’t understand that, do they?
focus.explanation: Once the characterisation of the other side is removed there is nothing left: no measure, cost, mechanism or outcome, only a claim about who members opposite are.
focus.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: So many people in Northland have had to park up their cars and drive utes so they can get around without blowing out tyres. Please go and check all the newsfeeds you like—you’ll see that.
rigor.explanation: A real inference about the policy — poor roads force ute ownership, so the fee falls on people with no substitute — but the support offered is an appeal to unspecified news coverage plus local anecdote. Nothing is cited that could be looked up.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Something I think those members and the seats opposite need to start realising is that unless New Zealand cuts its emissions, we will have to go out and buy international credits of other nations and pay for their decarbonisation.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion tracks the premise: under a binding emissions target, a domestic shortfall must be closed by purchasing offshore mitigation. The step is valid given the framework assumed; no fallacy or appeal is doing the work.
rigor.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: So I would say to you here now: farmers want to do their part to help with climate change. This is not one of them.
specificity.explanation: Rejects the measure and asserts general willingness to act on climate change, but supplies no alternative, no mechanism, no figure and no timeframe. Nothing here could be checked or acted on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: So I am going to look forward to, over the course of this debate, knowing what measures are being put in place to make up for the 900 to 3,000 kilotonnes of carbon that is going to increase in our economy as a result of this measure.
specificity.explanation: Quantifies the emissions gap the repeal is said to open — 900 to 3,000 kilotonnes — and asks precisely what must be substituted for it. The range is wide and no timeframe is attached, but the demand is concrete enough for the Government to answer against.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I’m proud to be part of a party that is going to back our farmers and back our rural sector and ensure that we get back to what we need to.
specificity.explanation: A slogan: "back our farmers" and "get back to what we need to" name no policy, figure, mechanism or date, and commit to nothing that could later be checked.
specificity.subject: speaker

divination.statement: It will result in between 100,000 and 350,000 fewer electric cars on New Zealand roads by 2030.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that repealing the Clean Vehicle Discount will leave the 2030 New Zealand light fleet 100,000 to 350,000 electric vehicles smaller than it otherwise would have been.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: NZTA motor vehicle register EV counts at 31 December 2030 compared against the pre-repeal projected trajectory (Ministry of Transport / Drive Electric baseline with the discount retained). True if the shortfall against that baseline falls within 100,000–350,000 vehicles; false if it is materially below 100,000 or above 350,000.

veracity.statement: Although, in a discussion and further investigation, at the time it was introduced, one little story the member might be interested in: the Ford Ranger, which was a very popular selling—still is popular selling—vehicle, basically runs a Euro5 motor.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Ford Ranger sold in New Zealand is fitted with a Euro 5 emissions-standard engine rather than a Euro 6 one.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ford New Zealand published specifications and NZTA vehicle emissions-standard records for the Ranger models on sale in 2021-2023; true if the mainstream NZ Ranger diesel was certified to Euro 5, false if it was certified to Euro 6.

veracity.statement: A billion dollars in one Budget alone for the rural sectors. Eight hundred million dollars from taxpayers to help eliminate Mycoplasma bovis, which, if it had been let run, would have imposed huge additional costs on farmers.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that taxpayers contributed roughly $800 million to the Mycoplasma bovis eradication programme, and that a Budget under the previous government allocated about $1 billion to the rural sector.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MPI/Treasury records of Crown funding for the Mycoplasma bovis eradication programme (the Crown share of the agreed programme cost) and the Vote Agriculture, Biosecurity, Fisheries and Food Safety appropriations in Budgets 2018-2023; true if the Crown contribution to M. bovis is around $800m and some single Budget allocated about $1bn to rural sectors, false if materially lower.

veracity.statement: Well, yesterday, the Minister of Transport revealed that the Clean Car Discount has become fiscally irresponsible, with taxpayers now footing a $302.5 million deficit.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Clean Car Discount scheme is running a $302.5 million shortfall between rebates paid out and fees collected, as stated by the Minister of Transport.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Transport Clean Car Discount scheme financial reporting to December 2023 and the Minister's release of the same week; true if rebates plus administration exceed charges collected by approximately $302.5m, false if the shortfall is materially different.

veracity.statement: So, as I outlined in my first speech on the first reading of this piece of legislation, the amount paid out in rebates has been $579 million, $13.5 million to administer the scheme, while only $290 million has been received from charges, leaving a hole of $302.5 million for taxpayers—hard-working taxpayers—to foot the bill.
veracity.explanation: Asserts three specific scheme totals — $579m in rebates paid, $13.5m in administration cost, $290m in charges received — netting to a $302.5m deficit.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Transport Clean Car Discount scheme financial data to late 2023 (rebates paid, administration cost, fees collected); true if each of the three figures matches within rounding, false if any is materially different.

specificity.statement: If Ford had chosen to be selling the Euro6 motor in New Zealand, the $8,000 or thereabouts tax that was being charged and had been charged would have been significantly lower because of the emissions profile of that vehicle.
specificity.explanation: Names a specific vehicle, a specific emissions standard and a specific dollar figure for the charge, and identifies the mechanism (the charge scales with the emissions profile).
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: A billion dollars in one Budget alone for the rural sectors. Eight hundred million dollars from taxpayers to help eliminate Mycoplasma bovis, which, if it had been let run, would have imposed huge additional costs on farmers.
specificity.explanation: Two concrete dollar figures attached to named programmes, but no Budget year, no appropriation line and no breakdown of what the billion covered.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Well, yesterday, the Minister of Transport revealed that the Clean Car Discount has become fiscally irresponsible, with taxpayers now footing a $302.5 million deficit.
specificity.explanation: Names the scheme, attributes the figure to a specific source and date, and gives the deficit to the decimal — directly checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: So, as I outlined in my first speech on the first reading of this piece of legislation, the amount paid out in rebates has been $579 million, $13.5 million to administer the scheme, while only $290 million has been received from charges, leaving a hole of $302.5 million for taxpayers—hard-working taxpayers—to foot the bill.
specificity.explanation: Itemised figures for rebates, administration and charges, with the arithmetic to the resulting shortfall — every component is separately checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: If Ford had chosen to be selling the Euro6 motor in New Zealand, the $8,000 or thereabouts tax that was being charged and had been charged would have been significantly lower because of the emissions profile of that vehicle.
rigor.explanation: The inference tracks the design of the scheme — a fee set by emissions would fall if a lower-emitting engine were supplied — though it leaps from a Euro standard to the CO2 g/km basis the charge actually used without bridging the gap.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: This was an incentive to move us in the right direction, and, indeed, the uptake of electric vehicles and hybrids in this country is a measure of the success of this piece of legislation—that’s now been backtracked.
rigor.explanation: Post hoc reasoning: treats observed EV uptake as proof the scheme caused it, offering nothing on the counterfactual (falling global EV prices, model availability) or on the scheme's cost.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Indeed, people like myself who were somewhat cynical about the effectiveness of an electric vehicle but was forced to have one by the Prime Minister—can I say that they are really, really smart vehicles. If you live in a city, everyone should have an electric vehicle. Everyone.
rigor.explanation: Generalises from a single personal anecdote to a universal prescription for all city dwellers — argument from anecdote, with nothing offered about cost, charging access or who the recommendation would not suit.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: But their answer would be to borrow more money—borrow more money from future generations to subsidise people who can already afford to buy these cars and who will continue to buy these cars and who don’t need a subsidy.
rigor.explanation: Strawman: assigns Labour a funding position it has not stated and then argues against it. The underlying point about deadweight subsidy is asserted rather than supported — no evidence is offered that recipients would have bought regardless.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: If it was that bad, I ask every single National Party and ACT member of Parliament that took up the subsidy, as they call it, and claimed it for the electric vehicles they purchased to pay it back.
focus.explanation: Nominally about the rebate, but the substance is the personal purchasing conduct of opposing MPs rather than any mechanism, cost or outcome of the scheme before the House.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: This Government is a backtrack Government with a backtrack piece of legislation.
focus.explanation: A characterisation of the government as a whole with no policy content — no mechanism, figure, cost or outcome is named, only a label applied to the other side.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: They hate the farmers. The Greenies hate the farmers. They want our farmers gone.
focus.explanation: Entirely a claim about what the Green Party is really like. No policy, measure, figure or outcome is named — the content is party motive alone.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: This is a Government, whether it be a three-headed monster or something else, that loves to use the word “back”—backwards-focused; back whatever.
focus.explanation: A characterisation of the coalition and its slogans with no policy content — no measure, figure or outcome from the bill under debate is engaged.
focus.subject: speaker

divination.statement: We are now starting to see—be it Rivian, be it Ford—a Ranger that is a hybrid vehicle coming on to the market next year.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that a hybrid version of the Ford Ranger will be available on the market in 2024.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Ford New Zealand model releases and NZTA new-vehicle registration records for 2024; true if a hybrid or plug-in hybrid Ranger was on sale in New Zealand during 2024, false if its release fell in 2025 or later.

divination.statement: But we’re also confident that there will continue to be an increased uptake of electric vehicles in New Zealand, and that is because car manufacturers around the world are switching from internal combustion engine vehicles to electric vehicles and hybrids and other low-emission technology.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that electric vehicle uptake in New Zealand will keep increasing after the Clean Car Discount is repealed.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: NZTA / Ministry of Transport new light-vehicle registration statistics for 2024 compared with 2023; true if battery-electric and plug-in hybrid registrations rose year on year, false if they fell.

civility.statement: They are well and truly down the road, gone, because that was just a pathetic attempt from the Hon Simeon Brown to justify this Government’s attempt to move in this particular direction.
civility.explanation: Lands on the named individual rather than the argument — calls the Minister's speech 'pathetic' and pronounces his leadership prospects dead, which goes to the person's standing and competence, not to the repeal.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: But the other is that this bill has not had the normal process of going through a select committee, and the Minister of Transport should hang his head in shame that members of the community, the hard-working folk around this country, organisations and other groups within and outside of the sector, have not had an opportunity to submit on this particular bill.
civility.explanation: "Should hang his head in shame" is pointed and lands partly on the Minister personally, but the grievance is a specific procedural decision (no select committee) rather than his character or competence. Robust, edging toward the person without contempt.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: So the Minister of Transport has clearly indicated that he is not interested in listening to the hard-working folk of this country; he is not interested in listening to the various organisations that exist within the sector; that he knows best.
civility.explanation: Moves from the procedural decision to the Minister's disposition — imputing indifference to the public and arrogance ("he knows best"). That is a characterisation of the person rather than of the policy, short of direct abuse.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I also think that many would think about whether or not it is appropriate for that to be the case; perhaps there are some members who have a conflict of interest in relation to this within the Government.
civility.explanation: Insinuates a conflict of interest — i.e. bad faith — against unnamed Government members. Hedged with "perhaps" rather than a direct insult, but it is an imputation of improper motive rather than an argument about the scheme.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: All silent waiting for the smoko break, probably.
civility.explanation: Mockery of members opposite — attributing their silence to wanting a break rather than engaging any point they made. Not a direct insult, but sneering rather than civil.
civility.subject: speaker

focus.statement: But the other is that this bill has not had the normal process of going through a select committee, and the Minister of Transport should hang his head in shame that members of the community, the hard-working folk around this country, organisations and other groups within and outside of the sector, have not had an opportunity to submit on this particular bill.
focus.explanation: Names a specific measure (this bill) and a specific procedural outcome (no select committee, no public submissions). This is scrutiny of a named process failing, not party-bashing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Well, I tell you this: it’s one thing to say that we went to an election and they told us this; well, there are many things that this Government went to the election on and they have failed to deliver, because they are a Government that has not been able to deliver.
focus.explanation: No policy, figure or named commitment appears — the content is a general characterisation of the other side as unable to deliver. This is party framing rather than accountability for any identified promise.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: It’s also interesting that this clearly is a Government that is very prepared to simply pull up the ladder from under them after households, like the Prime Minister’s household, have benefited from this very scheme that has been put in place.
veracity.explanation: Asserts as fact that the Prime Minister's own household received a benefit under the Clean Car Discount scheme that the bill would remove.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Records of Clean Car Discount rebate payments and contemporaneous reporting/ministerial statements on whether Christopher Luxon's household purchased an electric or low-emission vehicle that received a Clean Car Discount rebate before December 2023. True if such a rebated purchase by his household is documented; false if no rebate was claimed by his household.

divination.statement: They also, in terms of a further document that they sent through, which relates to some work by Concept Consulting, indicate that if policies and initiatives such as this are actually removed, then there is absolutely an expectation that the EV percentage of the sales mix to fall to similar levels to actually prior to the incentive coming in, prior to this scheme coming into place.
divination.explanation: Relays a forecast, attributed to Concept Consulting, that removing the incentive will return the electric-vehicle share of the new-sales mix to roughly its level before the scheme began.
divination.subject: other
divination.falsification_criterion: NZTA/Ministry of Transport new light-vehicle registration statistics for EV (BEV) share of new vehicle sales. True if, after the Clean Car Discount is removed at the end of 2023, the EV share of new sales falls back to approximately its pre-July-2021 level (low single-digit percent); false if it remains materially above that pre-incentive level.

rigor.statement: That means that the closer they are to a lower emissions future for them, their household, and their family is just one step further away as a result of this Government wanting to take limited to no action on climate change.
rigor.explanation: Generalises from a single constituent's account of having to save longer to the sweeping conclusion that the Government is taking "limited to no action on climate change". The anecdote supports at most that one household is delayed; the conclusion about the Government's whole climate programme does not follow from it — an appeal to anecdote with a large inferential gap.
rigor.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We have to tackle the climate crisis together, and that requires us to look at the system.
specificity.explanation: A framing statement about approach with no mechanism, figure, timeframe or named measure — 'look at the system' commits to nothing checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: But the new vehicles coming into New Zealand emitted 186 grams per kilometre on average before this policy, and within two years the average was down to 121 grams per kilometre.
specificity.explanation: Two precise figures, a named metric (grams per kilometre for new vehicle entries) and a stated period — anyone can go to the registration statistics and check it.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: But no matter what, despite the repeal today, we’ve saved 2 megatonnes of carbon, we’ve saved 70 million litres of petrol a year, there is $100 million a year that New Zealand is spending less on imported oil, and it would have been more if they’d carried on the policy.
veracity.explanation: Asserts three quantified outcomes attributed to the Clean Car Discount: 2 Mt CO2 abated, 70 million litres of petrol saved per year, and $100 million a year less spent on imported oil.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Transport / Waka Kotahi Clean Car Discount evaluation and monitoring reports up to Dec 2023, and the Climate Change Commission's assessment of the scheme; true if the published lifetime abatement estimate is around 2 Mt CO2-e and the fuel/import savings estimates are of the stated order, false if the official estimates are materially lower or if the figures are lifetime totals presented here as annual.

veracity.statement: But the new vehicles coming into New Zealand emitted 186 grams per kilometre on average before this policy, and within two years the average was down to 121 grams per kilometre.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the average CO2 emissions of newly registered light vehicles in New Zealand fell from 186 g/km before the Clean Car Discount to 121 g/km within two years.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Transport / Waka Kotahi light-vehicle fleet statistics on average CO2 g/km of new light vehicle registrations for 2020/21 and 2023; true if the series shows roughly 186 g/km pre-scheme and roughly 121 g/km by 2023, false if either figure is materially different or the comparison mixes new and used-import categories.

veracity.statement: We’re one of only three countries in the OECD to not have fuel economy standards—along with Australia and Russia—and we had no price incentive at the point of purchase.
veracity.explanation: Asserts New Zealand was one of only three OECD countries without fuel economy standards, naming Australia and Russia as the other two.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: OECD membership list and the IEA/ICCT survey of national light-duty fuel economy or CO2 standards as at 2021-2023; true if exactly three OECD members lacked such standards and those three were New Zealand, Australia and Russia, false if Russia is not an OECD member or if other OECD countries also lacked standards.

veracity.statement: It has already affected our rural areas: billions of dollars in damage because of storms that are directly caused by human-caused climate change, and those are going to keep flowing in.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that storms have already caused billions of dollars of damage to New Zealand rural areas and that those storms are directly caused by human-caused climate change.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Insurance Council of NZ payout totals and Treasury/government damage estimates for the 2023 Auckland floods and Cyclone Gabrielle for the damage figure, plus published event-attribution studies for those events; true if rural/regional damage runs to billions and attribution studies link the events to anthropogenic warming, false if the damage totals are well under a billion or attribution finds no anthropogenic signal. Note the criterion tests 'directly caused' against what attribution science actually claims (increased likelihood/intensity).

rigor.statement: The day after the Clean Car Discount was announced, they said, “We can have it within four weeks.” So this policy, the Clean Car Discount, changed the market of vehicles that were available to New Zealanders.
rigor.explanation: Argument from a single anecdote: one pair of friends' improved delivery date for an Ioniq is generalised to a market-wide change in vehicle supply. The conclusion may well be true on other evidence, but nothing offered here supports it beyond the anecdote.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: If the new National-ACT Government actually has any way of achieving the carbon budgets that they’ve signed up to, they are now going to have to rely on increasing the price of fuel.
rigor.explanation: A false dichotomy: it treats raising the fuel/carbon price as the only remaining lever once the Clean Car Discount is repealed, when other abatement options (fuel economy standards, which remained in force, plus non-transport abatement across the budget) are available. The inference from 'discount repealed' to 'must raise fuel prices' has a real gap in it.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: So I know maths is hard for the National Party—that is obvious—but the maths says that you are going to make it easier for farmers and easier for those tradies who need to drive utes to do their job and not be affected by the high price of fuel if you have a policy like the Clean Car Discount, which results in more zero- and low-emissions vehicles being brought into the country.
focus.explanation: There is a genuine policy point here — a named measure and its claimed effect on fuel costs for farmers and tradies — but it is wrapped in a jibe about the other party's competence, so the weight is split between the substance and the party framing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: That is the reality of this National - ACT - New Zealand First dinosaur Government taking us back into the dark ages with their culture wars.
focus.explanation: Names no policy, figure or outcome — purely a characterisation of the three governing parties as backward and culture-warring. No individual is insulted, so Civility is untouched; this is exactly the party-directed content Focus catches.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: I would like to invite that member, Julie Anne Genter, to nominate what kind of dinosaur she thinks I am.
focus.explanation: A rejoinder entirely about the exchange with another member during a debate on a repeal bill; it engages no part of the measure before the House.
focus.subject: speaker

divination.statement: They’re going to slow down progress, and that means it’s going to be more expensive later, it’s going to be harder for New Zealanders to access second-hand electric vehicles, because without the price incentive, we’re going to import fewer electric vehicles, which means there’s less vehicles in the second-hand fleet for New Zealanders to access.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that repealing the Clean Car Discount will reduce EV imports and so shrink the pool of second-hand electric vehicles available to New Zealanders.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Waka Kotahi / Ministry of Transport vehicle registration statistics for new and used-import battery and plug-in electric light vehicles; true if annual EV registrations in 2024 and 2025 fall materially below the 2023 level, false if EV registrations hold steady or grow after the scheme ends.

civility.statement: Simon Court very accurately says he can’t understand, and I can see members opposite are having a difficult time following me because it is a little bit complex.
civility.explanation: Turns a named member's interjection into a remark about the comprehension of the members opposite. It stops short of a direct insult, but it is condescension aimed at people rather than at the argument.
civility.subject: speaker

focus.statement: But what we do know is that this is yet another piece of legislation that this Government is putting up which is about dragging New Zealand backwards.
focus.explanation: Refers to the bill only as a generic instance of what 'this Government' does; no mechanism, figure, target or named outcome is engaged. Party framing carries the whole sentence.
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The ERP sets out the target to reduce transport emissions by 41 percent from 2019 levels by 2035.
specificity.explanation: A named document, a numeric target, a baseline year and an end date — fully checkable and actionable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I say to hard-working farmers, tradies, and all-round good New Zealanders who need their utes for everyday life that common sense has returned to the Government benches and help is on its way.
specificity.explanation: Names a group of beneficiaries but nothing checkable: no figure, no mechanism, no date. 'Common sense has returned' and 'help is on its way' commit to nothing that could be verified or acted on.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: The ERP sets out the target to reduce transport emissions by 41 percent from 2019 levels by 2035.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Emissions Reduction Plan contains a target of a 41 percent cut in transport emissions against a 2019 baseline by 2035.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The transport chapter of New Zealand's first Emissions Reduction Plan (2022): true if it states a 41% reduction in transport emissions from 2019 levels by 2035; false if the figure, baseline year or target year materially differ.

veracity.statement: We have our independent Climate Change Commission, and the report released just this week tells us that there needs to be supplementary measures to the ETS in order to drive the behavioural change.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Climate Change Commission's advice published in the week of 12 December 2023 concludes that measures complementary to the emissions trading scheme are required to shift behaviour.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Climate Change Commission's December 2023 advice on the second emissions budget: true if it states that complementary/supplementary policies beyond the ETS are needed to drive behaviour change (including in transport), false if it concludes the ETS alone is sufficient or makes no such finding.

veracity.statement: They haven’t said they can just get on with the roll-out of the 10,000 public electric vehicle (EV) chargers by 2030 that the National Party promised in their manifesto commitment.
veracity.explanation: Two joined factual assertions: that National's 2023 manifesto promised 10,000 public EV chargers by 2030, and that the National–ACT coalition agreement conditions that roll-out on a business case rather than endorsing it outright.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: National's 2023 election manifesto and the National–ACT coalition agreement: true if the manifesto commits to 10,000 public EV chargers by 2030 and the coalition agreement makes the roll-out subject to a business case; false if either the number/date differs or the coalition agreement adopts the commitment unqualified.

veracity.statement: Look around the world—to those on the Government benches—and you will see conservative Governments around the world have implemented similar schemes.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that conservative-led governments in other countries have implemented EV purchase incentive or feebate schemes comparable to the Clean Car Discount.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Records of EV purchase-incentive/feebate schemes and the political complexion of the government that introduced them (e.g. the UK plug-in car grant under the Conservatives, France's bonus-malus under centre-right administrations): true if at least one conservative-led government introduced or maintained a comparable scheme, false if no such scheme is attributable to a conservative-led government.

civility.statement: So I’m sure he’s got the details, because a Minister that is that confident must be all over every detail of the policy, and we’ll see that when it comes to committee stage.
civility.explanation: Sarcasm aimed at the Minister personally — the ostensible compliment is mockery of his command of his portfolio. Short of a direct insult, but it has left the substance and landed on the man.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Then we have heard the crocodile tears of the Government benches over the equity considerations of this policy.
civility.explanation: 'Crocodile tears' imputes bad faith: it says opponents' stated concern for equity is feigned rather than mistaken. That is the 0.5 failure — no individual is named or insulted, so it goes no lower.
civility.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Unfortunately for the members on the Government benches, their claims to finally be standing up for working New Zealanders, despite cutting employment as a Reserve Bank consideration and removing fair pay agreements yesterday, fall on deaf ears when you look at the evidence, when you see how the discount has been applied, who’s been benefiting from it, and who has been paying it.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion is supported by the rebate/charge breakdown just read out (used-import buyers received more rebates and paid fewer charges than new-vehicle buyers), which does bear on who benefits. It is weakened by the parenthetical appeal to two unrelated policies, which is guilt by association rather than evidence about this scheme's distributional effect.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Now, what we’ve heard from the Opposition—that previous group of political parties that passed the ute tax bill—is that this bill will lead to some kind of climate catastrophe, that our emissions will go through the roof, and that only with this policy would New Zealand’s transport emissions be reduced.
rigor.explanation: Strawman: the opposition's case was that the scheme was one effective lever, not that it was the only way transport emissions could fall. The rebuttal that follows is aimed at a position nobody advanced.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: There’s a much simpler solution: the emissions trading scheme. Every single vehicle that fills up with petrol or diesel in New Zealand pays for their emissions under the emissions trading scheme—somewhere between $9 or $10, maybe $12, for a 50-litre tank of petrol or diesel. That is an incentive to reduce fuel and move to a more efficient vehicle.
rigor.explanation: A genuine inference — if fuel already carries a carbon price, a separate purchase subsidy is redundant. The gap is that it asserts sufficiency without addressing whether a $10-per-tank signal changes vehicle purchasing at all, which is the contested premise.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: In the car park, I did not see Teslas; I saw utes. We did talk to tradies. The president of the club is a painter and decorator. Those are the people that you are punishing.
rigor.explanation: Argument from a single anecdote: one club car park is offered as evidence about who the scheme's fees fall on nationally. A vehicle-registration or fee-incidence dataset would settle it; a visit does not.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: When I had a look at this, what I saw was that—in terms of efficiency and performance—when we have the combination of the Clean Car Discount and the Clean Car Standard and applied them at the level of the supply into the country, because we gave the market the very clear dual signalling, we saw the vehicle importers encouraged to bring a greater choice of electric vehicles into the New Zealand market. We saw them coming in faster, just as the Hon Julie Anne Genter referred to earlier.
rigor.explanation: A causal argument with a stated mechanism — dual demand-and-supply signalling changed importer behaviour — and an observed outcome. The weakness is post hoc: the increase in EV supply is attributed to the two schemes without ruling out global supply and price trends over the same period.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: The clean car rebates and fee scheme was designed to be reviewed and adjusted regularly, so that the fees could generate enough revenue to cover such costs. What I’ve also observed is that there was actually an implementation delay in the period between when rebates were granted and when the fees were applied. That’s an implementation issue. The scheme is not broke.
rigor.explanation: A properly-formed rebuttal: it accepts the deficit figure and explains it by a timing lag between rebates starting and fees starting, concluding the design is not at fault. The conclusion follows, though it does not show the lag accounts for the whole shortfall.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Members on that side of the House: truly, we know this will not do anything or send any signals to the market. What it will do, though, is impose further costs on to the oil suppliers who will pass that on to the average people.
rigor.explanation: Bare assertion. 'We know this will not do anything' is offered with no supporting premise, and it sits awkwardly against the second sentence, which concedes the ETS does raise fuel costs — i.e. does send a price signal. The two claims undercut each other.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: It’s a day we can finally go into the local dealer and purchase a ute that we need so we can help drive New Zealand’s productivity and, therefore, get on with life without the restrictions of the previous legislation.
rigor.explanation: The 'therefore' does not carry the weight put on it: a fee on high-emitting vehicles is treated as having prevented ute purchase altogether, and the productivity link is asserted rather than shown. Utes remained purchasable under the scheme at a higher price.
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: The previous speaker, Julie Anne Genter, could not explain why this policy was necessary; she gave an overly complicated description of why it was necessary and how it would work.
civility.explanation: Pointed and edging toward the person — it characterises a named member as unable to explain her own policy rather than engaging what she said — but stops short of an attack on her character or competence generally.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Frankly, if the Government is truly concerned about the workers in this country, then maybe, just maybe, you might want to consider actually implementing higher corporate taxes, or introducing a capital gains tax.
civility.explanation: 'Truly concerned' and the drawn-out 'maybe, just maybe' impute insincerity rather than engaging the argument — a sneer at motive. Short of a personal attack, but past the standard.
civility.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: There’s a much simpler solution: the emissions trading scheme. Every single vehicle that fills up with petrol or diesel in New Zealand pays for their emissions under the emissions trading scheme—somewhere between $9 or $10, maybe $12, for a 50-litre tank of petrol or diesel. That is an incentive to reduce fuel and move to a more efficient vehicle.
specificity.explanation: Names the mechanism (ETS fuel obligation), gives a per-tank cost range and the unit it applies to. Checkable and actionable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We’re doing other things, too, in the macro. Low-methane genetics and blue carbon have the ability to solve a lot of our problems. We’re doing this sensibly, not with nanny State micro-managing solutions that disadvantage some members of our public over others.
specificity.explanation: Two technologies are named but nothing else: no programme, funding, timeframe, or expected abatement. 'Solve a lot of our problems' and 'doing this sensibly' commit to nothing checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The largest fee here in New Zealand is $6,900 on the most polluting vehicles in New Zealand, which, let us be clear, only the rich fullas can really understand at a retail of around $50-60,000.
specificity.explanation: A named maximum fee, the vehicle band it applies to, and an indicative retail price range. Precise enough to look up in the fee schedule.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Well, I’ll just point a couple of things out that a few people on the other side of the House might not be aware of, one of which is that Fonterra recently announced that we’re going to have a 30 percent reduction in our carbon intensity on-farm emissions by 2030.
specificity.explanation: A named organisation, a percentage, the metric (on-farm emissions intensity) and a target date.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: There’s a much simpler solution: the emissions trading scheme. Every single vehicle that fills up with petrol or diesel in New Zealand pays for their emissions under the emissions trading scheme—somewhere between $9 or $10, maybe $12, for a 50-litre tank of petrol or diesel. That is an incentive to reduce fuel and move to a more efficient vehicle.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the ETS cost embedded in a 50-litre tank of fuel in New Zealand at the time was about $9–12.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The NZU price prevailing in late 2023 multiplied by the petrol/diesel emissions factor (~2.3 kg CO2 per litre) for a 50-litre tank; true if the embedded ETS cost was roughly $9–12, false if materially outside that range.

veracity.statement: The trade-offs? A $300 million deficit, now, between the revenue collected under the scheme and what was paid out to people to subsidise them to buy electric vehicles.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a roughly $300 million gap between fees collected and rebates paid out under the Clean Car Discount at the time of the repeal.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Transport / Treasury reporting on Clean Car Discount fees collected versus rebates paid as at December 2023; true if the shortfall was approximately $300 million, false if materially different.

veracity.statement: The last point that he made, and that’s been introduced to me since the first reading, is the $302 million fiscal hole that this scheme was running into. This is a time when we’ve got a $3.4 billion Budget deficit and a huge infrastructure crisis, but yet the Labour Government chose to subsidise Teslas—absolutely unbelievable.
veracity.explanation: Two present-tense fiscal assertions: a $302 million shortfall in the Clean Car Discount, and a $3.4 billion Budget deficit at that time.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Two figures: (a) Ministry of Transport accounts for the Clean Car Discount — true if the shortfall was ≈$302 million; (b) Treasury's December 2023 HYEFU / Financial Statements of the Government — true if the operating (OBEGAL) deficit cited was ≈$3.4 billion. False if either figure is materially different from the official reported number.

veracity.statement: We have committed to putting some certainty around the emissions trading scheme, which the Labour Government tinkered with to the point of absolutely trashing it—against James Shaw’s recommendations.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the previous Government's changes to the ETS were made against the recommendations of its own Climate Change Minister, James Shaw.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Cabinet's decision on ETS unit price control settings (December 2022) set against the Climate Change Commission's advice and the position taken by the then Climate Change Minister; true if the Government adopted settings contrary to Shaw's recommendation, false if it adopted the settings he recommended.

veracity.statement: Fiscal neutrality was designed over a 10-year period, and here we are, not even 18 months before they are withdrawing early.
veracity.explanation: Two linked assertions about the scheme's design: that fiscal neutrality was planned across a ten-year horizon, and that fewer than 18 months of it had elapsed at repeal.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Cabinet paper and regulatory impact statement for the Clean Vehicle Discount; true if the scheme's self-funding was specified over an approximately 10-year horizon, false if fiscal neutrality was set over a shorter period or not specified. The '18 months' element checks against the scheme's fee commencement date (fees applied from 1 April 2022) and the December 2023 repeal.

veracity.statement: The largest fee here in New Zealand is $6,900 on the most polluting vehicles in New Zealand, which, let us be clear, only the rich fullas can really understand at a retail of around $50-60,000.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the highest fee charged under the scheme was $6,900, applying to the most polluting vehicles.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Clean Car Discount fee schedule in force in 2023 (Waka Kotahi); true if the maximum fee for the highest-emitting new vehicles was $6,900 including GST, false if the top fee was a materially different amount.

veracity.statement: So for me, that’s a win for the people in exercising their personal responsibility, and with two megatonnes of carbon dioxide saving, it’s a win for the planet as well.
veracity.explanation: Attributes roughly two megatonnes of carbon dioxide abatement to the Clean Car Discount scheme.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Transport / Climate Change Commission estimates of lifetime CO2 abatement attributed to the Clean Car Discount; true if the central estimate is approximately 2 megatonnes, false if the published estimate is materially lower or higher.

veracity.statement: Well, I’ll just point a couple of things out that a few people on the other side of the House might not be aware of, one of which is that Fonterra recently announced that we’re going to have a 30 percent reduction in our carbon intensity on-farm emissions by 2030.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Fonterra had recently announced a 30 percent on-farm carbon intensity reduction target for 2030.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Fonterra's public climate announcements and annual/climate reporting around late 2023; true if Fonterra announced a target of a ~30% reduction in on-farm emissions intensity by 2030 (against its stated baseline), false if no such target was announced or the figure/date differ materially.

focus.statement: In the car park, I did not see Teslas; I saw utes. We did talk to tradies. The president of the club is a painter and decorator. Those are the people that you are punishing.
focus.explanation: Squarely about the policy's incidence — who pays the fee and who is affected. Badly evidenced, but on the measure rather than about the other party.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: I cannot believe how out of touch the Labour Party is with their core working-class base.
focus.explanation: Entirely about the other party's character and its relationship with its voters. No policy, figure, mechanism or outcome is named; strip the party framing and nothing remains.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: The clean car rebates and fee scheme was designed to be reviewed and adjusted regularly, so that the fees could generate enough revenue to cover such costs. What I’ve also observed is that there was actually an implementation delay in the period between when rebates were granted and when the fees were applied. That’s an implementation issue. The scheme is not broke.
focus.explanation: Engages the specific mechanism of the scheme under repeal — its review clause, its fee-revenue balance and the sequencing of rebates and fees. Scrutiny of the stated reason for the repeal, with no party content.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: We know, in fact, that the departments involved in this legislation had already prepared a draft regulatory impact statement (RIS), yet we have not seen it, despite its existence.
veracity.explanation: Asserts as fact that a draft regulatory impact statement for this repeal bill was prepared by the responsible departments and has not been released to the House.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Transport / Treasury records and any OIA release relating to the Clean Car Discount repeal: true if a draft RIS was prepared before introduction and was not published or provided to the House at introduction; false if no draft RIS existed or one was released with the bill.

veracity.statement: In fact, when submissions were open over Christmas, there was much debate from the Opposition about how it was so unfair to have a six-week submission process that was over the Christmas break.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that during the previous Parliament's resource management reform, then-opposition members publicly objected to a six-week submission period falling over the Christmas break.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Hansard and Environment Committee records for the Natural and Built Environment Bill (introduced Nov 2022): true if the initial submission window was approximately six weeks spanning the Christmas period and opposition members are recorded objecting to it, false if the window or the objections are not on the record.

veracity.statement: And we know that because of this scheme, we have many more EVs on the road than we would have had without this scheme.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a causal claim: the Clean Car Discount materially increased the number of electric vehicles registered in New Zealand relative to the counterfactual without it.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZTA motor vehicle registration statistics for EV/PHEV registrations before and after 1 July 2021, together with Ministry of Transport evaluations of the Clean Car Discount: true if EV registrations rose substantially over the scheme period and official evaluation attributes a material share of that rise to the rebate, false if uptake tracked the pre-scheme trend or evaluations attribute the rise to other causes.

veracity.statement: The farmers that need to drive up the western faces of the Tararua Ranges, they don’t have an electric option and they don’t need another ute tax, and neither do the growers that are providing 30 percent of our leafy greens for New Zealand.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a specific production share: growers in the Horowhenua/Kāpiti area supply 30 percent of New Zealand's leafy greens.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Horticulture New Zealand / Stats NZ vegetable production data and Horowhenua District Council economic profiles on the region's share of national leafy-green or fresh-vegetable output: true if the region's share is about 30 percent, false if materially lower or if the figure applies to a different crop category.

rigor.statement: Of course, the Opposition can OIA it, but the point is, and the point of why that comment is cynical, is that we are doing, in urgency, all stages of the bill.
rigor.explanation: A sound inference: if all stages are taken under urgency, a document obtainable only later by OIA cannot inform the debate, so the OIA answer does not meet the objection. Premise and conclusion connect directly.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Electric vehicles are a great thing for New Zealand, they’re a great thing for our environment, and I’m proud to drive one, but I didn’t claim a discount on it. We don’t need that. There are plenty of incentives to make this shift.
rigor.explanation: Generalises from a single anecdote — his own purchase without a rebate — to the conclusion that no buyer needs the subsidy. The supporting premise, that 'plenty of incentives' already exist, is asserted without naming any, so the conclusion rests on personal anecdote.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: This is very specific to our carbon emissions, and you will see all through the Act and the repeal legislation that we are talking about the pollution, the pollution of the carbon dioxide from some cars, and how we cost that pollution to incentivise behaviour so that people have low-emitting vehicles.
