veracity.statement: I recently received the OECD Economic Survey of New Zealand 2024, which confirmed student achievement is declining, equity is not improving, and outcomes are too variable.
veracity.explanation: A relayed characterisation of what a specific, named OECD report found about New Zealand school achievement, equity and variability.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The education chapter of the OECD Economic Survey of New Zealand 2024: true if it finds declining student achievement, no improvement in equity and excessive variability in outcomes; false if its findings differ materially on any of those three points.

veracity.statement: The latest update I have received from the Education Review Office states that before the Government introduced this policy, one in five schools were not teaching an hour a day of reading, writing, and maths. By April this year, nearly 99 percent of schools that are required to teach an hour a day have now introduced a policy to do so. Additionally, ERO found that 92 percent of schools meet the requirement of the away all day cellphone policy.
veracity.explanation: Three specific statistics attributed to ERO about implementation of the hour-a-day and cellphone policies.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Education Review Office's 2024 monitoring reports on the one hour a day and phone-ban policies: true if ERO reported roughly 20 percent of schools not teaching an hour a day beforehand, near 99 percent having introduced a policy by April 2024, and 92 percent compliance with the cellphone policy; false if ERO's published figures differ materially.

veracity.statement: I demonstrated our commitment to supporting quality implementation with a commitment of $67 million from Budget 2024 for professional development and resources for teachers to ensure that every child learns to read using structured literacy approaches.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a specific Budget 2024 funding allocation of $67 million for structured literacy professional development and resources.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2024 education vote documents and the associated Government announcement: true if $67 million is allocated for structured literacy professional development and teaching resources; false if no such allocation exists or the figure differs materially.

focus.statement: If the Minister supports equal voting rights, will he commit to equal voting rights for busy working New Zealanders who get to vote only by enrolling on voting day?
focus.explanation: Squarely on a named policy question — election-day enrolment and who it affects — rather than on the other party's character or record.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: For most of the electoral democratic history of this country, people have had to enrol the day before election day—including in the 2017 election, which I think I recall was a reasonably important one for the Labour Party.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that historically, and specifically at the 2017 general election, enrolment had to be completed the day before election day (i.e. election-day enrolment was not available in 2017).
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ electoral law and Electoral Commission records: true if enrolment on election day was not permitted at the 2017 general election (i.e. same-day enrolment was introduced by later amendment, from 2020), false if voters could enrol and vote on election day in 2017.

veracity.statement: Does the Minister accept that racism and oppression are contributors to the fact that Māori women in pre-term labour are less likely to receive the full and necessary amount of antenatal steroids?
veracity.explanation: Embedded factual premise: that Māori women in pre-term labour receive a full course of antenatal corticosteroids at lower rates than non-Māori women in New Zealand.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Perinatal and Maternal Mortality Review Committee / Health Quality & Safety Commission data on antenatal corticosteroid administration for pre-term birth by ethnicity; true if Māori rates are materially lower than non-Māori, false if rates are equivalent or higher.

veracity.statement: That plan includes financing to deliver 810 new beds at Waikeria, taking its total capacity to over 1,860.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the announced Corrections investment funds 810 new beds at Waikeria Prison and lifts that prison's total capacity above 1,860.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2024 / Department of Corrections announcement documents for the $1.9 billion package; true if they specify 810 additional beds at Waikeria and a resulting total capacity above 1,860, false if the bed numbers materially differ.

veracity.statement: Well, this morning, I saw the comments from the Leader of the Opposition that children can “take comfort from the fact that if things go wrong for them, there’s an 810-bed prison waiting for them and they can get a free hot healthy lunch when they go to prison”. Not only is this deeply reductive, I find it highly offensive to consign our children to prison in this way, especially given that this Government has had to top the school lunches programme up after the previous Government left a fiscal cliff.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the current Government had to add funding to the school lunches programme because the previous Government's funding ran out (a 'fiscal cliff').
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Vote Education / Budget documents for the Ka Ora, Ka Ako healthy school lunches programme; true if prior funding was time-limited and expiring and the incoming Government appropriated additional money to continue it, false if funding was already baselined and no top-up was required.

veracity.statement: The Ministry of Justice estimates that 23 percent—nearly a quarter of New Zealanders—will experience sexual assault in their lifetime, with 26 percent of women and 11 percent of men experiencing this before the age of 15.
veracity.explanation: Attributes three specific prevalence figures to the Ministry of Justice: 23% lifetime sexual assault prevalence, and 26% of women / 11% of men experiencing it before age 15.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Justice NZ Crime and Victims Survey publications; true if the cited lifetime and pre-15 prevalence figures match those reported (within rounding), false if the published figures differ materially or the second pair does not refer to before age 15.

civility.statement: If he’s suggesting that somehow there was a democratic deficit in the 2017 election because people weren’t able to enrol on election day, I think he’s rather confused.
civility.explanation: Answers the substance but closes by characterising the questioner personally as 'rather confused' — condescension aimed at the member rather than his argument.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Well, this morning, I saw the comments from the Leader of the Opposition that children can “take comfort from the fact that if things go wrong for them, there’s an 810-bed prison waiting for them and they can get a free hot healthy lunch when they go to prison”. Not only is this deeply reductive, I find it highly offensive to consign our children to prison in this way, especially given that this Government has had to top the school lunches programme up after the previous Government left a fiscal cliff.
civility.explanation: Quotes the remark accurately and attacks it as 'deeply reductive' and 'highly offensive', but the charge of consigning children to prison edges from the remark onto the character of the person who made it.
civility.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: If he’s suggesting that somehow there was a democratic deficit in the 2017 election because people weren’t able to enrol on election day, I think he’s rather confused.
rigor.explanation: Rebuts a position the questioner did not take (that the 2017 election was democratically deficient) — a strawman — and leans on past practice as sufficient justification, an appeal to tradition.

veracity.statement: The children’s monitor must operate at arm’s length from the Government, and being based within the Education Review Office means it is not fully independent. rigor.statement: We believe children deserve a fierce, independent champion. In 2022, the Children’s Commissioner was disestablished and replaced by a five-person board. For years, the single, independent commissioner was effective, and we are restoring the single commissioner to be a strong advocate for children.

rigor.statement: The children’s monitor must operate at arm’s length from the Government, and being based within the Education Review Office means it is not fully independent. veracity.explanation: Asserts that a specific 26 percent water rate/charge increase for Auckland was proposed and has now been avoided under the Local Water Done Well arrangement.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Watercare/Auckland Council long-term plan and 2024 annual plan documents on proposed water charge increases; true if a ~26% increase was the signalled path and the adopted plan replaced it with a materially lower increase, false if no such increase was ever proposed or if the adopted increase remains around 26%.

veracity.statement: Aucklanders are rejoicing that as of 1 July there will be no Auckland regional fuel tax, a saving of 11.5c per litre for Auckland motorists.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the Auckland regional fuel tax ends by 1 July 2024 and that its rate is 11.5 cents per litre.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Land Transport Management (Regional Fuel Tax) legislation/repeal and NZTA published rate for the Auckland regional fuel tax; true if the tax ceased on or by 1 July 2024 and the rate was 11.5c/litre, false if the end date or rate differs materially.

veracity.statement: What’s more, only half of what’s collected since 2018 has been spent, with most spent on speed bumps, red-light cameras, and cycleways.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that roughly half of Auckland regional fuel tax revenue collected since 2018 remains unspent, and that the majority of what was spent went on speed bumps, red-light cameras and cycleways.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Auckland Transport / Auckland Council regional fuel tax revenue and expenditure reporting to 2024; true if unspent revenue is around 50% and the largest expenditure categories are traffic-calming, safety cameras and cycling, false if spending is materially higher or dominated by other categories such as road corridor and public transport projects.

veracity.statement: Despite them wasting $228 million on consultants after years of trying, the only thing Labour delivered on was a string of media releases.
veracity.explanation: Asserts $228 million was spent on consultants for the Auckland light rail project under the previous government.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Auckland Light Rail Ltd / Ministry of Transport published project expenditure figures; true if consultant and advisory spending totalled about $228 million, false if the figure is materially different or includes non-consultant costs.

veracity.statement: So the cost all up of $29 billion was averted with that light rail fail and they spent, of course, $30 million on the Kiwi Bacon building that was now not needed.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the total projected cost of Auckland light rail was $29 billion and that $30 million was spent acquiring the 'Kiwi Bacon' building for the project.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Auckland Light Rail Ltd indicative business case cost estimates and the property purchase record/price for the Kiwi Bacon building on Great North Road; true if the whole-of-project estimate was around $29b and the purchase price around $30m, false if either figure is materially different.

veracity.statement: Aucklanders are rejoicing that Labour’s $785 million cycle bridge across Auckland Harbour bridge is not getting off the ground. It was chucked in, but, of course, not before $51 million was spent on consultants, designs, and engineer fees.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the cancelled Auckland harbour cycle bridge carried a $785 million cost estimate and that $51 million was spent on consultants, design and engineering before it was abandoned.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Waka Kotahi NZTA published cost estimate for the Northern Pathway/SkyPath harbour crossing and its reported sunk costs; true if the estimate was about $785m and sunk design/consultant costs about $51m, false if materially different.

veracity.statement: Over 40 percent of Aucklanders voted for the National Party in October—over 40 percent.
veracity.explanation: Asserts National won over 40 percent of the party vote in Auckland at the October 2023 general election.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Electoral Commission official 2023 general election results aggregated over Auckland-region electorates; true if National's party vote share exceeds 40%, false if it is below.

veracity.statement: This was legislation where, of the 16,500 submissions, 95 percent opposed what was being introduced.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a submission count of 16,500 on the Therapeutic Products Bill and that 95 percent of those submissions opposed it.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Health Select Committee record and departmental report on the Therapeutic Products Bill, giving the number of submissions received and the committee's/officials' breakdown of support versus opposition; true if the count is about 16,500 and around 95% were opposed, false if either figure is materially different.

veracity.statement: Natural Health Products New Zealand estimates current outdated regulation is costing our country half a billion dollars in foregone export revenue.
veracity.explanation: Relays an industry body's estimate that outdated natural health product regulation costs New Zealand about $500 million in foregone export revenue.
veracity.subject: other
veracity.falsification_criterion: Published Natural Health Products NZ material or submissions; true if that organisation has published a foregone-export-revenue estimate of around half a billion dollars, false if no such estimate exists or the figure attributed differs materially.

veracity.statement: This legislation was not to come into effect until 2026, which gives Government and industry time to implement sound regulation.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the Therapeutic Products Act 2023 was not due to take full effect until 2026.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Commencement provisions of the Therapeutic Products Act 2023; true if the principal provisions were set to commence in 2026, false if they were due to commence earlier.

veracity.statement: First of all, I’d like to tell the Oxford Union that we’ve got the most unpopular Prime Minister in the history of Prime Ministers. No one has polled as low as this Prime Minister in recent weeks after an election.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Christopher Luxon's polling in mid-2024 was the lowest recorded for any New Zealand Prime Minister in the period following an election.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Published preferred-Prime-Minister polling series (1News Verian, Curia/Taxpayers' Union, Roy Morgan) for Luxon in April–May 2024 compared with historical post-election ratings for earlier PMs; true if his rating is the lowest post-election figure on record, false if any prior Prime Minister polled lower in a comparable post-election period.

veracity.statement: I know some of the Opposition may think it’s a little bit treacherous, but they should know all about that, given the Prime Minister, when he was the Leader of the Opposition, slammed the Government when he was over in England.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Christopher Luxon, while Leader of the Opposition, publicly criticised the New Zealand government during a visit to England.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Contemporaneous media reporting of Luxon's overseas trip as Opposition leader; true if he made recorded critical remarks about the then Labour government while in the United Kingdom, false if no such remarks are on record.

divination.statement: Auckland households will not be hit with huge water rate increases any more, and that’s thanks to this Government.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that Auckland households will not face large water charge increases in future under the new arrangement.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Auckland Council/Watercare adopted water charge increases for the 2025/26 and 2026/27 years; true if annual increases stay in single digits or well below the previously signalled path, false if households face increases of a comparable magnitude to those said to have been averted.

divination.statement: It’s been lauded in London, it’s been lauded in France, it’s been lauded everywhere, and this Government took the opportunity to get rid of that smoke-free legislation guaranteeing that thousands—thousands—more people will die.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that repealing the smokefree (denicotinisation and retailer-reduction) provisions will cause thousands of additional deaths.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Peer-reviewed modelling and Ministry of Health/Stats NZ smoking-attributable mortality and smoking prevalence data following the repeal; true if published estimates attribute thousands of additional deaths to the repeal relative to the retained legislation, false if prevalence and smoking-attributable mortality track the pre-repeal projected path.

focus.statement: Great projects that are being progressed by our Government, not by the last Government. They did nothing. In fact, they vindictively cancelled the likes of Mill Road.
focus.explanation: There is a real policy referent (Mill Road being cancelled), but the weight of the passage is a blanket characterisation of the previous government's motives — 'they did nothing', 'vindictively' — rather than engagement with the project's scope, cost or timing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Despite them wasting $228 million on consultants after years of trying, the only thing Labour delivered on was a string of media releases.
focus.explanation: A named project and a specific expenditure figure — legitimate scrutiny — but the conclusion is framed as a general jab at what Labour 'delivered' rather than an account of the project.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: They deserve some respite after this cost of living crisis that Labour have driven up after six long years of recklessness come the economy.
focus.explanation: Gestures at tax relief and the cost of living, but carries no policy content — no threshold, amount or mechanism — and resolves into a general characterisation of six years of the other party.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: What a disgraceful piece of legislation that keeps out communities, that keeps out iwi, that reduces this just to three Ministers.
focus.explanation: Squarely on the fast-track bill's actual mechanism — the removal of community and iwi participation and the vesting of decisions in three Ministers. Harsh, but it engages the measure rather than the other party.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: We went to a disability centre last week and we saw, firsthand—firsthand—the anger from workers there who now will be given no respite, no rest, nothing, because of this nasty, selfish Government.
focus.explanation: There is a genuine policy referent in the disability respite funding changes, but no scheme, figure or decision is named, and the point lands on the character of the Government rather than the change itself.
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Aucklanders are rejoicing that as of 1 July there will be no Auckland regional fuel tax, a saving of 11.5c per litre for Auckland motorists.
specificity.explanation: Names the levy, the cent-per-litre rate and the date it ends — fully checkable and actionable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The reality is that the TPA was not the answer. We were yet again heading down a path of over-regulation, overcomplexity, and over-costings. This is the clear message from the sector who have the knowledge and expertise on what is needed.
specificity.explanation: 'Over-regulation, overcomplexity, and over-costings' is a string of generic faults: no provision of the Act, compliance cost estimate or affected product class is named.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We are repealing the TPA, and will look at two options and interventions that will not only create clarity for the future but look at options for urgent relief to the sector.
specificity.explanation: The repeal itself is a named, concrete action, but the follow-up is left entirely open — 'two options and interventions' are neither described nor dated, and 'urgent relief' has no mechanism attached.
specificity.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Since taking on my role as Associate Health Minister, I have been listening. I have been listening to the consumers, to the industry groups, and to practitioners, and they have demonstrated that there is absolutely no level of comfort or satisfaction with the Therapeutic Products Act (TPA).
rigor.explanation: The absolute conclusion — that there is 'absolutely no level of comfort or satisfaction' anywhere — is drawn from unquantified conversations with self-selected stakeholders. Appeal to anecdote, plus a leap from 'those I spoke to' to a universal claim.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: The reality is that the TPA was not the answer. We were yet again heading down a path of over-regulation, overcomplexity, and over-costings. This is the clear message from the sector who have the knowledge and expertise on what is needed.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion that the Act was wrong rests on an appeal to authority — the sector 'have the knowledge and expertise' — rather than on any regulatory or cost analysis offered here.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: I know some of the Opposition may think it’s a little bit treacherous, but they should know all about that, given the Prime Minister, when he was the Leader of the Opposition, slammed the Government when he was over in England.
rigor.explanation: Tu quoque: the propriety of criticising the government abroad is defended solely on the ground that an opponent did the same, which does nothing to establish that the conduct is appropriate.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: It’s been lauded in London, it’s been lauded in France, it’s been lauded everywhere, and this Government took the opportunity to get rid of that smoke-free legislation guaranteeing that thousands—thousands—more people will die.
rigor.explanation: The case for the legislation rests on an appeal to overseas approval — 'lauded in London', 'lauded in France' — and the mortality conclusion is asserted as 'guaranteed' without any modelling or evidence being offered to connect repeal to the death toll.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: We went to a disability centre last week and we saw, firsthand—firsthand—the anger from workers there who now will be given no respite, no rest, nothing, because of this nasty, selfish Government.
rigor.explanation: A single site visit is offered as the whole basis for a general conclusion about disability support funding — appeal to anecdote — and the causal step to 'no respite, no rest, nothing' is asserted rather than shown.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Rather than just memorising the words, they were learning the basic sounds—and it works.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion that structured literacy 'works' rests entirely on a single classroom visit and the faces of children sounding out words — an appeal to anecdote and personal observation, with no outcome data offered.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: When I was a kid growing up on the farm, Dad would get the digger out and build a pond, store water in the summer, and use it in the winter because this makes total sense.
rigor.explanation: A childhood anecdote about her father's farm pond is offered as the justification for a national water-storage policy; 'this makes total sense' is an appeal to personal experience and common sense rather than an argument about present-day allocation or environmental constraints.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Realistically and logically, gas is an essential fuel at this time.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion is supported by premises he actually laid out — gas peakers start within minutes and cover dry, still, dark periods, and imported coal emits about twice as much — so the inference tracks. It is docked because the alternative he himself raised (grid-scale batteries) is not addressed before declaring gas 'essential'.
rigor.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Our National-led Government is laser-focused on education and lifting performance in our classrooms.
specificity.explanation: A slogan: no figure, mechanism, target or timeframe. 'Laser-focused' and 'lifting performance' commit to nothing checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: There is another alternative to keep our electricity supply secure, and that is grid-scale batteries. These store electricity that is excess supply to our demand, and then poke that electricity back into the grid when we need it.
specificity.explanation: Names a concrete technology and explains the mechanism, but carries no capacity figures, costs, sites or timeframe — a direction with some detail and no how-much or by-when.
specificity.subject: speaker

focus.statement: But on that side of the House, they’ve got bureaucracy far too involved in farming, with clipboards, paperwork, and officials—which has stagnated growth.
focus.explanation: There is a real policy point in here (regulatory compliance burden on farms), but it is framed as a characterisation of 'that side of the House' with no named regulation, rule or figure; the weight of the sentence is party framing rather than the measure.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: I’ve been receiving a lot of concerning feedback to my electorate as our Hawke’s Bay Regional Council moves to halve water allocations across the Heretaunga Plains.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Hawke's Bay Regional Council was, as at May 2024, moving to halve water allocations across the Heretaunga Plains.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Hawke's Bay Regional Council plan-change documents and council papers for the Heretaunga Plains (TANK plan change / groundwater allocation) current in 2024; true if a proposed allocation reduction of approximately 50% is on the record, false if the proposed reduction is materially smaller or no such allocation change was proposed.

veracity.statement: I’m so pleased that Hawke’s Bay’s four-lane expressway is on the roads of national significance and is a priority for our Government.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that a four-lane Hawke's Bay expressway is included on the Government's Roads of National Significance list as at May 2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Government Policy Statement on land transport 2024 / NZTA Roads of National Significance list published in 2024; true if a Hawke's Bay expressway appears on that list, false if it does not.

veracity.statement: This week, I was proud to receive this white camellia brooch as the symbol of women’s suffrage in New Zealand—and officially the 194th female member of our New Zealand Parliament.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Wedd is the 194th woman to become a member of the New Zealand Parliament.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Parliamentary Library / New Zealand Parliament records of women MPs in order of entry; true if Wedd's ordinal position is 194, false if the record gives a different number.

veracity.statement: I recently went to the opening of one of New Zealand’s first hydrogen-fuelling stations at Wiri, in Auckland. This is one of three stations now open and servicing the “golden triangle”—that being between Auckland, Hamilton, and Tauranga.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that as at May 2024 three hydrogen refuelling stations were open in New Zealand, serving the Auckland–Hamilton–Tauranga corridor, one of them at Wiri.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Hiringa Energy / MBIE records of publicly opened hydrogen refuelling stations in New Zealand as at May 2024; true if exactly three were open across Wiri, Hamilton and Tauranga, false if the count or locations differ materially.

veracity.statement: Just to remind everybody, coal is twice as bad emissions-wise than gas.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that coal produces roughly double the emissions of natural gas — on the natural reading, per unit of energy or electricity generated.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MBIE / IPCC emissions factors for coal versus natural gas combustion (kg CO2 per GJ or per MWh generated); true if the coal factor is approximately twice the gas factor, false if the ratio is materially different.

veracity.statement: We are looking at huge amounts of coal being imported from overseas.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that New Zealand was, at the time, importing large quantities of coal.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ overseas merchandise trade / MBIE energy statistics on coal imports for 2023–2024; true if imported coal tonnage was at or near record levels and a substantial share of coal used, false if imports were negligible or falling.

divination.statement: It is predicted that we need to generate twice the amount of renewable electricity we produce today to meet the 2050 demand forecast.
divination.explanation: Relays a forecast that New Zealand's 2050 electricity demand will require roughly double today's renewable generation.
divination.subject: other
divination.falsification_criterion: MBIE / Transpower / Climate Change Commission electricity demand and generation projections; true if actual (or, before 2050, officially projected) 2050 demand requires approximately twice 2024 renewable generation, false if the required increase is materially less or more than double.

civility.statement: I listened carefully to the Minister for Energy’s explanation of why we must continue to burn gas, and we know he loves gas, but what I also heard was a lot of gas and a poverty of imagination, because what is evident now is that this Government is intent on driving us backwards.
civility.explanation: Turns the pun on the Minister himself — 'we know he loves gas', 'a lot of gas' (i.e. hot air) and 'a poverty of imagination' are sneers at the person rather than criticism of the gas policy itself. Short of a direct insult, but no longer civil.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: The Minister talks about the 1990s as though it’s the nirvana of education. Well, I can tell you that there were a high number of young people in the 1990s for whom the curriculum completely failed, absolutely failed.
civility.explanation: Caricatures the Minister's position ('as though it's the nirvana of education') rather than quoting it, which edges toward mockery of the person, but stops short of attacking her character or competence.
civility.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Modelling by Mason and co. shows that a generation mix comprising 49 percent hydro, 23 percent wind, 13 percent geothermal, 14 percent pumped hydro, and 1 percent biomass fuel generation on an installed capacity basis—that’s a capacity market—is capable of ensuring security of supply, even through the dry years.
specificity.explanation: Names a source and gives a fully itemised generation mix with percentages by technology and the claimed outcome (security of supply through dry years). Someone could go and check the modelling.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The second recommendation is to improve the health of the home. So that’s to strengthen healthy homes standards, expand tenancy support, improve housing build standards—so improve the building code.
specificity.explanation: Names concrete levers (healthy homes standards, tenancy support, the building code) drawn from a named expert report, but gives no figures, thresholds or timeframes for any of them.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Modelling by Mason and co. shows that a generation mix comprising 49 percent hydro, 23 percent wind, 13 percent geothermal, 14 percent pumped hydro, and 1 percent biomass fuel generation on an installed capacity basis—that’s a capacity market—is capable of ensuring security of supply, even through the dry years.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that published modelling (attributed to 'Mason and co.') finds a specified renewable generation mix on an installed-capacity basis can maintain security of supply through dry years.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Locate the cited modelling (NZ energy-system modelling by an author named Mason, e.g. work on 100% renewable electricity scenarios); true if it reports a scenario with approximately those shares (49% hydro, 23% wind, 13% geothermal, 14% pumped hydro, 1% biomass by installed capacity) meeting security of supply in dry years; false if no such modelling exists or its mix/conclusion materially differs.

veracity.statement: Take, for example, the Minister of Education talking on The AM Show on Friday, when she let it be known that she was cutting reading recovery—thousands of jobs gone overnight; people heard about it in the media.
veracity.explanation: Two assertions: that the Minister of Education announced cuts to Reading Recovery in an AM Show interview on the Friday before 8 May 2024, and that this ended 'thousands of jobs'.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Broadcast/transcript record of The AM Show for early May 2024 and Ministry of Education advice on Reading Recovery; true if the Minister disclosed the cut in that interview AND the number of affected positions is in the thousands; false if the announcement was not made there, or if the affected Reading Recovery workforce numbered in the hundreds or fewer.

veracity.statement: I’m always really interested in how the other side of the House has so many arguments about that, but go back and read the history of what happened there and you will see that it was us that introduced that programme, and even your own Minister says that.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the previous Labour government introduced the structured literacy programme in the junior years, and that the current Minister of Education has acknowledged this.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Education announcements and Budget documents on structured literacy funding from 2017–2023, plus public statements by Erica Stanford; true if the junior-years structured literacy programme was initiated under the Labour government and the Minister has publicly credited it; false if it originated under the previous National government or the Minister has not said so.

focus.statement: It’s really impossible to marry the Government’s rhetoric on meeting our climate targets and their actions to pursue oil and gas through a fast-track power grab and species extinction.
focus.explanation: Does name concrete measures — climate targets, oil and gas exploration, the fast-track regime — but the weight of the sentence is a characterisation of the Government's motives ('power grab') rather than engagement with the mechanism.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Take, for example, the Minister of Education talking on The AM Show on Friday, when she let it be known that she was cutting reading recovery—thousands of jobs gone overnight; people heard about it in the media.
focus.explanation: Legitimate scrutiny: names a specific programme (reading recovery), a specific decision, and how it was communicated to the sector. This is on-policy accountability, not party-bashing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: I think this whole House knows what didn’t work out last time and, hopefully, we won’t be trying that for another 21 years.
focus.explanation: A jibe at the previous government's record with no policy named — no measure, figure, mechanism or outcome is identified, so there is nothing on-policy left once the swipe at the other side is removed.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: And it’s as if this is some kind of gotcha moment—this big conspiracy that we would introduce this thing that has decades of evidence behind it.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that structured literacy (systematic synthetic phonics) is backed by decades of research evidence.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Peer-reviewed synthesis evidence on systematic phonics instruction (e.g. the US National Reading Panel 2000 report, the UK Rose Review 2006, Cochrane/Campbell meta-analyses): true if multiple decades-spanning reviews find systematic phonics improves early reading outcomes; false if the research base is thin, recent, or does not support the approach.

veracity.statement: No one has died on this expressway.
veracity.explanation: Asserts there have been no fatalities on the Kāpiti Expressway (Mackays to Peka Peka) since it opened.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZTA Crash Analysis System / Waka Kotahi fatal crash records for the Mackays-to-Peka Peka expressway between its February 2017 opening and 8 May 2024: true if zero fatal crashes are recorded on that section, false if one or more fatalities are recorded.

veracity.statement: And I have to acknowledge the work that Steven Joyce and Nathan Guy did to make sure that we had that—opposed by Labour. They didn’t want any expressway.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Labour opposed the Kāpiti Expressway outright when it was proposed and built under the previous National government.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Labour Party statements, Hansard contributions and transport policy documents from the 2009–2017 Roads of National Significance period concerning the Mackays-to-Peka Peka / Kāpiti expressway: true if Labour's recorded position was opposition to building the expressway, false if Labour supported it or opposed only the route, timing or cost.

veracity.statement: But the court was of the view that, because the trust was established and its tenets were contained within legislation, it was for this House.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the High Court declined to vary the McLean Institute trust under the Charitable Trusts Act on the ground that the trust's terms sat in statute, so variation was a matter for Parliament.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The High Court judgment on the McLean Institute's variation application (searchable on the NZ courts judgment database): true if the court declined jurisdiction or directed the applicant to Parliament because the trust terms were contained in legislation, false if it declined on other grounds or granted the variation.

civility.statement: About the only thing that made sense from that last contribution was that she was confused—and she is. She certainly is confused about who brought in structured literacy.
civility.explanation: Dismisses the previous speaker's whole contribution and characterises her personally as confused, rather than engaging the substance of what she said. A personal jibe at another member's grasp of the topic, short of outright abuse.
civility.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Māori achievement is on par with Pākehā. This is what structured literacy does.
rigor.explanation: Generalises a causal claim about a national teaching method from a single school visit and a principal's remark. Post hoc reasoning from anecdote: no comparison, no control for other changes at the school over the four years, and no data offered beyond one conversation.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: You kind of actually can. We do 100 to 50 all the time and it works out fine.
rigor.explanation: An argument by analogy against the objection to a 110-to-80 speed transition. The analogy carries some weight (a larger drop is routinely managed), but nothing is offered on whether expressway-to-open-road transitions behave like urban ones, and 'works out fine' is asserted rather than evidenced.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Māori achievement is on par with Pākehā. This is what structured literacy does.
focus.explanation: Squarely on the structured literacy policy and a named outcome (achievement parity at a specific school), not on the other party. The inference is weak, but that is Rigor's problem, not Focus's.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: And we experimented with other things, we tried the no leadership from the Minister thing—that didn’t work.
focus.explanation: A swipe at the previous government's education leadership in general terms. No policy, programme, figure or outcome is named — the content is party framing about what the other side was like, wrapped around a gesture at literacy policy.
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: But don’t worry, because at each end of the 110 kilometre per hour section between Raumati and Ōtaki, we will have at least 1.6 kilometres of road—nice, safe, National Party - built road—at 100 kilometres per hour, so there won’t be any transition.
specificity.explanation: Names the endpoints of the proposed section, both speed values and a minimum buffer distance. Concrete enough that someone could check the design against it.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We don’t have a system of colonial aristocracy—at least I hope not—and so the new purposes in the legislation simply reframe that purpose of the trust to provide assistance and to promote the welfare and wellbeing of disadvantaged women residing in the region, being Canterbury, who the board considers are in need of care, support, and assistance due to poverty, ill health, or other circumstances, whether temporary or long term.
specificity.explanation: Sets out the actual replacement trust purpose — beneficiary class, geographic limit, the decision-maker and the qualifying circumstances. Checkable directly against the bill's text.
specificity.subject: speaker

divination.statement: Importantly, the other one thing I will mention, because it is really important, is we won’t be seeing the McLean Institute trust before this House again, because this makes it clear that the High Court will have the power to make trust variations, which will be a much more efficient process and quite possibly a lot cheaper.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that no further McLean Institute trust legislation will come before Parliament, because variation power passes to the High Court.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: The Parliament bills register: true if no further McLean Institute private bill or trust-variation bill is introduced by the resolve-by date, false if any such bill appears before the House.

rigor.statement: So one can see very clearly that to go through a process to amend the Act through legislation, like we’re doing, entails considerable cost.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion (legislating is costly) is drawn from the premises he has just laid out — the 1909 Act plus separate amending Acts in 1930 and 1934, and a failed High Court route. The inference tracks the evidence offered, though 'considerable cost' is asserted rather than quantified.
rigor.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The amendment that the bill seeks to make is to take the McLean Institute out of the legislative process, thereby saving on cost and allowing for the McLean Institute board to make decisions administratively with regard to the changing needs of the intended beneficiaries of the trust.
specificity.explanation: Names the actual mechanism of the bill — removal from the legislative amendment route and transfer of decision-making to the board administratively — with the High Court safeguard on trust objectives spelled out in the adjoining sentences.
