veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ Consumers Price Index release for the June 2024 quarter: true if annual CPI is 3.3% and the March quarter was 4.0%, quarterly movement 0.4% after 0.6%, and no annual print since mid-2021 was lower; false if any of those figures differ materially.

veracity.statement: We’re making a significant investment in front-line services with a record $16.7 billion in this year’s Budget, but that’s not enough.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Budget 2024 contained a record $16.7 billion health investment directed at front-line services.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2024 documents (Vote Health summary and Treasury Budget at a Glance): true if a health package of approximately $16.7 billion is identified and is the largest such allocation on record; false if the figure differs materially or is not a record, or if it is a multi-year total rather than 'this year's' investment as stated.

veracity.statement: That’s why we’re very proud to see smoking go from 8.6 percent to 6.8 percent in the last 12 months, and we’re going to continue that march.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the daily smoking rate fell from 8.6 percent to 6.8 percent over a twelve-month period.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Health Survey adult daily smoking prevalence series: true if consecutive annual surveys report 8.6% then 6.8%; false if those figures do not appear in consecutive years or if the movement described did not occur in the period claimed.

veracity.statement: Why does the Government continue to act in such a secretive manner regarding cigarettes and tobacco, particularly after the Minister responsible was ordered by the Ombudsman to apologise for keeping tobacco and vaping policies secret?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Minister responsible for tobacco policy was ordered by the Ombudsman to apologise for withholding tobacco and vaping policy information.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Chief Ombudsman's published opinion/finding concerning the Associate Minister of Health's handling of tobacco and vaping information requests: true if it directed or required an apology for withholding that material; false if no such finding or direction exists.

divination.statement: Well, the market’s expectation and the Reserve Bank’s expectation is that inflation will fall within the 1 to 3 percent target range this calendar year.
divination.explanation: Relays the Reserve Bank's and market's forecast that annual CPI inflation returns inside the 1–3 percent target band during calendar 2024.
divination.subject: other
divination.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ annual CPI prints for quarters within calendar 2024: true if at least one annual CPI reading published for a 2024 quarter falls between 1.0% and 3.0%; false if every 2024 quarterly annual print remains above 3.0%.

divination.statement: When interest rates fall, the economy will start recovering, which means higher incomes and more jobs.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that once interest rates come down the New Zealand economy will return to growth, with rising incomes and rising employment.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ GDP, HLFS employment and average weekly earnings in the 12 months after the RBNZ's first OCR cut: true if GDP returns to sustained quarterly growth and both employment and real incomes rise over that period; false if GDP contracts and employment falls or unemployment rises over the same window.

rigor.statement: The member opposite is interjecting to say that inflation could have come lower quicker—he’s 100 percent correct. If he hadn’t done so much more wasteful spending, we wouldn’t be here now.
rigor.explanation: A bare counterfactual: the conclusion that inflation would already be lower but for the member's spending is asserted with no mechanism, magnitude or evidence linking the two — post hoc causal attribution.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: I think it has been announced, and I think you obviously know about it by asking the question.
rigor.explanation: Non sequitur: that the questioner knows of the decision does not establish that it was publicly announced — the information could have reached him by any other route, which is precisely what was in dispute.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Which is a greater priority for the Government in its decision making around tobacco: advice from the Ministry of Health and health experts that the Government’s approach would increase addiction—particularly amongst young New Zealanders—and increase the risk of certain types of cancer; or the lobbying of the tobacco industry?
rigor.explanation: False dichotomy: it forces the decision into a choice between health advice and tobacco lobbying, excluding any other basis for the policy and presupposing the lobbying influence it purports to ask about.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: The member opposite is interjecting to say that inflation could have come lower quicker—he’s 100 percent correct. If he hadn’t done so much more wasteful spending, we wouldn’t be here now.
focus.explanation: There is a real policy point (fiscal spending and inflation) but it is delivered wholly as a personalised swipe across the House rather than engaging any named spending programme or figure.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Health New Zealand’s overly centralised operating model and poor financial controls have plagued the organisation since its creation by the previous Government. We’re taking decisive action to fix those problems by installing commissioners and giving them a mandate to deliver New Zealanders the healthcare that they deserve.
focus.explanation: Names a specific entity, a specific diagnosis (centralisation, financial controls) and a specific remedy (commissioners), rather than generalised party-bashing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Why does the Government continue to act in such a secretive manner regarding cigarettes and tobacco, particularly after the Minister responsible was ordered by the Ombudsman to apologise for keeping tobacco and vaping policies secret?
focus.explanation: Scrutiny anchored to a specific policy area and a specific, documented finding against a Minister rather than generalised attack on the governing parties.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Did the Ministry of Health advise the Government that heated tobacco products would likely compound existing concerns about youth uptake in addition to nicotine products, and that addiction rates for snus can be higher than for smoked tobacco products, and that snus can increase the risk of certain types of cancer?
focus.explanation: Entirely on the substance of the policy and the official advice behind it; no party framing at all.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Which is a greater priority for the Government in its decision making around tobacco: advice from the Ministry of Health and health experts that the Government’s approach would increase addiction—particularly amongst young New Zealanders—and increase the risk of certain types of cancer; or the lobbying of the tobacco industry?
focus.explanation: Anchored to a real policy and to named advice, though the framing carries substantial insinuation about motive rather than engaging the mechanism.
focus.subject: speaker

civility.statement: The member opposite is interjecting to say that inflation could have come lower quicker—he’s 100 percent correct. If he hadn’t done so much more wasteful spending, we wouldn’t be here now.
civility.explanation: Pointed and aimed at the member's record of decisions rather than at him as a person; robust, edging toward but not landing on the individual.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Health New Zealand’s overly centralised operating model and poor financial controls have plagued the organisation since its creation by the previous Government. We’re taking decisive action to fix those problems by installing commissioners and giving them a mandate to deliver New Zealanders the healthcare that they deserve.
civility.explanation: Harsh about an organisation's operating model and the previous Government's structural decision; no individual is attacked.
civility.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The academy will involve a three-month residential stage in a youth justice residence, followed by a nine-month stage focused on supporting the young people to transition back into the community.
specificity.explanation: Names the two stages of the programme with exact durations (three months residential, nine months transition) — concrete and checkable against the published pilot design.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: When fully established, the academy will be for a small cohort of young people who have two proven offences punishable by 10 years or more of imprisonment.
specificity.explanation: States a precise eligibility threshold (two proven offences carrying 10+ years' imprisonment); someone could check a young person's eligibility against it. 'Small cohort' is the only vague element.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The commissioner will focus on de-bureaucratisation, putting patient outcomes first, and ensuring that local staff are involved in decision making.
specificity.explanation: A string of generic goals with no figures, thresholds, timeframes or named mechanisms — nothing here that could later be checked to see whether the commissioner did it.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The first is this: the decision that our Cabinet made was to put $1.4 billion in additional funding into Health New Zealand for this fiscal year, with additional funding every year thereafter totalling more than $16 billion over three Budgets.
specificity.explanation: Two precise figures attached to a named entity and defined periods ($1.4b this fiscal year, $16b+ across three Budgets); directly checkable against the Budget documents.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Will she guarantee that the additional $1.4 billion of savings she wants will not come at the cost of front-line services to patients, given, when adjusted for inflation, total operating health expenditure only increased by 0.4 percent in her Budget?
specificity.explanation: A precise question rather than a precise announcement: names the $1.4b figure and an inflation-adjusted growth rate of 0.4 percent, either of which the Minister could be held to.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: The research shows that when family are involved and supportive, the chances of success are much greater.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the research literature finds family involvement substantially improves rehabilitation outcomes for young offenders.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Peer-reviewed evaluations and meta-analyses of youth justice rehabilitation (e.g. multisystemic and functional family therapy literature, NZ Oranga Tamariki evidence briefs); true if they consistently report significantly lower reoffending where family are engaged and supportive, false if the literature shows no material association.

veracity.statement: This includes Health New Zealand currently overspending at the rate of approximately $130 million a month.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a current monthly overspend by Health New Zealand of roughly $130 million.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Health New Zealand / Te Whatu Ora monthly financial reports and Treasury or Ministry of Health briefings for mid-2024; true if the reported monthly deficit is approximately $130m, false if materially different.

veracity.statement: What is correct is that an increase in back-office staff from 2018 to the current time, of 2,500, has contributed to the current financial position.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that non-front-line ('back-office') staff numbers in the health system grew by 2,500 between 2018 and mid-2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Health New Zealand / former DHB workforce data on non-clinical or administrative FTE for 2018 versus 2024, as cited in Ministry of Health or Public Service Commission workforce reporting; true if the non-clinical headcount increase is about 2,500, false if materially different or if the category used does not support the figure.

veracity.statement: We have record numbers of nurses employed in our health system right now.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that nursing employment in the public health system was at an all-time high as at July 2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Health New Zealand nursing FTE/headcount time series (and Nursing Council workforce data); true if the mid-2024 figure exceeds all previous recorded periods, false if any earlier period was higher.

veracity.statement: Second, I would note that the latest OECD data shows New Zealand’s health spending as a share of GDP is well above the OECD average; our spending per capita is also above the OECD average.
veracity.explanation: Two distinct comparative claims from OECD Health Statistics: that NZ health spending is well above the OECD average both as a share of GDP and per capita.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: OECD Health Statistics (Health at a Glance) for the most recent year available in mid-2024; true if NZ exceeds the OECD average on both health expenditure as % of GDP and per-capita spending in PPP terms, false if NZ is at or below the average on either measure.

veracity.statement: Will she guarantee that the additional $1.4 billion of savings she wants will not come at the cost of front-line services to patients, given, when adjusted for inflation, total operating health expenditure only increased by 0.4 percent in her Budget?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that real (inflation-adjusted) total operating health expenditure rose by only 0.4 percent in Budget 2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2024 Vote Health operating appropriations compared with the previous year, deflated by the Treasury's forecast CPI or an accepted health cost index; true if the real increase is about 0.4 percent, false if materially different on that basis.

veracity.statement: Why did her Budget barely provide enough to keep the lights on in health, insufficient funding to achieve at least four of the Government’s five health targets, but prioritised a $2.9 billion tax break for landlords?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the restoration of interest deductibility for residential landlords is worth $2.9 billion, and that Budget 2024 funds fewer than two of the Government's five health targets.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2024 tax policy costings in the Treasury/IRD documents for the interest deductibility change over the forecast period, and the health target funding assessments in Vote Health Budget documents or Health NZ advice; true if the deductibility cost is about $2.9b and departmental advice indicates at least four of the five targets are underfunded, false if either figure is materially wrong.

civility.statement: I would say to the young lady that I am sorry for what she has been through.
civility.explanation: Answering a hostile question that invoked an abuse-in-care survivor's criticism of her flagship policy, she responds with an apology rather than attacking the questioner or the survivor. 'The young lady' is faintly diminishing, which is all that keeps it off 1.0.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: The issues at Health New Zealand stem from the botched health reforms undertaken over the last two years.
civility.explanation: Blunt condemnation ('botched') aimed entirely at a policy programme; no person is disparaged, and the former Health Minister sitting opposite is not touched.
civility.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: What we cannot continue to do is do nothing. These young people deserve better, and their families deserve better.
rigor.explanation: False dichotomy plus appeal to emotion: the alternatives are framed as the military-style academy or 'nothing', when the question concerned whether this particular intervention repeats past harms, and the conclusion rests on 'deserve better' rather than on any offered evidence.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Deciding to break up the district health boards and to reform the health system in the middle of a pandemic was always destined to be challenging, and the situation we’re in right now is proof of that.
rigor.explanation: Post hoc reasoning: present difficulties are treated as 'proof' that the reform caused them, without excluding other causes (pay settlements, workforce costs, demand growth). The conclusion is asserted from sequence rather than from evidence linking reform to deficit.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: By definition, Budgets are about prioritising; they are not about funding everything an agency or Minister might propose. That would be fiscally irresponsible in the extreme.
rigor.explanation: A valid general inference: if budgeting is by nature allocation under constraint, then declining some agency bids follows. The gap is that it answers the general case rather than showing the particular refusals were the right ones, so it supports less than the question asked.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: If that member wants to get up in this House and defend hiring hundreds and thousands more health bureaucrats while waiting lists got longer, she’s welcome to do so.
rigor.explanation: Strawman: the question asked whether a recruitment freeze extends to nurses, and the reply substitutes a position — defending mass hiring of 'bureaucrats' — that was never advanced, then invites her to defend it instead of answering.
rigor.subject: speaker

divination.statement: I would also say to the young lady that we have taken learnings from what has happened in the past and we have put processes in place to make sure that those horrendous acts that have happened in the past will not continue.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that the safeguards put around the academy will prevent abuse and mistreatment of the sort documented in historic State care from recurring in the pilot.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Findings of the Independent Children's Monitor, the Chief Ombudsman, Oranga Tamariki reviews or coronial/court proceedings concerning the military-style academy pilot; true if no substantiated mistreatment, unlawful detention or abuse of participants is found, false if any such finding is made.

focus.statement: I’m seriously saying that six years of that Government and two years of a botched reform is seriously affecting where we are now.
focus.explanation: Half a policy point (the health reforms) wrapped in blanket party framing — 'six years of that Government' names no measure, figure or outcome, and the weight of the answer rests on whose term it was rather than on what was done.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Which is correct: the Minister’s statement yesterday on Checkpoint that overspend on back-office staff is the cause of Te Whatu Ora’s deficits, or Margie Apa’s statement today that rapid changes in the nursing workforce caused the deficit?
focus.explanation: Squarely on the substance: identifies two named, dated accounts of the cause of a specific deficit and asks the Minister to reconcile them. Legitimate scrutiny with no party framing at all.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Why did her Budget barely provide enough to keep the lights on in health, insufficient funding to achieve at least four of the Government’s five health targets, but prioritised a $2.9 billion tax break for landlords?
focus.explanation: Names a specific Budget, the Government's own five health targets and a costed tax measure, setting one against the other — accountability for named commitments, though 'keep the lights on' adds rhetorical framing.
focus.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Can the Minister name a single thing she has done for the health of New Zealanders that is greater than the benefits she has provided for Philip Morris?
civility.explanation: The question is framed so that the Minister's entire health record is set against benefits she is said to have handed a tobacco company — an imputation of bad faith and captured motive directed at the person, not a criticism of a policy on its merits.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Can I ask the Minister: is it a fact that this question is set in 2022, five years after the Labour Party was in Government, which demonstrates that they did sweet Fanny Adams about this issue when they were in power?
civility.explanation: Dismissive and crude in register, but the target is a party's record rather than any individual; no person's character or competence is attacked.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: How does the Minister for Māori Crown relations feel being wheeled out by this Government to answer a question that was directed to the Prime Minister, simply because he is Māori, and the Prime Minister wants to distance himself from the responsibilities of Te Tiriti o Waitangi?
civility.explanation: Casts the Minister personally as a token 'wheeled out' because of his ethnicity and imputes an evasive motive to the Prime Minister; the attack lands on the two men rather than on any decision.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Does the Minister think that attending a close relation’s tangi is a case of being wheeled out of this Parliament, as has been put by that last idiotic questioner?
civility.explanation: Labels another member an 'idiotic questioner' — a direct attack on the member's intelligence rather than on the content of the question, even though the factual correction embedded in it is fair.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Well, I think it tells me that we’ve still got a lot more work to do, and, thanks to that member, we inherited a shambles, but we are committed to fixing that.
civility.explanation: 'Thanks to that member' personalises the blame with a sneering aside directed at the questioner, rather than criticising the previous government's policy settings.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: How, then, does he explain the 18 percent of New Zealanders feeling less safe as a result of the Government’s law and order policies and 58 percent saying they make no difference at all, as recorded by a One News poll?
civility.explanation: In a hostile exchange where she could easily have gone after the Minister personally, the question is put entirely on the evidence and the policy.
civility.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Can the Minister name a single thing she has done for the health of New Zealanders that is greater than the benefits she has provided for Philip Morris?
focus.explanation: There is a real policy subtext (tobacco regulation and excise settings that advantage manufacturers), but no measure, figure or decision is named; the weight of the question rests on insinuation about the Minister rather than on policy content.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: The Opposition seem to be fixated on tobacco companies. They seem to have lost sight of the people we are trying to help, which is those who are currently smoking. They ignore the fact that the first thing I did as a Minister was raise excise tax, and that we are continuing to meet with quit-smoking groups to ensure they have the best tools.
focus.explanation: Opens with party framing about the Opposition's preoccupations, but then engages named policy substance — excise tax and engagement with quit-smoking providers. A genuine policy point wrapped in party framing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Can I ask the Minister: is it a fact that this question is set in 2022, five years after the Labour Party was in Government, which demonstrates that they did sweet Fanny Adams about this issue when they were in power?
focus.explanation: Entirely about the previous Labour government's record in general terms; no policy, measure, figure or outcome is named, so there is nothing for the House to engage with on the substance of tobacco control.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: How does the Minister for Māori Crown relations feel being wheeled out by this Government to answer a question that was directed to the Prime Minister, simply because he is Māori, and the Prime Minister wants to distance himself from the responsibilities of Te Tiriti o Waitangi?
focus.explanation: About who is answering and the Government's supposed motives for it; no Treaty policy, obligation or decision is engaged with.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Well, I think it tells me that we’ve still got a lot more work to do, and, thanks to that member, we inherited a shambles, but we are committed to fixing that.
focus.explanation: Responds to specific poll figures with a general characterisation of what was inherited; no policy, programme or number is engaged.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: I’ve already laid out for the member that this incoming Government (1) funded the Police properly, because the previous Government hadn’t; and (2) we’ve funded 500 additional police officers, and we are on track to deliver those 500 additional police officers.
focus.explanation: Answers on the substance — Police funding and a named recruitment commitment — though it substitutes an input claim for the staffing number he was asked about.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: How, then, does he explain the 18 percent of New Zealanders feeling less safe as a result of the Government’s law and order policies and 58 percent saying they make no difference at all, as recorded by a One News poll?
focus.explanation: Legitimate scrutiny: names the Government's law and order policies and confronts the Minister with published outcome data on public perceptions of safety.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: How does he propose to make New Zealanders feel safer when the National Gang Unit he announced would be operational by 1 July was not stood up by that date and now has only five staff members in it?
focus.explanation: Textbook accountability: a named initiative, a stated deadline and a staffing figure measured against the announcement.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: The Opposition seem to be fixated on tobacco companies. They seem to have lost sight of the people we are trying to help, which is those who are currently smoking. They ignore the fact that the first thing I did as a Minister was raise excise tax, and that we are continuing to meet with quit-smoking groups to ensure they have the best tools.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Costello's first action as a Minister was to raise tobacco excise tax.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministerial announcements and NZ Customs/Excise records for the period after Costello's appointment (Nov 2023): true if an excise increase on tobacco was a decision she took and it preceded her other ministerial actions; false if the tobacco excise rise in that period was the pre-legislated automatic CPI indexation that would have occurred without any ministerial decision.

veracity.statement: We are at 6.8 percent smokers as at the end of 2023, and we are continuing to track down.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the smoking prevalence rate was 6.8 percent as at the end of 2023.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: New Zealand Health Survey adult daily smoking prevalence for the 2022/23 year (published December 2023): true if the rate is 6.8% within rounding, false if materially different or if the figure refers to a different measure or period than stated.

veracity.statement: Last week, I announced that 4,000 additional job seekers aged 18 to 24 will receive support from a case manager over the phone. Fifteen hundred young people were receiving this new service at the beginning of July, and the roll-out to 4,000 young job seekers will be complete in two months.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that 1,500 young jobseekers were already receiving the new phone-based case management service at the beginning of July 2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Social Development reporting or OIA data on phone-based case management enrolments for 18–24 year old jobseekers as at early July 2024: true if approximately 1,500 were enrolled, false if materially fewer or if the service had not begun.

veracity.statement: In Ōpōtiki last year, we saw the Mongrel Mob take over the town. Schools were closed, roads were closed, and the town was, effectively, held under siege.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that during a Mongrel Mob gathering in Ōpōtiki in 2023 schools and roads were closed and the town was effectively under siege.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Contemporaneous news reporting, Police statements and Ministry of Education/school notices for Ōpōtiki in 2023: true if schools and roads were in fact closed during the gang gathering; false if schools and roads remained open or the closures were unrelated.

veracity.statement: How, then, does he explain the 18 percent of New Zealanders feeling less safe as a result of the Government’s law and order policies and 58 percent saying they make no difference at all, as recorded by a One News poll?
veracity.explanation: Asserts a One News poll found 18 percent of New Zealanders feel less safe as a result of the Government's law and order policies and 58 percent say they make no difference.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The published 1News–Verian poll results from mid-2024 on perceptions of the Government's law and order policies: true if the 18% / 58% figures match the reported breakdown, false if the figures or the question wording differ materially.

veracity.statement: How does he propose to make New Zealanders feel safer when there are 124 fewer police officers in New Zealand than when he took office?
veracity.explanation: Asserts there were 124 fewer police officers in New Zealand in July 2024 than when Mitchell became Minister of Police in late November 2023.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Police constabulary staffing (FTE or sworn officer) figures for November 2023 and June/July 2024 as published in Police workforce reporting or answers to written questions: true if the net change is a decrease of about 124, false if the number rose or the decrease is materially different.

veracity.statement: How does he propose to make New Zealanders feel safer when the National Gang Unit he announced would be operational by 1 July was not stood up by that date and now has only five staff members in it?
veracity.explanation: Asserts the National Gang Unit was announced as operational by 1 July, missed that date, and had only five staff as at 23 July 2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Government's/Police announcement of the National Gang Unit and Police staffing information for the unit as at July 2024: true if the announced date was 1 July, it was not operational then, and staffing was around five; false if the unit was operational by that date or was materially better staffed.

veracity.statement: How does he propose to make New Zealanders feel safer when Police have advised him they will be pulling out of family violence now and this will be done “regardless of the readiness of partner agencies” and Police have warned him in briefings that this could result in “threat to life”?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Police briefings to the Minister stated they would withdraw from family violence work regardless of partner agency readiness and warned this could create a threat to life.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Police briefings/advice to the Minister of Police released under the OIA in 2024: true if they contain the quoted phrases 'regardless of the readiness of partner agencies' and 'threat to life' in relation to Police withdrawing from family harm callouts; false if no such advice exists or the quotes are not in that context.

specificity.statement: We are at 6.8 percent smokers as at the end of 2023, and we are continuing to track down.
specificity.explanation: A precise figure attached to a stated date, drawn from a known official series — directly checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Last week, I announced that 4,000 additional job seekers aged 18 to 24 will receive support from a case manager over the phone. Fifteen hundred young people were receiving this new service at the beginning of July, and the roll-out to 4,000 young job seekers will be complete in two months.
specificity.explanation: Named cohort, age band, headcounts at two points in time, delivery mechanism and a completion timeframe — all concrete and checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Ministry of Social Development (MSD) case managers will contact young job seekers at least once every 28 days. There will be a set appointment time for the phone call.
specificity.explanation: States who does the contacting, by what means, and at what minimum frequency — an operational mechanism rather than a direction of travel.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Hugely successful operations were recently run across the country, including the Hutt and Wellington, where the Eagle helicopter was used to deter around 300 vehicles from gathering to disrupt the public. Police seized dozens of vehicles and hundreds of infringement notices were issued.
specificity.explanation: Named locations, a named asset, an approximate vehicle count and enforcement outputs; the 'dozens' and 'hundreds' are looser than the rest but the claim is broadly checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I’ve already laid out for the member that this incoming Government (1) funded the Police properly, because the previous Government hadn’t; and (2) we’ve funded 500 additional police officers, and we are on track to deliver those 500 additional police officers.
specificity.explanation: Gives one concrete figure (500 officers) but 'funded the Police properly' carries no amount, and no timeframe is attached to delivery.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: How, then, does he explain the 18 percent of New Zealanders feeling less safe as a result of the Government’s law and order policies and 58 percent saying they make no difference at all, as recorded by a One News poll?
specificity.explanation: Two precise percentages attributed to a named poll — someone could go and check both figures.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: How does he propose to make New Zealanders feel safer when there are 124 fewer police officers in New Zealand than when he took office?
specificity.explanation: A single precise headcount difference against a defined baseline (the date he took office) — directly checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

divination.statement: The challenging economic situation that we have inherited means that job seeker numbers were always due to increase and to peak at the start of 2025.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that jobseeker benefit numbers would reach their peak at the start of 2025.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: MSD monthly/quarterly benefit statistics for Jobseeker Support recipients: true if the recipient count peaks in roughly Q1 2025 and then declines; false if numbers continue rising materially through 2025 or peak substantially later.

rigor.statement: The challenging economic situation that we have inherited means that job seeker numbers were always due to increase and to peak at the start of 2025.
rigor.explanation: The step from a weak economy to rising jobseeker numbers is sound, but nothing is offered to support the specific peak timing — the precise conclusion outruns the premise supplied.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: We saw gang tangis and gang convoys that were taking over public roads and intersections, that were driving into oncoming cars, that were abusing members of the public—that’s not happening under this Government, because there has been a very strong response by police.
rigor.explanation: Post hoc reasoning: a change in behaviour is attributed to the Government's police response with nothing offered to connect the two, and the premise that such events have stopped is asserted rather than evidenced.
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: It is fair to ask that member to depart from her high horse when she campaigned on exactly the same amount of funding for Health New Zealand as this Government delivered.
civility.explanation: "Depart from her high horse" is a sneer at the member's posture rather than her argument — condescension short of a direct insult, though a substantive reason is attached.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Well, I’d just say to that member, if you cared about working New Zealanders you would support our tax relief plan because that actually would support low-income working New Zealanders.
civility.explanation: Imputes indifference to working New Zealanders to the member personally, rather than engaging the question asked.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I’d just say to the member, the member may not understand but what we are trying to do is to make sure that we deliver on our climate change emissions targets and goals.
civility.explanation: "The member may not understand" is condescension directed at the questioner rather than engagement with the point raised.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Is it appropriate for a Minister who clearly has no understanding of Te Tiriti o Waitangi to be directing Pharmac to ignore the Treaty?
civility.explanation: A direct attack on the Minister's personal understanding and competence, built into the premise of the question.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Why won’t she put as much effort into improving the health of New Zealanders as she will into helping Philip Morris?
civility.explanation: Imputes to the Minister personally a motive of assisting a tobacco company ahead of public health — an attack on her good faith rather than on the decision's merits.
civility.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: It is fair to ask that member to depart from her high horse when she campaigned on exactly the same amount of funding for Health New Zealand as this Government delivered.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Labour spokesperson campaigned on an identical quantum of Health New Zealand funding to that delivered in the Government's Budget.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Labour's 2023 election fiscal plan / health manifesto commitment for Health New Zealand operating funding, compared with the Health NZ uplift in Budget 2024; true if the two figures are materially the same, false if Labour's campaign commitment was materially larger or smaller.

veracity.statement: That is good news because our plan is starting to work: inflation is down to 3.3 percent, the lowest in three years; and more good news as personal income tax relief is coming next week for the first time in 14 years, as we campaigned on, letting Kiwis—hard-working Kiwis, the people that the Greens and Labour used to care about—get more of their own money.
veracity.explanation: Asserts annual inflation stands at 3.3 percent and is the lowest in three years, and that personal income tax relief takes effect the following week for the first time in 14 years.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ Consumers Price Index annual inflation for the June 2024 quarter; true if the annual rate is 3.3% and is the lowest annual print since mid-2021, false if the figure or the three-year claim is materially wrong.

veracity.statement: Emissions budget 1 has been delivered, emissions budget 2 is being delivered, emissions budget 3 will be delivered, but we have time for that to happen, and the draft for a plan is out there.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the first emissions budget has already been met and the second is on track.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry for the Environment / Climate Change Commission assessment of net emissions over the first emissions budget period (2022–2025) against the 290 Mt CO2e budget; true if net emissions fall within the budget, false if they exceed it. Note the period had not closed at the date of the statement.

veracity.statement: Is the Prime Minister aware that the Ministry for the Environment and Treasury have estimated that this country is potentially liable for anywhere near $24 billion if we fail to meet our Paris Agreement obligations to 2030—that is 6 years from now—which his Government’s decisions are demonstrably making it harder to do?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that two named agencies have estimated a potential liability approaching $24 billion for missing the 2030 Paris target.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Published Treasury / Ministry for the Environment advice on the fiscal cost of purchasing offshore mitigation to meet New Zealand's first Nationally Determined Contribution; true if an official estimate reaching approximately $24 billion exists, false if the published range tops out materially below that.

veracity.statement: Nationally Determined Contribution 2030 is tough, but the previous administration signed us up to it and made it incredibly difficult and didn’t deliver against it or make progress against it.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the previous government both committed New Zealand to the 2030 NDC and made no progress toward it.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The date and authorship of New Zealand's updated 2021 NDC submission to the UNFCCC, plus Ministry for the Environment greenhouse gas inventory data for 2017–2023; true if the previous government lodged the NDC and emissions showed no decline over its term, false if gross or net emissions fell materially during that period.

veracity.statement: Is repealing Māori wards, which the tribunal ruled breaches the principle of partnership and our right to representation, an example of his Government honouring Te Tiriti o Waitangi?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Waitangi Tribunal has ruled the Māori wards repeal breaches the partnership principle and Māori representation rights.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Waitangi Tribunal's 2024 urgent inquiry report into the Māori wards legislation; true if the Tribunal found the repeal breaches the principle of partnership and the right to representation, false if it made no such finding.

veracity.statement: All three parties in the coalition Government oppose the creation of Māori wards.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a uniform position across all three coalition parties opposing Māori wards.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The National–ACT and National–NZ First coalition agreements and each party's stated policy on Māori wards; true if all three parties are on record opposing the creation of Māori wards, false if any party's stated position is confined to requiring a referendum rather than opposing creation.

veracity.statement: And what I’ll just say is, compared to the previous administration, which failed to fund core Pharmac needs to the tune of $1.8 billion, we found 54 new medicines at $600 million to improve the lot of 175,000 Kiwis.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a $1.8 billion funding shortfall left by the previous government and a Budget package of 54 medicines at $600 million reaching 175,000 people.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2024 Pharmac funding announcement documents; true if the package funds 54 new medicines for approximately $600 million benefiting about 175,000 people, and Pharmac's pre-Budget advice identified a roughly $1.8 billion unfunded gap under the previous government, false if those figures are materially different.

veracity.statement: Already, we have delivered a record $2.07 billion for State highway pothole prevention over the next three years. That’s a 91 percent increase in funding compared to the previous three years under Labour.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a record $2.07 billion three-year allocation for state highway pothole prevention and a 91 percent increase on the previous three years.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The 2024–27 National Land Transport Programme state highway pothole prevention activity class allocation, compared with the equivalent 2021–24 spend; true if the allocation is about $2.07 billion and represents roughly a 91 percent increase, false if the figures or the comparison base differ materially.

veracity.statement: Is it correct that annual returns submitted to the Ministry of Health show $4,044,956.49 worth of heated tobacco products were sold in New Zealand in 2022, and that $3,924,816.06 of those sales were by the tobacco company Philip Morris?
veracity.explanation: Asserts specific dollar totals for heated tobacco product sales in 2022 and Philip Morris's share of them, sourced to ministry returns.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Health annual returns filed under the Smokefree Environments and Regulated Products Act for calendar year 2022; true if total heated tobacco product sales equal $4,044,956.49 with $3,924,816.06 attributable to Philip Morris, false if the returns show materially different figures.

specificity.statement: That is good news because our plan is starting to work: inflation is down to 3.3 percent, the lowest in three years; and more good news as personal income tax relief is coming next week for the first time in 14 years, as we campaigned on, letting Kiwis—hard-working Kiwis, the people that the Greens and Labour used to care about—get more of their own money.
specificity.explanation: Carries a precise figure, a comparison period and a date for the tax change — all checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Is the Prime Minister aware that the Ministry for the Environment and Treasury have estimated that this country is potentially liable for anywhere near $24 billion if we fail to meet our Paris Agreement obligations to 2030—that is 6 years from now—which his Government’s decisions are demonstrably making it harder to do?
specificity.explanation: Names the two agencies, a dollar figure and the deadline — a precise, checkable question.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I’d just say to the member, the member may not understand but what we are trying to do is to make sure that we deliver on our climate change emissions targets and goals.
specificity.explanation: A restatement of general intent to meet targets, with no mechanism, figure or timeframe, in answer to a question about specific Budget and ETS decisions.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: And what I’ll just say is, compared to the previous administration, which failed to fund core Pharmac needs to the tune of $1.8 billion, we found 54 new medicines at $600 million to improve the lot of 175,000 Kiwis.
specificity.explanation: Three precise, checkable quantities: medicines funded, dollars committed, and people affected.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Our Government’s pothole repair targets include 95 percent of potholes on high volume national and arterial State highways to be repaired within 24 hours of identification, and 85 percent of potholes on regional, primary collector, and secondary collector State highways repaired within 24 hours of identification.
specificity.explanation: Two numeric targets, each tied to a defined road class and a stated repair timeframe.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Is it correct that annual returns submitted to the Ministry of Health show $4,044,956.49 worth of heated tobacco products were sold in New Zealand in 2022, and that $3,924,816.06 of those sales were by the tobacco company Philip Morris?
specificity.explanation: Exact dollar figures to the cent, a named source document, a named year and a named company.
specificity.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: That is good news because our plan is starting to work: inflation is down to 3.3 percent, the lowest in three years; and more good news as personal income tax relief is coming next week for the first time in 14 years, as we campaigned on, letting Kiwis—hard-working Kiwis, the people that the Greens and Labour used to care about—get more of their own money.
rigor.explanation: Post hoc: the fall in inflation is attributed to "our plan" on the strength of timing alone, with nothing offered to connect the Government's measures to the CPI movement.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Is reducing emissions at least cost a great improvement on past policies where Governments sought to reduce carbon emissions at a cost many times greater than the emissions trading scheme (ETS) price, or, in other words, chose to take less carbon dioxide out of the air than they could have if they took a least-cost approach?
rigor.explanation: A coherent economic inference: if abatement was purchased above the ETS price, the same spend would have bought more abatement at the ETS price. The step from higher unit cost to less carbon removed follows, though it assumes a fixed budget and unlimited ETS supply without saying so.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Well, I’d just say to that member, if you cared about working New Zealanders you would support our tax relief plan because that actually would support low-income working New Zealanders.
rigor.explanation: Near-circular and a false dichotomy: the conclusion that the member should support the plan rests on the premise that caring about working New Zealanders entails supporting this particular plan, which is asserted rather than shown.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: That is good news because our plan is starting to work: inflation is down to 3.3 percent, the lowest in three years; and more good news as personal income tax relief is coming next week for the first time in 14 years, as we campaigned on, letting Kiwis—hard-working Kiwis, the people that the Greens and Labour used to care about—get more of their own money.
focus.explanation: Substantial policy content (inflation figure, tax thresholds), but the closing clause pivots to what the Greens and Labour supposedly no longer care about.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: And I just encourage the Greens—I would love it if the Greens came out and actually cared about emissions, and actually support our fast-track legislation so we can double the amount of renewable electricity in this country and lower our emissions in the process.
focus.explanation: Names a specific measure (the fast-track legislation) and a stated outcome, but the weight of the remark is a claim about whether the Green Party really cares about emissions.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: How exactly does the Government’s strategy for credible markets supporting the climate transition align with the Government’s Budget decision to shred funding for the emissions trading scheme and the recent failure of the ETS auction?
focus.explanation: Squarely on policy: names the Government's stated strategy, a specific Budget decision and a specific ETS auction outcome, and asks how they reconcile.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Is repealing Māori wards, which the tribunal ruled breaches the principle of partnership and our right to representation, an example of his Government honouring Te Tiriti o Waitangi?
focus.explanation: Names a specific legislative measure and a specific external finding about it — scrutiny of a named policy, not party framing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Are policies such as the Fast-track Approvals Bill, the Treaty principles bill, the removal of section 7AA from the Oranga Tamariki Act, the ministerial alienation of te reo Māori, and the disestablishment of the Māori Health Authority examples of the Government’s honouring of Te Tiriti o Waitangi?
focus.explanation: Names five specific measures and asks how they square with a stated government commitment — scrutiny anchored to identifiable policy.
focus.subject: speaker

divination.statement: Emissions budget 1 has been delivered, emissions budget 2 is being delivered, emissions budget 3 will be delivered, but we have time for that to happen, and the draft for a plan is out there.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that New Zealand will meet its third statutory emissions budget.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Climate Change Commission / Ministry for the Environment final accounting of net emissions for the third emissions budget period (2031–2035) against the legislated budget; true if net emissions are within budget, false if they exceed it.

divination.statement: We are committed to a programme of work, and we will achieve Smokefree Aotearoa 2025—highly likely that will be achieved this year.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that the Smokefree Aotearoa 2025 goal will be reached within the year.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: New Zealand Health Survey daily smoking prevalence for the 2024/25 year; true if the adult daily smoking rate is below the Smokefree 2025 threshold of 5 percent, false if it remains at or above 5 percent.

civility.statement: Well, I think it’s very irresponsible for the member to come into this House and tell the country that Police have said they are withdrawing from family harm incidents. That is not true.
civility.explanation: Characterises the member's conduct as 'very irresponsible' — pointed and edging toward the person rather than purely rebutting the claim, but stops short of attacking her character or competence.
civility.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Well, I think it’s very irresponsible for the member to come into this House and tell the country that Police have said they are withdrawing from family harm incidents. That is not true.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that NZ Police have not said they are withdrawing from family harm incidents.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Police public statements, operational directives and OIA-released advice from 2024 on attendance at family harm call-outs; true if Police made no statement or decision to withdraw from family harm incidents, false if Police announced or advised a withdrawal from attending family harm call-outs.

veracity.statement: I seek leave to table the Official Information Act document I’ve received, that’s not publicly available, that stipulates Police advising the Minister of Police that there is risk of loss of life if police pull out of family violence call-outs without partner agencies being in place.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the existence and content of an OIA-released document in which Police advise the Minister that withdrawing from family violence call-outs without partner agencies in place risks loss of life.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The OIA document tabled in the House (Hansard tabled-papers record) and NZ Police advice to the Minister of Police in 2024; true if that advice contains a stated risk of loss of life from withdrawing from family violence call-outs absent partner agencies, false if no such advice exists or it says something materially different.

veracity.statement: The Government appointed a Crown observer in December, given our longstanding concerns about the implementation of the health reforms that created Health New Zealand.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that a Crown observer/monitor was appointed to Health New Zealand in December (2023).
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministerial announcements and Health New Zealand board records for the appointment of a Crown observer/monitor; true if the appointment was made in December 2023, false if made in a different month or year.

veracity.statement: What I accept is the biggest contribution to health of roughly $16.67 billion across three Budgets in our last Budget.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Budget 2024 provided roughly $16.67 billion to health across three Budget years, and that this was the largest such contribution.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2024 Vote Health documents and Treasury Estimates; true if the announced health package was approximately $16.67b over the three-year forecast period, false if the figure differs materially.

veracity.statement: Does he accept that the overall health Budget funding has actually reduced by 4.5 percent per capita, and, if so, will he increase funding to sustainable levels so that our health system isn’t on its knees?
veracity.explanation: Asserts as a premise that overall health Budget funding has fallen by 4.5 percent per capita.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Treasury Budget 2024 Vote Health appropriations compared with prior years on a per-capita (and inflation-adjusted) basis, e.g. Council of Trade Unions / Treasury analyses; true if the per-capita reduction is about 4.5%, false if funding rose or fell by a materially different amount on that measure.

rigor.statement: But I can tell the member that I was on night shift myself in Auckland recently, where police were called to a job where it was a mother and a daughter arguing over an iPhone charger. Now, I’m sorry; having uniformed police officers standing in someone’s lounge room trying to settle an argument between a mother and daughter over an iPhone charger is not a good use of police time.
rigor.explanation: Appeal to a single personal anecdote: one trivial call-out is offered as grounds for a general conclusion about how police time is used across family harm call-outs. Hasty generalisation from an unrepresentative case.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: But I can tell the member that I was on night shift myself in Auckland recently, where police were called to a job where it was a mother and a daughter arguing over an iPhone charger. Now, I’m sorry; having uniformed police officers standing in someone’s lounge room trying to settle an argument between a mother and daughter over an iPhone charger is not a good use of police time.
focus.explanation: Squarely engages the policy question of what police should attend, with an example of the call-outs at issue; no party framing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: How will slashing up to 3,000 jobs from the organisation that employs doctors and nurses help to get more doctors and nurses on the front line to serve our people?
focus.explanation: Directed at a specific policy — the scale of job reductions at Health NZ — and its stated effect on frontline staffing; no party framing, though 'slashing' is loaded.
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I want police back on their core business. I want police doing the job so that when members of the public put their hand up and they want help, there are police officers who are able to respond to them instead of having to deal with all the social issues that this country has, and there’s a much better response for a lot of those people from other agencies, and not the Police.
specificity.explanation: States a direction ('core business', 'other agencies') without naming any agency, threshold, mechanism or timeframe for what police will stop attending or who will take it over.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: What I think is that it’s important to deliver timely access to quality healthcare for New Zealanders to improve life expectancy and quality of life.
specificity.explanation: A string of generic goals — timely access, quality, life expectancy — with no figure, mechanism, target or timeframe attached.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: What I will do is thank them for their work and tell them that this Government backs them and that we’re looking at ways to ameliorate some of the issues that they’re raising with us.
specificity.explanation: 'Looking at ways to ameliorate some of the issues' commits to no named action, no measure of the administrative burden and no timeframe.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: How will slashing up to 3,000 jobs from the organisation that employs doctors and nurses help to get more doctors and nurses on the front line to serve our people?
specificity.explanation: Names a concrete figure (up to 3,000 jobs) and a named organisation, so the premise is checkable, though no source or timeframe is given.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Does he accept that the overall health Budget funding has actually reduced by 4.5 percent per capita, and, if so, will he increase funding to sustainable levels so that our health system isn’t on its knees?
specificity.explanation: Carries a precise, checkable figure and measure (4.5 percent per capita), though the second half ('sustainable levels') is undefined.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: What will he say to senior doctors this weekend at the GP conference who have told us this morning that they are doing administrative tasks themselves because the back-office staff reductions at Te Whatu Ora are impacting them?
specificity.explanation: Names a specific group, a specific event and a specific consequence (clinicians doing administrative tasks) of a named policy, but gives no numbers or scale.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: We’ve heard today in question time about the record investment in health: $16.6 billion over the forecast period.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Budget 2024 committed $16.6 billion to health over the forecast period.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2024 documents (Budget at a Glance / Vote Health, Treasury); true if the health package is stated as approximately $16.6 billion over the forecast period, false if the figure is materially different or covers a different envelope.

veracity.statement: The major thing coming out of the Budget is the tax savings for ordinary New Zealanders, everyday New Zealanders—those caught in the tax squeeze, who haven’t had a tax change in the last 14 years and have seen their earnings whittle away because of inflation.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that personal income tax settings had not changed for 14 years before Budget 2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: IRD/Treasury record of personal income tax rate and threshold changes; true if no change to personal income tax thresholds occurred between 2010 and 2024, false if thresholds or rates affecting ordinary earners were altered in that window.

veracity.statement: The step to address it in the meantime is the tax cuts: $102 per fortnight for most families, and up to an additional $150 per fortnight for families with young children—and I think that’s a really important thing.
veracity.explanation: Asserts two specific fortnightly benefit figures from the Budget 2024 tax package — $102 for most families and up to a further $150 for families with young children.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Treasury/IRD Budget 2024 personal income tax package material; true if the published figures are $102 per fortnight for an average household with children and up to an additional $150 per fortnight for families with young children, false if the amounts or the groups they apply to differ materially.

veracity.statement: The second thing is getting inflation down, and the best news we’ve heard is the announcement that inflation is at 3.3 percent.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the most recently announced inflation rate at the time of speaking was 3.3 percent.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ Consumers Price Index release for the June 2024 quarter (published 17 July 2024); true if annual CPI inflation was 3.3%, false if a materially different figure.

specificity.statement: We’ve heard today in question time about the record investment in health: $16.6 billion over the forecast period.
specificity.explanation: Names a dollar figure, a portfolio and a time period — directly checkable against Budget documents.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The step to address it in the meantime is the tax cuts: $102 per fortnight for most families, and up to an additional $150 per fortnight for families with young children—and I think that’s a really important thing.
specificity.explanation: Gives precise amounts, a frequency and the groups affected; someone could check it against the Budget package.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The main focus of what we’re trying to do is to make sure that we’re getting better value for the investment we’re making, on behalf of New Zealanders, to support New Zealanders and businesses so that they can grow, prosper, and enjoy the style of life that they expect and that we should be achieving in New Zealand, and I think the big issue is there’s no longer a mythical money tree.
specificity.explanation: A statement of intent built from generic virtues — 'better value', 'grow, prosper' — with no figure, mechanism or timeframe attached.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: What we’ve done is we’ve allowed businesses to undertake what’s called smart factory assessments, or the Smart Industry Readiness Index. We’re tripling the number of those assessments.
specificity.explanation: Names a specific instrument and a proportional change, but gives no base number, cost or date.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: At a time when we’ve got businesses struggling to survive, we’ve maintained their budget of just under $16 million to support businesses.
specificity.explanation: Names a programme funding level and the decision taken on it; checkable against Budget appropriations.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We need to make sure they are much more supported and they have the information flows coming to them.
specificity.explanation: Commits to no mechanism, amount or timeframe — 'much more supported' and 'information flows' are unfalsifiable as stated.
specificity.subject: speaker

divination.statement: When we see that coming down, that will give the Reserve Bank the reason to drop the official cash rate.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that falling inflation will lead the Reserve Bank to cut the Official Cash Rate.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: RBNZ Monetary Policy Statement / OCR review decisions after 23 July 2024; true if the OCR was reduced at any review within the resolve-by window, false if it was held or raised throughout.

rigor.statement: This country has been in deficit for years, and we need to get back into a stage where we are running surpluses, because that gives us even more money to invest in building schools, invest in new roads, invest in better health facilities—all the good stuff that every Government wants, even including the members from the Opposition from the other side.
rigor.explanation: The inference leans on a household/business budget analogy offered just before it; a surplus does not in itself create investment capacity in the way asserted, and no mechanism or figures are given to bridge the gap between 'surplus' and 'more money to invest'. A false-analogy argument with a real gap, though not empty.
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: This country has been in deficit for years, and we need to get back into a stage where we are running surpluses, because that gives us even more money to invest in building schools, invest in new roads, invest in better health facilities—all the good stuff that every Government wants, even including the members from the Opposition from the other side.
civility.explanation: Contested fiscal territory, and the reference to Opposition members is generous rather than pointed; the criticism stays entirely on the fiscal position.
civility.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We brought significant change to the narrative to this rural budget, and I want to highlight a couple of very salient figures: $65 million accelerating development of greenhouse gas mitigation research and development—something very salient to rural New Zealand—increased funding to the Rotorua Te Arawa Lakes Programme of $13 million, and an overall $67 million in the budgetary allowance for fresh water.
specificity.explanation: Three named appropriations with dollar figures attached to identified programmes; directly checkable against the Budget documents.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: As we can see, the financial allowance in this year is $3.2 billion, which is less than the previous Labour Government’s, which was $3.5 billion, and I must also say that this is the lowest in real terms since the 2017 Budget.
specificity.explanation: Two precise figures, a comparison year and a real-terms benchmark; fully checkable against Treasury Budget documents.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: But this side—this Government—is on the side of victims, and that’s why $2.9 billion extra in operating and capital funding is in this Budget to restore law and order.
specificity.explanation: Attaches a precise funding figure to a named policy area, though the framing sentence around it is slogan-like and no breakdown is given.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: We brought significant change to the narrative to this rural budget, and I want to highlight a couple of very salient figures: $65 million accelerating development of greenhouse gas mitigation research and development—something very salient to rural New Zealand—increased funding to the Rotorua Te Arawa Lakes Programme of $13 million, and an overall $67 million in the budgetary allowance for fresh water.
veracity.explanation: Asserts three specific Budget 2024 funding amounts for rural/environmental programmes.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2024 appropriations (Vote Environment, Vote Agriculture, Vote Research Science and Innovation); true if the Budget allocates ~$65m to greenhouse gas mitigation R&D, ~$13m to the Rotorua Te Arawa Lakes Programme and ~$67m for fresh water, false if the figures differ materially or the programmes are not funded as stated.

veracity.statement: We collectively initiated an independent inquiry into the science of biogenic methane, a short-lived gas out of the ruminant animal sector that I have spoken of before.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the coalition parties jointly established an independent scientific review of biogenic methane.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry for the Environment / Ministry for Primary Industries announcements and terms of reference from 2024; true if the coalition Government established an independent review or panel into the science of biogenic methane, false if no such inquiry was set up.

veracity.statement: ACT put forward a member’s bill, as members would perhaps remember, in the previous Parliament that was speaking to localism—outcomes, farm management, fresh water, their assets—and understanding the nuances of on-farm practices and fresh water. Sadly, our friends on the left all voted it down.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that an ACT member's bill about localism and on-farm freshwater management existed in the previous Parliament and was voted down by Labour and the Greens.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Parliament's bills and divisions records for the 52nd/53rd Parliament; true if an ACT member's bill on localism/on-farm freshwater management was introduced and defeated on a vote with Labour and Green members voting against, false if no such bill was introduced or if it was never voted on.

veracity.statement: As we can see, the financial allowance in this year is $3.2 billion, which is less than the previous Labour Government’s, which was $3.5 billion, and I must also say that this is the lowest in real terms since the 2017 Budget.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the size of the Budget 2024 operating allowance relative to the previous Budget and to every Budget back to 2017.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Treasury Budget 2024 Fiscal Strategy Report and prior Budget documents; true if Budget 2024's operating allowance is $3.2b, the preceding Budget's was $3.5b, and $3.2b is the smallest allowance in real terms since Budget 2017; false if any of those three figures or the real-terms ranking is wrong.

veracity.statement: That’s where we think that there should be diverse opportunities available for students to take up education and reach their potential, and I’m really proud of Minister Seymour for the $153 million that is allocated in this Budget for charter schools.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a specific Budget 2024 allocation for charter schools.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2024 Vote Education appropriations; true if $153 million is allocated for charter schools, false if the allocated figure differs materially.

veracity.statement: Previously, we know that the Labour Government got rid of charter schools.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the previous Labour Government abolished charter schools.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Education Amendment Act 2018 and Ministry of Education records; true if the sixth Labour Government legislated to end the partnership school/kura hourua model, false if the model was retained.

veracity.statement: But this side—this Government—is on the side of victims, and that’s why $2.9 billion extra in operating and capital funding is in this Budget to restore law and order.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the size of the additional law and order funding package in Budget 2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2024 justice sector appropriations (Police, Corrections, Courts, Justice); true if the Budget provides approximately $2.9 billion in additional operating and capital funding across the law and order portfolios, false if the total differs materially.

focus.statement: The previous lot, I would argue, weren’t so good at listening to those kinds of realities.
focus.explanation: A general characterisation of the previous government's attentiveness; no policy, measure, figure or outcome is named, so there is nothing to hold anyone to account against.

focus.statement: ACT put forward a member’s bill, as members would perhaps remember, in the previous Parliament that was speaking to localism—outcomes, farm management, fresh water, their assets—and understanding the nuances of on-farm practices and fresh water. focus.explanation: Names a specific legislative measure and a specific parliamentary outcome (its defeat) rather than trading in general party characterisation, though the 'friends on the left' framing carries some tribal weight.

focus.statement: Under the previous Government, what we saw was that the situation was such that that Government was taking the side of criminals.

rigor.statement: I am also conscious that the cost of living crisis, because of that irresponsible spending of the previous Labour Government, caused a lot of suffering to New Zealanders, and this wasn’t just on their back pockets. rigor.explanation: A causal chain (previous government's spending -> cost of living crisis -> family breakdown) asserted without any supporting mechanism or evidence, then backed by an appeal to anecdote ('I have heard so many stories'). The conclusion is not supported by what is offered.
rigor.subject: speaker

divination.statement: Today is 23 July, and in eight days’ time, most New Zealanders will see that they will have more money in their wallets because of the prudent financial management of this Government.

civility.statement: That member, the Hon Andrew Bayly, started his speech by saying he took great pleasure in speaking to the Budget. No one listening to him found it particularly pleasurable and it wasn’t a very pleasure-filled speech, and can I just say that I don’t take any pleasure in speaking to that Government’s Budget.
