focus.explanation: Engages the substantive mechanism linking council infrastructure provision to housing affordability; no party content.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Well, firstly, it gets rid of co-governance, which was that awful, divisive, race-based solution to everything that the previous Labour Government tried to impose—who knew?—on concrete pipes and manholes and sewage treatment plants.
focus.explanation: Names a specific feature of the bill — removal of co-governance arrangements — but the weight of the sentence is characterising the previous government rather than explaining the mechanism.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: That’s one of the reasons why they got voted out, because not only does no one trust them to deliver anything, not only do New Zealanders reject out-of-hand crazy co-governance of things like water assets, also if you look at what they spent and what they got, off you go to the Opposition benches for a very, very, very, very, very, very, very long time.
focus.explanation: Almost entirely about the other party's electoral fate and general untrustworthiness; the only policy word ('co-governance') carries no mechanism, cost or outcome.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Some cities, like Dunedin, failed to detect that lead solder in pipe joints was poisoning people in suburbs like Karitane.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Dunedin's council failed to detect lead from solder in pipe joints and that this was poisoning residents in Karitane.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Dunedin City Council and Otago/Southern DHB reporting on the 2021 Waikouaiti–Karitane water lead contamination, plus the subsequent investigation into the source: true if the source was identified as lead solder/pipe fittings, detection failed over a period, and residents showed elevated blood-lead; false if the contamination source was other than solder joints or if testing found no human lead exposure.

veracity.statement: What that has meant is that not only are we left with a significant deficit in infrastructure quality, which necessitates a very significant investment—and I’ll get to that amount shortly—it means if you want to buy a new home or buy a home in Auckland now in 2024, the cost of that home relative to your income is now 10 times your income, on average, for the average home and the average-income earner.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the Auckland median house-price-to-income multiple stood at about 10 in 2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Demographia International Housing Affordability median multiple for Auckland (or Stats NZ / CoreLogic price-to-income measures) for 2024: true if the multiple is approximately 10, false if materially lower (e.g. under 8.5) or higher.

veracity.statement: Not only that, for the $1.2 billion the previous Government spent, most of it on consultants and navel-gazing, so much of it on developing IT systems for asset management.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the previous government spent $1.2 billion on the Three Waters reform programme and that most of that went on consultants and IT/asset-management systems.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Department of Internal Affairs / Treasury appropriations and Auditor-General reporting on Three Waters reform expenditure to 2023-24: true if total programme spend is around $1.2bn and the majority is consultancy plus IT/asset-management system development; false if the spend figure is materially different or if consultants and IT were a minority of it.

veracity.statement: And by the way, if people are telling you, “Oh, geez, you know, we’ve got to think about the cultural impacts of where we put the waste water.”, well, in places like Singapore, the waste water from buildings with 5,000 apartments and 5,000 people living in apartments can get turned back into drinking water.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that in Singapore waste water from residential buildings is treated to drinking-water standard and returned to the potable supply.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Singapore PUB documentation of the NEWater programme: true if reclaimed municipal waste water is treated to potable standard and supplied for drinking/indirect potable use; false if Singapore's reclaimed water is restricted to non-potable industrial use only.

specificity.statement: What that has meant is that not only are we left with a significant deficit in infrastructure quality, which necessitates a very significant investment—and I’ll get to that amount shortly—it means if you want to buy a new home or buy a home in Auckland now in 2024, the cost of that home relative to your income is now 10 times your income, on average, for the average home and the average-income earner.
specificity.explanation: Gives a concrete, checkable ratio (10x) for a named city and year, though no source or dollar figure for the infrastructure deficit he defers on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: This bill also requires councils to deliver water services plans within 12 months.
specificity.explanation: A named statutory requirement with a stated deadline — directly checkable against the bill and actionable for councils.
specificity.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: A large part of that unaffordability is the fact that over many, many decades, councils have failed to provision the infrastructure to enable land to be serviced and that serviced land to be used for housing.
rigor.explanation: A causal claim — infrastructure under-provision drives the price-to-income ratio — supported only by the earlier assertion that councils under-invested; he himself concedes other factors ('notwithstanding changes in interest rates') without weighing them, so the leap from one cause to 'a large part' is asserted rather than shown.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: So if we can’t treat our waste water to drinking-water standard and put it into a river, put it into a stream, put it into the harbour, because of some kind of cultural constraint, this country’s never going to succeed.
rigor.explanation: False dichotomy plus a vast non sequitur: from one class of consenting constraint on waste-water discharge he concludes national failure, with nothing offered to connect a discharge rule to the country's overall prospects.
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: This is the next stage of replacing Labour’s convoluted, divisive, massively over-expensive, centralised three waters legislation.
civility.explanation: Harsh, loaded criticism aimed entirely at a piece of legislation and its design; no individual is attacked or impugned.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: As my colleague from New Zealand First mentioned before, having more Government oversight of what’s going on with councils is a great help, because, obviously, when we look around, some councils have made a real hash of their water infrastructure assets.
civility.explanation: Blunt about the performance of councils as institutions; no individual member or official is attacked.
civility.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: To listen to what the Opposition is saying, you’d kind of think that if we’d left that in place, all the water would be fixed now. But that was never going to happen.
rigor.explanation: Strawman: he attributes to the Opposition a position (that three waters would have fixed everything immediately) that they have not stated, then refutes that instead of their actual argument.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: The people that were going to have to pay for that were the people that consumed the water or used the wastewater. And guess what! They are the same people, by and large. So it was still going to be a cost on the same people.
rigor.explanation: A valid inference given its premise: if the entities' revenue comes from water users, and water users are largely the same population as ratepayers, the cost incidence is unchanged. The conclusion tracks the premises, with only a small gap around the 'by and large' overlap.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: We’ve heard the comment that 10 years is not long enough. Actually, I’d be inclined to agree; a longer term is a good thing, because these assets are going to be assets which, by and large, should be lasting 100 years.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion (planning horizons should be longer than ten years) follows from the stated premise about asset life; a relevant reason is offered rather than an appeal.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: The problem with hierarchies is that I’ve seen them interpreted. No. 1 is the one that gets picked, and Nos 2 and 3 are there, but if there is any conflict between Nos 2 and 3 and No. 1, Nos 2 and 3 get ignored.
rigor.explanation: Generalises from the speaker's own unspecified observations of how hierarchies are interpreted to a conclusion about how Te Mana o te Wai will operate — an argument from anecdote, though the inference is at least on point.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: As my colleague from New Zealand First mentioned before, having more Government oversight of what’s going on with councils is a great help, because, obviously, when we look around, some councils have made a real hash of their water infrastructure assets.
rigor.explanation: Leans on an appeal to a colleague's assertion plus an unspecified anecdote ('when we look around'); the conclusion that central oversight helps does not follow merely from some councils having performed poorly.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: However, the clause doesn’t pose a constitutional risk, because Parliament actually had a policy that that will give effect to.
rigor.explanation: Non sequitur: the existence of a parliamentary policy the regulation would give effect to does not answer the Law Society's objection, which is about delegating to the executive the power to override primary legislation.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: When three waters came up from the previous Government, I don’t think I’ve seen as many road signs and had so much email traffic about anything, so water is very dear to people.
rigor.explanation: Infers general public sentiment from the speaker's personal impressions of road signs and his own inbox — an argument from anecdote and self-selected correspondence.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: To listen to what the Opposition is saying, you’d kind of think that if we’d left that in place, all the water would be fixed now. But that was never going to happen.
focus.explanation: There is a real policy point about delivery timeframes, but it is framed around characterising what 'the Opposition' supposedly believes rather than the mechanism itself.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: The other thing to remember—and we’ve had commentary there about the rates increases this year—is that three waters under Labour’s model wasn’t going to come in this year or next year.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that under the previous Government's water reform model no water services entity would have begun operating in 2024 or 2025.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The establishment/go-live dates set out in the Water Services Entities Act 2022 as amended by the Water Services Legislation Act 2023 and the Water Services Entities Amendment Act 2023: true if no entity was scheduled to take over service delivery before 1 January 2026; false if any of the ten entities had a statutory establishment date in 2024 or 2025.

veracity.statement: I’ve talked to council CEs, and they’ve said that the cost of the working on the roads, the traffic management, is up to 40 percent—40 percent—of the cost of delivering those projects, driven by health and safety and all the other things.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that temporary traffic management accounts for up to 40 percent of the cost of delivering council road/utility works.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZTA Waka Kotahi temporary traffic management cost reviews and Transport and Infrastructure Committee evidence from 2023-24: true if documented cases show TTM reaching ~40% of project delivery cost, false if the highest documented shares are materially below that.

veracity.statement: One example of this—the cost of working on the roads is definitely going to be part of this—is that in the last year, right before the 2022 election, we were faced with Wellington Water coming to the Wellington City Council and saying, “Oh, by the way, we’re going to have to revalue all the underground assets that we’ve got by”—10 percent, 20 percent, 30 percent?—“80 percent.”—80 percent.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that in 2022, before the local body election, Wellington Water proposed to Wellington City Council an 80 percent upward revaluation of the city's underground water assets.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Wellington City Council annual report / asset revaluation papers and Wellington Water board or council committee papers from 2022: true if a revaluation of the order of 80% was proposed for the underground water assets, false if the proposed revaluation was materially smaller or no such proposal exists.

veracity.statement: None the less, we had 182 submissions and actually they were high-quality submissions.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Finance and Expenditure Committee received 182 submissions on this bill.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Finance and Expenditure Committee's report on the Local Government (Water Services Preliminary Arrangements) Bill and the submissions list on parliament.nz: true if the submission count is 182, false if materially different.

specificity.statement: I’ve talked to council CEs, and they’ve said that the cost of the working on the roads, the traffic management, is up to 40 percent—40 percent—of the cost of delivering those projects, driven by health and safety and all the other things.
specificity.explanation: Gives a concrete, checkable proportion (up to 40 percent of project cost attributable to temporary traffic management) attached to a named cost driver, though the projects and sources are not itemised.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The problem with hierarchies is that I’ve seen them interpreted. No. 1 is the one that gets picked, and Nos 2 and 3 are there, but if there is any conflict between Nos 2 and 3 and No. 1, Nos 2 and 3 get ignored.
specificity.explanation: Correctly describes the three tiers of the Te Mana o te Wai hierarchy, but the asserted misapplication is illustrated with no named decision, consent or case.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Everybody does, and, actually, this bill restores equality when it comes to governance arrangements and access to water, and that’s as it should be.
specificity.explanation: An abstract claim about restoring 'equality' with no clause, mechanism or governance arrangement identified; nothing here could be checked or acted on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We had to get clearance under Standing Order 295(1)(b) to get the power to consider an out-of-scope amendment, which was Amendment Paper 41, which was appropriate, but I think it’s the first time I’ve struck that in select committee, so it was rather unique, and that brought a lot to the table.
specificity.explanation: Names the exact Standing Order, the exact Amendment Paper and the procedural step taken — fully checkable against the committee record.
specificity.subject: speaker

focus.statement: This is yet another example of a Government that is taking New Zealand backwards.
focus.explanation: A characterisation of the Government in general direction-of-travel terms; no policy, mechanism, figure or outcome is named in the sentence itself, so it sits close to pure party framing even though the surrounding speech is substantive.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: You may well have been misled. You may well have been led down the garden path by a Government that went on the campaign hustings, saying one thing, but has come to the House with a piece of legislation that does the exact opposite.
focus.explanation: Holds the Government to a named pre-election commitment (restoring local decision-making) against the legislation actually introduced — legitimate scrutiny — though the specific policy content sits in the preceding paragraphs rather than this sentence.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: I need a Government member to stand in this House today and give an ironclad guarantee that they are not setting up to hock off our water assets and get them out of public ownership. Because the fact they would not commit to that is something to be afraid of.
focus.explanation: Engages a specific feature of the bill — the absence of public-ownership protections that existed in the previous legislation — rather than the other party in general.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Under this bill, the community—and I think this is very important for people to understand—will have no guaranteed right to be part of the process where their local councils prepare the central government - mandated water services plans.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the bill before the House contains no guaranteed right of community participation in the preparation of council water services plans.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The text of the Local Government (Water Services Preliminary Arrangements) Bill as read on 2024-07-25: true if no clause requires public consultation on the preparation of a water services plan (consultation obligations attaching only to establishing/joining/amending CCOs and to the DIA secretary's rule-making), false if a clause mandates community consultation on the plan itself.

veracity.statement: Let’s go through some numbers: 15.8 percent rates increases, that’s Tauranga City Council; 17 percent, that’s Kāpiti Coast; let’s look at 18.5 percent, that’s Wellington; and 14.75 percent, that’s Kaikōura.
veracity.explanation: Asserts specific average rates increases adopted by Tauranga City Council (15.8%), Kāpiti Coast (17%), Wellington (18.5%) and Kaikōura (14.75%), implicitly for the 2024/25 year.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The adopted 2024/25 annual plans / rates resolutions of Tauranga City Council, Kāpiti Coast District Council, Wellington City Council and Kaikōura District Council: true if the average rates increases match the four figures within rounding, false if any is materially different.

veracity.statement: Under Labour’s legislation, there were protections around public ownership—that was not something that Government members were even willing to countenance.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the previous Labour government's water services legislation contained statutory protections against privatisation of water assets.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Water Services Entities Act 2022 as enacted: true if it contains provisions restricting divestment or requiring public ownership of water services assets (e.g. restrictions on transfer of ownership requiring a supermajority/referendum), false if no such provisions exist.

veracity.statement: We had a member of the executive in Simon Court—who is an under-secretary who was sworn in as a member of the executive—stand up and talk about sacking councils if they fail to provide what was expected of them.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Simon Court, an under-secretary, spoke in this debate about removing or sacking councils that fail to meet the bill's requirements.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Hansard record of the 2024-07-25 debate on the Local Government (Water Services Preliminary Arrangements) Bill: true if Simon Court's speech refers to sacking/replacing councils that fail to deliver, false if no such remark appears.

veracity.statement: Look, I would just like to answer to the member who’s been speaking, Megan Woods, about costs on the other side of the House and I’ll give her a figure: $1.2 billion of wasteful spending on consultants, on your controversial, divisive three waters—$1.2 billion worth of wasteful spending with nothing, absolutely nothing, to show for it.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that $1.2 billion was spent on consultants under the previous government's Three Waters reform programme, with no delivery resulting.
veracity.subject: other
veracity.falsification_criterion: Department of Internal Affairs / Treasury reporting and Official Information Act releases on Three Waters reform programme expenditure: true if consultant/contractor spending on the programme totalled approximately $1.2 billion, false if the $1.2b figure covers total programme expenditure (including Better Off funding and entity establishment) rather than consultants.

veracity.statement: For days, we were drinking contaminated water that was making thousands of people sick—over 5,000 people.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that more than 5,000 people fell ill in the Havelock North drinking water contamination event.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Government Inquiry into Havelock North Drinking Water (2017) report and Hawke's Bay DHB estimates of campylobacteriosis cases: true if the estimated number of people who became ill exceeds 5,000, false if materially fewer.

veracity.statement: Four people died because we did not have safe drinking water.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that four deaths were attributable to the Havelock North drinking water contamination.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Government Inquiry into Havelock North Drinking Water report and coronial/DHB findings: true if four deaths were linked to the August 2016 campylobacter outbreak, false if a different number was attributed.

veracity.statement: Hastings District Council has already spent $100 million on creating a world first, a world-class drinking-water system.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Hastings District Council has spent $100 million on its post-outbreak drinking water system upgrade.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Hastings District Council annual plans/reports and its Drinking Water Strategy programme cost reporting: true if cumulative expenditure on the drinking water upgrade is approximately $100 million, false if materially different.

specificity.statement: Under this bill, the community—and I think this is very important for people to understand—will have no guaranteed right to be part of the process where their local councils prepare the central government - mandated water services plans.
specificity.explanation: Names the instrument, the actor (local councils), the specific document (water services plans) and the precise defect (no guaranteed right of participation) — checkable against the bill text.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Let’s go through some numbers: 15.8 percent rates increases, that’s Tauranga City Council; 17 percent, that’s Kāpiti Coast; let’s look at 18.5 percent, that’s Wellington; and 14.75 percent, that’s Kaikōura.
specificity.explanation: Four named councils each with a stated percentage rates increase; directly checkable against council annual plans.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Look, I would just like to answer to the member who’s been speaking, Megan Woods, about costs on the other side of the House and I’ll give her a figure: $1.2 billion of wasteful spending on consultants, on your controversial, divisive three waters—$1.2 billion worth of wasteful spending with nothing, absolutely nothing, to show for it.
specificity.explanation: Supplies a dollar figure and a named programme and spending category, though no time period or source is given.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Hastings District Council has already spent $100 million on creating a world first, a world-class drinking-water system.
specificity.explanation: Names the council, the dollar amount and the project; checkable against council financial reporting.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Look, we’re a Government of delivery and we are delivering good legislation which is going to deliver local democracy and going to deliver good water infrastructure.
specificity.explanation: A repetition of 'deliver' with no mechanism, figure, timeframe or named provision; nothing here could be checked or acted on.
specificity.subject: speaker

civility.statement: You may well have been misled. You may well have been led down the garden path by a Government that went on the campaign hustings, saying one thing, but has come to the House with a piece of legislation that does the exact opposite.
civility.explanation: Imputes bad faith, but to the Government collectively rather than to any individual member; no person's character, competence or worth is attacked. The charge is about a campaign commitment versus the bill delivered.
civility.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: I need a Government member to stand in this House today and give an ironclad guarantee that they are not setting up to hock off our water assets and get them out of public ownership. Because the fact they would not commit to that is something to be afraid of.
rigor.explanation: Argument from absence of evidence: the conclusion that privatisation is intended rests solely on the Government not having given a guarantee. A refusal to rebut is treated as proof of the allegation, which does not follow.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: They got together and they supported National’s “water done well”, because councils support localism and keeping our assets in local ownership, and that is why this is a good bill.
rigor.explanation: Appeal to authority/popularity plus a hasty generalisation: the merits of the bill are inferred from the fact that some Hawke's Bay councils backed the policy, and the support of a few councils is generalised to 'councils' as a class. Nothing is offered about what the bill does that makes it work.
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I take the points that the member who has just spoken, Catherine Wedd, made about the need for safe drinking water.
civility.explanation: In a contested debate she opens by crediting an opposing member's point rather than dismissing her; engages the substance, attacks no one.
civility.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: What happened in Havelock North was a tragedy. People died because the water that came out of their taps that should have been safe was not.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that people died as a result of contaminated reticulated drinking water in Havelock North.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Government Inquiry into Havelock North Drinking Water (2017) and coronial/Hawke's Bay DHB records on the August 2016 campylobacter outbreak; true if deaths were attributed to the contaminated town water supply, false if no deaths were linked to it.

veracity.statement: My colleague Megan Woods ran us through it: 15.8 percent in Tauranga, 17.1 percent on the Kāpiti Coast, 18.5 percent in Wellington, 14.75 percent in Kaikōura.
veracity.explanation: Asserts specific average rates increases set by Tauranga, Kāpiti Coast, Wellington and Kaikōura councils for the 2024/25 year.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The adopted 2024/25 long-term plans / annual plans of Tauranga City Council, Kāpiti Coast District Council, Wellington City Council and Kaikōura District Council; true if each council's stated average rates increase matches the figure given within rounding, false if any is materially different.

veracity.statement: In the Far North, 20 percent of ratepayers have not been able to pay their latest rates instalment.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that one in five Far North District Council ratepayers failed to pay the most recent rates instalment as at July 2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Far North District Council rates-arrears reporting or council statements on the instalment due mid-2024; true if the unpaid proportion was around 20%, false if materially lower.

specificity.statement: I want to call to the House’s mind a submission that was made by one particular district council. I’m not going to name who this district council was because, frankly, I was appalled by what they said.
specificity.explanation: Offers a submission as evidence while deliberately withholding the submitter's identity, so nothing here can be located or checked; the 'quotation' that follows is her own gist rather than the text.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: My colleague Megan Woods ran us through it: 15.8 percent in Tauranga, 17.1 percent on the Kāpiti Coast, 18.5 percent in Wellington, 14.75 percent in Kaikōura.
specificity.explanation: Four named councils with rates-rise percentages to one and two decimal places — precise and directly checkable against council decisions.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Now, this bill is here to provide the preliminary and the foundational provision for the framework of long-term, new, sustainable, certain, water-quality infrastructure for all of New Zealand.
specificity.explanation: Describes the bill entirely through a string of generic virtues — long-term, new, sustainable, certain — with no mechanism, funding figure, timeframe or named provision.
specificity.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: We were going to share the cost across the country, because that’s what we do as New Zealanders: we look after each other.
rigor.explanation: The cost-sharing model is justified by an appeal to national character and tradition ('that's what we do as New Zealanders') rather than by any argument about cost, capacity or outcome.
rigor.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Income tax thresholds are being increased tomorrow. The in-work tax credit for low and middle income working families is being increased tomorrow. The independent earner tax credit is being extended to $70,000 of income tomorrow.
specificity.explanation: Three named tax measures with a threshold figure and a stated commencement date; directly checkable against the enacted package.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Delivering tax relief to employees requires more than 242,000 employers and more than 120 payroll providers to be ready.
specificity.explanation: Two precise counts of the parties that must implement the change; someone could check both.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: But, on average, households will benefit by $60 a fortnight, and households with children by $78 a fortnight.
specificity.explanation: Two exact dollar figures on a stated per-fortnight basis, split by household type.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The number of people using the calculator has now risen to 561,000 people—up almost 45,000 since the statement last week.
specificity.explanation: A precise usage count and a precise weekly increment, tied to a named tool.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: It outlines the five changes in the Budget 2024 tax package, which total $3.68 billion in average annual cost.
specificity.explanation: A named document, a count of measures and an exact average annual cost figure.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Every single dollar of that is funded from baseline savings: closing stupid Labour programmes like industry transformation plans; a climate dividend; commercial buildings depreciation; taxing online casino operators, which the Minister of Internal Affairs issued a press release about just this morning, I believe; revenue from immigration levies; replacing first-year fees free with final-year fees free; and investment in tax compliance activities.
specificity.explanation: Itemises seven named funding sources and mechanisms for the tax package rather than asserting it is funded in general terms.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: How can she say the Government is not borrowing extra for tax cuts when her own Budget shows that the income tax cuts cost $10 billion and the Government is issuing an additional $12 billion of debt bonds?
specificity.explanation: Two precise dollar figures tied to identified Budget documents, making the challenge checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Can the Minister confirm that the Government is committed to spending reductions of over $13 billion over four years and an operating allowance of over only $2.4 billion, or 1.7 percent of total spending for the next four years, and has the ACT Party leader said anything about how excited he is about that prospect?
specificity.explanation: Carries three precise fiscal parameters — savings total, operating allowance and its share of total spending — over a stated four-year horizon.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Income tax thresholds are being increased tomorrow. The in-work tax credit for low and middle income working families is being increased tomorrow. The independent earner tax credit is being extended to $70,000 of income tomorrow.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that from 31 July 2024 income tax thresholds rise, the in-work tax credit rises, and the independent earner tax credit extends to $70,000 of income.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Taxation (Budget Measures: Personal Income Tax) Act 2024 and IRD guidance on changes effective 31 July 2024; true if thresholds and the in-work tax credit were increased and the IETC eligibility extended to $70,000 income from that date, false if any of the three did not take effect then or at different values.

veracity.statement: Delivering tax relief to employees requires more than 242,000 employers and more than 120 payroll providers to be ready.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that more than 242,000 employers and more than 120 payroll providers must update systems for the 31 July 2024 tax changes.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Inland Revenue published counts of registered employers and of payroll software providers at mid-2024; true if both figures are at or above the stated numbers, false if materially below.

veracity.statement: But, on average, households will benefit by $60 a fortnight, and households with children by $78 a fortnight.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the Budget 2024 tax package delivers an average gain of $60 a fortnight per household and $78 a fortnight for households with children.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2024 documents (Budget at a Glance / Treasury tax package costings) average household gain estimates; true if they state $60 and $78 per fortnight respectively, false if the published averages differ materially.

veracity.statement: The number of people using the calculator has now risen to 561,000 people—up almost 45,000 since the statement last week.
veracity.explanation: Asserts 561,000 people had used the budget.govt.nz tax calculator by 30 July 2024, about 45,000 more than the 517,000 cited the previous week.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Treasury/Ministerial figures on budget.govt.nz tax calculator usage as at late July 2024 (including the Minister of Finance's Hansard statement of 25 July 2024); true if the reported figures are 517,000 and 561,000, false if materially different.

veracity.statement: Kiwis can’t wait for tax relief, because they haven’t had it in 14 long years.
veracity.explanation: Asserts New Zealanders have received no income tax relief in the 14 years before 31 July 2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Record of personal income tax rate/threshold changes since the October 2010 package; true if no personal income tax rate or threshold reduction took effect between 2010 and 2024, false if any did (e.g. threshold changes or tax credit increases taking effect in that period).

veracity.statement: And I just remind the House, members opposite voted against it.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Labour members voted against the Budget 2024 tax relief legislation.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Division record for the Taxation (Budget Measures: Personal Income Tax) Bill in 2024; true if the Labour Party votes were cast against, false if Labour voted in favour or abstained.

veracity.statement: It outlines the five changes in the Budget 2024 tax package, which total $3.68 billion in average annual cost.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the Budget 2024 tax package comprises five changes costing $3.68 billion in average annual cost.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2024 'Budget at a Glance' and Treasury tax package tables; true if they list five tax changes totalling about $3.68 billion average annual cost, false if the count or total differs materially.

veracity.statement: And I would contrast that and compare it to the large operating allowances set by the previous Minister of Finance, which were notable by the fact that he never once met them.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the previous Minister of Finance exceeded his stated operating allowance at every Budget he delivered.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget documents 2018–2023 comparing the operating allowance signalled at each Budget/fiscal update with the new operating spending actually allocated; true if the allocation exceeded the signalled allowance in every one of those Budgets, false if any Budget came in at or under the allowance.

veracity.statement: We are working hard as a Government to get inflation back under control and be a friend to monetary policy, which is quite a contrast from the last three years when inflation peaked at over 7 percent, forcing the governor to hike interest rates very rapidly, which has put enormous pressure on households.
veracity.explanation: Asserts annual inflation peaked above 7 percent in the three years to mid-2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ Consumers Price Index annual inflation series 2021–2024; true if the peak annual rate exceeded 7.0%, false if it did not.

veracity.statement: How can she say the Government is not borrowing extra for tax cuts when her own Budget shows that the income tax cuts cost $10 billion and the Government is issuing an additional $12 billion of debt bonds?
veracity.explanation: Asserts Budget 2024 shows income tax cuts costing $10 billion and an additional $12 billion of government bond issuance.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2024 tax package costings over the forecast period and the New Zealand Debt Management bond programme forecast revisions between HYEFU 2023 and BEFU 2024; true if the tax cuts total about $10 billion and the bond programme rose by about $12 billion, false if either figure is materially different.

divination.statement: Budget documents, including the Budget at a Glance document, clearly show that the $3.7 billion per annum of tax relief is fully funded from savings and revenue initiatives, so the Government is not borrowing to fund tax relief and it won’t add to inflation.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that the Budget 2024 tax package will not add to inflationary pressure.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: RBNZ Monetary Policy Statements and Treasury economic updates through 2025 assessing the fiscal impulse of Budget 2024, together with Stats NZ CPI; true if official assessments find fiscal policy did not add to inflation pressure and annual CPI continued to fall back into the 1–3% band over 2025, false if RBNZ/Treasury attribute added inflation pressure to the Budget 2024 tax package.

focus.statement: But net debt continues to increase, as the member knows, because we have inherited a fiscal mess from the previous Government, and we are having to work as hard as we can to get debt under control.
focus.explanation: Concedes a real fiscal outcome (net debt rising) and points at a debt-reduction objective, but the explanatory weight is carried by generalised blame of the previous Government rather than any named measure or figure.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: How can she say the Government is not borrowing extra for tax cuts when her own Budget shows that the income tax cuts cost $10 billion and the Government is issuing an additional $12 billion of debt bonds?
focus.explanation: Direct scrutiny of a named commitment against two figures drawn from the Budget itself; entirely about the measure, not the other party.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Can the Minister confirm that the Government is committed to spending reductions of over $13 billion over four years and an operating allowance of over only $2.4 billion, or 1.7 percent of total spending for the next four years, and has the ACT Party leader said anything about how excited he is about that prospect?
focus.explanation: The first half engages the Budget's fiscal settings squarely; the tail turns the question into a self-referential party aside with no policy content.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Can the Minister confirm that some of the people browsing on the Treasury’s tax calculator have been found, by analysis, to be Labour voters from Wadestown browsing in incognito mode?
focus.explanation: A joke entirely about the other party's supporters; no policy, figure or outcome is engaged even though the tax package was the matter before the House.
focus.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Well, I don’t often agree with Shamubeel Eaqub, although I have respect for him, and I don’t agree with him in this circumstance. There is no doubt that the Government is not borrowing for tax relief in this Budget. I invite the member to read the Budget at a Glance document, which she is clearly unfamiliar with.
civility.explanation: Substantive on the Budget financing and courteous to the economist quoted, but the closing clause is a condescending jab at the questioner's competence rather than at her argument.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: And I would contrast that and compare it to the large operating allowances set by the previous Minister of Finance, which were notable by the fact that he never once met them.
civility.explanation: Hard criticism of a predecessor's fiscal management, framed entirely around his budget decisions rather than his character.
civility.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: The member cannot have it both ways. She cannot argue that debt is too high and also that we should go back on a spending spree.
rigor.explanation: Strawman plus false dichotomy: the questioner argued the tax cuts were debt-funded, not that spending should rise, and the two options offered (tax cuts or a 'spending spree') do not exhaust the alternatives.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: All of these, on the Treasury’s numbers, add up to more than the cost of the tax package, so it is simply fallacious to claim the Government is borrowing for tax cuts.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion tracks the stated premise (savings exceed the package cost), but the inference ignores the fungibility of money and the fact that the overall fiscal balance, not a hypothecated ledger, determines borrowing — so the 'fallacious' verdict is stronger than the argument supports.
rigor.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: From tomorrow, 3.5 million individuals will keep more of what they earn.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that 3.5 million individuals will receive a tax reduction when the new thresholds take effect on 31 July 2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: IRD/Treasury costings and Budget 2024 tax package documentation on the number of individuals receiving a tax reduction from 31 July 2024; true if ~3.5 million, false if materially fewer.

veracity.statement: We’re boosting Working for Families payments by up to $50 a fortnight, and that comes on top of our other changes to support Kiwis with the cost of living crisis.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the Budget 2024 Working for Families change increases payments by up to $50 a fortnight for some families.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2024 Working for Families in-work tax credit changes as legislated; true if the maximum fortnightly increase for an eligible family is around $50, false if the stated maximum is materially different.

veracity.statement: Does he stand by the commitment made by Christopher Luxon in the 2023 general election leaders’ debate to halve child poverty by 2028?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that in a 2023 general election leaders' debate Christopher Luxon committed to halving child poverty by 2028.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Transcript or recording of the 2023 general election leaders' debates; true if Luxon stated a commitment to halve child poverty by 2028, false if no such commitment was made.

veracity.statement: Why, then, did his Government quietly weaken child poverty targets last month, allowing approximately 23,000 more children to be pushed into hardship?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Government revised the child poverty reduction targets downward in June/July 2024 and that the revision corresponds to about 23,000 additional children in material hardship.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The child poverty reduction targets gazetted/announced by the Government in 2024 under the Child Poverty Reduction Act, compared with the previous targets; true if the new targets are less demanding and the gap equates to roughly 23,000 children on the material hardship measure, false if the targets were not weakened or the arithmetic gap is materially different.

veracity.statement: How is it fair that his tax cut package, which he keeps saying will benefit low and middle income earners—while analysis in fact shows that 64 percent of the benefit goes to the top 40 percent of households—will see children and families struggling the most get nothing because they’re on benefits?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that distributional analysis of the 2024 tax package shows 64 percent of the benefit accruing to the top 40 percent of households.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Published distributional analysis of the Budget 2024 personal income tax package by household income decile (e.g. Treasury, NZCTU, or NZIER); true if a credible analysis puts the top 40 percent of households at about 64 percent of the total benefit, false if the published share is materially different.

veracity.statement: Ninety-four percent of households across New Zealand are going to get tax relief; 83 percent of individuals in this country are going to get tax relief.
veracity.explanation: Asserts two coverage figures for the 2024 tax package: 94 percent of households and 83 percent of individuals receive tax relief.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Treasury/IRD distributional analysis accompanying Budget 2024; true if the share of households receiving any tax reduction is about 94 percent and the share of individuals about 83 percent, false if materially different.

veracity.statement: The previous Government’s botched merger left Health New Zealand with broken governance and poor financial controls.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the 2022 health reforms left Health New Zealand with defective governance arrangements and weak financial controls.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Findings of the 2024 Health NZ Crown observer / ministerial review (Lester Levy) and Health NZ's audited financial statements and Office of the Auditor-General commentary; true if those sources identify governance failure and inadequate financial controls, false if they attribute the deficit and structure to other causes or find controls adequate.

veracity.statement: Well, as I was saying, the amazing thing with our health system that we inherited from the previous Government is that a patient interacts with a team member, the team member reports to the team supervisor, who reports to the team leader, the team leader reports to the assistant manager, the assistant manager reports to the manager, who reports to the service manager, who then reports to the general manager.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a specific chain of reporting layers existing within Health New Zealand between a front-line team member and the general manager.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Health New Zealand's published organisational structure and position hierarchy documents; true if a role chain matching those named layers exists, false if the described chain is not reflected in the organisation's structure.

veracity.statement: Does he stand by his statement that his Government has a laser-like focus on bringing down the cost of living; if so, did hiking car registration fees and expanding road-user charges raise or lower the cost of living for New Zealand families?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Government increased motor vehicle registration fees and extended road-user charges to additional vehicle classes.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2024 / NZTA announcements on motor vehicle annual licensing fee increases and the extension of road user charges to electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles; true if both changes were made by this Government, false if either was not.

veracity.statement: Did that laser-like focus on bringing down the cost of living compel him to reintroduce prescription co-payments, driving people away from preventative care towards hospitals, costing more in the long run?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Government reintroduced the prescription co-payment.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2024 decisions and Pharmac/Ministry of Health rules on the $5 prescription co-payment; true if the co-payment was reinstated for most people from 1 July 2024, false if it was not.

veracity.statement: Did that laser-like focus on bringing down the cost of living lead to charging children more for public transport, which has resulted in some young families spending hundreds of dollars more per week just to send their children to school?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the end of free public transport for children has cost some families hundreds of dollars more per week.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Community Connect fare changes for 5–12 year olds from 2024 and the resulting fare schedules; true if a plausible family case reaches additional costs in the hundreds of dollars per week, false if realistic maximum additional costs are an order of magnitude lower (tens of dollars per week).

veracity.statement: Yeah, and what I’d say is that a majority of New Zealanders don’t use public transport, and some of them actually drive, and some of them really appreciate the removal of the Auckland regional fuel tax, and some of them really appreciate the removal of the ute tax.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that a majority of New Zealanders do not use public transport.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Transport Household Travel Survey / Census journey-to-work data on public transport use; true if a majority of New Zealanders do not use public transport, false if a majority do.

veracity.statement: They assumed that people would get a prescription every single week, but there’s actually a $100 cap on those fees per household.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that prescription co-payment charges are capped at $100 per household.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Health / Pharmac rules on the $5 prescription co-payment; true if an annual cap of $100 per family/household applies, false if no such cap exists or it is set at a different amount.

veracity.statement: Who was that laser focus concentrated on: pensioners, who can expect to get just $2.50 a week; minimum wage earners, who can expect to get $12.50; or one Philip Morris, who just got $216 million in tax cuts?
veracity.explanation: Asserts three figures: $2.50 a week for pensioners, $12.50 a week for minimum wage earners, and $216 million in tax relief flowing to Philip Morris.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Treasury's Budget 2024 tax package tables for a superannuitant and a full-time minimum wage earner, and the Regulatory Impact Statement / officials' costing of the heated tobacco products excise reduction; true if the weekly gains match and the excise measure is costed at about $216 million attributable to Philip Morris, false if the weekly figures are materially different or the $216 million is not the costed value or is not specific to that company.

veracity.statement: We can lead a national discussion about the role of rare-earth minerals, including vanadium located in the iron sands off the coast of Taranaki.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that vanadium is a rare-earth mineral and that it is present in the Taranaki iron sands.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Standard mineralogical classification of rare earth elements (the lanthanides plus scandium and yttrium) and GNS Science / published resource assessments of West Coast North Island ironsand composition; true if vanadium is classed as a rare earth and is documented in Taranaki ironsands, false if vanadium is not a rare earth element or is not present there.

specificity.statement: We’re boosting Working for Families payments by up to $50 a fortnight, and that comes on top of our other changes to support Kiwis with the cost of living crisis.
specificity.explanation: Names a specific payment and a dollar figure per fortnight, though the second half slides into general cost-of-living framing.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Why, then, did his Government quietly weaken child poverty targets last month, allowing approximately 23,000 more children to be pushed into hardship?
specificity.explanation: Names the policy instrument, the timing, and a numerical consequence — checkable as stated.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Yes, we’re going to work incredibly hard to lower child poverty across the country.
specificity.explanation: Answering a question about a numeric 2028 target with effort language: no target, no measure, no timeframe, nothing checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We are determined to rebuild this economy so that we can grow the prosperity and wealth of all families and take children out of poverty.
specificity.explanation: A statement of intent built entirely from generic goals — no mechanism, figure, or date that anyone could check or act on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Ninety-four percent of households across New Zealand are going to get tax relief; 83 percent of individuals in this country are going to get tax relief.
specificity.explanation: Two precise percentages tied to clearly defined populations; directly checkable against the Budget analysis.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Can the Prime Minister confirm that the Government is committed to spending wisely and cutting waste in order that it can afford to tax hard-working Kiwis less and provide the essential services they rely on?
specificity.explanation: A string of generic commitments — 'spending wisely', 'cutting waste', 'essential services' — with no programme, figure or timeframe attached.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Absolutely, and that was what was a feature of this last Budget—was that we were able to invest more in front-line services, remove wasteful spending, give people tax relief, and lay out the conditions for growth going forward.
specificity.explanation: Refers to the Budget but supplies no appropriation, saving figure or named service — four generic achievements with nothing quantified.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Who was that laser focus concentrated on: pensioners, who can expect to get just $2.50 a week; minimum wage earners, who can expect to get $12.50; or one Philip Morris, who just got $216 million in tax cuts?
specificity.explanation: Three named groups each with a precise dollar figure; every element can be checked against the Budget documents.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: These 15 summits will begin on 12 August in Nelson, but, most importantly, we need to boost economic resilience and create further opportunities to drive productivity, given the woeful state of the economy inherited when we arrived in power.
specificity.explanation: A count, a date and a starting location are concrete; the rest ('boost economic resilience', 'drive productivity') carries no mechanism or measure.
specificity.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Does he stand by the commitment made by Christopher Luxon in the 2023 general election leaders’ debate to halve child poverty by 2028?
focus.explanation: Names a specific commitment with a target and a date and asks whether it still stands — textbook accountability, not party-bashing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Does he stand by his statement that his Government has a laser-like focus on bringing down the cost of living; if so, did hiking car registration fees and expanding road-user charges raise or lower the cost of living for New Zealand families?
focus.explanation: Names two specific government charges and tests them against a specific stated commitment — scrutiny of a named policy, not party framing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: But what they all certainly appreciate is tax relief for low and middle income workers, a group of people who the Labour Party used to care about, but it has lost its way. David Parker cares about them, but the Labour Party doesn’t.
focus.explanation: Once the party characterisation is removed nothing about the policy remains — it is a claim about what Labour is 'really like' and its internal divisions, with no mechanism, figure or outcome named.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: I don’t want any more Green ideological sludge from that side of the House. This is a pure economic development approach. Co-governance is gone; co-investment is in.
focus.explanation: Responds to an interjection about climate change by characterising the other party's contribution rather than engaging it; the only policy content is the slogan-level 'co-investment is in', with no measure, cost or mechanism named.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: There’s no place in these serious debates for Green quackery. This will focus on those measurable types of investments, including that announced during the course of the Budget, which is to boost resilience through ensuring that our river systems and our catchments are better managed with flood management.
focus.explanation: Contains a genuine policy point — a Budget-announced flood management and catchment resilience investment — but it is wrapped in a dismissal of the other party rather than an answer to the point put.
focus.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Is he saying that children deserve to live in poverty if their parents’ income comes from benefits?
rigor.explanation: A loaded question that attributes to the Prime Minister a position he has not advanced — a strawman. The inference from 'the tax package excludes beneficiary families' to 'you believe their children deserve poverty' does not follow.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Centre-left and centre-right Governments do this all around the world—of adjusting tax thresholds. That’s why we would hope that the Greens and Labour would support this adjustment.
rigor.explanation: Appeal to common practice: that governments of both stripes elsewhere adjust thresholds does not establish that this particular adjustment is warranted or that opposition parties should support it. The premise supports 'this is not unusual', not the conclusion drawn.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Yeah, and what I’d say is that a majority of New Zealanders don’t use public transport, and some of them actually drive, and some of them really appreciate the removal of the Auckland regional fuel tax, and some of them really appreciate the removal of the ute tax.
rigor.explanation: Non sequitur: that most people do not use public transport and that other charges were removed does not answer or rebut the claim that the fare change raised costs for the families affected. The premises are irrelevant to the conclusion implied.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: They assumed that people would get a prescription every single week, but there’s actually a $100 cap on those fees per household.
rigor.explanation: A valid rebuttal structure: if the opposing calculation assumes weekly charges with no ceiling and a ceiling exists, the calculation overstates the cost. The inference tracks the premise offered.
rigor.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We’re rolling out a new risk-based approach to temporary traffic management which will see less reliance on road cones, requiring the New Zealand Transport Agency (NZTA) to report publicly on how much taxpayers’ money it’s spending on temporary traffic management, and we’re appointing independent members to the Road Efficiency Group to manage the reduction in expenditure and ensure all road-controlling authorities are focused on this outcome.
specificity.explanation: Names three concrete mechanisms (risk-based model, public NZTA reporting, independent appointees to a named group), but carries no figures, targets or dates.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: NZTA conducted a review of temporary traffic management at 800 maintenance work sites on the State highway network across the country in February and found that 145 of these sites were not needed, revealing how out of control the use of road cones and temporary traffic management has become.
specificity.explanation: Named agency, named month, sample size and count — fully checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Can he confirm that one of the reasons New Zealanders are faced with a sea of orange road cones is unclear health and safety obligations, and that’s why this Government is going to make sure that our health and safety rules are clear, sensible, and proportionate to risk?
specificity.explanation: Identifies a cause (unclear health and safety obligations) but the remedy is a string of generic virtues — 'clear, sensible, and proportionate' — with no named change, mechanism or timeframe.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: In regards to the evidence, the design of the pilot was informed by evidence and lessons from other military-style programmes, such as the Limited Service Volunteer programme and the Military-style Activity Camp programme, as well as overseas examples.
specificity.explanation: Names two specific precedent programmes, but the 'lessons' and the 'overseas examples' are left unidentified and no documents or findings are cited.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Nobody can guarantee the actions of others, but what we can do is make sure we put everything in place to make sure that the risks are as low as possible and that, if something does happen, we act quickly and efficiently and in the right way.
specificity.explanation: Commits to 'everything in place' and acting 'in the right way' without naming a single safeguard, oversight body, reporting line or complaint process.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I’ve seen evidence that the previous approaches to youth crime saw a 291 percent increase in ram raids over the last six years. In 2023, over 85 percent of offenders were younger than 18.
specificity.explanation: Two precise percentages attached to a named offence type and a stated period — directly checkable against police data.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Isn’t it the case that there are no drills at these military-style boot camps, no military fatigues, no military staff, and, in fact, there’s nothing particularly military at all about these military-style boot camps?
specificity.explanation: Three concrete, observable features are named and denied, making the claim directly checkable against the programme's content.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: It prohibits the display of gang insignia in public places, gives police the ability to issue dispersal notices to gatherings that disrupt the public, it creates new non-consorting orders, and amends the Sentencing Act to make gang membership, on its own, an aggravating factor.
specificity.explanation: Four specific legislative mechanisms in a named bill, including the statute amended — anyone can check each against the bill text.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: How will including violent attacks on sole-charge workers as an aggravating factor at sentencing, as outlined in the ACT and National coalition agreement, contribute to law and order?
specificity.explanation: Names a precise sentencing mechanism and the document it comes from, though it attaches no figures, timeframe or implementation detail.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: NZTA conducted a review of temporary traffic management at 800 maintenance work sites on the State highway network across the country in February and found that 145 of these sites were not needed, revealing how out of control the use of road cones and temporary traffic management has become.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that an NZTA review of 800 State highway maintenance sites in February found 145 of them did not need temporary traffic management.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The NZTA temporary traffic management site review of February 2024: true if it covered approximately 800 State highway maintenance sites and identified about 145 where TTM was not required; false if the sample size or the count of unnecessary sites differs materially, or no such review exists.

veracity.statement: Auckland Council Mayor Wayne Brown has also released a report showing that $145 million of expenditure has been incurred by his council group every single year.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that a report released by the Auckland mayor puts the council group's annual temporary traffic management spend at $145 million per year.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Auckland Council / mayoral report on traffic management costs released in 2024: true if it states annual council-group expenditure of approximately $145 million; false if it states a materially different figure or no such report exists.

veracity.statement: When I became transport Minister, I asked NZTA to outline how much money has been spent by NZTA each year for the past three years on temporary traffic management, and was advised this information was not available as it was not compiled.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that NZTA told the incoming Minister it did not hold compiled annual figures for its temporary traffic management spending.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZTA advice to the Minister of Transport (ministerial correspondence/briefings released under the OIA, or NZTA's own statements in 2024): true if NZTA advised that annual TTM expenditure was not compiled and therefore unavailable; false if NZTA had and supplied such annual figures.

veracity.statement: The New Zealand Defence Force has been involved from the very beginning in designing the programme, training the staff, and actually making sure that this is a well-rounded programme.
veracity.explanation: Asserts NZDF involvement in the military-style academy pilot from the outset, covering programme design and staff training.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Oranga Tamariki and NZDF documentation on the 2024 military-style academy pilot (design documents, OIA releases, agency statements): true if NZDF participated in designing the programme and training its staff from the pilot's inception; false if NZDF involvement began later or was limited to incidental activities.

veracity.statement: I’ve seen evidence that the previous approaches to youth crime saw a 291 percent increase in ram raids over the last six years. In 2023, over 85 percent of offenders were younger than 18.
veracity.explanation: Two figures: a 291 percent rise in ram raids over six years, and more than 85 percent of ram raid offenders in 2023 being under 18.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Police retail crime / ram raid statistics for the six years to 2023-24: true if reported ram raids rose by about 291 percent over that window and over 85 percent of identified 2023 offenders were under 18; false if either figure is materially different on the police series.

veracity.statement: Isn’t it the case that there are no drills at these military-style boot camps, no military fatigues, no military staff, and, in fact, there’s nothing particularly military at all about these military-style boot camps?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the military-style academy pilot involves no drills, no military uniforms and no military personnel.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Oranga Tamariki programme documentation and contemporaneous reporting on the 2024 military-style academy pilot: true if the residential phase included no drill activity, no military dress and no NZDF personnel; false if any of those three elements was present.

veracity.statement: In response to a significant increase in retail crime over the past five years, with the total number of reported victimisations up 86 percent, the Government tasked its ministerial advisory group for the victims of retail crime with developing specific proposals to address urgent challenges in retail crime, starting with considering greater powers for security guards to detain thieves.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that reported retail crime victimisations rose 86 percent over the five years to 2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Police victimisation statistics for retail premises over the five years to mid-2024: true if total reported retail victimisations rose by approximately 86 percent; false if the increase over that period is materially different.

rigor.statement: NZTA conducted a review of temporary traffic management at 800 maintenance work sites on the State highway network across the country in February and found that 145 of these sites were not needed, revealing how out of control the use of road cones and temporary traffic management has become.
rigor.explanation: Hasty generalisation: 145 of 800 sites (about 18 percent) is offered as showing the system is 'out of control', a conclusion considerably stronger than the figure supports.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Yes, I agree with the Prime Minister, particularly when he said, “it’s actually been a botched restructuring and a botched merger that actually hasn’t delivered an efficient operating model.”, and that’s obvious when you talk to the front-line staff—the doctors and the nurses at the front line.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion that the merger was botched rests on an appeal to authority (the Prime Minister's words) plus unquantified anecdote ('when you talk to the front-line staff'); no evidence about the operating model itself is offered.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: They were run inappropriately, with staff who were not trained, in a remote isolated area with no way to actually seek help. This is not what we’re doing, and I am proud to stand by this Government in working with these young people to address serious youth offending.

rigor.statement: These young people are in a youth justice facility currently because they have committed serious offences. It is obvious that approaches that have been tried beforehand haven’t worked. That is why we are trying a new approach.

focus.statement: Is she able to guarantee that young people will not be at risk of abuse in military-style boot camps, and, if not, why is she ploughing ahead with a failed system that puts young people at risk?

focus.statement: Does he agree with Christopher Luxon, who said, “I’m telling you, when we get in Government, we’re not doing working groups and endless kumbaya and lots of talking.”, and, if so, why is he setting up a working group that has two years of talking before reporting back?

specificity.statement: This Government agrees, which is why, in Budget 2024, we provided an additional $8 million over four years to increase financial grants to victims of serious crime through the Victim Assistance Scheme and why we’ve set an ambitious target to reduce the number of people who are the victims of assault, robbery, or sexual assault by 20,000 by 2029.

specificity.statement: I’ve made it very clear that I want that group, which will be chaired by Sunny Kaushal, to come up with specific proposals, quickly, on how we can deal with the retail crime that we’ve got.

specificity.statement: The Tertiary Education Commission (TEC) has recently exercised its statutory intervention power to require Te Pūkenga to obtain specialist external help to conduct the necessary cost-out work, to develop clear pathways to re-establishing an Institutes of Technology and Polytechnics of New Zealand (ITP) network and to implement this work.

specificity.statement: Overall, it showed a weakening of farmer confidence with a net 66 percent of farmers pointing out that current economic conditions are very challenging and that profit margins for many are squeezed.

specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: For example, I am fast progressing our work to simplify and reduce costs in freshwater farm planning to provide a robust but affordable way of managing the environmental risks of farming.

veracity.statement: This Government agrees, which is why, in Budget 2024, we provided an additional $8 million over four years to increase financial grants to victims of serious crime through the Victim Assistance Scheme and why we’ve set an ambitious target to reduce the number of people who are the victims of assault, robbery, or sexual assault by 20,000 by 2029.

veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2024 Vote Justice estimates and the Government's published target set; true if Vote Justice shows an additional ~$8m over four years for the Victim Assistance Scheme and the published target is a reduction of 20,000 victims of assault/robbery/sexual assault by 2029, false if the amounts, period or target figures differ materially.

veracity.statement: Does he agree with Christopher Luxon, who said, “I’m telling you, when we get in Government, we’re not doing working groups and endless kumbaya and lots of talking.”, and, if so, why is he setting up a working group that has two years of talking before reporting back?
