specificity.statement: So it’s not either/or, and there is no suggestion that one piece of legislation will solve the problem by itself. It has to be part of a holistic plan across all Government.
specificity.explanation: Offered as substantive content but carries none: 'holistic plan across all Government' names no mechanism, agency, figure or timeframe, and nothing here could be checked or acted on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I do think that there are some potentially problematic things that could come out of this because “public places” could include, for example, a polling booth, and “gang members” could include people who are wanting to exercise their democratic right.
specificity.explanation: Anchored in named clauses and quoted definitional language with a concrete example (a polling booth), though the consequence is stated as a possibility rather than a quantified or bounded effect.
specificity.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Where we sometimes differ—and I don’t want to misinterpret what her party is saying, but it’s one thing to understand the context, but no society can function if people aren’t accountable for the decisions that they make today whether or not to commit a crime or intimidate people or engage in drug dealing or a whole host of things that have been associated with many gangs in the past.
civility.explanation: A contested committee-stage exchange where an attack was available; instead he states the disagreement on its merits and expressly guards against misrepresenting the other party. No person is targeted.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I have full confidence and faith that none of the current members of this current House are in any way tyrannical or autocratic, and I don’t suggest that anyone here would move to use it, but it does create a precedent whereby some future administration which might have ill intent could use clause 3(b) to misclassify people as gang members and to prohibit them from exercising their democratic rights.
civility.explanation: Raises an allegation of potential authoritarian misuse while expressly exempting every present member from the charge; the objection lands on the drafting, not on any person.
civility.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: I have full confidence and faith that none of the current members of this current House are in any way tyrannical or autocratic, and I don’t suggest that anyone here would move to use it, but it does create a precedent whereby some future administration which might have ill intent could use clause 3(b) to misclassify people as gang members and to prohibit them from exercising their democratic rights.
rigor.explanation: Partly a slippery-slope: the conclusion depends on an unevidenced future actor with ill intent and on misclassification occurring. It is better than a bare slippery slope because the breadth of the clause 3(b) power and the clause 4 definition are actually cited as the mechanism, but nothing is offered to bridge from 'the power is broad' to 'it will be abused'.
rigor.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: But part of that is having the police resource to be able to do that and to be able to make sure—so we do know that Police received about $107 million less in the last Budget than they did the one before that.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the most recent Budget appropriated roughly $107 million less to Police than the preceding Budget.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Vote Police appropriations in Budget 2024 compared with Budget 2023 (Treasury Estimates of Appropriations / Budget at a Glance): true if total or new operating funding for Police is about $107m lower in Budget 2024 than Budget 2023, false if funding is equal or higher on the comparable measure.

veracity.statement: I would make the point that, of course, in the broader context that all New Zealanders will be aware of a very difficult Budget environment where—even notwithstanding all the many savings that my colleague Nicola Willis made on behalf of the Government—New Zealand will still be running a very substantial deficit of around $13 billion this year.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the Crown's operating deficit for the current year is approximately $13 billion.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Treasury Budget 2024 Economic and Fiscal Update OBEGAL forecast for the 2023/24 and 2024/25 years: true if the relevant year's forecast deficit is around $13bn (say $11–15bn), false if materially outside that range.

veracity.statement: In that context, one of the areas where the Government did choose to invest more was—alongside health—with additional resources to the police and for 500 extra police officers.
veracity.explanation: Asserts Budget 2024 provided additional police funding including funding for 500 extra police officers.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2024 Vote Police appropriation documents and the associated Police Minister press release: true if new funding is appropriated explicitly for 500 additional sworn officers, false if no such allocation exists or the number differs materially.

veracity.statement: But it doesn’t really take into account that the majority of gangs in this country are actually gangs that have no Māori association with them at all.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that, counted as organisations, most gangs in New Zealand have no Māori affiliation — the outlaw motorcycle clubs outnumbering Mongrel Mob and Black Power chapters as distinct groups.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Police National Gang List / gang harm insights enumeration of distinct gangs and chapters: true if more than half the listed gangs are groups without Māori affiliation (e.g. outlaw motorcycle clubs), false if predominantly Māori-associated gangs make up the majority of listed groups.

veracity.statement: Less than 0.5 percent of the Māori population are involved in gang activity.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that fewer than one in two hundred Māori are involved in gangs.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Police National Gang List membership by ethnicity divided by the Stats NZ Māori usual resident population: true if Māori gang members are under 0.5% of the Māori population, false if 0.5% or above.

rigor.statement: I would go so far as to say that it would be irresponsible of this Government to promise to New Zealanders that this legislation will, in fact, deliver a restoration of law and order if, with one hand, they are taking away a gang patch and, with the other hand, they are closing a police station, because that would seem to be counterintuitive to the purposes of what they promised at the election and what New Zealanders are expecting them to deliver.
rigor.explanation: A conditional argument: new enforcement powers cannot deliver the promised outcome without the front-line presence to exercise them. The inference is coherent and explicitly conditional, though the premise that stations are closing is asserted rather than shown.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: It would be quite hard to issue dispersal notices and remove gang patches if there’s no front-line police officer paid and resourced to be able to be there and doing that work.
rigor.explanation: A tight, almost definitional inference: powers that require an officer on the spot cannot be exercised where no officer is funded to be there. The conclusion follows directly from the premise.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: That’s why we’ve tightened up our spending: so as to reduce inflation, so as to reduce interest rates, so as to take pressure off households.
rigor.explanation: A causal chain — restrain spending, lower inflation, lower interest rates, relieve households — that is a recognised mechanism but is asserted rather than evidenced, and skips the step where fiscal restraint of this size actually moves the inflation rate.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: If the Minister is really keen on what the Government does in terms of how we really address the problem—because this is dropping the hammer on them, no doubt about it—if we really want to see gangs gone, then we have to address the intergenerational nature of gangs in this country, and address things like my mate Tamatha over here keeps bringing up, like poverty, lack of opportunity, economic marginalisation, and all of those things.
rigor.explanation: Argues that eliminating gangs requires addressing their intergenerational drivers. The premise-to-conclusion step is reasonable but the causal link between the named drivers and gang formation is asserted, with no evidence offered to close the gap.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: I would go so far as to say that it would be irresponsible of this Government to promise to New Zealanders that this legislation will, in fact, deliver a restoration of law and order if, with one hand, they are taking away a gang patch and, with the other hand, they are closing a police station, because that would seem to be counterintuitive to the purposes of what they promised at the election and what New Zealanders are expecting them to deliver.
focus.explanation: Engages the measure before the House and a named resourcing consequence (patch ban powers versus station closures) rather than the other party in general; legitimate scrutiny of a specific election commitment.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Also, moral support for the police is important, which is why we were so distressed yesterday with the implication or the question posed by the Greens that police are more of a menace to society than gangs, or could be regarded as such, and we didn’t think that was at all appropriate.
focus.explanation: Pivots from the bill to what another party is alleged to have implied about police the previous day; there is a thread of policy content (backing for police as part of the response) but the weight of the remark is on characterising the Greens rather than on the measure before the committee.
focus.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I would go so far as to say that it would be irresponsible of this Government to promise to New Zealanders that this legislation will, in fact, deliver a restoration of law and order if, with one hand, they are taking away a gang patch and, with the other hand, they are closing a police station, because that would seem to be counterintuitive to the purposes of what they promised at the election and what New Zealanders are expecting them to deliver.
civility.explanation: Hard criticism aimed at the Government's policy choices and promises; calls the hypothetical course 'irresponsible' but attacks no individual.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Maybe the Minister can speak to that, because I do see that there are quite big parts of this legislation that appear to be cosmetic, that are good window dressings, that enable the Minister to be able to stand up like he did in the House yesterday and say that he’s putting gangs on notice and that we will no longer tolerate this kind of disruption to our communities.
civility.explanation: Dismissive of the legislation as 'window dressing' and points at the Minister's public posturing, but the charge is levelled at the bill and the performance rather than at the man's character or competence.
civility.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Maybe the Minister can speak to that, because I do see that there are quite big parts of this legislation that appear to be cosmetic, that are good window dressings, that enable the Minister to be able to stand up like he did in the House yesterday and say that he’s putting gangs on notice and that we will no longer tolerate this kind of disruption to our communities.
specificity.explanation: Characterises 'quite big parts' of the bill as cosmetic without naming a clause, a power or an example of what is merely presentational.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: If the Minister is really keen on what the Government does in terms of how we really address the problem—because this is dropping the hammer on them, no doubt about it—if we really want to see gangs gone, then we have to address the intergenerational nature of gangs in this country, and address things like my mate Tamatha over here keeps bringing up, like poverty, lack of opportunity, economic marginalisation, and all of those things.
specificity.explanation: Names a direction — tackle intergenerational causes, poverty, lack of opportunity, economic marginalisation — but supplies no mechanism, programme, cost or timeframe.
specificity.subject: speaker

focus.statement: And then, in clause 3 of the bill, there is “reasonable grounds”. What is the definition of “reasonable grounds”?
focus.explanation: Engages the measure before the committee directly, naming a specific clause and the statutory term she wants defined.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Now, if it turns out that a Crusaders cap or beanie means you belong to a particular gang, then it falls within “gang insignia”, even though an ordinary person on a street wouldn’t necessarily look at a person and know.
focus.explanation: Entirely about the drafting of a named definition in the bill before the committee; no party framing at all.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: In terms of the broader question, also in relation to different communities, certainly our expectation is that this legislation will be enforced without any reference to ethnicity but focused on the purpose, which is to reduce the ability of gangs to operate and cause fear, intimidation, and disruption to the public.
focus.explanation: Addresses how the legislation before the committee is to be enforced and what it targets; on the policy, not on the other party.
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: And then, in clause 3 of the bill, there is “reasonable grounds”. What is the definition of “reasonable grounds”?
specificity.explanation: Points to a named clause and a named phrase in the bill; a precise question that could be answered precisely, though it supplies no figures or alternative wording.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Sixty police officers to a tangihanga, throughout Hauraki-Waikato, in rohe like Hauraki, Ngāruawāhia, Whatawhata, having armed checkpoints with M4s, and then on burial day having an Eagle helicopter circling the urupā of a cemetery as karakia commences, as they lower the caskets of their loved ones.
specificity.explanation: Carries a headcount, named locations, named equipment and a described sequence of events — concrete enough for someone to check or respond to.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: In terms of the broader question, also in relation to different communities, certainly our expectation is that this legislation will be enforced without any reference to ethnicity but focused on the purpose, which is to reduce the ability of gangs to operate and cause fear, intimidation, and disruption to the public.
specificity.explanation: States an expectation and a general purpose but offers no mechanism, monitoring, reporting requirement or safeguard by which non-discriminatory enforcement would be secured or checked — the very thing the questions asked for.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Sixty police officers to a tangihanga, throughout Hauraki-Waikato, in rohe like Hauraki, Ngāruawāhia, Whatawhata, having armed checkpoints with M4s, and then on burial day having an Eagle helicopter circling the urupā of a cemetery as karakia commences, as they lower the caskets of their loved ones.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that police deployed roughly sixty officers, armed checkpoints and the Eagle helicopter at tangihanga in the Hauraki-Waikato rohe.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Police operational statements/OIA responses and contemporaneous news coverage (2024) of policing at tangihanga in Hauraki, Ngāruawāhia and Whatawhata; true if deployments of that scale, with armed checkpoints and aerial surveillance over an urupā, are documented, false if police records and reporting show no such deployment.

veracity.statement: But we have to remember that gangs came from the abuse of this State. They came from this House, and we heard that last week.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that New Zealand gangs originated in State abuse, and that this was established in evidence heard the previous week (the Abuse in Care Royal Commission reporting).
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Royal Commission of Inquiry into Abuse in Care final report (July 2024) and peer-reviewed NZ gang histories; true if those sources find State care and State abuse to be a documented origin pathway for NZ gangs, false if they attribute gang formation to unrelated causes or make no such finding.

veracity.statement: I want to assure that member that of course the operational activities of the police are, by law, independent, and no Minister would ever seek to direct the police and how they go about those prosecutions and activities.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that police operational activity is legally independent of ministers.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Policing Act 2008, particularly section 16 on the Commissioner's independence in respect of enforcement decisions and investigations; true if the statute places operational and prosecution decisions beyond ministerial direction, false if ministers have a legal power of direction over those matters.

rigor.statement: Now, if it turns out that a Crusaders cap or beanie means you belong to a particular gang, then it falls within “gang insignia”, even though an ordinary person on a street wouldn’t necessarily look at a person and know.
rigor.explanation: A valid over-breadth argument: applies the bill's own definitional test to a concrete case and shows the result diverges from the stated purpose of preventing intimidation. The conclusion follows from the definition he quoted.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: I want to assure that member that of course the operational activities of the police are, by law, independent, and no Minister would ever seek to direct the police and how they go about those prosecutions and activities.
rigor.explanation: Answers an empirical claim (that police on the ground said they were acting on direction from Wellington) with a statement of legal form. That a direction would be unlawful does not establish that no direction or signal was given — a real gap between premise and conclusion.
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I want to assure that member that of course the operational activities of the police are, by law, independent, and no Minister would ever seek to direct the police and how they go about those prosecutions and activities.
civility.explanation: Directly rebuts a serious allegation about his Government without any sneer, imputation of bad faith, or attack on the member who made it.

divination.statement: Non - gang members, of course, will not be directly affected by this legislation.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that the operation of the gang insignia and related provisions will not directly touch people who are not gang members.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: NZ Police charge and dispersal-notice data plus court decisions under the Gangs Act 2024 in its first two years of operation; true if enforcement actions are recorded essentially only against identified gang members, false if a material number of dispersal notices, stops or charges are recorded against people not identified as gang members.

focus.statement: So I want to pick up firstly on subclause (b), where it says, “providing for the issue of dispersal notices to stop gang members from gathering in public places”. focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Firstly: why the three years? This seems incredibly arbitrary. How on earth would this actually be monitored and how would this be implemented?

focus.statement: So I’d really like him to address the question of the breadth of the definition of insignia and the fact that it captures pieces of clothing, bandanas, jewellery, and, in fact, many, many—an unlimited range of things.

focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: So going back to the definition of immediate family, I wanted to know from the Minister how would one define “culturally recognised”, and, more importantly, who would be the kind of person that determines what is considered to be culturally recognised when it comes to dispersion?

focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: So I want to pick up firstly on subclause (b), where it says, “providing for the issue of dispersal notices to stop gang members from gathering in public places”. I’d love to hear what feedback the Minister has actually had from police about their ability to prevent gang members from gathering in public places, what do the police have to say, and how has that fed into the bill here.
specificity.explanation: Names the exact subclause and quotes its text, and specifies what evidence is sought (police feedback on implementation), though it asks rather than supplies figures or mechanisms.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: So I’d really like him to address the question of the breadth of the definition of insignia and the fact that it captures pieces of clothing, bandanas, jewellery, and, in fact, many, many—an unlimited range of things.
specificity.explanation: Names the defined term at issue and enumerates the categories of item it would capture, though 'an unlimited range of things' is loose and no clause number is given.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: So going back to the definition of immediate family, I wanted to know from the Minister how would one define “culturally recognised”, and, more importantly, who would be the kind of person that determines what is considered to be culturally recognised when it comes to dispersion?
specificity.explanation: Pins down a named term in a named definition and asks two precise, answerable questions (the test, and the decision-maker applying it).

civility.statement: She is obviously not aware that there has been a 50 percent increase in gang membership over the last six years, and that’s not the progress we want to see.
civility.explanation: Answers on the substance but frames it as the member being 'obviously not aware' — a condescending imputation of ignorance to the individual rather than simply contesting her claim. Short of an insult, but it lands on her rather than her argument.
civility.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: She is obviously not aware that there has been a 50 percent increase in gang membership over the last six years, and that’s not the progress we want to see.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that gang membership in New Zealand rose by 50 percent over the six years preceding August 2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Police National Gang List membership counts for 2018 and 2024 (as reported to Parliament / in written question answers); true if the increase over that six-year span is approximately 50 percent or greater, false if materially less.

veracity.statement: We’ve also seen an increase in violent crime in our community by 30 percent, and that is not an increase we want to see.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that violent crime in New Zealand has increased by 30 percent over the period implied (the preceding six years to August 2024).
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Police victimisation statistics and/or the NZ Crime and Victims Survey measure of violent offending/victimisation over roughly 2018–2024; true if the increase is around 30 percent on a recognised violent-crime series, false if materially different or if no series supports it.

veracity.statement: We will have increased the police force by 500 when we reach 10,711 constabulary.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the coalition's '500 more police' commitment is measured against a baseline such that 10,711 constabulary officers equals an increase of 500 (i.e. a baseline of 10,211).
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NZ Police constabulary staffing figures and the Government's stated baseline for the '500 more police' commitment (Police workforce reporting / Minister's statements): true if the baseline is 10,211 constabulary so that 10,711 represents +500, false if the baseline figure differs materially.

veracity.statement: The maths results released on the weekend are absolutely appalling, when four out of five of our children at year 8 are below where they need to be, and three out of five are more than a year behind where they need to be.
veracity.explanation: Two statistical claims about the maths results released in early August 2024: that ~80% of year 8 students are below the expected level, and that ~60% are more than a year behind.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Education Curriculum Insights and Progress Study year 8 mathematics results released in the first week of August 2024: true if roughly 80% are recorded below the expected curriculum level and roughly 60% more than a year behind, false if either proportion is materially different.

veracity.statement: Why should the New Zealand public have confidence in his Government’s reintroduction of boot camps and that they won’t result in a repeat of the shocking abuse highlighted in last week’s royal commission report when his Minister for Children said last week that she cannot guarantee that abuse won’t take place?

veracity.falsification_criterion: Recorded statements by the Minister for Children in the last week of July / first week of August 2024 (Hansard, select committee transcripts or broadcast interviews): true if she declined to guarantee that no abuse would occur, false if no such statement exists or she gave the guarantee.

veracity.statement: Will he assure the public that he will not intervene in any future fast-track resource consent applications, as he did in the case of the redevelopment of a disused petrol station in Cockle Bay, which was being redeveloped into 54 apartments, where his objection was cited as one of the reasons it isn’t going ahead?

veracity.falsification_criterion: Auckland Council resource consent submission records for the Cockle Bay petrol station site and the developer's public statements on why the project was abandoned: true if an objection in the Prime Minister's name is on the record and the developer cited it among the reasons, false if no such objection exists or it was not among the cited reasons.

specificity.statement: In response to this, the Ministry for Regulation is working in three areas: carrying out sector reviews on the stock of existing regulation, preparing a revised regulatory standards bill to uphold standards for new regulatory initiatives, and also improving the culture and workforce of regulatory agencies so that those who apply rules to people in their workplaces are better equipped to help them, rather than hinder them, go to work and get home safely.
specificity.explanation: Names three concrete workstreams and a named bill, but carries no figures, no timeframes and no detail on what the sector reviews or workforce changes actually involve.

specificity.statement: Again, we think charter schools are an important feature of innovation to bring into the education system. They will be held ruthlessly accountable for delivering improved academic achievement, attendance, a number of key metrics, and then left to get on with the job that they need to get on with.

specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Well, I am guaranteeing that we are doing everything we can to turn those lives around.
specificity.explanation: 'Doing everything we can' commits to nothing checkable — no threshold, no safeguard, no measure that anyone could verify or act on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Will he assure the public that he will not intervene in any future fast-track resource consent applications, as he did in the case of the redevelopment of a disused petrol station in Cockle Bay, which was being redeveloped into 54 apartments, where his objection was cited as one of the reasons it isn’t going ahead?
specificity.explanation: Names the site, the prior use, the number of dwellings and the asserted effect of the objection — precise enough that the underlying case can be located and checked.

rigor.statement: Well, in days gone by in this Parliament, you would see spending and money printing completely out of control in a sort of politicised wild west of fiscal and monetary policy. Since then, the Public Finance Act and the Reserve Bank of New Zealand Act have led to some certainty and some consistency in the way that the Government spends and the Reserve Bank operates. We have no such statutory base for the way that the Government regulates people’s private property and its use and exchange.
rigor.explanation: An argument by analogy: statutory frameworks disciplined fiscal and monetary policy, therefore an equivalent statute would discipline regulation. The analogy is coherent and the gap in the statutory landscape is genuinely identified, but nothing is offered to show the two domains are alike enough for the transfer to hold — the conclusion leans on the analogy alone.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Well, again, what I’d say to you is that the royal commission of inquiry report into the boot camps at Aotea Great Barrier are incredibly different from what we are proposing here—completely different. What we’ve got is unvetted and unqualified staff, as that member would have read in that report. Here we have senior psychologists and two social workers working with 10 kids. We had very isolated conditions, appalling conditions. We have a three-month residential programme that involves the family, whānau, siblings, and community organisations from the get-go. On the other hand, it was focused on punishment and also abuse. This is focused on powerful interventions in these young people’s lives to turn them around. And there was no oversight or monitoring, as the member would understand from that reporting, and there is deep monitoring and protection in place under our military-style academies.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion ('incredibly different') is supported point by point — staffing, setting, programme design, oversight — so the inference tracks what is offered. It stops short of the stronger conclusion the question sought (that abuse will therefore not recur), but that stronger claim is not made here.
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: We have an outstanding Minister of Education, Erica Stanford, who has achieved more, I think, in six days than the last member did and the last Government did in six years, and it is more evidence for what Kiwis already know: that this is a Government that is for the parents and also for education.
civility.explanation: Belittles the questioner personally — 'more in six days than the last member did in six years' is a sneer at an individual's worth as a Minister rather than criticism of a decision or policy.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Does the Prime Minister have any reflections, in the wake of the royal commission on abuse in State care, on politicising the grotesque, violent suffering outlined in that report by making comparisons that are totally invalid to something that is actually completely separate?
civility.explanation: Imputes bad faith to the questioner — that he is exploiting victims' suffering for political advantage — rather than contesting the comparison on its merits.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: As I said, they’re incredibly different, and I think it’s disingenuous to compare them.
civility.explanation: 'Disingenuous' imputes deliberate bad faith to the person asking rather than disputing the comparison itself; short of a direct insult but no longer civil.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Look, the member has gotten very petty in Opposition.
civility.explanation: A direct characterisation of the questioner's character rather than any response to the substance of what was asked.
civility.subject: speaker

focus.statement: We have an outstanding Minister of Education, Erica Stanford, who has achieved more, I think, in six days than the last member did and the last Government did in six years, and it is more evidence for what Kiwis already know: that this is a Government that is for the parents and also for education.
focus.explanation: A comparison of parties and personalities with a tagline about who the Government is 'for'; no measure, figure or mechanism is named in this sentence, though the surrounding answer is on education.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Why should the New Zealand public have confidence in his Government’s reintroduction of boot camps and that they won’t result in a repeat of the shocking abuse highlighted in last week’s royal commission report when his Minister for Children said last week that she cannot guarantee that abuse won’t take place?
focus.explanation: Names a specific policy (the reintroduction of boot camps), a specific document (the royal commission report) and a specific ministerial statement. Straightforward scrutiny of a named government programme, with no party-bashing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: One of the big observations of the previous Government was that there were lots of words, lots of post-it notes, lots of strategies, and nothing getting done.
focus.explanation: A generalised jab at the previous government's way of working — no policy, programme, figure or outcome is named, so there is nothing here that could be checked or engaged with.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: In fact, it is the lowest operating allowance since Steven Joyce’s Budget in 2017.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the $2.4 billion Budget 2025 operating allowance is the smallest operating allowance set by any Budget since Budget 2017.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Treasury Budget documents (Fiscal Strategy Report / BEFU) listing the operating allowance set at each Budget from 2017 to 2024; true if the $2.4b Budget 2025 allowance is strictly lower than every allowance from Budget 2018 onward, false if any of those (e.g. Budget 2018's allowance) was equal or lower.

veracity.statement: The Government has pre-committed $1.37 billion per annum against the Budget 2025 allowance to meet forecast demographic, volume, and price pressures for front-line health services delivered by Health New Zealand.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a specific pre-commitment of $1.37 billion per annum from the Budget 2025 allowance to Health New Zealand for cost pressures.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2024/2025 Treasury and Vote Health documents recording pre-commitments against the Budget 2025 operating allowance; true if a health pre-commitment of ~$1.37b per annum is recorded, false if the recorded figure is materially different or no such pre-commitment exists.

veracity.statement: Because if that member wants to contend that every dollar of public money being used today is always being used wisely, then I would invite her to reflect on this: in the last Budget, our Government found $23 billion of savings and reprioritisation—that’s $5.9 billion every year over the next four years—and it only took us a few months to find it.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Budget 2024 identified $23 billion of savings and reprioritisation, averaging $5.9 billion per year across the four-year forecast period.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2024 Treasury savings and reprioritisation tables; true if total savings/reprioritisation over the forecast period is ~$23b (~$5.9b p.a.), false if materially lower or if the figure includes items not classified as savings or reprioritisation.

veracity.statement: Can the Minister promise that her operating allowance, which is $100 million lower than Treasury says is necessary just to keep the lights on in this country, will not result in front-line service cuts?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Treasury's estimate of the allowance required to maintain existing services exceeds the Government's $2.4 billion allowance by $100 million.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Treasury Budget Economic and Fiscal Update / Budget Policy Statement estimate of the operating allowance needed to meet existing cost pressures; true if that estimate is ~$2.5b against a $2.4b allowance, false if Treasury's stated figure differs materially from a $100m gap.

veracity.statement: The latest maths data shows that just 8 percent—8 percent—of children in our lowest-decile schools are at curriculum in maths in year 8, and we can and will do so much better than that.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that in the most recent maths achievement data, 8 percent of year 8 students in the lowest-decile schools are at the curriculum level.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Curriculum Insights and Progress Study / NMSSA year 8 mathematics results broken down by school decile or equity index; true if the lowest-decile at-curriculum rate is ~8%, false if materially different.

veracity.statement: What I accept is that four out of five of our kids not being where they need to be at year 8 and three out of five being more than a year behind is utterly unacceptable, and we make no apologies for focusing the education system around academic achievement.
veracity.explanation: Asserts two achievement proportions: four in five year 8 students below the expected standard, and three in five more than a year behind.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Education Curriculum Insights and Progress Study year 8 results; true if roughly 80% are below curriculum expectation and roughly 60% are more than one year behind, false if either proportion is materially different.

veracity.statement: I’d just also say the Treasury advised us, in the changes in the last Budget, that we will lift 17,000 children out of poverty.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Treasury advice on the Budget 2024 package projected 17,000 children lifted out of poverty.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2024 Treasury child poverty impact analysis / Child Poverty Report; true if Treasury's published estimate for the Budget package is ~17,000 children, false if the figure differs materially or no such Treasury estimate exists.

veracity.statement: Is she aware that since KiwiRail contracted for the ferries, the price of new ships has risen by 50 percent in US dollars; and can she guarantee the new ferries and sunk costs from cancelling the ferries will be less than $2 billion?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that newbuild ship prices in US dollars have risen 50 percent since KiwiRail signed the Hyundai Mipo contract.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Clarksons Research newbuilding price index (USD) from the 2021 contract signing to mid-2024; true if the index rose approximately 50%, false if materially lower or higher.

veracity.statement: Is she aware the E-Flexer ferries the ministerial advisory group recommends are at least 50 percent larger than the largest current ferry, and will need new wharves and infrastructure, meaning she will have to make most of the land-side investments that she cancelled under the Cook Strait ferry project?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the ministerial advisory group recommends E-Flexer class ferries and that these are at least 50 percent larger than the largest ferry currently operating on Cook Strait.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The ministerial advisory group report on Cook Strait ferry replacement once published, plus published E-Flexer specifications compared with the Kaitaki's gross tonnage/length; true if E-Flexers are recommended and are ≥50% larger on the stated measure, false otherwise.

specificity.statement: The Government has pre-committed $1.37 billion per annum against the Budget 2025 allowance to meet forecast demographic, volume, and price pressures for front-line health services delivered by Health New Zealand.
specificity.explanation: Names the exact pre-commitment figure, the period, the recipient agency and the purpose — fully checkable against Budget documents.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Despite some members predicting that the sky would fall in if the Government made any savings whatsoever, we found that $5.9 billion per year so that we could direct it to higher-value uses—things like 500 additional police, things like Gumboot Friday, things like new classrooms and maintaining our existing classrooms—and I am confident that across the public sector there are many more savings and re-prioritisation opportunities.
specificity.explanation: Carries a per-annum savings figure and several named spending destinations, though the further savings opportunities are asserted without amounts or areas.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Can the Minister promise that her operating allowance, which is $100 million lower than Treasury says is necessary just to keep the lights on in this country, will not result in front-line service cuts?
specificity.explanation: A precise question: names the allowance, quantifies the shortfall against a named source, and asks for a specific guarantee.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The latest maths data shows that just 8 percent—8 percent—of children in our lowest-decile schools are at curriculum in maths in year 8, and we can and will do so much better than that.
specificity.explanation: A precise, sourced-style figure tied to a named cohort and year level.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We want the legislation to make sure it protects the wellbeing and the interests of our children above and beyond anything else and is unambiguous doing so.
specificity.explanation: Asked what a named statutory provision currently does, the reply supplies only generic aims — no mechanism, no description of the section, no change detailed.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Is she aware that since KiwiRail contracted for the ferries, the price of new ships has risen by 50 percent in US dollars; and can she guarantee the new ferries and sunk costs from cancelling the ferries will be less than $2 billion?
specificity.explanation: Quantifies both the claimed price movement and the cost threshold the guarantee is sought against.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Is she aware that procuring new ferries that are not rail-enabled will cost $150 to $200 per container; and is putting that extra cost on Kiwi businesses a priority for her Government?
specificity.explanation: Puts a concrete per-unit cost range on the consequence of a specific procurement choice.
specificity.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Well, I think the member clearly drafted her question before she listened to the answers to my earlier supplementaries, because the key point here is that in order to meet cost pressures, we will need to find savings elsewhere.
civility.explanation: Opens by characterising the questioner as not listening and working from a pre-written script — a sneer at the member rather than at her argument, though it stops short of a direct insult before moving to substance.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I’d say to that member, if she cares about equality of opportunity, get on board and back these changes.
civility.explanation: Conditional framing that puts the member's commitment to equality of opportunity in question rather than engaging her point; pointed and personal but short of a direct insult.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Does the Prime Minister see any problem at all with his coalition agreement promise to make decisions based on data and evidence, and his complete inability to produce any data and evidence about why he wants to remove the section of the Oranga Tamariki Act which does the bare minimum on upholding Te Tiriti o Waitangi?
civility.explanation: "His complete inability" shifts from the missing evidence to the Prime Minister's personal capacity; robust and edging onto the person while still anchored to the policy.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: First, the member is making a series of assertions about a report that is not in the public domain, and I would suggest to her she be very careful about whether or not the sources she is getting her information from are providing her with accurate, fully contextualised information, because it will eventually go to her credibility if she makes assertions in this House that are incorrect.
civility.explanation: Rather than answering the substance, warns the member about her personal credibility — an attack on the questioner's standing dressed as advice.
civility.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Because if that member wants to contend that every dollar of public money being used today is always being used wisely, then I would invite her to reflect on this: in the last Budget, our Government found $23 billion of savings and reprioritisation—that’s $5.9 billion every year over the next four years—and it only took us a few months to find it.
rigor.explanation: Strawman: the question asked for a guarantee against front-line cuts, not the claim that every dollar is spent wisely. The savings evidence rebuts a position the member never took, so the conclusion does not answer the inference actually at issue.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: That does not mean that we won’t strive to find new and better ways to deliver public services, and sometimes that will entail change. Because the alternative is that we accept that every service being delivered by a public agency today is being delivered the best way.
rigor.explanation: False dichotomy: the options offered are her programme of change or accepting that every current service is delivered optimally, when many intermediate positions exist.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Does the Prime Minister see any problem at all with his coalition agreement promise to make decisions based on data and evidence, and his complete inability to produce any data and evidence about why he wants to remove the section of the Oranga Tamariki Act which does the bare minimum on upholding Te Tiriti o Waitangi?
focus.explanation: Names a specific commitment (the coalition agreement's evidence-based decision-making clause) and a specific measure (repeal of section 7AA), and tests one against the other — squarely policy scrutiny, not party framing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Is she aware the E-Flexer ferries the ministerial advisory group recommends are at least 50 percent larger than the largest current ferry, and will need new wharves and infrastructure, meaning she will have to make most of the land-side investments that she cancelled under the Cook Strait ferry project?
focus.explanation: Engages the mechanism directly — the recommended vessel class, its dimensions, and the landside consequence for cancelled infrastructure investment.
focus.subject: speaker

divination.statement: On the advice I have received to date, I can be very confident that the cost of delivering new ferries will be less than the projected cost of the failed and flawed project iReX, even when sunk costs are taken into account.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that the total cost of the replacement ferry programme, including sunk costs from cancelling iReX, will come in below iReX's projected cost.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Final/updated Crown cost estimates for the replacement Cook Strait ferry programme (Ferry Holdings / Treasury) including landside works and iReX sunk and cancellation costs, compared with the last published iReX projected cost (~$3b); true if the replacement total is lower, false if it equals or exceeds it.

civility.statement: Again, the member is, unfortunately, making assertions without grounding in fact.
civility.explanation: Pointed and dismissive of the member's contribution, but the charge is about the factual basis of her assertions rather than her character; edges toward the person without landing on them.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: What it actually says—what it actually says—is that gas production is 20 percent down, and the result and the blame for that degradation of gas resilience can be laid at the feet of that Prime Minister and that Minister, who, in thinking that they were going to enjoy the political upside of the term “a nuclear moment”, cancelled the gas industry in New Zealand.
civility.explanation: Imputes a self-serving motive to two named individuals — that they acted for the 'political upside' of a phrase rather than on the merits. Short of a direct insult, but it attributes bad faith to the people rather than criticising the decision.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: If the member had listened to any of the answers that I gave before, she will have understood.
civility.explanation: Condescension: rather than answering, it suggests the questioner was not paying attention. The jab is at the member's conduct in the House, not at the substance of her question.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: But can I just say, if the member can’t understand the gravity of 22 percent, she received, when she was the Minister, 42 percent, and what happened under her watch? Absolutely nothing.
civility.explanation: A personal attack: it questions the member's capacity to understand a figure and charges her personally with having done 'absolutely nothing' in office, rather than criticising the previous policy settings.
civility.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: So I would point this out to the member: she is now in the position of defending a project which blew out to a total cost of at least $3 billion.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the iReX Cook Strait ferry project's total estimated cost had escalated to at least $3 billion.
veracity.subject: other
veracity.falsification_criterion: Treasury / KiwiRail / Ministerial advice on the iReX project's total estimated cost at the point of cancellation in December 2023; true if the documented total project estimate was $3 billion or more, false if the best documented estimate was materially below $3 billion.

veracity.statement: Now, the cost of that project, members—only a tiny percentage, around 21 percent, was actually for the cost of ships; the rest of it was all for building berths and facilities that were big enough to take ships.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that vessels accounted for roughly 21 percent of the iReX project's total cost, with the remainder being landside port infrastructure.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The iReX project cost breakdown in KiwiRail/Treasury documentation; true if vessel costs are approximately 21% of the total project estimate, false if the vessel share is materially different (e.g. above 35% or below 10%).

veracity.statement: Second, I’d just like to make this point to the House: today, yesterday, and the day before, there were crossings by the Bluebridge ferry company that were on time and reliable.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Bluebridge sailings on the three days up to 6 August 2024 all ran on time and reliably.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Bluebridge/StraitNZ published sailing schedules, cancellation notices and contemporaneous news reports for 4–6 August 2024; true if no Bluebridge Cook Strait sailings were cancelled or materially delayed on those days, false if any were.

veracity.statement: What it actually says—what it actually says—is that gas production is 20 percent down, and the result and the blame for that degradation of gas resilience can be laid at the feet of that Prime Minister and that Minister, who, in thinking that they were going to enjoy the political upside of the term “a nuclear moment”, cancelled the gas industry in New Zealand.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Gas Industry Co. quarterly report released that day records gas production down 20 percent.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Gas Industry Co. quarterly gas production report current at 6 August 2024; true if it reports production approximately 20% down on the comparison period, false if the reported decline is materially different.

veracity.statement: Not only is the ongoing availability of gas and, sadly, Indonesian coal—how perverse that those people who thought that they would improve energy resilience in New Zealand are now reduced to requiring ongoing imports of Indonesian coal.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that New Zealand is currently relying on ongoing imports of Indonesian coal.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ merchandise import statistics for coal by country of origin, and Genesis Energy disclosures on Huntly coal sourcing, 2023–2024; true if substantial ongoing coal imports from Indonesia are recorded, false if imports were negligible or from other origins.

veracity.statement: Data from the Curriculum Insights and Progress Study show that just 22 percent of year 8 students in New Zealand are at the expected curriculum benchmark in year 8 for mathematics, and it showed that just 12 percent of Māori students were where they should be and that 63 percent of the overall year 8 cohort are more than a year behind.
veracity.explanation: Asserts three specific figures from the Curriculum Insights and Progress Study: 22% of year 8 students at curriculum benchmark in maths, 12% of Māori students, and 63% more than a year behind.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The 2024 Curriculum Insights and Progress Study (CIPS) mathematics report; true if the published figures match 22%, 12% and 63% for those cohorts, false if materially different.

veracity.statement: Does she agree with the Curriculum Insights and Progress Study from Otago University and the New Zealand Council for Educational Research (NZCER), which says trend data from the National Monitoring Study of Student Achievement (NMSSA) indicates that at year 8 there has been no statistically significant change in mathematics achievement scores since at least 2013; and if so, why is her data so different, when the NMSSA also measured in a single year—not, as she said earlier, in a multi-year band?
veracity.explanation: Relays a claim attributed to the CIPS/NZCER report: that NMSSA trend data shows no statistically significant change in year 8 mathematics achievement since at least 2013, and that NMSSA measured a single year level rather than multi-year bands.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The CIPS 2024 report and the NMSSA year 8 mathematics trend reports (2013 onwards); true if the trend analysis reports no statistically significant change at year 8 and NMSSA sampled a single year level, false if a significant change is reported or NMSSA used multi-year bands.

veracity.statement: But can I just say, if the member can’t understand the gravity of 22 percent, she received, when she was the Minister, 42 percent, and what happened under her watch? Absolutely nothing.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the member, as Minister of Education, received a figure of 42 percent on a comparable measure of year 8 mathematics achievement.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: NMSSA/Ministry of Education year 8 mathematics achievement reporting provided to the Minister of Education during Jan Tinetti's tenure (2023); true if a figure of approximately 42% at curriculum level was reported to her, false if no such figure exists or it is materially different.

specificity.statement: Now, the cost of that project, members—only a tiny percentage, around 21 percent, was actually for the cost of ships; the rest of it was all for building berths and facilities that were big enough to take ships.
specificity.explanation: Gives a named proportion (21 percent) and identifies precisely what the balance was spent on — checkable against the project cost breakdown.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Is it prudent financial management for her to cancel the Cook Strait ferry project with no alternative plan, to have no idea what the contract break fees would be, and to have no idea how much alternative ferries and infrastructure would cost?
specificity.explanation: Identifies the measure and three concrete categories of unknown cost, but supplies no figures or dates of its own.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I recently announced that a study of New Zealand’s fuel security, including investigating the reopening of the Marsden Point refinery, is getting under way, as per the coalition agreement.
specificity.explanation: Names the specific action (a fuel security study), its scope (reopening Marsden Point) and its origin (the coalition agreement), but gives no timeframe, budget or terms of reference.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Additional work will take place to ensure that the energy settings, the electrical industry settings, are such that it gives a greater level of competitiveness, and we will stand with industry and ensure that industry is not monstered by green termites nibbling away at our economic capital.
specificity.explanation: 'Additional work' on 'energy settings' to deliver 'a greater level of competitiveness' — no mechanism, no figure, no timeframe and no named policy. Nothing here could be checked or acted on.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: This Government has announced four immediate interventions as part of our Make It Count maths action plan to turn around our poor results. We’re accelerating the shift to a new maths curriculum next year. To support teachers, we are delivering targeted professional development focused on structured maths for primary and intermediate teachers, alongside providing quality resources aligned to the curriculum. Thirdly, there will be twice-yearly assessments for maths in primary school, for years 3 to 8, starting from next year so that we can provide the support where needed.
specificity.explanation: Named programme, a counted set of interventions, the year levels covered (years 3 to 8), the assessment frequency and the start date. Each element is checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Data from the Curriculum Insights and Progress Study show that just 22 percent of year 8 students in New Zealand are at the expected curriculum benchmark in year 8 for mathematics, and it showed that just 12 percent of Māori students were where they should be and that 63 percent of the overall year 8 cohort are more than a year behind.
specificity.explanation: A named study and three precise percentages tied to a named year level and cohort — directly checkable against the source.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: As part of this announcement, $20 million is being made available within the professional learning and development budget to build confidence and capability in our teaching workforce.
specificity.explanation: A named dollar figure attached to a named budget line and a stated purpose, though without a timeframe or breakdown of how the funding is allocated.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Does she agree with the Curriculum Insights and Progress Study from Otago University and the New Zealand Council for Educational Research (NZCER), which says trend data from the National Monitoring Study of Student Achievement (NMSSA) indicates that at year 8 there has been no statistically significant change in mathematics achievement scores since at least 2013; and if so, why is her data so different, when the NMSSA also measured in a single year—not, as she said earlier, in a multi-year band?
specificity.explanation: Names two research institutions, two named studies, the year level, the statistical test and the baseline year — a precise, checkable challenge.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: It’s an excellent question, and for the first time, what we are seeing is a Government who have an excellent relationship with kura kaupapa, who have set aside multiple tens of millions—in fact, $100 million—to make sure that we are building more classrooms and redeveloping more kura kaupapa schools.
specificity.explanation: Supplies a named figure ($100 million) and the purposes it is directed to (classrooms and kura kaupapa redevelopment), but no timeframe, no number of classrooms and no allocation detail.
specificity.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Is it prudent financial management for her to cancel the Cook Strait ferry project with no alternative plan, to have no idea what the contract break fees would be, and to have no idea how much alternative ferries and infrastructure would cost?
focus.explanation: Names a specific decision (cancellation of the Cook Strait ferry project) and three specific gaps — alternative plan, break fees, replacement costs. This is scrutiny of a named policy, not party-bashing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Now, this study, it may come to pass, does not find favour with those who do not support the business community—they sit on the other side of the House, not with me.
focus.explanation: Abandons the substance of the study to characterise the parties opposite as anti-business. No mechanism, cost, figure or outcome is named — the content is entirely about the other team.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Additional work will take place to ensure that the energy settings, the electrical industry settings, are such that it gives a greater level of competitiveness, and we will stand with industry and ensure that industry is not monstered by green termites nibbling away at our economic capital.
focus.explanation: Begins on the policy (energy settings) but the weight of the sentence is a characterisation of environmental opponents as 'green termites' rather than any policy content.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Does she agree with the Curriculum Insights and Progress Study from Otago University and the New Zealand Council for Educational Research (NZCER), which says trend data from the National Monitoring Study of Student Achievement (NMSSA) indicates that at year 8 there has been no statistically significant change in mathematics achievement scores since at least 2013; and if so, why is her data so different, when the NMSSA also measured in a single year—not, as she said earlier, in a multi-year band?
focus.explanation: Squarely on the evidence base for the Minister's announcement, testing a named dataset against a named claim. Textbook scrutiny of a specific policy justification.
focus.subject: speaker

divination.statement: The internal combustion engine is not going anywhere in a hurry. No doubt, we will see a slow growth in electrical vehicles, the growth of which will be determined by investment in the electricity system, and work is under way to ensure that our electricity system does not contain any deficiencies that might impede competitiveness.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that electric vehicle uptake in New Zealand will grow only slowly, with internal combustion vehicles remaining dominant.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: NZTA motor vehicle registration statistics for the light fleet, 2024–2026; true if annual EV/PHEV new registrations grow slowly or decline and EVs remain a small minority of the light fleet, false if EV registrations grow rapidly (e.g. more than doubling annually) or EVs reach a substantial share of new registrations.

rigor.statement: What it actually says—what it actually says—is that gas production is 20 percent down, and the result and the blame for that degradation of gas resilience can be laid at the feet of that Prime Minister and that Minister, who, in thinking that they were going to enjoy the political upside of the term “a nuclear moment”, cancelled the gas industry in New Zealand.
rigor.explanation: Post hoc reasoning: a 20 percent production decline is attributed wholly to the 2018 exploration ban with nothing offered to connect them — no account of field decline at existing fields or of the lead times over which exploration affects production.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Her Māori students are now achieving at the same rate and, in some cases, above the average students in her school for the first time. This announcement is just one step towards closing the equity gap across New Zealand, giving our children every opportunity to succeed and setting New Zealand up for future prosperity.
rigor.explanation: Appeal to anecdote: results at two individual schools are generalised to a nationwide closing of the equity gap, with no control, no comparison group and no account of what else differs at those schools.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Is it her plan to achieve the Prime Minister’s target of 20,000 fewer victims of crime simply by making it harder for victims to report family violence and even harder for them to get the help they need?
focus.explanation: Names a specific government commitment (the 20,000 fewer victims of crime target) and a specific policy consequence (family violence reporting and support), so this is scrutiny of a named policy rather than generic party-bashing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: The Government has begun a six-week period of consultation on the proposed reforms for New Zealand’s vocational education and training system. We propose to replace the top-heavy, centralised Te Pūkenga with a network of regional institutes of technology and polytechnics and an industry training system that is closer to industry.
focus.explanation: Entirely on the substance of the vocational education reform proposal — the mechanism and the institutional change — with no reference to opposing parties.
focus.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Is it her plan to achieve the Prime Minister’s target of 20,000 fewer victims of crime simply by making it harder for victims to report family violence and even harder for them to get the help they need?
civility.explanation: Framed as a question about policy, but the wording imputes to the Minister a deliberate plan to hit a target by obstructing victims — an imputation of bad faith rather than a purely substantive challenge. Falls short of a direct personal insult.
civility.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: My role is just to facilitate all the Government agencies. What happens after that is the responsibility of the individual Ministers.
specificity.explanation: States a direction (her role is facilitation, delivery sits with portfolio Ministers) but names no agency, mechanism, process or timeframe by which that facilitation happens.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The Government has begun a six-week period of consultation on the proposed reforms for New Zealand’s vocational education and training system. We propose to replace the top-heavy, centralised Te Pūkenga with a network of regional institutes of technology and polytechnics and an industry training system that is closer to industry.
specificity.explanation: Gives a defined consultation period (six weeks), the named entity to be disestablished (Te Pūkenga) and the proposed replacement structure (regional ITPs plus an industry training system). Checkable and actionable, though no dollar figures or implementation dates.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: These proposals will put the vocational education and training system on a sustainable path and restore accountability and responsibility to communities and industries while removing unnecessary complexity and bureaucracy.
specificity.explanation: A string of generic virtues — sustainability, accountability, responsibility, less bureaucracy — with no figure, mechanism, threshold or date attached to any of them.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: The Government has begun a six-week period of consultation on the proposed reforms for New Zealand’s vocational education and training system. We propose to replace the top-heavy, centralised Te Pūkenga with a network of regional institutes of technology and polytechnics and an industry training system that is closer to industry.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that as at this statement the Government had opened a six-week consultation on vocational education and training reform proposing to replace Te Pūkenga with regional polytechnics and a separate industry training system.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Education / Tertiary Education Commission consultation documents and the Minister's August 2024 announcement on the future of vocational education: true if a public consultation of approximately six weeks was open at that date and the discussion document proposes disestablishing Te Pūkenga in favour of regional ITPs and an industry training arrangement; false if no such consultation was open, if the period was materially different from six weeks, or if the proposals do not include replacing Te Pūkenga.

veracity.statement: Ms Genter wrote to us on 16 May 2024, apologising for her actions in the Chamber.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Julie Anne Genter sent the Privileges Committee a written apology for her chamber conduct, dated 16 May 2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Privileges Committee's 2024 report on the conduct of Hon Julie Anne Genter during the committee of the whole House and its appended correspondence: true if the report records a written submission from Genter dated 16 May 2024 containing an apology for her actions; false if no such letter exists, is dated materially differently, or contains no apology.

rigor.statement: In answer to the first part of the question, yes, in the context in which I said it, which was in relation to the proposed Oranga Tamariki organisational restructure. In answer to the second part of the question, because it’s not an option to keep the status quo. To do so would say we’re happy with how the organisation is running now and delivering for children—and we know it’s not.
rigor.explanation: False dichotomy: the argument presents only two options — the proposed restructure or endorsing the status quo — and treats any reluctance to restructure as contentment with current performance. Nothing is offered to exclude alternative reforms.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: What I would say is that since I’ve started as the children’s Minister, I have always made it very clear that the best interests and the safety of the children should be at the forefront of every decision made, whether you’re Māori, non-Māori, or any ethnicity in this country, because I’m sick to death of us accepting the fact that we lose one baby every five weeks in this country to the hands of somebody who is supposed to care about them.
rigor.explanation: Appeal to emotion: the stated reason for the position is the speaker's exasperation plus a death statistic, neither of which connects to the question about whether repealing 7AA serves Ngāpuhi tamariki. The conclusion does not follow from what is offered.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Yes, the hard-working member for Rangitīkei has passed on to me that as she meets with retailers in her communities, the feedback has been extraordinary. Everyone is delighted to see police back on the beat and keeping our community safe.
rigor.explanation: Appeal to anecdote and hasty generalisation: second-hand reports relayed by a government colleague are offered as grounds for the universal conclusion that 'everyone is delighted' and that communities have benefited.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: I’d just like to say, police will always play a role when it comes to responding to violence, including family violence or where there has been a crime where someone is in immediate danger. But I would also like to remind them that it’s important to note that the six-month proof of concept trial for this was trialled by the previous Government before we even began this. So this is something that the previous Government was on board with and I would expect they still will be.
rigor.explanation: The inference — that the previous Government was 'on board' because it ran the proof-of-concept trial — is reasonable but leaps from piloting a concept to endorsing the rolled-out policy; trialling something is not the same as supporting its adoption.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: In answer to the first part of the question, yes, in the context in which I said it, which was in relation to the proposed Oranga Tamariki organisational restructure. In answer to the second part of the question, because it’s not an option to keep the status quo. To do so would say we’re happy with how the organisation is running now and delivering for children—and we know it’s not.
focus.explanation: Squarely engages the measure at issue (the proposed Oranga Tamariki restructure) and gives a reason for it; no party framing at all.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: If his primary concern is prioritising “health and wellbeing of the individual child”, why doesn’t he strengthen section 4A of the Oranga Tamariki Act, which makes it clear that “well-being and best interests of the child or young person are the first and paramount consideration”, instead of repealing section 7AA?
focus.explanation: Entirely about the legislative mechanism before the House — a named section, its wording, and the alternative to repeal. No party framing.
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Is cutting $120 million in community prevention services, like Family Start, the change that community organisations have called for when Social Service Providers Aotearoa chief executive Belinda Himiona is saying that providers are very worried that child safety and that whānau wellbeing is going to be impacted by these reductions?
specificity.explanation: Carries a dollar figure, a named programme (Family Start), a named organisation and a named chief executive — all checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The maths achievement data released on the weekend was deeply concerning, especially for the just 12 percent of young Māori who are not at curriculum in maths at year 8, according to the data from last year. Shockingly, 76 percent were more than a year behind.
specificity.explanation: Two precise percentages tied to a named cohort (year 8 Māori students), a subject, and a dated data release — fully checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Well, no Government can guarantee that, but they can do everything they possibly can to make sure there is protection and safeguards in place for our children. These are our most vulnerable children. We want powerful, targeted interventions, and we’re putting huge amounts of service around them to make sure that they are safe.
specificity.explanation: Asked about safeguards in boot camps, the answer offers only 'protection and safeguards', 'powerful, targeted interventions' and 'huge amounts of service' — no mechanism, no funding figure, no named safeguard.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: If his primary concern is prioritising “health and wellbeing of the individual child”, why doesn’t he strengthen section 4A of the Oranga Tamariki Act, which makes it clear that “well-being and best interests of the child or young person are the first and paramount consideration”, instead of repealing section 7AA?
specificity.explanation: Names two specific statutory provisions, quotes the operative wording of one, and poses a precise alternative course of action.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We want the immediate safety, stability, and wellbeing of a child to be at the heart of what the Government does, caring for our most vulnerable children—period.
specificity.explanation: Answering a question about a specific statutory section, this offers only a string of generic aspirations — no mechanism, no provision, no commitment anyone could check.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Well, following a central Wellington retailer reporting a woman putting clothing in her bag, early last month, the beat team responded swiftly. They apprehended the woman, who turned out to be a prolific shoplifter with over $1,000 worth of products on her person from several of the other shops in the area. A store manager contacted police and provided highly complimentary feedback on the beat initiative, the visibility of police staff, and the timely response she received.
specificity.explanation: A concrete, dated, located incident with a dollar value attached — checkable detail, though it describes one case rather than any programme-level measure.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: In answer to the first part of the question, yes. In answer to the second part of the question, the Government is currently working on the second action plan to implement Te Aorerekura, the 25-year strategy to address family and sexual violence in this country. This action plan is expected to be published in the last quarter of 2024, and this will help drive collective efforts and investment decisions across Government in the family violence and sexual violence space. Family violence and sexual violence are an important component of the Government target to reduce violent crime by having 20 percent fewer people be the victims of assaults, robberies, and sexual assaults by 2029.
specificity.explanation: Names the strategy, the deliverable (second action plan), a publication timeframe (last quarter of 2024) and a quantified target with a date (20 percent fewer victims by 2029).
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Why, then, has there been a reduction in victimisations where the offender is known to the victim, by 24 percent since December last year?
specificity.explanation: A precise percentage against a defined measure (victimisations where the offender is known to the victim) with a stated baseline date.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: What would the Minister say to Teresea Olsen from Kokiri Marae, one of the only 7AA partners to have the status of chief executive over tamariki, who has just found out that they have lost $1.5 million in contracts with Oranga Tamariki and is stripping community providers on the ground already working with whānau of funding what change looks like to her?
specificity.explanation: Names an individual, an organisation, its statutory status under 7AA and a dollar figure for the contracts lost — checkable, though the sentence is garbled at the end.
specificity.subject: speaker
