civility.statement: Yes, which is why the official invitation to Matariki contained te reo Māori—as I have here—entitled “Mānawa maiea te Mātahi o te Tau” [“Arise the New Year”], and he would know this if he’d checked with his leader, the Rt Hon Chris Hipkins, who received one of the invitations and declined to come.
civility.explanation: Substantively answers with the document, but the closing clause is a dig at the questioner's failure to do his homework — pointed and slightly belittling without being a personal insult.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: No, I wasn’t aware of that quote, and I must say I’m amazed that that member thinks that this is a matter that deserves an urgent debate in the House and that my writing to an Australian Minister is a matter of such interest.
civility.explanation: 'I’m amazed that that member thinks' is condescension directed at the questioner's judgement rather than at the argument, though it stops well short of a direct insult.
civility.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Well, because gang membership increased by 51 percent in the previous six years and, at the same time, violent crime in our communities had gone up by 33 percent.
specificity.explanation: Two precise percentage figures over a named time window, both of which someone could go and check against published statistics.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: In answer to the second part of the question, they deserve a Minister that will fight for better health outcomes, and this Minister is fighting for better health outcomes by delivering a transformative investment in cancer treatments for New Zealanders.
specificity.explanation: Repeats the questioner's framing with an unquantified 'transformative investment'; no figure, mechanism or timeframe is supplied at this point in the answer.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I was pleased to announce yesterday that wait times for New Zealand passports have halved, and New Zealanders should now allow up to five weeks for a standard New Zealand passport, down from a peak of 10 weeks.
specificity.explanation: Gives the current advertised wait time (five weeks) against a stated peak (10 weeks) — concrete and checkable against the department's published guidance.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: For context, 11,598 photos were rejected by the Passport Office in February alone this year, which delays the application process.
specificity.explanation: An exact count for a named month from a named agency — precise enough that it could be checked or acted on directly.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Based on their own quarterly reports and our internal review of all Family Start contracts between 2022 and January 2024, they achieved, on average, 80 percent of the whānau volumes, lower numbers of home visits than were expected, and based on this information, we have reduced their fulltime-equivalents (FTEs) from 12.75 to 10.
specificity.explanation: Names the evidence source, the review period, the delivery percentage and the exact before-and-after FTE numbers.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: How does she reconcile this commitment to no reduction in front-line services with Family Start losing 40 percent of their front-line staff due to their funding being cut by $14 million per year, compromising their ability to support at-risk infants in Nelson?
specificity.explanation: A named programme, a percentage staff loss, a dollar figure per year and a named region — a precise question, as checkable as a precise answer.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Yes, and to name a few reasons why, in 2023 all previous Institutes of Technology and Polytechnics of New Zealand (ITPs) individual business units recorded deficits, with at least three recording deficits in excess of $20 million and all but two previous ITP individual business units forecasting deficits in 2025.
specificity.explanation: Names the year, the entities, a dollar threshold and counts of business units in deficit — detailed enough to be checked against Te Pūkenga's financial reporting.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Why, then, in the regulatory impact statement prepared by her own officials, does the Minister’s preferred option rank as “worse” than the status quo when it comes to system sustainability and to learner and employer needs?
specificity.explanation: Cites a named document and the specific criteria on which it ranks the preferred option, quoting the ranking term used.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Well, because gang membership increased by 51 percent in the previous six years and, at the same time, violent crime in our communities had gone up by 33 percent.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a 51% rise in gang membership over the previous six years and a 33% rise in violent crime over the same period.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Police National Gang List membership numbers for the six years to 2023 (true if the increase is ~51%), and the NZ Crime and Victims Survey / Police victimisation data for violent offences over the same period (true if ~33% rise). Materially different figures would make it false.

veracity.statement: I’m pleased to see that Health New Zealand has taken a pragmatic approach informed by clinical advice to deliver these treatments, thanks to the Government’s transformative investment to deliver up to 26 cancer treatments.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the Government's investment delivers up to 26 cancer treatments.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Government's/Pharmac's June 2024 cancer medicines funding announcement: true if the announced package covers up to 26 cancer treatments, false if the number of treatments funded is materially different.

veracity.statement: Is it correct that documents released under the Official Information Act show he did not progress work on his original promise to fund cancer medicines to a Cabinet paper until public backlash against the Budget, and don’t New Zealanders deserve a Minister that will fight for better healthcare for them?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that OIA documents show no Cabinet paper work on the cancer medicines promise until after public backlash against Budget 2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The OIA-released Ministry of Health / Minister's office documents on the cancer medicines commitment: true if the first Cabinet paper progressing the promise is dated after the post-Budget 2024 (30 May 2024) public reaction, false if Cabinet work on it is documented before that reaction.

veracity.statement: I was pleased to announce yesterday that wait times for New Zealand passports have halved, and New Zealanders should now allow up to five weeks for a standard New Zealand passport, down from a peak of 10 weeks.
veracity.explanation: Asserts passport wait times halved from a 10-week peak to up to five weeks.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Department of Internal Affairs published passport processing guidance and its 2024 wait-time series: true if the advertised standard passport wait was reduced to about five weeks in August 2024 from a peak of about 10 weeks, false if either figure is materially different.

veracity.statement: How does she reconcile this commitment to no reduction in front-line services with Family Start losing 40 percent of their front-line staff due to their funding being cut by $14 million per year, compromising their ability to support at-risk infants in Nelson?
veracity.explanation: Asserts a $14 million per year funding cut to Family Start and a consequent 40 percent loss of front-line staff.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Oranga Tamariki Family Start contract and funding records for 2024: true if the national Family Start funding reduction is about $14 million per year and front-line staffing fell by about 40%, false if the reduction or the staffing change is materially different.

veracity.statement: Does cutting funding for Family Start Nelson meet her expectations for Oranga Tamariki’s savings initiative, when evaluation found that their programme reduced overall post-neonatal mortality in the first year of life by 42 percent, and, if not, why is Family Start facing these cuts?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that an evaluation of Family Start found a 42 percent reduction in post-neonatal mortality in the first year of life.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The published evaluation of the Family Start programme (Ministry of Social Development / Vaithianathan et al.): true if it reports an approximately 42% reduction in post-neonatal mortality in the first year of life, false if no such finding or a materially different figure appears.

veracity.statement: Further, Te Pūkenga has overseen a 9 percent decline in domestic enrolments.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a 9 percent fall in domestic enrolments under Te Pūkenga.
veracity.subject: other
veracity.falsification_criterion: Tertiary Education Commission / Te Pūkenga domestic enrolment data from the merger to 2024: true if domestic enrolments fell by about 9%, false if the decline is materially smaller or enrolments rose.

veracity.statement: Why, then, in the regulatory impact statement prepared by her own officials, does the Minister’s preferred option rank as “worse” than the status quo when it comes to system sustainability and to learner and employer needs?
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the officials' regulatory impact statement ranks the Minister's preferred option worse than the status quo on two named criteria.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The regulatory impact statement for the vocational education reform proposals (2024): true if it rates the Minister's preferred option 'worse' than the status quo against system sustainability and learner/employer needs, false if it rates it equal or better on those criteria.

civility.statement: Well, how much advice does he need in order to recognise that blocking early access to a life-saving cancer drug is a bad idea?
civility.explanation: Sharp and sarcastic in form ('how much advice does he need'), nudging at the Minister's judgement rather than purely the decision, but stops short of a personal attack.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Can he confirm he is still the Minister of Health, or has the Prime Minister’s office decided to try out some talented associates for the role?
civility.explanation: Mockery aimed at the Minister personally — suggesting he has been sidelined and is being replaced — rather than at any decision or policy.
civility.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Well, how much advice does he need in order to recognise that blocking early access to a life-saving cancer drug is a bad idea?
focus.explanation: Squarely on a named policy decision — blocking early access to Keytruda — rather than on the other party in general.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Can he confirm he is still the Minister of Health, or has the Prime Minister’s office decided to try out some talented associates for the role?
focus.explanation: Carries no policy content at all: it is entirely about the standing and internal arrangements of the other side.
focus.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Based on their own quarterly reports and our internal review of all Family Start contracts between 2022 and January 2024, they achieved, on average, 80 percent of the whānau volumes, lower numbers of home visits than were expected, and based on this information, we have reduced their fulltime-equivalents (FTEs) from 12.75 to 10.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion (reduced FTEs) is drawn from stated delivery data and tracks it proportionately; the inference from 80% of contracted volumes to a roughly 20% FTE reduction follows, though the link between volumes and staffing is asserted rather than shown.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: As we saw under previous years, you can throw more and more money at a problem, but unless you demand results, things can get worse.
rigor.explanation: A general maxim offered as if it settled the question, with no evidence connecting increased funding to worse outcomes in this sector — an appeal to received wisdom rather than an argument from the data she had just cited.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: I have taken a range of advice and, as well, I have relied on the over 30 years that I’ve spent in the sector, and so options are there for the sector to submit on.
rigor.explanation: Offered as grounds for preferring an option that her own officials ranked worse than the status quo, the support given is her personal experience — an appeal to authority that does not engage the regulatory impact statement's reasoning.
rigor.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: In the face of the last six years of declining results, 42 percent of our kids at the National Monitoring Study of Student Achievement are not at Curriculum for mathematics; half of our kids are not able to pass a functional literacy and numeracy assessment at NCEA; three consecutive years of dropping NCEA results; Programme for International Student Assessment, Trends in International Mathematics and Science Study, and Progress in International Reading Literacy Study results dropping like a stone.
veracity.explanation: Asserts four separate education data claims: an NMSSA maths figure of 42 percent not at curriculum, an NCEA literacy/numeracy co-requisite pass rate of about half, three consecutive years of falling NCEA results, and declining NZ results across PISA, TIMSS and PIRLS.
veracity.subject: other
veracity.falsification_criterion: NMSSA reports for the most recent cycle (proportion of students not at curriculum expectation in mathematics); NZQA published pass rates for the NCEA literacy and numeracy co-requisite pilots; NZQA NCEA attainment series for the three years to 2023; OECD PISA 2022, IEA TIMSS 2022/23 and PIRLS 2021 NZ mean scores versus prior cycles. True if each figure matches the published source within rounding and the international series show declines; false if any figure is materially different or a series did not decline.

veracity.statement: We saw in the last few weeks that our maths results of those young students who are measured at year 8 against the Curriculum benchmark—only 22 percent of them were at curriculum for mathematics.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that a recently released measurement of year 8 students against the curriculum benchmark found only 22 percent at curriculum level in mathematics.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The NMSSA / curriculum-benchmark maths report released in mid-2024 for year 8 students; true if the reported proportion at curriculum expectation is 22 percent (± rounding), false if materially different or if the figure refers to a different year level.

veracity.statement: Let’s look at the reality tamariki face growing up in New Zealand today: over 200,000 children live in households below the poverty line.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that more than 200,000 New Zealand children currently live in households below the poverty line.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ child poverty statistics release for the year ended June 2023; true if any of the primary poverty measures (BHC50, AHC50 or material hardship) puts the count above 200,000 children, false if all primary measures are materially below that.

veracity.statement: The royal commission of inquiry into abuse in care concluded just last month that 200,000 kids had been abused by the State in care.
veracity.explanation: Relays a finding attributed to the Royal Commission's final report: that 200,000 children were abused by the State while in care.
veracity.subject: other
veracity.subject_name: Royal Commission of Inquiry into Abuse in Care
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Royal Commission of Inquiry into Abuse in Care final report 'Whanaketia' (July 2024); true if the report estimates roughly 200,000 children abused in State care, false if the estimate covers a different population (e.g. State and faith-based care combined, or adults as well as children) or a materially different number.

veracity.statement: Of the 5,977 tamariki and rangatahi currently in the State care system, only 56 percent of these tamariki are enrolled with a primary health organisation.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a current count of children in State care and the proportion of them enrolled with a primary health organisation.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Oranga Tamariki quarterly reporting on children in care as at mid-2024, and its outcomes/health reporting on PHO enrolment; true if the care population is about 5,977 and PHO enrolment is about 56 percent, false if either figure is materially different.

veracity.statement: The Government indexed main benefits to inflation, which their own officials warned could place as many as 13,000 more children in poverty.
veracity.explanation: Relays official advice that switching main benefit indexation from wages to CPI could put up to 13,000 additional children into poverty.
veracity.subject: other
veracity.falsification_criterion: MSD/Treasury regulatory impact statements and Budget 2024 advice on the change to benefit indexation; true if officials' advice states up to around 13,000 more children in poverty, false if the advised figure is materially different or no such advice exists.

veracity.statement: Last month, the Government launched boot camps just five days after the royal commission of inquiry released its findings on horrific abuse at State boot camps.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a specific interval — five days — between the release of the Royal Commission's findings and the launch of the Government's military-style academy pilot.
veracity.subject: other
veracity.falsification_criterion: Publication date of the Royal Commission's final report and the announced start date of the Oranga Tamariki military-style academy pilot in July 2024; true if the gap is about five days, false if materially longer or shorter.

veracity.statement: We have seen almost 3,000 submissions to the Social Services and Community Committee on the removal of 7AA of the Oranga Tamariki Act.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the volume of public submissions received by a named select committee on the repeal of section 7AA.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Social Services and Community Committee records for the Oranga Tamariki (Repeal of Section 7AA) Amendment Bill; true if submissions received number close to 3,000, false if materially fewer or more.

specificity.statement: In the face of the last six years of declining results, 42 percent of our kids at the National Monitoring Study of Student Achievement are not at Curriculum for mathematics; half of our kids are not able to pass a functional literacy and numeracy assessment at NCEA; three consecutive years of dropping NCEA results; Programme for International Student Assessment, Trends in International Mathematics and Science Study, and Progress in International Reading Literacy Study results dropping like a stone.
specificity.explanation: Names four distinct assessment programmes with percentages and a stated trend period; a reader could look each one up.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We’re making sure, through the Teaching Council, that initial teacher education providers are properly teaching teacher trainees the math that they need to be confident—we’re investing $20 million into professional learning and development to do this.
specificity.explanation: Names the delivery body (Teaching Council), the target group (initial teacher education providers and trainees) and a dollar figure, though no timeframe is given.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Of the 5,977 tamariki and rangatahi currently in the State care system, only 56 percent of these tamariki are enrolled with a primary health organisation.
specificity.explanation: An exact population count and a precise percentage on a named administrative measure; directly checkable against Oranga Tamariki reporting.
specificity.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Parents know it, because after-school tuition is full, and maths and literacy and Kip McGrath and NumberWorks’nWords are all full, which is exacerbating the equity gap that we have in this country that we are trying so desperately to close.
rigor.explanation: The evidence offered for a nationwide attainment problem is that private tutoring franchises are busy — an appeal to anecdote, and the further step to 'exacerbating the equity gap' is asserted rather than shown.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Just last month, the Government diluted child poverty targets, showing the Government is comfortable putting a further 17,000 tamariki into material hardship.
rigor.explanation: Non sequitur on motive: revising a target may change what the Government is aiming for, but nothing offered establishes that it is 'comfortable' putting 17,000 children into hardship — an intention is inferred from an administrative decision.
rigor.subject: speaker

focus.statement: It was really telling today in the House that the questions from the other side were around a letter that was written to an Australian Minister in English rather than using te reo, when 20 percent of our kids are at curriculum for mathematics, and 12 percent of our Māori kids, and yet nothing from the other side on these really important issues.
focus.explanation: Carries two real attainment figures, but the weight of the sentence is on what the opposition chose to ask about rather than on the policy itself.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: It shows why in the last six years they achieved exactly nothing in education.
focus.explanation: Entirely a characterisation of the other party's record in general; no policy, measure or outcome is named.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Just last month, the Government diluted child poverty targets, showing the Government is comfortable putting a further 17,000 tamariki into material hardship.
focus.explanation: Names a specific policy decision (the revised child poverty targets), the affected measure (material hardship) and a numeric consequence.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: This attack on tamariki by the Government is targeted and deliberate. There is so much happening and it is designed this way so people switch off because it’s too painful, it’s too hard to bear witness to. This is an intentional strategy to collectively exhaust the public.
focus.explanation: No policy, figure or mechanism appears; the passage is entirely about the Government's supposed motives and character as an opponent.
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: This Government is very focused on ensuring that all regions have access to vocational education and training. We understand that it is a pathway to employment for individuals such as school leavers and those returning to the workforce. It is absolutely critical that options that we look at ensure that regional delivery can occur. The proposal that is out for consultation enables the Open Polytechnic to support those smaller regional polytechnics to be able to maintain that level of provision.
specificity.explanation: Names a real mechanism (Open Polytechnic supporting smaller regional polytechnics, out for consultation) but supplies no figures, no timeframe and no detail on how the support would work; the first three sentences are generic statements of intent.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Why is she ignoring the advice of her seven specialist advisers, who—at a cost of $2,000 a day each—told her to keep the Te Pūkenga model with some regional groupings?
specificity.explanation: Carries a count (seven advisers), a daily rate ($2,000 each), a named institution and the precise content of the advice claimed — every element is checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: I would note, again, that they were not my specialist advisers, but I would also note that under a new chief executive at Te Pūkenga, who has experience in and understanding of the sector; a new chair; and a clear set of expectations from this Minister, Te Pūkenga is at last undertaking the cost-out work and is forecasting a year-to-date surplus for the six months to 30 June 2024 of $28.5 million.
specificity.explanation: Gives a dated financial figure ($28.5 million surplus, six months to 30 June 2024) and named governance changes, though the "clear set of expectations" and "cost-out work" are left undescribed.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: The previous Government wrecked confidence in energy with the oil and gas exploration ban, with a hare-brained and wildly expensive Lake Onslow scheme, which wasn’t going to provide energy until 2038 at the earliest, costing at least $16 billion, and with their reckless 100 percent renewable electricity target by 2030.
specificity.explanation: Names three specific policies and attaches a cost ($16 billion), a commissioning date (2038) and a target with a year (100 percent renewable by 2030) — all checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Figures obtained from our gas producers released earlier this year show a 20 percent decrease in proven plus probable reserves from 1,635 petajoules to 1,300 petajoules.
specificity.explanation: Names the source of the figures, both reserve levels in petajoules, and the percentage change — fully checkable against the published series.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: This Government is taking action to respond to this through the Gas Security Response Group and the work the Gas Industry Company is leading on this issue.
specificity.explanation: Names two specific bodies doing the work, but says nothing about what actions they will take, on what timeframe, or at what cost.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Today, the Labour Party has called on the Government to use its Government procurement rules to ban Government agencies from purchasing goods and services from Israel’s illegal settlements in the Occupied Palestinian Territories, and we are also asking the Government to communicate directly to the Government of Israel that it should act immediately on the ruling of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) and withdraw from the occupied territories now.
specificity.explanation: Names the exact instrument (Government procurement rules), the exact action (barring agency purchases of goods and services from the settlements), and a second concrete diplomatic step, though no timeframe or scope of agencies is given.
specificity.subject: speaker

focus.statement: This Government is very focused on ensuring that all regions have access to vocational education and training. We understand that it is a pathway to employment for individuals such as school leavers and those returning to the workforce. It is absolutely critical that options that we look at ensure that regional delivery can occur. The proposal that is out for consultation enables the Open Polytechnic to support those smaller regional polytechnics to be able to maintain that level of provision.
focus.explanation: Entirely about the vocational education proposal itself — the delivery model, who it serves and what the consultation covers. No party framing at all, despite an obvious opening to attack the previous government's Te Pūkenga creation.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: The Labour Government had spent up large, the cupboards were bare, education, law and order, health—all were going back in the wrong direction.
focus.explanation: A sweeping characterisation of the other party's record across three portfolios with no named policy, measure, figure or outcome attached to any of them. Broad party framing rather than scrutiny of a specific commitment.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: The previous Government wrecked confidence in energy with the oil and gas exploration ban, with a hare-brained and wildly expensive Lake Onslow scheme, which wasn’t going to provide energy until 2038 at the earliest, costing at least $16 billion, and with their reckless 100 percent renewable electricity target by 2030.
focus.explanation: Criticism aimed at three named policies of the previous government rather than at the party in general — legitimate scrutiny with specific measures attached, though the pejorative framing ("hare-brained", "reckless") adds a partisan layer.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Today, the Labour Party has called on the Government to use its Government procurement rules to ban Government agencies from purchasing goods and services from Israel’s illegal settlements in the Occupied Palestinian Territories, and we are also asking the Government to communicate directly to the Government of Israel that it should act immediately on the ruling of the International Court of Justice (ICJ) and withdraw from the occupied territories now.
focus.explanation: Entirely about a proposed policy measure and the reasons for it; no party-versus-party content in the ask itself.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Why is she ignoring the advice of her seven specialist advisers, who—at a cost of $2,000 a day each—told her to keep the Te Pūkenga model with some regional groupings?
veracity.explanation: Asserts as fact that seven specialist advisers, paid $2,000 a day each, recommended retaining Te Pūkenga with regional groupings and that the Minister is departing from that advice.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The advisers' report/advice to the Minister or Te Pūkenga (proactively released papers, or an OIA release) and the contracts covering their fees; true if seven specialist advisers engaged at about $2,000 per day each recommended retaining the Te Pūkenga model with regional groupings, false if the number, the rate, or the substance of the recommendation differs materially.

veracity.statement: Well, I would note that they were not my specialist advisers. They were Te Pūkenga’s specialist advisers, and they gave a range of options, of which the option that we are consulting on was one.
veracity.explanation: Two factual assertions: that the advisers were Te Pūkenga's rather than the Minister's, and that their advice presented a range of options one of which is the proposal being consulted on.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The engagement/terms of reference for the advisers and their report; true if they were contracted by Te Pūkenga rather than the Minister and their advice set out multiple options including the one now out for consultation, false if they were engaged by the Minister or recommended a single option that excludes the consultation proposal.

veracity.statement: I would note, again, that they were not my specialist advisers, but I would also note that under a new chief executive at Te Pūkenga, who has experience in and understanding of the sector; a new chair; and a clear set of expectations from this Minister, Te Pūkenga is at last undertaking the cost-out work and is forecasting a year-to-date surplus for the six months to 30 June 2024 of $28.5 million.
veracity.explanation: Asserts Te Pūkenga was forecasting a year-to-date surplus of $28.5 million for the six months to 30 June 2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Te Pūkenga's reported financial position for the six months to 30 June 2024 (monthly/interim financial reporting or its 2024 annual report); true if a year-to-date surplus of about $28.5 million was forecast or reported for that period, false if the figure or the direction (surplus vs deficit) differs materially.

veracity.statement: The previous Government wrecked confidence in energy with the oil and gas exploration ban, with a hare-brained and wildly expensive Lake Onslow scheme, which wasn’t going to provide energy until 2038 at the earliest, costing at least $16 billion, and with their reckless 100 percent renewable electricity target by 2030.
veracity.explanation: Asserts the Lake Onslow pumped-hydro scheme would have cost at least $16 billion and delivered no energy before 2038 at the earliest.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The NZ Battery Project / Lake Onslow detailed business case published by MBIE in 2023; true if its capital cost estimate was at least $16 billion and its earliest commissioning date was 2038 or later, false if the business case put the cost materially below $16 billion or first generation materially earlier than 2038.

veracity.statement: The result is that New Zealanders are now paying the highest electricity prices in the Western World.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that New Zealand's electricity prices are, at the time of speaking, the highest in the Western world.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: International electricity price comparisons for 2024 (IEA Energy Prices, Eurostat household and industrial electricity prices, or equivalent), converted on a common basis; true if New Zealand's electricity prices were the highest among Western/OECD countries, false if any comparable Western country had higher prices.

veracity.statement: Just this morning, the spot price in Northland reached over $1,700 per megawatt hour.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a specific wholesale spot price observation for Northland on the morning of the speech.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Electricity Authority EMI wholesale spot price data for Northland nodes on 7 August 2024; true if any trading period that morning cleared above $1,700/MWh, false if the day's maximum was below that.

veracity.statement: We’ve seen that, in recent days, with the announcement of several hundred job losses at Winstone Pulp and at OJI’s Penrose facility.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that recent closure/consultation announcements at Winstone Pulp and Oji's Penrose facility together involved several hundred job losses.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Company announcements and contemporaneous reporting from mid-2024 for Winstone Pulp International and Oji Fibre Solutions' Penrose mill; true if the combined announced job losses were in the several hundreds, false if the combined total was materially below that.

veracity.statement: Figures obtained from our gas producers released earlier this year show a 20 percent decrease in proven plus probable reserves from 1,635 petajoules to 1,300 petajoules.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a roughly 20 percent year-on-year fall in proven plus probable gas reserves, from 1,635 PJ to 1,300 PJ, from producer-supplied figures released in 2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MBIE's annual petroleum reserves data (producer-supplied 2P reserves as at 1 January 2024 versus the prior year); true if 2P gas reserves fell from about 1,635 PJ to about 1,300 PJ, false if the published figures differ materially.

veracity.statement: The world has watched in horror over the last eight months as Israel has killed nearly 40,000 civilians in Gaza, in spite of repeated calls by the United Nations General Assembly for a permanent ceasefire.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a death toll of nearly 40,000 civilians in Gaza over the eight months to August 2024; the contested element is both the magnitude and the attribution of the whole total to civilians.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Gaza Ministry of Health and UN OCHA casualty reporting as at early August 2024, and whether those totals are civilian-only or all deaths; true if close to 40,000 civilian deaths were recorded over the preceding eight months, false if the ~40,000 figure covers all deaths including combatants or the total differs materially.

veracity.statement: Governments, like New Zealand, have a duty to act and this builds on a range of initiatives and policies that successive New Zealand Governments have held on this issue, and I want to reference when Murray McCully was the Foreign Minister of the National Government of the time, in 2016, New Zealand then held a non-permanent seat on the UN Security Council and co-sponsored a resolution that was passed in the Security Council that condemned Israel’s illegal settlements and called on Governments—with the force of international law—to differentiate between Israel the State, and the Occupied Palestinian Territories.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that New Zealand, under Foreign Minister Murray McCully and while on the Security Council in 2016, co-sponsored a resolution condemning Israeli settlements and calling for differentiation.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: UN Security Council records for December 2016: the sponsorship list and text of Resolution 2334, and New Zealand's Security Council membership term; true if New Zealand co-sponsored a 2016 resolution condemning the settlements while holding a non-permanent seat under Foreign Minister Murray McCully, false if it did not co-sponsor or the resolution's content differs.

veracity.statement: I also want to point out that our Government, in recent days, has called on the Government of New Zealand to recognise Palestine, to give it diplomatic recognition, just as Ireland has done in recent days, just as Spain and Norway have done—144 other countries in the United Nations have recognised Palestine, as a way of signalling the need for a negotiated political settlement in the region.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that 144 other UN member countries had recognised Palestine, and that Ireland, Spain and Norway had recently done so.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Scoped to the count only: UN and foreign-ministry records of states recognising the State of Palestine as at August 2024, including the 2024 recognitions by Ireland, Spain and Norway; true if the number of UN member states recognising Palestine was about 144, false if materially higher or lower. (The opening clause is a live-speech slip for the Labour Party, not a claim to be checked.)

civility.statement: Why is she ignoring the advice of her seven specialist advisers, who—at a cost of $2,000 a day each—told her to keep the Te Pūkenga model with some regional groupings?
civility.explanation: Pointed accountability question about the Minister's handling of advice; it presses hard on her decision but does not attack her character.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: Isn’t it true that the real, abject failure here is a Minister who is so set on protecting her own pet institution that she just doesn’t give a damn about the needs of the rest of the country?
civility.explanation: Turns from the policy to the Minister personally — imputes self-interested motive ("protecting her own pet institution") and personal indifference ("doesn't give a damn"). A clear personal attack rather than criticism of the proposal.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: You’d think somebody with a modicum of education would not begin by “Isn’t it true”, but then that soon was compounded by her outrageous sort of venting of her dislike for the Minister and not knowing her subject at the same time.
civility.explanation: Sustained attack on another member personally: her education, her emotional state, and her competence on the subject. Nothing is directed at the argument.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I would note, again, that they were not my specialist advisers, but I would also note that under a new chief executive at Te Pūkenga, who has experience in and understanding of the sector; a new chair; and a clear set of expectations from this Minister, Te Pūkenga is at last undertaking the cost-out work and is forecasting a year-to-date surplus for the six months to 30 June 2024 of $28.5 million.
civility.explanation: Responds to a question that accused her of not giving a damn by dealing with the substance — the advisers' provenance and Te Pūkenga's finances — without retaliating against the questioner.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: The previous Government wrecked confidence in energy with the oil and gas exploration ban, with a hare-brained and wildly expensive Lake Onslow scheme, which wasn’t going to provide energy until 2038 at the earliest, costing at least $16 billion, and with their reckless 100 percent renewable electricity target by 2030.
civility.explanation: Harsh language, but every barb lands on the policies — the ban, the scheme, the target — and not on any individual.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: After stifling investment in the gas sector, after increasing our sovereign risk as a country, and after six long years of Megan Woods thinking she knows best, New Zealand now finds itself in an energy crunch with dry year conditions being compounded by a low supply of gas, which is critically important at this time.
civility.explanation: Sneers at a named member's judgement — "six long years of Megan Woods thinking she knows best" imputes arrogance to the person rather than criticising the decisions she made.
civility.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: The high electricity prices New Zealanders are facing are deeply concerning and a direct result of those policies.
rigor.explanation: A single-cause attribution: the surrounding remarks do supply a mechanism (exploration ban reducing gas supply, generators burning coal and diesel, peakers idle), but the conclusion that prices are a "direct result" of those policies discounts the dry-year hydrology he himself names in the same speech. Post hoc reasoning with a partial mechanism behind it.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: If this Government doesn’t speak out on this question that the ICJ has ruled on, if it doesn’t take the kind of practical actions that we are calling for today—at least in the beginning, a ban on Government procurement of goods and services produced in the illegal settlements—then this Government is inviting people to accuse it of being selective, inconsistent, and hypocritical and undermining New Zealand’s standing in the world.
rigor.explanation: A genuine consistency argument: the premise that the Government professes support for the rules-based order, plus an ICJ finding of obligations on all states, supports the conclusion that inaction would expose it to charges of inconsistency. The weaker link is the jump to "undermining New Zealand's standing in the world", which is asserted rather than supported.
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: This Government is being led by a dark triad, and let me explain what that means. Three personality traits: the Machiavellian, the psychopath, and the narcissist, and I’ll get you to guess which one is which.
civility.explanation: Ascribes psychopathy, narcissism and manipulativeness to the three identifiable coalition leaders and invites the House to match the trait to the individual — an attack on personal character rather than on any policy.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: How has ACT groomed the Prime Minister and, indeed, National into deliberately exercising ethnocide?
civility.explanation: Imputes to the Prime Minister personally both susceptibility to 'grooming' and deliberate intent to destroy a culture; the charge lands on the person, not on a measure.
civility.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Māori-focused solutions designed for generations are ending. The Māori Health Authority is demolished. Māori mokopuna in State detention with solutions like section 7AA—gone. Auahi kāti programmes, demolishing Māori wards, fast-tracking seabed mining.
focus.explanation: Names specific measures — the Māori Health Authority, section 7AA of the Oranga Tamariki Act, smokefree programmes, Māori wards, fast-track seabed mining — rather than characterising the other parties in general terms.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: This Government has lost control. It is very clear, whānau mā, that National is being run by ACT, and they’re allowing them to destroy our culture, one repeal, one piece of legislation, one punch, at a time—very hard and very low, and it’s deeply, deeply dark.
focus.explanation: Entirely about the internal dynamics between the two governing parties — who is running whom — with no named repeal, bill or outcome despite a policy debate being available to engage.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Women are too smart to fall for lip-service. They were not interested in the press releases and proclamations of the Labour Government.
focus.explanation: Characterises the previous government's communications as empty without naming a single policy, figure or outcome; the content is entirely about the other party.
focus.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Māori-focused solutions designed for generations are ending. The Māori Health Authority is demolished. Māori mokopuna in State detention with solutions like section 7AA—gone. Auahi kāti programmes, demolishing Māori wards, fast-tracking seabed mining.
specificity.explanation: Names identifiable policies and statutory provisions that a reader could look up, but supplies no figures, dates or mechanisms.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: We have been delighted to announce our FamilyBoost policy in this year’s Budget, which enables parents who qualify up to $150 a fortnight to go towards childcare, to get our mums back into the workforce, if they so choose.
specificity.explanation: Names the policy, its source (Budget 2024), the amount ($150 a fortnight), the eligibility qualifier and the intended effect — all checkable.
specificity.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: The Māori Health Authority is demolished.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the Māori Health Authority (Te Aka Whai Ora) has been abolished as at August 2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Pae Ora (Disestablishment of Māori Health Authority) Amendment Act and Ministry of Health/Te Whatu Ora records: true if Te Aka Whai Ora had been disestablished by legislation with functions transferred before 7 August 2024; false if it remained a standing statutory entity at that date.

veracity.statement: I think back to the previous Labour Government voting down Nicola Willis’ member’s bill that would have allowed parents to share their leave.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Labour MPs voted to defeat a Nicola Willis member's bill providing for shared/transferable parental leave.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Hansard division record for the first reading of Nicola Willis' member's bill on shared parental leave: true if the bill was defeated with Labour voting against, false if it was never voted on, was not her bill, or Labour did not vote it down.

veracity.statement: We’re in the business of boosting Pharmac to $6.3 billion over the next four years—that is the largest budget that Pharmac has ever seen.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a $6.3 billion four-year Pharmac allocation and that this is the largest Pharmac budget in its history.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Budget 2024 Vote Health / Pharmac appropriation documents and Pharmac's historical annual budgets: true if the four-year combined allocation is approximately $6.3 billion and exceeds all prior equivalent allocations; false if the figure is materially different or a prior allocation was higher.

veracity.statement: Under the last Government, it sat on or around 9 percent for six long years.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the gender pay gap remained at roughly 9 percent throughout the 2017–2023 Labour-led governments.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ gender pay gap series (Household Labour Force Survey / New Zealand Income Survey) for 2017 through 2023: true if the published gap sat within about a percentage point of 9% across those years, false if it moved materially outside that band.

focus.statement: National promised voters that the cost of living would come down, that crime would stop, incomes would grow, climate change would be addressed, and we would all be better off, but that is not what we are seeing.
focus.explanation: Scrutiny of a set of named campaign commitments, which is on-policy accountability, but the promises are listed only in general terms with no specific measure or figure attached.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: You just can’t trust this Government, because nothing they do stacks up. It’s just slogans.
focus.explanation: Entirely a characterisation of the other side — trustworthiness and sloganeering in general. No policy, measure, figure or outcome is named in the statement itself.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: I think he spends more time working outside of Auckland than in, but he also has no plan to reduce congestion, to reduce crime, and, what I’ve spoken to today, he’s got no plan to reduce the cost of living.
focus.explanation: Three real policy areas are named (congestion, crime, cost of living), but the weight of the sentence is on the Minister's absence and an unevidenced 'no plan' assertion rather than on the content of any plan.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Now, those folks on the other side of the House will find every reason to oppose this and to rail against this, and they’ll say that the curriculum won’t be right or that it was National’s fault, or whatever other rebuttal they’ll come up with.
focus.explanation: Pre-emptively characterises how the Opposition will behave rather than engaging the education policy itself; strip out the claim about the other side and no policy content remains.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: I just want to say, too, to the good hard-working taxpaying people of New Zealand who are now enjoying tax relief for the first time in 14 years, we won’t be taking advice from an Opposition who overtaxed, overspent, and, now, is over there.
focus.explanation: Touches one real policy (the 2024 tax relief) but the sentence's weight is a general characterisation of the Opposition's record and its place on the benches, with no measure, figure or mechanism named.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: Under National, “back on track” means rents are up, unemployment is up, benefit numbers are up, groceries are up.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that four indicators — rents, unemployment, benefit recipient numbers and grocery prices — have all risen since the National-led Government took office in late 2023.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Stats NZ rental price index, HLFS unemployment rate, food price index, and MSD benefit numbers between the December 2023 quarter and the June 2024 quarter; true if all four rose, false if any of the four fell or was flat.

veracity.statement: Auckland businesses are closing at a much higher rate than their counterparts in the rest of the country.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a regional differential in business closures: Auckland closing/liquidation rates materially exceed the rest of New Zealand at the time of speaking.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Companies Office liquidation/removal data or Centrix business insolvency reporting broken down by region for 2024; true if Auckland's closure rate per capita of registered businesses clearly exceeds the national ex-Auckland rate, false if it is comparable or lower.

veracity.statement: They believe that the still-to-be-proven repeal of the regional fuel tax eases the cost of living, and even if this was so, that gives Aucklanders back a mere $2 per week.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that removing Auckland's regional fuel tax returns about $2 per week to the average Aucklander.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The 11.5c/litre (incl. GST) regional fuel tax rate applied to average Auckland household weekly petrol consumption, per Ministry of Transport / Auckland Council household fuel-use estimates; true if the resulting saving is around $2/week, false if materially larger (e.g. the ~$5-7/week figures cited by the Government).

veracity.statement: Even with all of their talk of tax cuts, an average Auckland family will pay at least $80 more per week under this National Government—$80 more per week.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a net weekly cost increase of at least $80 for an average Auckland family after accounting for the Government's tax cuts.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: An itemised costing comparing the 2024 personal income tax threshold changes plus regional fuel tax repeal against increases in motor vehicle registration fees, public transport fares, prescription charges and fuel excise for a median Auckland household; true if the net weekly position is -$80 or worse, false if the net position is materially better than that.

veracity.statement: In addition to that, huge cuts to Oranga Tamariki funding, including the North Shore Women’s Centre, leaving up to 500 women—vulnerable women and their tamariki—without support and forcing their closure.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Oranga Tamariki funding cuts led to the North Shore Women's Centre closing and left up to 500 women and children without support.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Oranga Tamariki contract records and the North Shore Women's Centre's own 2024 statements/media coverage; true if the centre lost OT funding and announced closure in 2024 with a client base of that order, false if it did not close or its closure is not attributable to OT funding decisions.

veracity.statement: Beach Haven Primary School, Birkenhead Primary, and Willow Park Schools—they’ve cancelled the building of our classrooms.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that planned classroom construction at three named North Shore schools was cancelled by the Government.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Education school property programme records and the December 2023/2024 announcements on paused or cancelled school property projects; true if projects at Beach Haven Primary, Birkenhead Primary and Willow Park School were cancelled, false if they were deferred only or remain funded.

veracity.statement: Only 22 percent of our year 8 students are achieving at year 8 level.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that 22 percent of New Zealand Year 8 students are achieving at the expected curriculum level (in the context of the maths and literacy results reported that week).
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Ministry of Education's curriculum benchmarking study of Year 8 mathematics achievement reported in 2024; true if the proportion at expected curriculum level is about 22%, false if materially different or if the figure applies to a different year level or subject than stated.

veracity.statement: Regular attendance ranges from 29 percent in some towns to 59 percent, which is the highest, across thousands of students in our electorate.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that regular school attendance rates within the East Coast electorate span from 29 percent at the low end to 59 percent at the high end.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Ministry of Education regular attendance data by territorial authority/town for the East Coast electorate area, 2023-24; true if the lowest and highest town-level rates are approximately 29% and 59%, false if the observed range differs materially.

veracity.statement: What I can’t help but shake my head at is a member of the Green Party, a former Minister of Transport no less, who, in speaking against the bill, said of the evidence that deaths and serious road accidents caused by drugs was only 7 percent and, therefore, in her terms, weren’t that serious.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that a Green Party member and former Transport Minister, speaking against the roadside drug-testing bill, cited a 7 percent figure for drug-caused road deaths and characterised that as not serious.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Hansard record of the Land Transport (Drug Driving) Amendment Bill debate in the weeks before 7 August 2024; true if the member cited ~7% and dismissed its seriousness, false if she cited a different figure or did not characterise the deaths as not serious.

veracity.statement: I just want to say, too, to the good hard-working taxpaying people of New Zealand who are now enjoying tax relief for the first time in 14 years, we won’t be taking advice from an Opposition who overtaxed, overspent, and, now, is over there.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the 2024 tax relief is the first tax relief New Zealanders have received in 14 years, i.e. since 2010.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The legislative record of personal income tax rate and threshold changes since 2010; true if no reduction in personal income tax rates or increase in thresholds took effect between 2010 and 2024, false if any such relief (including the Independent Earner Tax Credit changes or other threshold adjustments) took effect in that period.

specificity.statement: Under National, “back on track” means rents are up, unemployment is up, benefit numbers are up, groceries are up.
specificity.explanation: Names four checkable indicators and a direction of travel, but supplies no figures, no magnitudes and no time period.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: They believe that the still-to-be-proven repeal of the regional fuel tax eases the cost of living, and even if this was so, that gives Aucklanders back a mere $2 per week.
specificity.explanation: Names the specific policy (regional fuel tax repeal) and puts a precise per-household weekly figure on its benefit, which someone could check or recompute.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Beach Haven Primary School, Birkenhead Primary, and Willow Park Schools—they’ve cancelled the building of our classrooms.
specificity.explanation: Names three individual schools and a specific action taken against each; precise enough that the Ministry's property records would settle it.
specificity.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Even with all of their talk of tax cuts, an average Auckland family will pay at least $80 more per week under this National Government—$80 more per week.
rigor.explanation: The conclusion is reached by summing a list of added costs (rego, public transport, prescriptions, fuel excise) while netting out only a dismissed $2 fuel-tax saving; the $50 rego increase is an annual figure being marshalled toward a weekly total, so the arithmetic does not support the stated per-week conclusion.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Well, tell that to the parents and friends and family of people who died because people took drugs and drove their vehicles.
rigor.explanation: A bare appeal to emotion: the grief of bereaved families is offered in place of any engagement with the 7 percent figure, so nothing is supplied that would show the statistical premise wrong or the policy conclusion right.
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I think he spends more time working outside of Auckland than in, but he also has no plan to reduce congestion, to reduce crime, and, what I’ve spoken to today, he’s got no plan to reduce the cost of living.
civility.explanation: The second half criticises the Minister's policy programme, but the opening imputes personal neglect of the job — a sneer at how the man spends his time rather than at any decision he has made.
civility.subject: speaker

civility.statement: What I can’t help but shake my head at is a member of the Green Party, a former Minister of Transport no less, who, in speaking against the bill, said of the evidence that deaths and serious road accidents caused by drugs was only 7 percent and, therefore, in her terms, weren’t that serious.
civility.explanation: Identifies a specific member ('a former Minister of Transport no less') and attributes to her the position that road deaths 'weren't that serious' — mockery that imputes callousness to the individual rather than engaging her statistical point.
civility.subject: speaker

focus.statement: We’ve seen broken promises with the number of psychiatrists promised by this National-led Government before the election—14; we have not seen any movement of that.
focus.explanation: Names a specific pre-election commitment (14 psychiatrists) and a specific outcome (no movement). This is scrutiny of a named policy promise, not party-bashing.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: I have to say that my leader, the Rt Hon Winston Peters, would have to be the hardest-working and most highly respected Foreign Minister.
focus.explanation: Praise of a colleague's personal standing with no policy, mechanism, figure or outcome attached — the content is about the team, not the policy.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: In fact, that previous Government were absent in terms of their connection with the Pacific.
focus.explanation: A blanket characterisation of the previous Government's record with no named programme, visit, funding line or measurable outcome; pure party contrast rather than policy content.
focus.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: We’ve seen broken promises with the number of psychiatrists promised by this National-led Government before the election—14; we have not seen any movement of that.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the National Party promised 14 additional psychiatrists before the 2023 election and that no progress has been made on delivering them.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: National's 2023 mental health policy document and costings for the number of psychiatrists promised; then Health NZ / Ministry of Health workforce reporting or ministerial answers on psychiatrist numbers since October 2023. True if the promise was 14 and psychiatrist numbers show no net increase by August 2024; false if the promised figure differs materially or if additional psychiatrists had been placed.

veracity.statement: They’ve promised 500 new mental health staff and yet they haven’t even been able to get the 50 extra doctors placed that they had promised prior to the election.
veracity.explanation: Two factual assertions: that the Government promised 500 new mental health staff and 50 extra doctors, and that the 50 doctors had not been placed as at August 2024.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: National/coalition mental health policy announcements for the figures 500 mental health workers and 50 doctors; Health NZ or ministerial statements on placements as at August 2024. True if both figures match the announced commitments and no doctor placements had occurred; false if the figures are wrong or placements had been made.

veracity.statement: To get that funding, the organisations have to have a minimum of 80 full-time employees and $250,000 in matching funding.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the eligibility criteria for the remaining health innovation/mental health fund require applicants to have at least 80 full-time employees and $250,000 in matching funding.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The published eligibility criteria / request for proposals for the Budget 2024 mental health innovation fund administered by Health NZ. True if the criteria specify a minimum of 80 FTE and $250,000 co-funding; false if the thresholds differ or no such thresholds exist.

veracity.statement: We have seen that in Southland, no less—the area where both Marty and I were very approximate to—where staff had sent emails showing that vacancies for mental health nurses, despite the fact that those roles are desperately needed, ads have been pulled down from Health New Zealand’s website.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that internal staff emails show Health NZ removed advertisements for vacant mental health nursing roles in Southland from its website.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Health NZ Southland job-advertisement record, the leaked staff emails, or Health NZ's response to media/OIA on whether mental health nurse vacancies were de-advertised in mid-2024. True if vacancy ads were withdrawn while roles remained unfilled; false if no such removal occurred.

veracity.statement: Today, in the House, this very day, the Prime Minister actually noted that the Foreign Minister is doing an exceptional job as a Foreign Minister for New Zealand and that we should be incredibly proud of him, because he’s lifting the intensity and urgency of our relationships across the Indo-Pacific like no one has done before.
veracity.explanation: Relays a specific claim attributed to the Prime Minister earlier the same sitting day, that the Foreign Minister is doing an exceptional job and lifting the intensity of Indo-Pacific relationships like no one before.
veracity.subject: other
veracity.falsification_criterion: The Hansard record for 7 August 2024 (question time/debate). True if the Prime Minister made substantially these remarks about the Foreign Minister that day; false if no such statement appears in the day's record.

veracity.statement: Our Māori Centre, $50 million has been sent off to the Pacific to support sustainable Pacific Islands fisheries development over the next four years.
veracity.explanation: Asserts a $50 million New Zealand funding commitment to Pacific Islands sustainable fisheries development spread over four years.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MFAT/Ministry for Oceans and Fisheries announcements and Budget 2024 Pacific development allocations in 2024. True if a $50m, four-year Pacific fisheries package was announced; false if the amount or duration differs materially or no such package exists.

veracity.statement: I have been to New Caledonia, where I was able to attend the Anzac celebrations earlier this year—the first time a Government representative in more than a decade visited Noumea for those Anzac celebrations.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that her April 2024 attendance at Anzac commemorations in Noumea was the first visit by a New Zealand Government representative to those commemorations in over ten years.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: MFAT records and NZ High Commission/consular reporting on New Zealand ministerial or parliamentary representation at Anzac Day commemorations in Noumea, 2014-2023. True if no Government representative attended in that period; false if one did.

specificity.statement: To get that funding, the organisations have to have a minimum of 80 full-time employees and $250,000 in matching funding.
specificity.explanation: Two precise, checkable eligibility thresholds (80 FTE, $250,000 matching funding) attached to a named funding round.
specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Our Māori Centre, $50 million has been sent off to the Pacific to support sustainable Pacific Islands fisheries development over the next four years.
specificity.explanation: Gives an amount ($50 million), a purpose (sustainable Pacific fisheries development) and a timeframe (four years), though the delivery mechanism and recipients are unnamed.
specificity.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: I would challenge any member of this House to tell me which community mental health group has a spare $250,000 kicking around in their bank account, or, if they did, that it would not be taken back by this Government as we heard in question time today.
rigor.explanation: The inference that the criteria exclude community providers rests on a rhetorical challenge to disprove rather than on evidence about the sector's finances — a shifting-the-burden move — though the underlying point about the matching-funding threshold is a real one.
rigor.subject: speaker

civility.statement: I would challenge any member of this House to tell me which community mental health group has a spare $250,000 kicking around in their bank account, or, if they did, that it would not be taken back by this Government as we heard in question time today.
civility.explanation: Sharp criticism aimed entirely at the funding design and the Government's conduct; no individual member is attacked or impugned.
civility.subject: speaker

veracity.statement: In fact, 145 years ago, the first ship arrived delivering the first group of what turned out to be more than 60,000 people who the British colonial authorities shipped from India to cut sugar cane in Fiji, and it was indentured labour.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that the first ship of Indian indentured labourers arrived in Fiji 145 years before the statement (i.e. 1879) and that the total shipped exceeded 60,000.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Fiji/Indian indenture historical records: date of arrival of the first indenture ship to Fiji (true if 1879, giving 145 years from 2024) and the total number of Indian indentured labourers transported to Fiji (true if the total exceeds 60,000; false if materially fewer or if the first-ship date is materially different).

veracity.statement: I was thinking how good it would have been if they’d supported the tax relief the hard-working low and middle income earners are now getting in their back pockets. Not only didn’t they support it, some of them even asked for it to be donated to them.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that Opposition members voted against the Government's 2024 tax relief package and that some of them publicly asked for their share to be donated.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Hansard division record for the Taxation (Budget Measures) Bill 2024 / the Budget 2024 tax threshold changes — true if Labour voted against; plus contemporaneous reporting or statements of Labour MPs saying they would donate or decline their tax cut. False if Labour supported the measure or no such donation statements exist.

veracity.statement: Only one member of the Māori Battalion is still alive, and this bill will help preserve the legacy and mana of the Māori Battalion by ensuring there is representation of Māori soldiers or veterans on the board.
veracity.explanation: Asserts that as at August 2024 exactly one veteran of the 28th (Māori) Battalion was still living.
veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: Contemporaneous NZDF / 28th Māori Battalion association records and news reporting on surviving veterans as at August 2024; true if exactly one veteran was then living, false if more than one (or none) were.

focus.statement: So my question to the Minister, really quickly, is just about understanding the beneficial part, the subjective part of it, and the hierarchy of subclauses (1), (2), and (3). I think there is no hierarchy, but I just want to make it clear for Hansard.
focus.explanation: Entirely directed at the mechanism of the clause before the committee — the threshold for appointing a Crown facilitator. No party content at all.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: There’s a range of possible scenarios, and I don’t think it’s helpful for the committee to speculate, but, ultimately, this is a broad range of powers which can be applied in a broad range of circumstances, and which option is required will be used depending on what the circumstances are.
focus.explanation: Despite its vagueness it is squarely about the intervention powers in Subpart 2 and says nothing about the opposition or any party. High focus, low specificity — the two come apart cleanly here.
focus.subject: speaker

focus.statement: Now, why it’s so important that regional councils are actually involved in the planning, the alternative consultation, and potential joint water service arrangements is that we know that councils, particularly district, city, and unitaries, swear this oath when they’re elected—councillors do—and they are subjected to their oath and then making the best decisions for the citizens in their rohe or their territorial authority boundary. Why it’s so important, when we’re talking about collective water services, that regional councils actually have a voice in this is because it automatically gives the elected member representation to be a voice for the good of the entire region.
focus.explanation: Argues for a named amendment (No. 66, clause 8A) on a specific mechanism — regional council participation in joint water service arrangements. No party framing whatsoever.
focus.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: I kind of don’t understand why that would be necessary, because then if they can’t agree to a joint plan, they don’t have a joint plan. It doesn’t meet the definition which is in Part 1 of this bill, which is what a joint service delivery plan is, which I kind of had talked about the drafting in clause 9 being a little bit muddled and trying to understand that.
rigor.explanation: A real inference about the drafting: if the group cannot agree, no joint plan exists on the Part 1 definition, so the trigger in subclause (2) is said to be redundant. The step is coherent but has a gap — the intervention power is arguably aimed at producing agreement in the first place, which the argument does not address.
rigor.subject: speaker

rigor.statement: Now, why it’s so important that regional councils are actually involved in the planning, the alternative consultation, and potential joint water service arrangements is that we know that councils, particularly district, city, and unitaries, swear this oath when they’re elected—councillors do—and they are subjected to their oath and then making the best decisions for the citizens in their rohe or their territorial authority boundary. Why it’s so important, when we’re talking about collective water services, that regional councils actually have a voice in this is because it automatically gives the elected member representation to be a voice for the good of the entire region.
rigor.explanation: A structured inference: territorial councillors are bound by oath to their own district's interests, water services under the bill cross district boundaries, therefore a body whose mandate is regional should have a seat. The step from 'regional council involved' to 'automatically gives' a whole-of-region voice is asserted rather than shown, and regional councillors are themselves elected from constituencies — a real gap, but the structure holds.
rigor.subject: speaker

divination.statement: I think, ultimately, the Government’s very clear message here is our expectation is that councils will work, either themselves or collaborate with other councils, to put forward these plans within the time frame and that they will put them forward, that they’ll be accepted, and that they will implement them and then they will deliver against them.
divination.explanation: Forecasts that territorial authorities — third parties, not the speaker's own government — will submit water services delivery plans within the statutory timeframe and have them accepted, without the backstop powers being needed at scale.
divination.subject: speaker
divination.falsification_criterion: Department of Internal Affairs / Secretary for Local Government records of water services delivery plan submissions under the Local Government (Water Services Preliminary Arrangements) Act; true if substantially all territorial authorities submitted a plan by the statutory deadline (3 September 2025) and those plans were accepted; false if a material number of councils missed the deadline or had plans rejected.

veracity.statement: Wellington Region and Horowhenua District’s joint council submission picked this up really clearly when they talked about the impacts and views relating to an entire joint service area—i.e., considerations beyond the council’s own district and communities.

veracity.subject: speaker
veracity.falsification_criterion: The written submissions to the Finance and Expenditure Committee on the Local Government (Water Services Preliminary Arrangements) Bill, published on parliament.nz; true if a joint submission from Wellington Region councils together with Horowhenua District exists and argues for considering impacts and views across the whole joint service area; false if no such joint submission exists or it makes no such argument.

focus.statement: Well, I would just say to the member, that bill is very important to this Government, as is Celebrity Treasure Island to the Opposition.

focus.statement: Again, on behalf of the Minister of Finance, we have inherited a number of challenges as a Government, which we are having to clean up with the mess left behind by the previous Government. They were spending like drunken sailors, they were borrowing, they had interest rates and inflation through the roof, and this Government has been elected to fix this economy, to ensure our public services are delivering on the front line for New Zealanders, but we have a huge mess to clean up.

specificity.statement: From today, it will be able to support leverage for water council-controlled organisations (CCOs) up to a level equivalent of 500 percent of revenue—around twice that of existing financing levels for councils, subject to water organisations meeting prudent credit criteria.

specificity.statement: On behalf of the Minister of Health, our aspiration is to grow a domestic pipeline of representative workforce for New Zealanders.

specificity.subject: speaker

specificity.statement: Are they not delivering in health because her Government is leaving clinics like those in Dargaville, Wellsford, Kenepuru, Napier, and Rotorua unstaffed overnight?

veracity.statement: From today, it will be able to support leverage for water council-controlled organisations (CCOs) up to a level equivalent of 500 percent of revenue—around twice that of existing financing levels for councils, subject to water organisations meeting prudent credit criteria.
